（24：24）：我知道这是一个不同的话题，但是脱掉你的鞋子，把你的笔记本电脑从你的包里拿出来，把它放在扫描仪上，提供先进的乘客信息。你通过了安检，你的身份证被检查了四次。你不能用无人机这么做。你有一些东西出现在雷达上或被探测到的东西，然后你需要遵循非常具体的步骤来进行积极的识别。然后，即使在做出肯定的鉴定之后，你也需要有如何处理这种情况的步骤。我们已经在航空安全的反恐方面做了所有这些工作，以应对简易爆炸装置、劫机类型的情况以及飞机上可能发生的其他形式的非法干扰。我们已经分享了所有这些信息，自9/11以来，作为一个行业，我们一直在努力工作，虽然乘客可以看到一些有形的东西，但也有幕后的协调，以确保以最有效的方式应对威胁。
（25：36）：无人机的困难在于，从航空安全的反恐角度来看，它通常涉及民事和军事协调，这是不一样的。因为我们处理这种冲突和溢出视角，甚至是有国家行为者参与的混合战争，这使国家在信息共享方面处于冲突状态。我们不是在与恐怖分子打交道，可以这么说，一般来说，每个人都可以参与进来，以阻止威胁的发生。现在的问题是，你站在冲突的哪一边？你是站在俄罗斯一边还是站在北约一边？你站在乌克兰一边吗？你是白俄罗斯那边的吗？地缘政治与无人机威胁交织在一起，我认为从反恐的角度来看，我们在处理后9/11时代时并不存在这种情况。因此，我们需要审视9/11事件后为信息共享、威胁识别和缓解措施制定的框架，然后提出一种方法，我们可以克服一些地缘政治动力，这些动力已经否定了我们以同样的方式处理无人机威胁的能力。
凯伦·沃克（26：41）：令人着迷。以一种相当残酷的方式，这是一个全新的世界，不是吗？这很有趣。我的意思是，我们在这里纪念9/11袭击25周年，我认为你已经提出了一些非常好的观点，当然从中学到了很多东西，但你仍然要继续适应，因为每个人都在适应，不是吗？
马特·博里（27：05）：我们现在面临的问题是，自2014年以来，已经有三架客机被击落，而每架飞机的情况并没有太大的不同。我的观点是，如果自2014年以来，有三架客机以大致相同的方式被爆炸装置炸毁，我们就会对正在发生的事情采取不同的方法。但是，冲突地区的最大问题是我们正在处理的这些冲突，它们是国家对国家的冲突，对吧？这不是全球反恐战争中的伊拉克和阿富汗，你有一个明确的敌人，那就是联合国承认的恐怖组织。你有单独的国家，这些冲突是跨国界的。俄罗斯-乌克兰不仅影响俄罗斯，也影响乌克兰。它蔓延到波兰，立陶宛，拉脱维亚，爱沙尼亚，芬兰，罗马尼亚，保加利亚，土耳其，对吗？是乔治亚。这是中东的一场冲突，有多少国家的领空受到影响，他们都应该相互分享关于这是如何发生的信息。
（28：15）：伊朗不会与约旦分享关于何时发射导弹和无人机的信息，假设根据导弹或无人机的发射方式，中间有三个空域。他们没有告诉沙特阿拉伯，“哦，顺便说一下，我们将向约旦发射一些导弹，它们可能会穿过你们的领空。”这是技术上应该发生的事情，但我们都知道它不是。因此，这种类型的常规冲突使得避免像客机被击落这样的灾难性事件所需的合作变得更加困难，而在9/11后的世界里，反恐信息共享是每个人的工作，每个人都明白这是我们要做的，以确保航空旅行的安全。对此有一种更具协作性的方法。我不是说它是完美的，但这一次的合作，它正在发生，但它发生在竖井里，那里仍然有好人和坏人，由于地缘政治，克服这一点很难。
凯伦·沃克（29：13）：有很多值得思考的东西，马特。非常感谢您再次加入我们，并感谢您对此的专业见解。我希望你能再次加入我们。我相信这些问题不会消失，所以继续回来。
马特·博里（29：27）：希望在一场或多场冲突中实现了和平，我们将讨论如何在冲突地区环境中开放空域，而不是讨论内部的一些影响。
凯伦·沃克（29：42）：谢谢。也感谢我们的制作人，科里·希特和娜塔莉亚·佩拉约，当然，非常感谢你们，我们的听众。通过订阅苹果播客或任何你喜欢收听的地方的窗口座位，确保你不会错过我们。我是凯伦·沃克，从靠窗的座位下来。
_source.trans_title: 播客：冲突地区无人机，民用航空和空域安全

_source.content:
A screening of a film in a small room in a downtown Taipei office building has raised fears in the country’s government.
It comes after Russian officials hosted an unusual screening of an old Soviet documentary called "Smashing Militarist Japan" for some 20 Taiwanese guests.
Despite the small audience, the screening of the 81-year-old film has alarmed Taiwan's government. Russia, it believes, is helping China push its narrative of a rising military threat from Japan, and is seeking to sow ⁠discord over Taipei's relations with Tokyo and other Western partners.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi last year suggested a hypothetical Chinese attack on Taiwan could trigger a Japanese military response, causing a diplomatic crisis between Tokyo and Beijing and prompting repeated warnings from Beijing that Japan is seeking a return to its aggressive past.
Officials in Taiwan say they believe the closed-door screening last week of the film by the de facto Russian embassy in Taipei is part of a new effort to spread and bolster China's "new militarism" line against Japan, a key though unofficial ally ⁠of Taipei.
Russia's foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment. China's foreign ministry ​said ⁠it was unaware of the screening of the old Soviet-era film.
It added that Allied powers, including China, Russia and the U.S., had defeated Japanese militarism, and that "upholding and promoting a correct historical view of World War Two is the shared responsibility of the international community".
The film shown ⁠was 1945's black-and-white "The Defeat of Militarist Japan", which the Russian office translated into Chinese on Facebook as "Smashing Militarist Japan".
The film, available on YouTube under the ​name "The defeat of Japan", ⁠shows images of the Soviet attack on Japanese-occupied Manchuria and the ‌Kuril Islands. A voiceover denounces the "robber philosophy of the divine superiority of the Japanese race" and shows footage of Japanese atrocities against Chinese civilians.
The showing of the film sits in a sensitive area for Taiwan: freedom of speech is constitutionally protected, but it also has laws, including the 2019 Anti-Infiltration Act, aimed at preventing ‌hostile foreign forces — chiefly China — from covertly influencing its politics.
There was no police presence outside the ‌screening and no effort was made to shut it down.
Taiwan's National Security Council, its highest government body overseeing security and counter-intelligence, told Reuters it was "closely monitoring" Chinese-Russian military and "cognitive warfare" cooperation when asked about the screening.
"The two countries are attempting to amplify specific topics and distort historical facts and political issues," it said.
Taiwanese officials said Russia posed a new challenge because Moscow could approach some Taiwan contacts with less immediate legal ⁠scrutiny than if Chinese officials were to do so, as their activities are subject to Taiwan's security laws.
Taiwan's foreign ministry told Reuters that around 20 people from the "academic world" had been invited to the screening.
While Taiwan respects the "lawful conduct of normal exchanges", activities held by the Russian office "should also respect historical facts and conform to universal values such as democracy and freedom", the ministry added.
Staff from the Russian office, including the deputy representative, Sergey Chudodeev, declined entry to Reuters reporters, saying it was an invitation-only event.
After the screening, the Russian representative, Pavel Lapin, said Moscow's Taipei office hoped to organise similar events in the future, a person who attended the event said.
"The Soviet Union and the Chinese people endured the heaviest casualties in that war. The contributions they made toward crushing German fascism and Japanese militarism are indisputable ‌and cannot be diminished," the Russian office said in a Facebook post about the screening.
A person who attended said those present included former journalists, ​business figures, academics and other public-facing figures.
In August, China and Russia issued a joint statement warning against remilitarisation in the Asia-Pacific.
Russian diplomats in Taipei ‌have generally kept a very low profile since Russia invaded Ukraine in ⁠2022, according to diplomatic sources.
The Russian office in Taipei opened in 1996, and it has always had a more understated presence in Taiwan compared ⁠with the de facto embassies of countries like the United States, European Union and Britain, diplomatic sources say.
China's Taiwan Affairs Office dismissed Taiwan's concerns about the film as "another ploy to manipulate anti-China sentiment for political gain".
Taiwan has ‌been on Russia's "unfriendly" countries and territories list since it ​joined other Western allies in sanctioning the country following its invasion of Ukraine, ‌and senior Russian officials have openly backed China's claims to the democratically-governed island.
Moscow and ​Tokyo have their own long-running dispute over Russia's seizing four Kuril Islands off northern Japan at the end of World War Two, one of which Russian President Vladimir Putin visited last month, drawing condemnation from Tokyo.

_source.movement_abstract: 【英国路透社报道】俄罗斯驻台北代表处近期在台北市中心举办闭门放映活动，向约20名台湾学术界及商界人士放映1945年苏联纪录片《粉碎军国主义日本》。台湾国家安全会议表示正密切监控中俄军事及认知战合作，认为此举旨在配合中国渲染日本军事威胁论调，破坏台日关系及台湾与西方伙伴联系。影片内容包含苏联进攻中国东北及库页岛画面，并谴责日本种族优越论。台湾外交部指出，俄罗斯利用其非官方身份规避台湾《反渗透法》严格审查，构成新型安全挑战。俄罗斯代表帕维尔·拉平表示未来将举办类似活动，强调中俄在二战中的牺牲与贡献。中国外交部称不知晓此次放映，但重申维护二战正确历史观是国际责任。中国国台办则指责台湾借机操弄反中情绪。背景显示，中俄8月曾联合声明反对亚太再军事化，且俄罗斯自2022年入侵乌克兰后在台北保持低调，但近期活动频率有所增加。

_source.title: Why a Russian screening of an 81-year-old film has alarmed Taiwan
_source.trans_cont:
在台北市中心办公楼的一个小房间里放映一部电影，引发了台湾政府的担忧。
在此之前，俄罗斯官员为大约20名台湾客人举办了一场不寻常的放映活动，放映了一部名为“粉碎军国主义日本”的旧苏联纪录片。
尽管观众不多，但这部有81年历史的电影的放映还是引起了台湾政府的警觉。它认为，俄罗斯正在帮助中国推进其关于日本军事威胁上升的说法，并试图在台北与东京和其他西方伙伴的关系上挑拨离间。
日本首相高市早苗（Sanae Takaichi）去年表示，假设中国进攻台湾，可能会引发日本的军事反应，从而引发东京和北京之间的外交危机，并促使北京反复警告日本正在寻求回到过去的侵略状态。
台湾官员表示，他们认为，俄罗斯驻台湾大使馆上周闭门放映这部影片，是一项新的努力的一部分，目的是传播和支持中国针对日本的“新军国主义”路线。日本是台湾的一个重要盟友，尽管不是官方盟友。
俄罗斯外交部没有回应置评请求。中国外交部表示，对放映这部苏联时代的老电影一事并不知情。
它补充说，包括中国、俄罗斯和美国在内的同盟国打败了日本军国主义，“维护和促进正确的二战历史观是国际社会的共同责任”。
放映的影片是1945年的黑白片《军国主义日本的失败》，俄罗斯办公室在脸书上翻译成中文是“粉碎军国主义日本”。
这部名为“日本战败”的影片在YouTube上播放，展示了苏联进攻日本占领的满洲和千岛群岛的画面。画外音谴责“日本种族神圣优越性的强盗哲学”，并播放了日本对中国平民暴行的镜头。
这部电影的上映对台湾来说是一个敏感领域：言论自由受宪法保护，但台湾也有法律，包括2019年的《反渗透法》，旨在防止外国敌对势力（主要是中国）暗中影响台湾政治。
安检现场外没有警察，也没有采取任何措施将其关闭。
台湾国家安全委员会（NationalSecurityCouncil）对路透社（Reuters）表示，它正在“密切监视”。在被问及中俄军方与“认知战”合作的放映情况时。
“这两个国家正试图扩大特定话题，歪曲历史事实和政治问题，”它说。
台湾官员表示，俄罗斯构成了一个新的挑战，因为与中国官员相比，莫斯科与台湾的一些接触可能不会受到那么直接的法律审查，因为他们的活动受到台湾安全法的约束。
台湾外交部告诉路透社，约有20名来自“学术界”的人被邀请参加放映。
外交部补充道，虽然台湾尊重“正常交流的合法进行”，但俄罗斯办事处举办的活动“也应尊重历史事实，并符合民主和自由等普世价值”。
俄罗斯办事处的工作人员，包括副代表谢尔盖·丘多杰耶夫（Sergey Chudodeev），拒绝路透社记者进入，称这是一个仅限受邀者参加的活动。
放映结束后，俄罗斯代表帕维尔·拉宾（Pavel Lapin）表示，莫斯科台北办事处希望将来组织类似的活动，一位参加活动的人士说。
苏联和中国人民在那场战争中遭受了最惨重的伤亡。“他们为粉碎德国法西斯主义和日本军国主义所做的贡献是无可争议的，不能被削弱，”俄罗斯办公室在脸书上关于放映的帖子中说。
一位与会者说，出席者包括前记者、商界人士、学者和其他公众人物。
今年8月，中国和俄罗斯发表联合声明，对亚太地区重新军事化发出警告。
据外交消息人士透露，自2022年俄罗斯入侵乌克兰以来，俄罗斯驻台北外交官一直保持低调。
外交消息人士称，俄罗斯驻台北办事处于1996年成立，与美国、欧盟和英国等国家事实上的大使馆相比，该办事处在台湾的存在一直较为低调。
中国国务院台湾事务办公室（Taiwan Affairs Office）将台湾对这部电影的担忧斥为“操纵反华情绪以获取政治利益的又一伎俩”。
在俄罗斯入侵乌克兰后，台湾与其他西方盟国一起制裁俄罗斯，自那以来，台湾一直在俄罗斯的“不友好”国家和领土名单上，俄罗斯高级官员公开支持中国对这个民主治理的岛屿的主权要求。
俄罗斯在二战结束时占领了日本北部的四个千岛群岛（Kuril Islands），俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京（Vladimir Putin）上个月访问了其中一个岛屿，引起了东京的谴责。

（中央社台北11日綜合外電報導）路透社報導，俄羅斯駐台機構「莫北協駐台代表處」近日在台北閉門放映紀錄片「粉碎日本軍國主義」引發關注，台灣擔憂俄羅斯試圖挑撥台灣與日本及其他西方夥伴的關係。根據路透社，莫斯科台北經濟文化協調委員會駐台北代表處（莫北協駐台代表處）上週在台北市中心一棟辦公大樓的小型會議室為約20名台灣賓客舉行「粉碎日本軍國主義」放映會。儘管觀眾人數不多，這部81年前的蘇聯紀錄片引發台灣政府不安。路透社指出，台灣政府認為，俄羅斯正協助中國宣揚日本軍事威脅日益升高的論述，並企圖挑撥台日關係以及台灣和其他西方夥伴的關係。據報導，放映的影片是1945年黑白紀錄片「軍國主義日本敗北」（The Defeat of Militarist Japan），莫北協駐台代表處在臉書（Facebook）上將片名譯為中文「粉碎日本軍國主義」。莫北協駐台代表處貼文說：「蘇聯與中國人民在那場戰爭中蒙受了最為慘重的損失，他們對擊潰德國法西斯主義與日本軍國主義所作出的貢獻，不容質疑，亦不容貶低。」
這部影片在YouTube上也可找到，當中呈現蘇聯攻擊日軍占領下的滿洲及千島群島的畫面。旁白譴責「日本民族神聖優越的強盜哲學」，並播出日軍對中國平民施暴的畫面。根據路透社，台灣官員認為此舉是俄羅斯展開新行動的一環，意在散播並強化中國針對日本的「新軍國主義」論述。台灣的國家安全會議被問到這場放映會相關問題時告訴路透社，他們持續「密切監控」中俄軍事與「認知作戰」合作。國安會說：「這兩國正試圖擴大特定議題並扭曲歷史事實與政治問題。」
路透社報導，台灣官員表示，俄羅斯構成新的挑戰，因為相較於中國官員，俄方接觸部分台灣人士時，較少立即受到台灣安全法規檢視。台灣的外交部告訴路透社，約有20名「學術界」人士受邀參加這場放映會。外交部還說，台灣尊重「合法的正常交流活動」，但莫北協駐台代表處舉行的活動「也應尊重歷史事實，並符合民主、自由等普世價值」。副代表史鐸傑（Sergey Chudodeev）等莫北協駐台代表處人員拒絕讓路透社記者進入，表示這是僅限受邀人士參加的活動。與會人士表示，出席者包括前記者、商界人士、學者及其他經常公開露面的人士。透過 Google News
追蹤中央社
與會人士透露，放映結束後，代表拉賓（Pavel Lapin）說，莫北協駐台代表處希望未來舉辦類似活動。俄羅斯外交部未回應置評請求。中國外交部表示不曉得這場放映會，並表示當年中國、蘇聯及美國等同盟國擊敗日本軍國主義，「維護並弘揚正確二戰歷史觀是國際社會共同責任」。（編譯：
盧映孜
）1150911

Summary
Russian office screened 'Smashing Militarist Japan' in Taipei
Taiwan says Russia helping China sow discord
China, Japan ties in crisis over Japan PM comments on Taiwan
China calls for 'correct historical view' of World War Two
TAIPEI, Sept 11 (Reuters) - In a small meeting room in a downtown Taipei office building, Russian officials hosted an unusual screening of an old Soviet documentary called "Smashing Militarist Japan" for some ​20 Taiwanese guests.
Despite the small audience, the screening of the 81-year-old film has alarmed Taiwan's government. Russia, it believes, is helping China push its narrative of a rising ‌military threat from Japan, and is seeking to sow discord over Taipei's relations with Tokyo and other Western partners.
Make sense of global markets with the Trading Day newsletter. Sign up
here.
Advertisement · Scroll to continue
Japanese Prime Minister
Sanae Takaichi
last year suggested a hypothetical Chinese attack on Taiwan could trigger a Japanese military response, causing a diplomatic crisis between Tokyo and Beijing and prompting repeated warnings from Beijing that Japan is seeking a return to its aggressive past.
Officials in Taiwan say they believe the closed-door screening last week of the film by the de ​facto Russian embassy in Taipei is part of a new effort to spread and bolster China's "
new militarism
" line against Japan, a key though unofficial ally of Taipei.
Russia's foreign ministry did ​not respond to a request for comment. China's foreign ministry said it was unaware of the screening of the old Soviet-era film.
Advertisement · Scroll to continue
It added that Allied ⁠powers, including China, Russia and the U.S., had defeated Japanese militarism, and that "upholding and promoting a correct historical view of World War Two is the shared responsibility of the international ​community".
'SMASHING MILITARIST JAPAN'
The film shown was 1945's black-and-white "The Defeat of Militarist Japan", which the Russian office translated into Chinese on Facebook as "Smashing Militarist Japan".
The film, available on YouTube under the name "The defeat ​of Japan", shows images of the Soviet attack on Japanese-occupied Manchuria and the Kuril Islands. A voiceover denounces the "robber philosophy of the divine superiority of the Japanese race" and shows footage of Japanese atrocities against Chinese civilians.
The showing of the film sits in a sensitive area for Taiwan: freedom of speech is constitutionally protected, but it also has laws, including the 2019
Anti-Infiltration Act
, aimed at preventing hostile foreign forces — chiefly China — from covertly influencing its politics.
There was ​no police presence outside the screening and no effort was made to shut it down.
Taiwan's National Security Council, its highest government body overseeing security and counter-intelligence, told Reuters it was "closely monitoring" Chinese-Russian ​military and "cognitive warfare" cooperation when asked about the screening.
"The two countries are attempting to amplify specific topics and distort historical facts and political issues," it said.
Taiwanese officials said Russia posed a new challenge because Moscow ‌could approach ⁠some Taiwan contacts with less immediate legal scrutiny than if Chinese officials were to do so, as their activities are subject to Taiwan's security laws.
Taiwan's foreign ministry told Reuters that around 20 people from the "academic world" had been invited to the screening.
Advertisement · Scroll to continue
While Taiwan respects the "lawful conduct of normal exchanges", activities held by the Russian office "should also respect historical facts and conform to universal values such as democracy and freedom", the ministry added.
INVITATION ONLY EVENT
Staff from the Russian office, including the deputy representative, Sergey Chudodeev, declined entry to Reuters reporters, saying it was an invitation-only event.
After the screening, ​the Russian representative, Pavel Lapin, said Moscow's Taipei ​office hoped to organise similar events in ⁠the future, a person who attended the event said.
"The Soviet Union and the Chinese people endured the heaviest casualties in that war. The contributions they made toward crushing German fascism and Japanese militarism are indisputable and cannot be diminished," the Russian office said in a Facebook post ​about the screening.
A person who attended said those present included former journalists, business figures, academics and other public-facing figures.
In August, China and Russia issued ​a joint statement warning ⁠against remilitarisation in the Asia-Pacific.
Russian diplomats in Taipei have generally kept a very low profile since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, according to diplomatic sources.
The Russian office in Taipei opened in 1996, and it has always had a more understated presence in Taiwan compared with the de facto embassies of countries like the United States, European Union and Britain, diplomatic sources say.
'PLOY'
China's Taiwan Affairs Office dismissed Taiwan's concerns about ⁠the film as "another ​ploy to manipulate anti-China sentiment for political gain".
Taiwan has been on Russia's "unfriendly" countries and territories list since it joined other ​Western allies in sanctioning the country following its invasion of Ukraine, and senior Russian officials have openly
backed
China's claims to the democratically-governed island.
Moscow and Tokyo have their own long-running dispute over Russia's seizing four Kuril Islands off northern Japan at the end of ​World War Two, one of which Russian President Vladimir Putin visited last month, drawing
condemnation
from Tokyo.
Reporting by Reuters bureau; Editing by Michael Perry

Japanese Prime Minister
Sanae Takaichi
last year suggested a hypothetical Chinese attack on Taiwan could trigger a Japanese military response, causing a diplomatic crisis between Tokyo and Beijing and prompting repeated warnings from Beijing that Japan is seeking a return to its aggressive past.
Officials in Taiwan say they believe the closed-door screening last week of the film by the de ​facto Russian embassy in Taipei is part of a new effort to spread and bolster China's "
new militarism
" line against Japan, a key though unofficial ally of Taipei.
Russia's foreign ministry did ​not respond to a request for comment. China's foreign ministry said it was unaware of the screening of the old Soviet-era film.
Advertisement · Scroll to continue
It added that Allied ⁠powers, including China, Russia and the U.S., had defeated Japanese militarism, and that "upholding and promoting a correct historical view of World War Two is the shared responsibility of the international ​community".
'SMASHING MILITARIST JAPAN'
The film shown was 1945's black-and-white "The Defeat of Militarist Japan", which the Russian office translated into Chinese on Facebook as "Smashing Militarist Japan".
The film, available on YouTube under the name "The defeat ​of Japan", shows images of the Soviet attack on Japanese-occupied Manchuria and the Kuril Islands. A voiceover denounces the "robber philosophy of the divine superiority of the Japanese race" and shows footage of Japanese atrocities against Chinese civilians.
The showing of the film sits in a sensitive area for Taiwan: freedom of speech is constitutionally protected, but it also has laws, including the 2019
Anti-Infiltration Act
, aimed at preventing hostile foreign forces — chiefly China — from covertly influencing its politics.
There was ​no police presence outside the screening and no effort was made to shut it down.
Taiwan's National Security Council, its highest government body overseeing security and counter-intelligence, told Reuters it was "closely monitoring" Chinese-Russian ​military and "cognitive warfare" cooperation when asked about the screening.
"The two countries are attempting to amplify specific topics and distort historical facts and political issues," it said.
Taiwanese officials said Russia posed a new challenge because Moscow ‌could approach ⁠some Taiwan contacts with less immediate legal scrutiny than if Chinese officials were to do so, as their activities are subject to Taiwan's security laws.
Taiwan's foreign ministry told Reuters that around 20 people from the "academic world" had been invited to the screening.
Advertisement · Scroll to continue
While Taiwan respects the "lawful conduct of normal exchanges", activities held by the Russian office "should also respect historical facts and conform to universal values such as democracy and freedom", the ministry added.
INVITATION ONLY EVENT
Staff from the Russian office, including the deputy representative, Sergey Chudodeev, declined entry to Reuters reporters, saying it was an invitation-only event.
After the screening, ​the Russian representative, Pavel Lapin, said Moscow's Taipei ​office hoped to organise similar events in ⁠the future, a person who attended the event said.
"The Soviet Union and the Chinese people endured the heaviest casualties in that war. The contributions they made toward crushing German fascism and Japanese militarism are indisputable and cannot be diminished," the Russian office said in a Facebook post ​about the screening.
A person who attended said those present included former journalists, business figures, academics and other public-facing figures.
In August, China and Russia issued ​a joint statement warning ⁠against remilitarisation in the Asia-Pacific.
Russian diplomats in Taipei have generally kept a very low profile since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, according to diplomatic sources.
The Russian office in Taipei opened in 1996, and it has always had a more understated presence in Taiwan compared with the de facto embassies of countries like the United States, European Union and Britain, diplomatic sources say.
'PLOY'
China's Taiwan Affairs Office dismissed Taiwan's concerns about ⁠the film as "another ​ploy to manipulate anti-China sentiment for political gain".
Taiwan has been on Russia's "unfriendly" countries and territories list since it joined other ​Western allies in sanctioning the country following its invasion of Ukraine, and senior Russian officials have openly
backed
China's claims to the democratically-governed island.
Moscow and Tokyo have their own long-running dispute over Russia's seizing four Kuril Islands off northern Japan at the end of ​World War Two, one of which Russian President Vladimir Putin visited last month, drawing
condemnation
from Tokyo.

_source.trans_cont:
总结
俄罗斯办公室在台北放映“粉碎军国主义日本”
台湾称俄罗斯帮助中国挑拨离间
中日关系因日本陷入危机首相评论台湾
中国呼吁树立正确的二战历史观
台北，9月11日（路透社）-在台北市中心办公楼的一间小会议室里，俄罗斯官员为大约20名台湾客人举办了一场不同寻常的放映活动，放映一部名为“粉碎军国主义日本”的旧苏联纪录片。
尽管观众不多，但这部有81年历史的电影的放映还是引起了台湾政府的警觉。它认为，俄罗斯正在帮助中国推进其关于日本军事威胁上升的说法，并试图在台北与东京和其他西方伙伴的关系上挑拨离间。
通过交易日简讯了解全球市场。报名参加
在这里。
广告·滚动以继续
日本首相
高市早苗
去年曾暗示，假设中国对台湾发动攻击，可能会引发日本的军事回应，从而引发东京和北京之间的外交危机，并促使北京方面一再警告称，日本正寻求回到过去的侵略老路。
台湾官员表示，他们认为俄罗斯驻台北大使馆上周闭门放映这部影片，是传播和支持中国大陆的新努力的一部分。
新军国主义
反对日本的路线，尽管是台北的一个重要的非官方盟友。
俄罗斯外交部没有回应置评请求。中国外交部表示，对放映这部苏联时代的老电影一事并不知情。
广告·滚动以继续
它补充说，包括中国、俄罗斯和美国在内的同盟国打败了日本军国主义，“维护和促进正确的二战历史观是国际社会的共同责任”。
“粉碎军国主义日本”
放映的影片是1945年的黑白片《军国主义日本的失败》，俄罗斯办公室在脸书上翻译成中文是“粉碎军国主义日本”。
这部名为“日本战败”的影片在YouTube上播放，展示了苏联进攻日本占领的满洲和千岛群岛的画面。画外音谴责“日本种族神圣优越性的强盗哲学”，并播放了日本对中国平民暴行的镜头。
这部电影的上映对台湾来说是一个敏感的领域：言论自由受到宪法保护，但它也有法律，包括2019年。
反渗透法案
旨在防止外国敌对势力（主要是中国）暗中影响其政治。
安检现场外没有警察，也没有采取任何措施将其关闭。
台湾国家安全委员会（NationalSecurityCouncil）对路透社（Reuters）表示，它正在“密切监视”。在被问及中俄军方与“认知战”合作的放映情况时。
“这两个国家正试图扩大特定话题，歪曲历史事实和政治问题，”它说。
台湾官员表示，俄罗斯构成了一个新的挑战，因为与中国官员相比，莫斯科与台湾的一些接触可能不会受到那么直接的法律审查，因为他们的活动受到台湾安全法的约束。
台湾外交部告诉路透社，约有20名来自“学术界”的人被邀请参加放映。
广告·滚动以继续
外交部补充道，虽然台湾尊重“正常交流的合法进行”，但俄罗斯办事处举办的活动“也应尊重历史事实，并符合民主和自由等普世价值”。
仅限邀请事件
俄罗斯办事处的工作人员，包括副代表谢尔盖·丘多杰耶夫（Sergey Chudodeev），拒绝路透社记者进入，称这是一个仅限受邀者参加的活动。
放映结束后，俄罗斯代表帕维尔·拉宾（Pavel Lapin）表示，莫斯科台北办事处希望将来组织类似的活动，一位参加活动的人士说。
苏联和中国人民在那场战争中遭受了最惨重的伤亡。“他们为粉碎德国法西斯主义和日本军国主义所做的贡献是无可争议的，不能被削弱，”俄罗斯办公室在脸书上关于放映的帖子中说。
一位与会者说，出席者包括前记者、商界人士、学者和其他公众人物。
今年8月，中国和俄罗斯发表联合声明，对亚太地区重新军事化发出警告。
据外交消息人士透露，自2022年俄罗斯入侵乌克兰以来，俄罗斯驻台北外交官一直保持低调。
外交消息人士称，俄罗斯驻台北办事处于1996年成立，与美国、欧盟和英国等国家事实上的大使馆相比，该办事处在台湾的存在一直较为低调。
'阴谋'
中国国务院台湾事务办公室（Taiwan Affairs Office）将台湾对这部电影的担忧斥为“操纵反华情绪以获取政治利益的又一伎俩”。
自从台湾在俄罗斯入侵乌克兰后与其他西方盟国一起制裁该国以来，台湾一直在俄罗斯的“不友好”国家和领土名单上，俄罗斯高级官员公开表示
有后盾的
中国对这个民主治理的岛屿的主权要求。
俄罗斯在二战结束时占领了日本北部的四个千岛群岛，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京上个月访问了其中一个岛屿，莫斯科和东京之间也存在着长期的争端。
谴责
来自东京。

_source.trans_title: 为什么俄罗斯向极少数观众放映一部81年前苏联时代的电影会引起台湾的警觉

_source.author_name: 自由時報電子報 記者蘇永耀／台北報導
_source.content:
俄羅斯與中國對於在第一島鏈合作達成新的共識，在訊息面上運用彼此的資源和通路，放大特定的認知主題，外電路透披露，俄羅斯官員上週在台北播放「粉碎軍國主義日本」紀錄片，這是最近俄中聯手的首例。（俄羅斯駐台代表處臉書）
我國安部門日前警示，俄羅斯與中國對於在第一島鏈合作達成新的共識，在訊息面上運用彼此的資源和通路，放大特定的認知主題，尤其是對選舉等政治訊息，以各自的在地資源或組織來協力對方工作。果不其然，外電路透今披露，俄羅斯官員上週在台北播放「粉碎軍國主義日本」紀錄片，這是最近俄中聯手的首例，共同協力在軍事和「認知作戰」進行合作。路透今日發自台北報導指出，俄羅斯駐台代表處（莫北協駐台代表處）在台北的會議室裡，為大約20名台灣賓客主持了一場不尋常的放映會，播放81年前「粉碎軍國主義日本」的古老蘇聯紀錄片。這部黑白電影刻意展示當年蘇聯進攻日本佔領下的滿洲和千島群島的畫面。旁白譴責了「大和民族神聖優越性的強盜哲學」。請繼續往下閱讀...
路透在報導中說，日本首相高市早苗去年曾暗示，中國若對台灣發動假想攻擊，可能會引發日本的軍事回應；這引發了東京與北京之間的外交危機，並引來北京多次警告日本正試圖重蹈其侵略歷史的覆轍。台灣官員因此表示，他們認為俄羅斯駐台北代表處上週閉門放映該影片的舉動，是為了散佈並強化中國針對日本的「新軍國主義」論調所做出的新嘗試，而日本是台北關鍵的盟友。中國國家主席習近平8月31日在吉爾吉斯出席上合組織峰會期間會見俄羅斯總統普廷，強化中俄戰略合作關係，我國安部門也掌握到最新動態指出，俄中在第一島鏈合作達成新的共識，在訊息面上運用彼此的資源和通路，放大特定的認知主題，以各自的在地資源或組織來協力對方工作。我國安單位密切注意，對年底台灣九合一大選是否會有類似情況發生。莫北協駐台代表處在臉書貼文說：「蘇聯和中國人民在那場戰爭中承受了最慘重的傷亡。他們為粉碎德國法西斯主義和日本軍國主義所作出的貢獻無庸置疑，亦不可磨滅。」
對於俄羅斯官員在台北放映關於日本「軍國主義」與第二次世界大戰的電影，台灣官員並向路透坦言，俄羅斯帶來了新的挑戰，因為莫斯科接觸某些台灣人士時受到的法律審查，可能不如中國官員接觸時那麼直接。該影片放映約有20名台灣人士獲邀參加，包括前新聞工作者、商業人士、學者和其他公眾人物。一名與會人士向路透說，放映會結束後，俄羅斯駐台代表 Pavel Lapin 表示希望未來能舉辦類似活動。俄羅斯官員上週在台北播放「粉碎軍國主義日本」紀錄片，這是最近俄中協力認知戰的首例。（俄羅斯駐台代表處臉書）
俄羅斯官員上週在台北播放「粉碎軍國主義日本」紀錄片，這是最近俄中協力認知戰的首例。（俄羅斯駐台代表處臉書）
_source.movement_title: 俄罗斯驻台代表处放映纪录片强化中俄认知战协作
_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾中央社 2026 年 9 月 11 日报导】台湾安全部门警示，俄罗斯与中国已就第一岛链合作达成新共识，双方在讯息面运用各自资源与通路，放大特定认知主题，并针对选举等政治讯息进行协作。路透社披露，俄罗斯驻台代表处（莫北协驻台代表处）于台北会议室为约 20 名台湾宾客举办闭门放映会，播放苏联纪录片《粉碎军国主义日本》。该片展示苏联进攻日本占领下的满洲及千岛群岛画面，旁白谴责大和民族优越性。台湾官员指出，此举意在散布并强化中国针对日本的「新军国主义」论调，回应日本首相高市早苗关于台海冲突可能引发日本军事回应的言论。中国国家主席习近平与俄罗斯总统普廷于 8 月 31 日在吉尔吉斯上合组织峰会期间会晤，进一步强化战略合作。台湾官员坦言，俄罗斯接触台湾人士时面临的法律审查较中国官员松散，构成新的挑战。与会者包括前新闻工作者、商界人士及学者，俄罗斯驻台代表 Pavel Lapin 表示希望未来举办类似活动。台湾安全单位正密切监控年底九合一大选期间是否出现类似认知作战情况。

Washington should press Taipei to strengthen its defenses without suggesting that American support depends on Taiwan passing an ever-moving readiness test.
This month, Taiwan's Cabinet approved a record defense budget proposal for 2027. At NT$1.1225 trillion, about $35 billion, it is the first to cross the trillion-NT-dollar mark and runs roughly 18 percent above this year's spending. Yet in Washington a familiar question is already circulating: has Taiwan done enough?
Let me concede something at the outset: Washington is right to demand more from Taiwan. But there is a difference between telling Taipei it must do more and allowing Beijing to hear, however unintentionally, that American support depends on Taiwan having done enough. The first strengthens deterrence. The second quietly undermines it.
Washington Has a Point
Taiwan cannot treat American support as an entitlement, and spending figures alone do not equal readiness. Reserve training remains uneven. Munitions stockpiles are thinner than a protracted conflict would demand. Procurement execution has been slow, and civil defense is only beginning to be taken seriously as a whole-of-society task. When American officials press on asymmetric capabilities over prestige platforms, they are pressing on real weaknesses, and Taiwanese who care about their country's survival should welcome the scrutiny rather than resent it.
Pressure is necessary. Conditionality is something else.
The Trap of an Undefined "Enough"
The problem is that "enough" has never been defined, and the benchmark keeps moving. For years, American officials and analysts pressed Taiwan toward defense spending of 3 percent of GDP. Taiwan budgeted NT$949.5 billion for 2026, a 22.9 percent jump in a single year that works out to 3.32 percent of GDP under NATO-standard accounting. President Lai Ching-te has pledged 5 percent of GDP by 2030, and this month's record 2027 proposal is a step toward it. In November 2025, his government proposed an eight-year, NT$1.25 trillion (roughly $40 billion) special budget devoted to the very asymmetric capabilities and resilience Washington has asked for. The opposition-controlled legislature approved NT$780 billion of it in May, a reminder that Taiwan's defense debate is contested at home too, and the government has since moved to restore the remainder through annual and supplemental budgets. The benchmark was moving all the while. At his March 2025 confirmation hearing, Elbridge Colby, now the Pentagon's under secretary for policy, argued that Taiwan should be spending "more like 10 percent" of GDP.
Each individual demand is defensible. Two percent, three, five, ten — a case can be made for any of them, just as cases can be made for better reserves, deeper stockpiles, harder infrastructure. The trap lies in letting these demands accumulate into prerequisites. If every reform surfaces a new deficiency that must be remedied before support is merited, there is no finish line. There will never be a militarily perfect Taiwan, any more than there will be a perfectly prepared Japan, Poland, or America. Deterrence conditioned on perfect readiness is deterrence never quite extended.
What Beijing Hears
Deterrence across the Strait rests on two beliefs in Beijing: that Taiwan will resist, and that the United States and its partners will impose unacceptable costs on aggression. Public discourse that frames American support as contingent eats away at the second belief. It invites Beijing to conclude that American commitment is not a fixed obstacle but a variable that can be manipulated. If Washington's resolve depends on Taiwan passing a readiness test, then persuading Americans that Taiwan has failed the test becomes a cheaper path to victory than defeating Taiwan's military.
And Beijing is already working that path. In February 2025, Taiwan's coast guard detained the Chinese-crewed freighter Hong Tai 58 after an undersea cable linking Taiwan and Penghu was severed; a court sentenced the captain to three years in prison for intentionally damaging it, the first conviction of its kind, and the sentence held up on appeal. Last December, Beijing staged its largest war games yet around the island, the "Justice Mission" exercise, rehearsing a blockade and firing rockets that landed within Taiwan's 24-nautical-mile contiguous zone. The Taiwan-Matsu No. 3 cable broke again this April. Warships and aircraft press in almost daily; the disinformation never stops.
But the campaign targets more than cables, airspace, and supply chains. It targets perceptions, through a steady stream of cognitive warfare designed to convince Taiwanese that resistance is futile and Americans that Taiwan is indefensible, unserious, or unworthy. The readiness debate itself is part of the attack surface. When American pressure is framed, or received, as a test of whether Taiwan is worthy of support, Beijing's information operators get free ammunition. No U.S. official has declared that support hinges on a spending threshold; the risk lies in the accumulated signal, not in any single statement. Beijing does not need to win the argument. It only needs the argument to continue.
The strongest objection deserves a direct answer. Conditionality, its defenders argue, is the leverage that produced results: American pressure helped drive the 3.32 percent budget and the special procurement package. True. But that pressure worked through consultations, defense reviews, and hard conversations behind closed doors. It did not require a public doctrine that support is contingent. Private pressure disciplines a partner. Public doubt informs an adversary. The United States can keep the first without paying the strategic cost of the second.
Reciprocal Responsibility, Not a Loyalty Test
What should replace the readiness test is reciprocal responsibility. Taiwan commits to things that can be measured: asymmetric procurement over prestige purchases, munitions and energy stockpiles, reserve reform on a published timeline, hardened critical infrastructure. The United States commits in parallel: working down the nearly $30 billion backlog of Foreign Military Sales notified to Congress but not yet delivered, pre-positioned stockpiles, sustained intelligence sharing, and joint planning against the blockade and gray-zone scenarios that are likelier than an outright invasion. Both sides hold each other to the ledger in closed channels, where accountability belongs, not in public messaging, where Beijing is the most attentive audience.
None of this is a plea for unconditional charity. The demand signal and the deterrence signal travel on different frequencies, and Washington has been letting them interfere.
Push Harder, Signal Steadier
Taiwan's reforms are incomplete, and American impatience is legitimate. Washington should keep pushing Taipei, harder and more specifically, while making one point unmistakable to Beijing: Taiwan's imperfections are not an invitation. Deterrence means demanding more from Taiwan without ever letting "not enough" sound, in Beijing, like a green light.
Hong-Yu Harper Chen, J.S.D., is a U.S.-licensed attorney admitted in New York and Washington, D.C., and an adjunct assistant professor at the Institute of China and Asia-Pacific Studies, National Sun Yat-sen University in Taiwan, where she teaches international law.

华盛顿应该敦促台北加强防御，而不是暗示美国的支持取决于台湾能否通过不断变化的战备测试。
本月，台湾内阁批准了创纪录的2027年国防预算提案。新台币1.1225万亿元，约合350亿美元，首次突破万亿元大关，比今年的支出高出约18%。然而，在华盛顿，一个熟悉的问题已经在流传：台湾做得够吗？
让我在一开始就承认：华盛顿对台湾提出更多要求是正确的。但是，告诉台北它必须做得更多和让北京听到（尽管是无意的）美国的支持取决于台湾已经做得足够多，这两者之间是有区别的。第一，加强威慑力。第二个悄悄地破坏了它。
华盛顿说得有道理。
台湾不能将美国的支持视为一种权利，仅有支出数字并不等于准备就绪。后备训练仍然不均衡。弹药储备比一场旷日持久的冲突所需要的要少。采购执行缓慢，民防作为一项全社会的任务才刚刚开始受到重视。当美国官员在声望平台上强调不对称能力时，他们是在强调真正的弱点，关心国家生存的台湾人应该欢迎这种审查，而不是怨恨它。
压力是必要的。条件性是另一回事。
未定义的“足够”的陷阱
问题是，“足够”从未被定义，而基准一直在移动。多年来，美国官员和分析人士一直向台湾施压，要求其国防开支达到GDP的3%。台湾2026年的预算为新台币9，495亿元，一年内增长了22.9%，按照北约标准计算，相当于GDP的3.32%。总统赖清德承诺到2030年达到GDP的5%，本月创纪录的2027年提案是向这一目标迈出的一步。2025年11月，他的政府提出了一项为期八年、1.25万亿新台币（约合400亿美元）的特别预算，专门用于华盛顿所要求的非常不对称的能力和恢复力。反对派控制的立法院在5月批准了其中的7800亿新台币，这提醒人们，台湾的国防辩论在国内也是有争议的，政府已经采取行动，通过年度和补充预算来恢复剩余部分。基准一直在移动。在2025年3月的听证会上，现任五角大楼负责政策的副部长埃尔布里奇·科尔比（Elbridge Colby）认为，台湾的支出应该占到GDP的“ 10%左右”。
每个人的要求都是站得住脚的。2%、3%、5%、10%——其中任何一个都可以成为理由，就像可以成为更好的储备、更深的储备、更坚固的基础设施一样。陷阱在于让这些需求累积成先决条件。如果每一项改革都出现了新的缺陷，必须在得到支持之前加以弥补，那么就没有终点线。永远不会有一个军事上完美的台湾，就像永远不会有一个准备充分的日本、波兰或美国一样。以完全准备就绪为条件的威慑是永远不会延伸的威慑。
北京听到的
两岸威慑取决于北京的两个信念：一是台湾会抵抗，二是美国及其伙伴将为侵略付出不可接受的代价。将美国的支持框定为偶然的公共话语侵蚀了第二种信念。它促使北京得出这样的结论：美国的承诺不是一个固定的障碍，而是一个可以操纵的变量。如果华盛顿的决心取决于台湾能否通过战备测试，那么说服美国人相信台湾未能通过测试，就成了比击败台湾军队更便宜的胜利之路。
北京已经在走这条路了。2025年2月，在连接台湾和澎湖的海底电缆被切断后，台湾海巡署扣留了中国大陆货轮“洪泰58号”。一家法院以故意损坏的罪名判处船长三年监禁，这是此类案件中的首次定罪，该判决在上诉中被维持。去年12月，北京在台湾举行了迄今规模最大的军事演习——“正义使命”演习，演练了封锁行动，并发射了落在台湾24海里毗连区内的火箭弹。台湾马祖号今年4月，3号电缆又断了。军舰和飞机几乎每天都会开来。假情报从未停止。
但这场运动的目标不仅仅是电缆、空域和供应链。它以认知为目标，通过持续不断的认知战，让台湾人相信抵抗是徒劳的，让美国人相信台湾是站不住脚的、不严肃的或不值得的。准备辩论本身就是攻击面的一部分。当美国的压力被用来测试台湾是否值得支持时，北京的信息运营商就得到了免费的弹药。没有美国官员宣称支持取决于支出门槛。风险在于累积的信号，而不是任何单一的声明。北京不需要赢得这场争论。它只需要继续争论。
最强烈的反对意见应该得到直接的回答。其辩护者认为，条件性是产生结果的杠杆：美国的压力帮助推动了3.32%的预算和特别采购计划。真的。但这种压力通过磋商、国防审查和关起门来的艰难对话发挥了作用。它不需要一种公共理论，即支持是有条件的。私人压力会约束合作伙伴。公众的怀疑通知了对手。美国可以保住第一，而不必付出第二的战略代价。
对等责任，而不是忠诚测试
应该取代准备测试的是对等责任。台湾承诺做一些可以衡量的事情：不对称采购而不是购买特权、军火和能源储备、在公布的时间表上进行储备改革、强化关键基础设施。美国同时承诺：减少已通知国会但尚未交付的近300亿美元积压的对外军售，预先部署库存，持续的情报共享，以及针对封锁和灰色地带情景的联合规划，这些情景比直接入侵的可能性更大。双方在封闭的渠道中相互问责，而不是在公共信息传递中，北京是最专注的听众。
这些都不是对无条件施舍的恳求。需求信号和威慑信号在不同的频率上传播，华盛顿一直让它们进行干扰。
用力推，信号更稳定
台湾的改革是不完整的，美国的不耐烦是合理的。华盛顿应该继续向台北施压，力度更大、更具体，同时向北京明确指出一点：台湾的不完美不是邀请。威慑意味着向台湾要求更多，而不让北京发出“不够”的声音，就像绿灯一样。
陈宏宇（Hong-Yu Harper Chen，J.S.D.）是纽约和华盛顿特区注册的美国律师，也是台湾国立中山大学中国与亚太研究所的兼职助理教授，教授国际法。

American Institute in Taiwan Director Raymond Greene speaks at the Taipei Security Dialogue yesterday.
Photo: Tien Yu-hua, Taipei Times
PROGRESS:Taiwan has made impressive improvements in energy resilience, while increasing defense spending and upgrading its military tactics, the AIT director said
By Jonathan Chin / Staff writer with CNA
請繼續往下閱讀...
Taiwan must guard against artificial intelligence （AI）-enabled information manipulation ahead of local elections on Nov. 28, American Institute in Taiwan （AIT） Director Raymond Greene said yesterday.
Although Taiwan has earned acclaim for its efforts to counter disinformation, it must still brace for a new wave of sophisticated, AI-powered cognitive warfare, Greene said during his keynote speech at the Taipei Security Dialogue hosted by the Institute for National Defense and Security Research.
Taiwan also urgently needs to defend financial institutions and critical infrastructure against AI-powered cyberattacks, he said.
The US’ top diplomat in Taiwan also touched on issues such as defense spending, military reforms and energy resilience.
Taiwan has made great progress in energy resilience by increasing the importation and storage of liquefied natural gas, which the international community has taken note of, Greene said.
The nation has also made less visible, but equally impressive, improvements in its electricity allocation policy, power-grid decentralization, use of coal-fired plants and renewables, and exploration of alternative energy sources, including small modular reactors and geothermal energy, he said.
Washington welcomes President William Lai’s （賴清德） commitment to increase defense spending to 5 percent of GDP by 2030, as US allies face rising security threats around the globe, he said.
US President Donald Trump has been calling on European countries to take on greater responsibilities for their self-defense, he said, adding that Ukraine has shown that sustained military spending can improve a nation’s military capabilities.
Compared with many other US partners, Taiwan is far better placed financially to boost its defense, Greene said.
Military preparedness should not just aim to win a war, but to prevent a conflict from breaking out altogether, he said.
Deterring Chinese aggression is paramount for Taiwan and the world, he said.
“Beyond the human toll, any conflict across the Taiwan Strait would have a bigger impact on the global economy than the Second World War,” Greene said.
The Trump administration has made preserving peace in the Indo-Pacific region one of its top priorities, he said.
That includes “vigorous” diplomacy, especially at the highest levels, he said.
“The upcoming US-China summit is an opportunity to further advance a relationship of strategic stability, on the basis of fairness and reciprocity, that can avoid misunderstandings and miscalculations,” Greene added.
At the same time, the US is reinforcing its presence and partnerships in the Indo-Pacific region to maintain a “favorable regional balance of power,” while supporting Taiwan’s work to enhance its ability to defend itself, he said.
Claims that Taiwan’s efforts to bolster national defense are provocative and accusations that the US aims to change the “status quo” in the region are false, he said.
Taiwan has been rapidly implementing lessons learned from Ukraine’s use of asymmetric warfare and emerging technology to fend off Russia’s invasion, Greene said.
Taiwan has many strategic advantages Ukraine and many other countries do not have, including advanced manufacturing capabilities, sea barriers and formidable natural geography, he said.
Taiwan’s armed forces are rapidly adapting to mission-command concepts, as demonstrated in the latest Han Kuang exercises, he added.
Such flexibility has been vital in Ukraine’s defense against Russia’s military, which has been hobbled by its rigid and hierarchical command structure, Greene said.
Taiwan and the US must constantly improve their defensive capabilities to safeguard peace, he said.
 Additional reporting by Reuters
TAIPEI TIMES
_source.movement_title: 美国在台协会主任呼吁台湾防范 AI 认知战并提升防务
_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾《台北时报》2026 年 9 月 9 日报道】美国在台协会（AIT）主任雷蒙德·格林昨日在台北安全对话上发表主旨演讲，指出台湾必须警惕 11 月 28 日地方选举前利用人工智能（AI）进行的信息操纵及认知战。格林强调，台湾需加强金融机构和关键基础设施的防御，以应对 AI 驱动的网络攻击。在能源韧性方面，台湾通过增加液化天然气进口储备、优化电力分配及探索小型模块化反应堆等替代能源取得显著进展。格林表示，美方欢迎台湾总统赖清德承诺至 2030 年将国防预算提升至 GDP 的 5%，并指出台湾具备比乌克兰更优越的财政基础。格林称，威慑中国侵略对台湾及全球至关重要，台海冲突对全球经济的影响将超过二战。特朗普政府将维护印太和平列为优先事项，通过高层外交及强化区域伙伴关系维持力量平衡。格林驳斥了台湾加强防务具有挑衅性及美国意图改变现状的说法。此外，台湾正借鉴乌克兰经验，利用不对称作战和新兴技术，并在汉光演习中展示任务式指挥概念的适应性，以应对僵化的指挥结构。

美国在台协会主任雷蒙德·格林昨天在台北安全对话上发言。
图片来源：台北时报田玉华
进展：台湾在能源弹性方面取得了令人印象深刻的进步，同时增加了国防开支并升级了其军事战术，AIT主任说
作者：Jonathan Chin/CNA特约撰稿人
請繼續往下閱讀...
美国在台协会（AIT）主任雷蒙德·格林（Raymond Greene）昨天表示，在11月28日的地方选举之前，台湾必须防范人工智能（AI）的信息操纵。
格林在国防与安全研究所（Institute for National Defense and Security Research）主办的台北安全对话（Taipei Security Dialogue）上发表主旨演讲时表示，尽管台湾在对抗虚假信息方面的努力赢得了赞誉，但它仍必须准备好迎接新一波复杂的、以人工智能为动力的认知战。
他说，台湾还迫切需要保护金融机构和关键基础设施免受人工智能驱动的网络攻击。
美国驻台最高外交官还谈到了国防开支、军事改革和能源弹性等问题。
格林说，台湾通过增加液化天然气的进口和储存，在能源韧性方面取得了很大进步，国际社会已经注意到这一点。
他说，中国还在电力分配政策、电网分散化、燃煤电厂和可再生能源的使用以及替代能源的探索（包括小型模块化反应堆和地热能源）方面做出了不那么明显但同样令人印象深刻的改进。
他说，华盛顿欢迎威廉·莱总统（賴清德）承诺到2030年将国防开支增加到GDP的5%，因为美国的盟友在全球面临着不断上升的安全威胁。
他说，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普一直呼吁欧洲国家承担更大的自卫责任，并补充说，乌克兰已经表明，持续的军费开支可以提高一个国家的军事能力。
格林说，与许多其他美国伙伴相比，台湾在财政上处于更有利的地位，可以加强其国防。
他说，军事准备的目标不应该仅仅是赢得一场战争，而是要完全防止冲突的爆发。
他说，遏制中国的侵略对台湾和世界都至关重要。
格林说：“除了人员伤亡，台湾海峡两岸的任何冲突对全球经济的影响都会比第二次世界大战更大。”
他说，特朗普政府已将维护印度-太平洋地区的和平作为其首要任务之一。
他说，这包括“积极的”外交，特别是在最高级别。
格林补充说：“即将到来的美中峰会是在公平和互惠的基础上进一步推进战略稳定关系的机会，可以避免误解和误判。”
他说，与此同时，美国正在加强其在印度-太平洋地区的存在和伙伴关系，以保持“有利的地区力量平衡”，同时支持台湾增强其自卫能力的工作。
他说，声称台湾加强国防的努力是挑衅性的，指责美国旨在改变该地区的“现状”是错误的。
格林说，台湾一直在迅速实施从乌克兰使用不对称战争和新兴技术抵御俄罗斯入侵中吸取的教训。
他说，台湾拥有许多乌克兰和其他许多国家所没有的战略优势，包括先进的制造能力、海上屏障和令人生畏的自然地理。
他补充说，正如最近的汉光演习所展示的那样，台湾武装部队正在迅速适应任务指挥概念。
格林说，这种灵活性对于乌克兰防御俄罗斯军队至关重要，俄罗斯军队因其僵化和等级森严的指挥结构而步履蹒跚。
他说，台湾和美国必须不断提高他们的防御能力，以维护和平。
路透社补充报道
台北时报

The 2026
(NDAA) required the Department of War to define cognitive warfare by March 31, 2026. The deadline passed with no public definition of any kind, even as officials warn that China and Iran are already targeting entire populations with tailored disinformation and influence campaigns. Cognitive warfare runs on data. This essay argues that the debate has overlooked the mechanism that distinguishes cognitive warfare from propaganda: the algorithmic profiling of personal data at scale. It proposes a data-centric definition, treats bulk data theft and the future decryption of stored communications as cognitive-warfare logistics, and closes with five actions that follow.
directed the Department of War to define cognitive warfare, relate it to existing doctrine, identify responsible organizations, and assess the value of “narrative intelligence.” Nearly four months after the deadline, no public definition has been released, and the
did not address the gap. By early June, the debate had turned inward, focused on whether the term describes anything new at all, with some arguing the concept is
inside the Pentagon. Meanwhile, a senior defense official
that China and Iran are already using cognitive warfare to “alter the thinking of entire populations.”
The core issue is simple: adversaries are conducting cognitive warfare, and the US government has yet to define what it is. The delay stems not from a lack of words but from a debate focused on the wrong layer.
Serious work on cognitive warfare has converged on a decision-centric view, meaning it defines the activity by human decision-making, rather than by any communication medium or message. The strongest formulation,in Small Wars Journal, defines cognitive warfare as “a sustained and adaptive contest over human decision-making in which adversaries seek relative advantage by shaping or disrupting perception, interpretation, judgment, and action over time horizons.” Cognitive warfare runs below the threshold of armed conflict, waged continuously, in peacetime and in war, without a shot fired. The same body of work separates cognitive warfare from information operations, psychological operations, and influence activities. Practitioners of those disciplines tend to measure success by sentiment rather than by changed decisions. NATO’s scientists reached the same decision-centric conclusion from a different direction, calling the mind the battlefield and cognition a proposed
of warfare.
The
,, and Small Wars Journal definitions correctly identify the objective: shaping decisions. They do not explain the mechanism, or how cognitive warfare fundamentally differs from traditional propaganda. The difference is precision: the ability to deliver a tailored message to each person rather than broadcasting one message to a mass audience. That precision comes from the underlying data, not from the message itself.
Here is a definition worth adding to the debate:
Cognitive warfare is a sustained, below-threshold contest to shape a population’s perceptions, judgments, and decisions through the profiling of personal data, which allows influence with a degree of accuracy that mass propaganda could never achieve.
In cognitive warfare, personal data is the targeting package. A recent
from Rushing, Hersch, and Xu grounds the discussion in the
and treats it as an interactive attacker-defender exchange. The definition proposed here adds that precision is a function of the personal data collected on the defender’s population. Making data central to the definition, rather than incidental, shifts the focus of the conflict. The contest is no longer simply about messages and platforms, but about control of the data that enables accurate targeting.
Defining cognitive warfare by its data dependence shows that two issues, often considered separately, are part of the same challenge.
The first is bulk data theft. Over the past decade, Chinese state actors breached the
,,, and
, in what US officials now
a single coordinated campaign. Recently declassified White House materials include a
held by a People’s Republic of China computer network exploitation actor around 2019, listing American voter rolls, social media account data, medical records with Social Security numbers, and biometric data. These incidents raise privacy and counterintelligence concerns, but under the proposed definition they are the deliberate accumulation of data that cognitive targeting requires. The ammunition is already stockpiled.
The second is encryption. Adversaries are believed to be collecting encrypted American communications now, intending to decrypt them once quantum computing matures. This strategy is known as
. Those communications contain private thoughts and conversations, the most valuable input a cognitive campaign could ask for. Decryption is not simply a cryptographic concern; it marks the next phase of data acquisition. Together, collection and future decryption form the logistics chain of cognitive warfare.
Generative AI accelerates the payoff. Tasks that once required analysts to draft messages by hand can now be performed by models across millions of profiles simultaneously, turning stolen communications, behavioral histories, and identity records into tailored messages at machine speed. Data is the ammunition, the model is the delivery system, and the target is human judgment.
Because data remains valuable over time, the campaign’s time horizon extends beyond election cycles and spans a generation.
Consider where children’s data goes. The
has acted against
, a robot-toy maker whose app allowed a third party in China to collect geolocation data from children without parental consent. The 2025 update to the
expanded protected personal information to include children’s biometric identifiers, such as voice prints and audio recordings, an acknowledgment that this material is being collected at scale. The
requiring divestiture of
from its foreign-adversary parent rests on the same concern: a hostile state compelling the handover of Americans’ data, including that of minors.
Under the proposed definition of cognitive warfare, a biometric and behavioral profile built on a 14-year-old becomes the profile of a future cleared analyst, defense engineer, or field-grade officer. An adversary harvesting data on minors is not committing a short-term privacy violation; it is preparing targeting data for cognitive and counterintelligence campaigns decades in advance, against individuals who have not yet entered public service. Collecting children’s data is the longest and most patient logistical effort in this domain.
The data-dependent nature of cognitive warfare creates a structural disadvantage for the United States that cannot and should not be engineered away. American laws and norms prohibit the intelligence community and military from collecting data on or conducting influence operations against US persons. While
of the National Defense Authorization Act authorizes information operations abroad, domestic restrictions are intentional. Adversaries targeting American minds face no such limitations and can freely collect American data. The protections of an open society become a vulnerability when an adversary can gather in bulk the very data the United States is prohibited from collecting on its own citizens.
The solution is not to dismantle domestic protections or adopt adversary tactics against Americans. Analyzing foreign adversaries’ decision-making is a legitimate intelligence function, and developing outward-facing narrative intelligence, the assessment of how narratives form and spread in foreign information environments, is appropriate. Defending the American population, however, must run through resilience and through denying adversaries the data itself.
This is the practical benefit of a precise definition. If cognitive warfare relies on data, then cognitive defense is fundamentally data defense, much of which already exists under other names.

in the United States, and Federal Trade Commission

（NDAA）要求战争部在2026年3月31日前定义认知战争。最后期限已过，但没有任何形式的公开定义，尽管官员们警告说，中国和伊朗已经在针对整个人口开展有针对性的虚假信息和影响力活动。认知战争依赖于数据。这篇文章认为，这场辩论忽略了区分认知战和宣传的机制：大规模个人数据的算法分析。它提出了一个以数据为中心的定义，将批量数据窃取和存储通信的未来解密视为认知战后勤，并以接下来的五个行动结束。
指导陆军部定义认知战，将其与现有条令联系起来，确定责任组织，并评估“叙述性情报”的价值。在最后期限过去近四个月后，仍未公布任何公开定义，
没有解决差距。到6月初，争论已经转向内部，集中在这个词是否描述了任何新的东西，一些人认为这个概念是
五角大楼内部。与此同时，一位高级国防官员
中国和伊朗已经在使用认知战来“改变整个人口的思维”。
核心问题很简单：对手正在进行认知战，而美国政府尚未定义它是什么。拖延不是因为缺乏措辞，而是因为辩论集中在错误的层面上。
关于认知战的严肃工作已经集中在以决策为中心的观点上，这意味着它通过人类决策来定义活动，而不是通过任何通信媒介或信息。《小型战争杂志》（Small Wars Journal）中最有力的表述是，将认知战争定义为“一种对人类决策的持续和适应性竞争，在这种竞争中，对手通过在时间范围内塑造或破坏感知、解释、判断和行动来寻求相对优势。”认知战争低于武装冲突的门槛，在和平时期和战争中持续不断，不费一枪一弹。同样的工作将认知战与信息战、心理战和影响活动分开。这些学科的从业者倾向于用情绪而不是改变的决定来衡量成功。北约的科学家从不同的方向得出了同样的以决策为中心的结论，称头脑是战场，认知是被提议的
战争。
这个
、和《小型战争》杂志的定义正确地确定了目标：塑造决策。他们没有解释其中的机制，也没有解释认知战与传统宣传的根本区别。不同之处在于精确性：能够向每个人传递量身定制的信息，而不是向大众传播一条信息。这种精确性来自底层数据，而不是消息本身。
这里有一个值得加入辩论的定义：
认知战是一场持续的、低于门槛的竞赛，通过对个人数据的剖析来塑造人口的认知、判断和决策，这使得影响力达到了大众宣传永远无法达到的准确程度。
在认知战中，个人数据就是目标包。最近的
从拉什，赫施和徐的理由讨论在
并将其视为一种交互式的攻击者-防御者交换。此处提出的定义补充说，精确度取决于所收集的维权者人口的个人数据。让数据成为定义的核心，而不是附带的，可以转移冲突的焦点。这场竞赛不再仅仅是关于信息和平台，而是关于对数据的控制，从而实现准确定位。
通过数据依赖性来定义认知战表明，通常分开考虑的两个问题是同一挑战的一部分。
首先是批量数据窃取。在过去的十年里，中国的国家行为者违反了
、、和
那么，美国官员现在在什么？

由中华人民共和国计算机网络开发人员在2019年左右持有，列出了美国选民名单、社交媒体账户数据、带有社会安全号码的医疗记录和生物特征数据。这些事件引发了隐私和反间谍方面的担忧，但根据拟议的定义，它们是认知定位所需的数据的故意积累。弹药已经储存起来了。

解决办法不是废除国内保护措施，也不是对美国人采取敌对策略。分析外国对手的决策是一项合法的情报职能，开发面向外部的叙事情报，即评估叙事如何在外国信息环境中形成和传播，是适当的。然而，保卫美国人民必须通过恢复力和不让对手获得数据本身来实现。

在美国，联邦贸易委员会
应该作为认知防御来对待和提供资源，让战争部成为其威胁图景的长期消费者，而不是旁观者。
第三，缩小儿童数据差距。批量转移限制应该明确针对未成年人的生物特征和行为数据，因为它在对手的战役中拥有最长的后勤线路，并且防御最少。
第四，加速加密时钟。为后量子时代的迁移提供资金，以防止未来的解密通信落入对手之手，并首先移动寿命最长的个人数据。
第五，构建面向外部的叙事智能和面向内部的韧性。提供国会要求的叙事情报评估，保持针对国内收集的法律壁垒完好无损，并投资于信息来源标准和公民教育，帮助公民认识到他们的判断何时成为目标。
国会要求给出一个定义，而整个国家仍在等待。定义不是词汇练习，延迟也不是没有代价的。在美国说出什么是认知战以及它在什么基础上运行之前，它将继续准备保卫对手已经在数据层悄悄穿越的地形，一次一个收获的记录。

（中央社記者
游凱翔
台北9日電）美國戰爭部前印太安全事務首席副助理部長羅耶爾今天指出，威懾核心在具備可靠且反應迅速的無人系統，以及無人機後端的指揮控制架構，他強烈建議立院通過更充裕總體國防預算，加速無人機生產。國防部智庫、國防安全研究院上午在台北君悅飯店舉行「2026台北安全對話」，副總統蕭美琴、國防院董事長霍守業、美國在台協會處長谷立言（Raymond Greene）、日本前海上自衛隊幕僚長武居智久、美國戰爭部前印太安全事務首席副助理部長羅耶爾（Jedidiah P. Royal）等多名專家學者與會。羅耶爾在專題演講時表示，印太地區有兩個時鐘正同時滴答作響，第1個是「威脅時鐘」（Threat Clock），全球觀察家持續討論中國國家主席習近平提及的2027年、2035年與2049年等時間節點，亦持續看到解放軍執行威脅性的繞島巡航、實彈演習、進入台灣24浬鄰接區，以及旨在恐嚇脅迫的言論。他認為，雖然這些時間點不意味著衝突難以避免，但明確的戰略軌跡已經設定，「中國正動用國家力量獲取戰略優勢」。羅耶爾指出，他非常嚴肅看待習近平的宣示與「威脅時鐘」，但還有第2個是台灣建軍備戰的「落實時鐘」（Delivery Clock）也在滴答作響。當威脅時鐘走向危險時，落實時鐘能提供威懾與穩定，能延後最壞情況並降低風險，而台灣完全有能力加速建軍備戰「落實時鐘」，但必須展現出高度的專注與行動力。他表示，最緊迫的是，台灣必須提出足夠預算與計畫，以迅速加速國內無人機生產。坦白說，他一年前原以為進度會比現在更為超前，然近期公布的新台幣2400億元無人載具預算固然值得肯定，但威懾核心在於具備可靠且反應迅速的無人系統，以及無人機後端的指揮控制架構。他指出，隨著解放軍大量投資於高科技與高致命性武器，傳統裝備的效能將隨著時間遞減。台灣完全有能力在非紅供應鏈的基礎上，成為各領域高品質無人機的主要供應者；他強烈建議立法院通過更充裕的總體國防預算，因為增加國防支出能實質買回「落實時鐘」的時間。羅耶爾表示，台灣必須持續提升全社會防衛韌性與實戰準備，他高度肯定台灣過去5年在漢光演習、城鎮韌性演習中所取得的進展。在擬真情境、新作戰概念、去中心化指揮管制以及前沿科技導入方面，均展現出強大的防禦成效，讓國軍能更專注於「拒止戰略」，但未來仍需擴大獲取訓練場地、降低動員法規限制、深化跨軍種整合並強化資訊安全防禦。羅耶爾建議，鑑於台灣無法單打獨鬥，台灣應把防務政策「對齊」區域夥伴戰略，在研發、供應鏈韌性、生產與後勤維保上展開跨國合作，例如澳洲擁有頂尖測試設施、日本在機器人領域具備深厚工業底蘊、菲律賓則有高素質勞動力與地理接近性；若能整合區域資源，將能建立前瞻造船廠、彈性製造生產線、加固倉儲及區域維修中心，縮短後勤補給線。透過 Google News

_source.movement_title: 美前官员建议台加速无人机生产并增加国防预算
_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾中央社2026年9月9日报道】2026年9月9日，美国战争部前印太安全事务首席副助理部长罗耶尔在台北举行的'2026台北安全对话'上发表演讲。罗耶尔指出，印太地区面临'威胁时钟'与'落实时钟'的双重压力，中国正利用国家力量获取战略优势，解放军频繁进行绕岛巡航及实弹演习。他强调，台湾必须加速建军备战，核心在于建立可靠且反应迅速的无人系统及指挥控制架构。尽管台湾已公布2400亿元新台币无人载具预算，但罗耶尔强烈建议立法院通过更充裕的总体国防预算，以实质买回备战时间。他肯定台湾过去5年在汉光演习及城镇韧性演习中的进展，建议未来扩大训练场地、降低动员法规限制并深化跨军种整合。此外，罗耶尔呼吁台湾将防务政策与区域伙伴对齐，利用澳洲、日本、菲律宾等资源建立区域维修中心及弹性生产线。他同时敦促美国加速对台军售交付，将承诺转化为区域内的硬实力，以减缓威胁时钟的滴答声。

文：丹尼爾．依里亞德（Daniel Iriarte）
納粹分子現身說法
聯邦調查局探員麥克．傑曼（Michael German）長年在美國白人優越主義運動社群中臥底，他在二○○七年出版著作《像恐怖分子一樣思考》（
Thinking Like a Terrorist
）中提到，在一九八○年代末期、一九九○年代這段期間，新納粹圈子裡常流傳關於幕後黑暗強權的陰謀論，例如光明會（Illuminati）、錫安長老會紀要（The Protocols of the Elders of Zion）、畢德堡會議及三邊委員會（Trilateral Commission）的神祕故事、猶太控制政府（Zionist Occupation Government）等。雖然如今反猶太色彩較淡一些，但令人訝異的是，不少這類陰謀論仍在許多圈子裡流行。極端主義要存在，陰謀論必不可少，在承平時期，除非有什麼難以置信的想法可以合理化憎恨，否則人們不太會把憎恨當成志業。例如，他們在為某種更高的目標奮鬥、有人預謀毀滅他們的文化，或是敵對社群或成員不配為人。為了理解這種思考模式，研究陰謀論和激進化過程中的連結非常重要。大衛．薩維德拉（David Saavedra）是西班牙退役軍人，他曾是國家社會主義的信徒，但最後選擇與老戰友分道揚鑣。他說：「一開始，記者最常問我，那些四處演講倡導這種意識型態的人，例如貝德羅．瓦瑞拉（Pedro Varela，西班牙家喻戶曉的國家社會主義分子）這群人，是否真的相信自己所說的話，或他們根本是在用這些話術騙人、蠱惑年輕人？我覺得沒有半個記者相信我的回答。」
就私人和情感層面來說，與戰友決裂對他衝擊甚大。二○二五年三月，本書付印前夕，我有機會和他坐下來聊聊，當時他還在處理決裂帶來的震撼中。「我覺得大部分的記者都認為是後者，但事情並非如此。就我而言，包含我在內所有我認識的人，可以說百分之百盲目地相信我們說出口的話。我們相信這整個信念，相信一般人的常識有問題，相信我們才是好人，相信在黑暗中潛伏著一股不懷好意的邪惡力量，而我們是對抗它的勇士。」
過去二十年間，薩維德拉在西班牙國家社會主義運動圈中占有一席之地。或許社會大眾不熟悉，但他在圈內赫赫有名。他協助出版刊物、組織獨立行動小組，在國家聯盟黨（Alianza Nacional）內做事。直到有一天，他的思考邏輯出現一道道裂縫，致使成年身分認同仰賴的意識型態堡壘分崩離析。這並非一夕之間發生，而是各種境遇緩緩引導他走向這一步。首先是私人問題；再來是軍中工作，和不同國籍、種族的人接觸，特別是那些意識型態泡泡以外的人，帶給他新的視野。最後，他發現自己變成某民兵團的一分子，而他們正準備更進一步行動，而且不惜採用暴力，種種因素讓他認為該退出了。二○二一年出版的著作《前納粹分子回憶錄》（
Memorias de un exnazi
），就詳實記載他的心路歷程。薩維德拉的案例特別有趣，他的自省能力非常強，花時間反思自身經驗與心路歷程：從利用過濾機制全盤控制極端團體成員思想，到「去激進化」。他對我說：「論述和意識型態就像一件被單。當你把政治或意識型態拿掉後，剩下的就是我稱為『思想泡泡』的心理框架，在這裡，情緒特別重要。無論拿什麼被單蓋在他身上，他就是會變激進，就是會走向極端。一位激進分子就算說自己已經不再激進了，體內仍然流著激進的血液。這和酗酒的人有點相似，就算二十年沒喝酒，照樣會說自己酗酒。說真的，不管我相信的是什麼意識型態，就算是人權也好，我的腦袋照樣會把它變得激進。你可能會問：『要如何激進化人權？』很簡單，把所有沒有按照我的方式捍衛人權的人都說成是納粹就好了。」
薩維德拉會去學校與教育單位演講，試著拉某些青少年一把，避免他們踏上激進之路。他表示，這個變化過程其實和成為聖戰主義分子或加入拉丁樂團是一樣的，因此這些年輕人不一定會變成極右派。只要以同理心對待，並且適時引導他們前往正確的方向，就可以把這股煩躁不安之情帶往更富建設性的道路。薩維德拉也在YouTube 頻道上討論這些議題。「我現在在開發可以盡早發現這種思想泡泡的工具，搶在意識型態浮現前，就先引導到其他方向。意識型態、論述或宗教一旦生成，腦袋就會像上鎖一樣。意識型態讓你腦海中的東西成形，它把事情拼湊起來，組織你看待世界和自己的方式。然而，一切在更早之前就開始了，孩子們在校園高喊『希特勒萬歲』，讓大家心中的警鈴大作，但是警報在這之前就已經響很久了：當孩子開始覺得事情非黑即白，開始變得傲慢、不再好奇，開始一副『無所不知，無所不曉』的態度，這種行為就是危機開始的徵兆。」
他認為，「陰謀主義不外乎源於自戀，而且它鼓勵你變成自戀狂，無限膨脹自我，成天覺得自己想的最對，其他人都是白痴。這種說法不難理解，但我們也必須保持開放心態，接受其他原因：恐懼和不安全感。很少人會注意到極右派在疫情期間急速壯大。原因很明顯，疫情讓眾人的心中充滿不安，害怕接下來會發生什麼事，疫情提供激進化一片成長的沃土。我記得疫情時，在路上看到窗邊貼著一張小孩畫的彩虹圖案，上面寫著『一切都會變好的』，然後人們在陽台上拍手叫好。當時我的內心覺得一陣平靜。不過，現在我們卻說：『嘖，別傻了！』那張圖極具象徵意義，它鼓舞人心，助人保持正向，但在同一時期，有人卻陷入黑暗漩渦中無法脫身，到現在還爬不出來。」
薩維德拉會接觸到國家社會主義狂熱，完全是「出於好奇」。十四歲時，有一天看到父親在觀看希特勒紀錄片，年輕的他完全被紐倫堡大審判所吸引。他詢問這些人的領袖是誰，父親回答：「一個神經病。」但是他覺得聽起來不太合理，一個神經病怎麼動員得了這麼多的群眾？因此開始對納粹主義感興趣。「我不知道你是否能對自己十四歲時的經歷感同身受，但我可以，我仍然記得當時大受感動。就像有些別人認為根本是雞毛蒜皮的小事，對我來說會深深烙印在腦海中。是的，我還記得那個感覺。縱使兒時發生的事對成年人來說看似微不足道，但對這些兒童而言，卻可能決定他們是否陷入深淵或擁有正常生活。我開始（對納粹主義）感興趣，並問了一堆問題：『這些人是怎樣的人？他們怎麼想？為什麼？』
大人只對我說，這些人晚上喝得爛醉，然後成群結黨地獵殺同性戀，就是這樣。他們就只是這麼對我說。因此，當我在老家加利西亞（Galicia）初次和真的納粹分子面對面時，我發現他們只是正常的普通人，他們根本沒有剃光頭，為人友善、知識淵博、飽讀詩書......好，我知道，他們看的都是納粹的著作。但如果你只是十四歲的毛頭小子，根本無從察覺，只知道這個人出口成章，熟知歷史故事，你只看得到這些；而如果你是歷史學家，可能就會馬上察覺有異，並對他說：『是不是也該講講歷史的另一面？』但是當你只有十四歲時，這個衝擊非常大。這時候你開始覺得自己長年視為模範的那些人、事、物，像是父母、老師、歷史課本等，並不如想像得那麼可靠。」
薩維德拉把這段青少年經驗用容易理解的方式呈現出來，目的在於避免並阻止激進化發生。「我用三個元素來描述激進化過程。第一是好奇心，它最後可能會變成確認偏誤，忽視與自身觀念相互衝突的事物。」在這裡，他提到「塞麥爾維斯反射」（Semmelweis Reflex），也就是人們拒絕接受任何和其既定信念相互衝突的訊息。「在學校演講時，我常以戀愛做譬喻。喜歡上一個人就好像頓悟一樣，眼中看到的就只有這個人，大腦會忽略任何關於這個人的負面言論。大腦表示：『我沒有興趣知道這些。』我的納粹主義塞麥爾維斯反射則是『哇！超酷的！』而不是『哇！我好同意他們的論述！』它一向都和情緒有關。之後我開始做功課，讀到納粹大屠殺及其他罪行，但腦海中卻記得好的一面。我在課堂上給學生看我從前做的希特勒拼貼畫，上面有希特勒餵食小鹿的照片，也有希特勒與小狗、小孩的合照，以及在車內對德國群眾揮手的照片，看起來一副受人愛戴的樣子。我在那幅畫裡建立一個『好好希特勒先生』的形象。我會這麼做的原因很簡單，因為它反映了當初『哇！超酷的！』那個情緒。有了這個情緒作為開端，一連串的激進化過程隨之而來，一切都是建立在情緒之上。」
之後，陰謀論就會開始對人產生影響。「當你說出『我看透了一切』這句話時，就表示自我開始作祟了。陰謀論的厲害之處在於，把所有的細節都照顧到了，一切的一切都非常合理。如果你和學問淵博的人聊天，例如科學家，會發現他們謹言慎行，而且常說：『我讀得越多，越覺得自己無知。』
激進分子卻正好相反，他越激進，就覺得自己越聰明，而且因為他的世界非黑即白，所以其他人就越笨；他的地位越高，其他人就越低賤。這個過程永無止境，他聰明到無極限，別人蠢到無下限，因此和非我族類講話時，他會一臉不屑，把對方當成三歲小孩。到了這個階段，他只會與抱持同樣看法的人來往，關在同溫層裡，和外界越離越遠。他會高談闊論奮鬥的目標，但這些意識型態討論，充其量只是在為自身行為找藉口罷了。」
一旦到了這個階段，人們的思想就會完全受到意識型態泡泡宰制，它會控制人如何處理新訊息，並且變造新訊息以符合僵化思維。如果事實與認知不一致，要處理的就是事實，而非看待事實的方式。書籍介紹

我們正生活在一場戰爭之中，卻渾然不知。西班牙地緣政治專家丹尼爾．依里亞德（Daniel Iriarte），透過在五十個國家採訪與多年的假訊息分析經驗，發現認知作戰的策略包括：
1. 訊息轟炸與情緒煽動：透過社群媒體的短影音、圖卡與貼文，快速引發接收者的憤怒或震驚等極端情緒，進而在沒有查證的情況下相信並轉發錯誤資訊。2. 協同造假的大量網軍：利用AI打造大量偽裝地點與身分的假帳號，偽裝成當地人進行「協同造假行為」，在網路空間營造出眾人支持的假象，引導輿論走向。3. 迷因武器化：將希望大眾厭惡的資訊或對象，包裝成諷刺或可笑的迷因，進而引發仇恨與不信任。4. 操弄演算法與AI深偽技術：善用平台演算法推送極端、聳動的內容，並運用AI生成的「深偽」（Deepfake）影音與錄音，發動真假難辨的選舉干預與資訊操弄。你可以放鬆滑手機，但請嚴謹判讀接收的一切。別讓你的手機，成為敵人攻陷你大腦的後門！【加入關鍵評論網會員】每天精彩好文直送你的信箱，每週獨享編輯精選、時事精選、藝文週報等特製電子報。還可留言與作者、記者、編輯討論文章內容。立刻點擊免費加入會員！責任編輯：翁世航

_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾关键评论网2026年9月9日报导】西班牙退役军人大卫·萨维德拉（David Saavedra）曾长期活跃于国家社会主义运动，现已脱离极端组织并致力于去激进化工作。萨维德拉指出，激进化过程始于好奇心，随后演变为确认偏误与情绪主导的「思想泡泡」。他强调，阴谋论源于自恋与不安全感，使个体陷入非黑即白的二元对立思维，拒绝接受与既定信念冲突的资讯，即「塞麦尔维斯反射」。在极端状态下，个体自认聪明而视他者为愚昧，最终封闭于同温层中。萨维德拉认为，疫情期间的不安情绪为极右派壮大提供了沃土。他提出，应在青少年形成意识型态前，透过同理心引导其情绪，避免其走向暴力。西班牙地缘政治专家丹尼尔·依里亚德（Daniel Iriarte）在著作《战争，从手机开始》中分析，认知战策略包括讯息轰炸、协同造假网军、迷因武器化及利用AI深伪技术操弄演算法。这些手段旨在引发极端情绪、制造舆论假象并撕裂社会，显示现代国家安全威胁已从传统军事转向认知领域。

）中提到，在一九八○年代末期、一九九○年代這段期間，新納粹圈子裡常流傳關於幕後黑暗強權的陰謀論，例如光明會（Illuminati）、錫安長老會紀要（The Protocols of the Elders of Zion）、畢德堡會議及三邊委員會（Trilateral Commission）的神祕故事、猶太控制政府（Zionist Occupation Government）等。
雖然如今反猶太色彩較淡一些，但令人訝異的是，不少這類陰謀論仍在許多圈子裡流行。
極端主義要存在，陰謀論必不可少，在承平時期，除非有什麼難以置信的想法可以合理化憎恨，否則人們不太會把憎恨當成志業。例如，他們在為某種更高的目標奮鬥、有人預謀毀滅他們的文化，或是敵對社群或成員不配為人。為了理解這種思考模式，研究陰謀論和激進化過程中的連結非常重要。
大衛．薩維德拉（David Saavedra）是西班牙退役軍人，他曾是國家社會主義的信徒，但最後選擇與老戰友分道揚鑣。
他說：「一開始，記者最常問我，那些四處演講倡導這種意識型態的人，例如貝德羅．瓦瑞拉（Pedro Varela，西班牙家喻戶曉的國家社會主義分子）這群人，是否真的相信自己所說的話，或他們根本是在用這些話術騙人、蠱惑年輕人？我覺得沒有半個記者相信我的回答。」
就私人和情感層面來說，與戰友決裂對他衝擊甚大。二○二五年三月，本書付印前夕，我有機會和他坐下來聊聊，當時他還在處理決裂帶來的震撼中。
「我覺得大部分的記者都認為是後者，但事情並非如此。就我而言，包含我在內所有我認識的人，可以說百分之百盲目地相信我們說出口的話。我們相信這整個信念，相信一般人的常識有問題，相信我們才是好人，相信在黑暗中潛伏著一股不懷好意的邪惡力量，而我們是對抗它的勇士。」
過去二十年間，薩維德拉在西班牙國家社會主義運動圈中占有一席之地。或許社會大眾不熟悉，但他在圈內赫赫有名。他協助出版刊物、組織獨立行動小組，在國家聯盟黨（Alianza Nacional）內做事。直到有一天，他的思考邏輯出現一道道裂縫，致使成年身分認同仰賴的意識型態堡壘分崩離析。
這並非一夕之間發生，而是各種境遇緩緩引導他走向這一步。首先是私人問題；再來是軍中工作，和不同國籍、種族的人接觸，特別是那些意識型態泡泡以外的人，帶給他新的視野。最後，他發現自己變成某民兵團的一分子，而他們正準備更進一步行動，而且不惜採用暴力，種種因素讓他認為該退出了。二○二一年出版的著作《前納粹分子回憶錄》（
Memorias de un exnazi
），就詳實記載他的心路歷程。
薩維德拉的案例特別有趣，他的自省能力非常強，花時間反思自身經驗與心路歷程：從利用過濾機制全盤控制極端團體成員思想，到「去激進化」。他對我說：「論述和意識型態就像一件被單。當你把政治或意識型態拿掉後，剩下的就是我稱為『思想泡泡』的心理框架，在這裡，情緒特別重要。無論拿什麼被單蓋在他身上，他就是會變激進，就是會走向極端。
一位激進分子就算說自己已經不再激進了，體內仍然流著激進的血液。這和酗酒的人有點相似，就算二十年沒喝酒，照樣會說自己酗酒。說真的，不管我相信的是什麼意識型態，就算是人權也好，我的腦袋照樣會把它變得激進。你可能會問：『要如何激進化人權？』很簡單，把所有沒有按照我的方式捍衛人權的人都說成是納粹就好了。」
薩維德拉會去學校與教育單位演講，試著拉某些青少年一把，避免他們踏上激進之路。他表示，這個變化過程其實和成為聖戰主義分子或加入拉丁樂團是一樣的，因此這些年輕人不一定會變成極右派。只要以同理心對待，並且適時引導他們前往正確的方向，就可以把這股煩躁不安之情帶往更富建設性的道路。薩維德拉也在YouTube 頻道上討論這些議題。
「我現在在開發可以盡早發現這種思想泡泡的工具，搶在意識型態浮現前，就先引導到其他方向。意識型態、論述或宗教一旦生成，腦袋就會像上鎖一樣。意識型態讓你腦海中的東西成形，它把事情拼湊起來，組織你看待世界和自己的方式。
然而，一切在更早之前就開始了，孩子們在校園高喊『希特勒萬歲』，讓大家心中的警鈴大作，但是警報在這之前就已經響很久了：當孩子開始覺得事情非黑即白，開始變得傲慢、不再好奇，開始一副『無所不知，無所不曉』的態度，這種行為就是危機開始的徵兆。」
他認為，「陰謀主義不外乎源於自戀，而且它鼓勵你變成自戀狂，無限膨脹自我，成天覺得自己想的最對，其他人都是白痴。這種說法不難理解，但我們也必須保持開放心態，接受其他原因：恐懼和不安全感。很少人會注意到極右派在疫情期間急速壯大。原因很明顯，疫情讓眾人的心中充滿不安，害怕接下來會發生什麼事，疫情提供激進化一片成長的沃土。
我記得疫情時，在路上看到窗邊貼著一張小孩畫的彩虹圖案，上面寫著『一切都會變好的』，然後人們在陽台上拍手叫好。當時我的內心覺得一陣平靜。不過，現在我們卻說：『嘖，別傻了！』那張圖極具象徵意義，它鼓舞人心，助人保持正向，但在同一時期，有人卻陷入黑暗漩渦中無法脫身，到現在還爬不出來。」
薩維德拉會接觸到國家社會主義狂熱，完全是「出於好奇」。十四歲時，有一天看到父親在觀看希特勒紀錄片，年輕的他完全被紐倫堡大審判所吸引。他詢問這些人的領袖是誰，父親回答：「一個神經病。」但是他覺得聽起來不太合理，一個神經病怎麼動員得了這麼多的群眾？
因此開始對納粹主義感興趣。
「我不知道你是否能對自己十四歲時的經歷感同身受，但我可以，我仍然記得當時大受感動。就像有些別人認為根本是雞毛蒜皮的小事，對我來說會深深烙印在腦海中。是的，我還記得那個感覺。縱使兒時發生的事對成年人來說看似微不足道，但對這些兒童而言，卻可能決定他們是否陷入深淵或擁有正常生活。我開始（對納粹主義）感興趣，並問了一堆問題：『這些人是怎樣的人？他們怎麼想？為什麼？』
大人只對我說，這些人晚上喝得爛醉，然後成群結黨地獵殺同性戀，就是這樣。他們就只是這麼對我說。因此，當我在老家加利西亞（Galicia）初次和真的納粹分子面對面時，我發現他們只是正常的普通人，他們根本沒有剃光頭，為人友善、知識淵博、飽讀詩書......好，我知道，他們看的都是納粹的著作。
但如果你只是十四歲的毛頭小子，根本無從察覺，只知道這個人出口成章，熟知歷史故事，你只看得到這些；而如果你是歷史學家，可能就會馬上察覺有異，並對他說：『是不是也該講講歷史的另一面？』但是當你只有十四歲時，這個衝擊非常大。這時候你開始覺得自己長年視為模範的那些人、事、物，像是父母、老師、歷史課本等，並不如想像得那麼可靠。」
薩維德拉把這段青少年經驗用容易理解的方式呈現出來，目的在於避免並阻止激進化發生。
「我用三個元素來描述激進化過程。第一是好奇心，它最後可能會變成確認偏誤，忽視與自身觀念相互衝突的事物。」在這裡，他提到「塞麥爾維斯反射」（Semmelweis Reflex），也就是人們拒絕接受任何和其既定信念相互衝突的訊息。「在學校演講時，我常以戀愛做譬喻。喜歡上一個人就好像頓悟一樣，眼中看到的就只有這個人，大腦會忽略任何關於這個人的負面言論。
大腦表示：『我沒有興趣知道這些。』我的納粹主義塞麥爾維斯反射則是『哇！超酷的！』而不是『哇！我好同意他們的論述！』它一向都和情緒有關。之後我開始做功課，讀到納粹大屠殺及其他罪行，但腦海中卻記得好的一面。我在課堂上給學生看我從前做的希特勒拼貼畫，上面有希特勒餵食小鹿的照片，也有希特勒與小狗、小孩的合照，以及在車內對德國群眾揮手的照片，看起來一副受人愛戴的樣子。
我在那幅畫裡建立一個『好好希特勒先生』的形象。我會這麼做的原因很簡單，因為它反映了當初『哇！超酷的！』那個情緒。有了這個情緒作為開端，一連串的激進化過程隨之而來，一切都是建立在情緒之上。」
之後，陰謀論就會開始對人產生影響。「當你說出『我看透了一切』這句話時，就表示自我開始作祟了。陰謀論的厲害之處在於，把所有的細節都照顧到了，一切的一切都非常合理。如果你和學問淵博的人聊天，例如科學家，會發現他們謹言慎行，而且常說：『我讀得越多，越覺得自己無知。』
激進分子卻正好相反，他越激進，就覺得自己越聰明，而且因為他的世界非黑即白，所以其他人就越笨；他的地位越高，其他人就越低賤。這個過程永無止境，他聰明到無極限，別人蠢到無下限，因此和非我族類講話時，他會一臉不屑，把對方當成三歲小孩。
到了這個階段，他只會與抱持同樣看法的人來往，關在同溫層裡，和外界越離越遠。他會高談闊論奮鬥的目標，但這些意識型態討論，充其量只是在為自身行為找藉口罷了。」
一旦到了這個階段，人們的思想就會完全受到意識型態泡泡宰制，它會控制人如何處理新訊息，並且變造新訊息以符合僵化思維。如果事實與認知不一致，要處理的就是事實，而非看待事實的方式。

3. 迷因武器化：將希望大眾厭惡的資訊或對象，包裝成諷刺或可笑的迷因，進而引發仇恨與不信任。

台北8日電）副總統蕭美琴7日接見美國學者訪團時表示，台灣將持續與理念相近國家深化交流，共同因應威權政權日益加劇的侵略行為及各項挑戰，守護台灣得來不易的自由民主，維護台灣人民共同打造的開放社會及民主制度。總統府今天發布新聞稿指出，蕭副總統7日下午接見美國史丹福大學胡佛研究所「台灣在印太地區」（TIPR）計畫學者訪團，分享台灣在國防、經濟、兩岸關係等領域的發展。副總統致詞時表示，感謝訪團長期關注台灣與台美關係，以及雙方基於共同利益推動的各項合作，一起促進區域和平穩定及雙方人民繁榮；維護區域和平穩定一直是台灣政府的施政目標，總統賴清德也發表「和平四大支柱行動方案」，包括強化國防、提升經濟繁榮、與民主陣營建立夥伴關係，以及在兩岸關係上展現有原則的領導。談及國防議題，副總統表示，政府除了持續增加國防預算，也透過追加預算及特別預算等方式，提出額外的國防支出規劃；但不能僅透過增加預算達成最終目標，政府也同步推動一系列國防改革措施，包括軍事改革與戰力提升。她指出，近期舉行的漢光演習也首次結合「城鎮韌性演習」，讓軍事演習更貼近實戰演練，並能與民防整備相互結合，顯示台灣看待國家安全不僅限於軍事層面，也相當重視全社會共同參與所發揮的力量，賴總統推動的「全社會防衛韌性」對於提升台灣安全與韌性具有重要意義。對於國際夥伴關係，她表示，無論是半導體或更廣泛的人工智慧供應鏈生態系，台灣在科技領域所取得的進展，都不是單一經濟體或國家可獨立完成，而是國際合作的成果，包括台灣新竹、美國矽谷，到台灣眾多中小企業共同打造的全球科技供應鏈產業生態系。副總統說，期盼在面對關稅及其他地緣政治因素的挑戰下，台美夥伴關係仍能展現韌性並持續深化，相信兩國合作不僅對強化台灣有所助益，也有助美國推動再工業化及在人工智慧領域保有優勢領先地位，這也是雙方持續進行經貿協商的重要目標之一。她表示，台灣也會持續拓展與其他理念相近國家深化交流，包括歐洲、新南向政策所涵蓋的亞太地區國家，以及日本等鄰近國家；這些合作將不僅限於經濟領域，也將共同面對威權政權日益加劇的侵略行為，以及人工智慧、社群媒體、資訊戰、心理戰、政治干預等新型威脅。談及兩岸關係，副總統說，當前兩岸關係相當艱難，中國領導階層持續拒絕與台灣民選政府進行直接對話與溝通，但台灣立場始終如一，台灣不會挑釁，也不會在得來不易的自由民主上妥協。訪團成員、資深研究員戴雅門（Larry Diamond）致詞時表示，台灣不僅因半導體產業以及在印太地區的重要戰略地位而受到重視，更因即使處於極具挑戰的環境，台灣的民主自由仍持續深化且展現高度韌性，成為民主自由的典範。透過 Google News
追蹤中央社
戴雅門指出，民主國家必須努力捍衛自身制度與價值，同時妥善處理並化解日益極化的政治對立。面對台灣當前複雜的政治情勢，期盼各方以理性務實的態度，讓政府有效運作、立法程序順利進行，共同維護憲法法庭健全運作，以化解彼此分歧。訪團成員埃利斯（James O. Ellis Jr.）表示，他高度肯定台灣政府將國防支出提高到國內生產毛額的3%，並以進一步提高為目標，也肯定台灣針對實際面臨的威脅，推動國軍現代化的願景，這些都是在現實限制下所做出的重大選擇。此外，美國對台灣的支持依然強而有力、根基深厚，且是跨黨派共識。#人工智慧

_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾中央社2026年9月8日报道】2026年9月7日，台湾副总统萧美琴在台北接见美国斯坦福大学胡佛研究所‘台湾在印太地区’计划学者访团。萧美琴表示，台湾将深化与理念相近国家交流，共同应对威权政权侵略及新型威胁。她重申赖清德总统提出的‘和平四大支柱行动方案’，涵盖强化国防、提升经济繁荣、建立民主伙伴及展现两岸关系原则性领导。在国防方面，台湾除增加国防预算至GDP的3%并计划进一步提高外，同步推动军事改革与战力提升。近期‘汉光演习’首次结合‘城镇韧性演习’，体现‘全社会防卫韧性’理念。萧美琴强调，台湾在半导体及人工智能供应链的成就源于国际合作，包括新竹与硅谷的协同。她指出，面对关税及地缘政治挑战，台美伙伴关系需展现韧性，合作将助力美国再工业化及保持AI优势。此外，台湾将拓展与欧洲、新南向政策国家及日本的合作，共同应对信息战、心理战等威胁。访团成员戴雅门肯定台湾民主韧性，呼吁化解内部政治对立；埃利斯肯定台湾国防支出及现代化愿景，重申美国对台支持为跨党派共识。

Legal Gazette
The NATO Legal Gazette is an educational outreach publication produced by the HQ SACT Legal Offices in Norfolk and Staff Element Europe co-located at SHAPE in Mons, Belgium.
The NATO Legal Gazette contains thematically organized articles usually written by authors who are military or civilian legal personnel working at NATO or in the governments NATO and partner nations.
Its purpose is to share articles of significance for the large NATO legal community and connect legal professionals of the Alliance.
The NATO Legal Gazette is not a formal NATO document. Its articles do not represent the official opinions or positions of NATO or individual governments.
NATO Legal Gazette Issue 43
Issue 43 of the NATO Legal Gazette focuses on the international law and policy adjacent the international security challenges posed by climate change.
As climate change continues to influence NATO’s and nations’ conduct of strategic affairs and military operations, we offer this issue of the NATO Legal Gazette as our contribution to the debate and discussion. The effects of climate change on mass migration, competition for food and water, and effects on coastal and maritime communities, among others, will be long-lasting, severe, and somewhat unpredictable.
It is our earnest hope this issue of NATO Legal Gazette contributes to the awareness of both legal practitioners and academics and the scientific, strategy, policy and operations communities with regard to the effects of climate change on NATO’s force structure, posture, and conduct of operations, and the changing operational environment.
We are grateful in particular for the contribution of our team of editors, with key contributions by Headquarters Supreme Allied Commander Transformation’s Robert “Butch” Bracknell, Galateia Gialitaki, Mette Prassé Hartov and Madeleine Goddrie, as well as our reserve staff legal officers, Commander Todd Richards, United States Navy Reserve, and Lieutenant Colonel Scott Lucchesi, United States Marine Corps Reserve and Lieutenant Colonel David Devenney of the Allied Command Transformation Communications Branch.
NATO Legal Gazette Issue 42
Issue 42 of NATO Legal Gazette covers the legal aspects of NATO’s newest domain, space. It is meant to complement other strands of work in NATO on space, framing some important and sometimes vexing legal issues pertaining to space operations (both military and “dual-use” activities), presence, exploitation of resources, the application of terrestrial law in space, and the intersection of the law governing space and cyber.
We are particularly fortunate to have a foreword including an update on the space law manuals projects convened by two consortia of organizers – Professor Dale Stephens of the University of Adelaide offers a succinct description of the work ongoing on the Woomera Manual, and Professors David Kuan-Wei Chen, Roy Ballest, Ram Jakhu, and Steven Freedland explain the scope and progress of the MILAMOS (McGill Manual on the International Law Applicable to Military Uses of Outer Space) project. Both these manuals will follow the model of the Tallinn Manual on cyber law, describing the current state of space law in the view of the manual’s contributors.
We are grateful in particular for the contribution of our team of editors, with key contributions by HQ SACT’s Galateia Gialitaki and our legal interns, Muge Karatas and Davis Wright. Galateia’s tireless efforts in leading the organization and editing process ensured this significant editorial undertaking spanning three continents and 14 time zones was a success.
NATO Legal Gazette Issue 41
This issue of the NATO Legal Gazette is the brain child of Robert (Butch) Bracknell who advocated using the Gazette to share and socialise innovative legal transformational ideas from legal advisors in academia, international organizations, commercial practice, and industry.
Issue 41 begins with a Preface by Geoffrey and Gary Corn, retired U.S. Army Judge Advocates and now noted academics. They consider technological changes from the 1980s to the present and incisively invite our attention to: “1) the development of the cyber domain and the adoption of cyber operations as a means and method of military and other security related operations; 2) the movement towards the development of lethal autonomous weapon systems (LAWS); and 3) the reshaping of the information environment and the attendant impact on perceptions of strategic legitimacy,” knowing that “NATO’s best minds must stake out the cutting edge territory of these innovations.”
Antoaneta Boeva is a lawyer for the ITER Organization in Saint-Paul-lès-Durance, France. Her article, Innovation for peaceful purposes only: Where there is the will, there is ITER describes the remarkable engineering and legal efforts to create a star on Earth in the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor. Lauren Brown, an Associate in the International Trade Group of Squire Patton Boggs, a full-service global law firm, writes about the power of innovation in NATO’s relationships in Partnership, Not Pivot, NATO’s Legal Answer to China.
Theodora Vassilika Ogden, a Fellow at the Human Security Centre in London who is currently studying at Leiden University, and Gregg Curley, a Judge Advocate in the U.S. Marine Corps, accept the challenge to stake out their perspectives on LAWS and autonomous weapons. Ms. Ogden’s article considers Responsibility, Liability and Lethal Autonomous Weapon Systems and Major Curley provides his views in Autonomous Weapons: A Pragmatic Approach.
Christopher Timura, Judith Alison Lee, R.L. Pratt and Scott Toussaint, who are attorneys in the Washington D.C. office of Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP and members of the firm’s International Trade Practice Group provide us an important article on the interplay between industry and national security is U.S. Export Controls: The Future of Disruptive Technologies. Martijn Antzoulatos-Borgstein, the Trade Compliance Manager for Rockwell Automation for Europe, Middle East and Africa, follows by proposing collective actions by NATO and partner nations to better manage the industry-security interplay in The Relevance and Benefits of Integrated Compliance Strategy (ICS) for NATO Defence Forces.
Rodrigo Vázquez Benítez is an Assistant Legal Advisor in the Allied Command Operations Office of Legal Affairs at the NATO Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe. He addresses the reshaping of the information environment by providing a description of the exploitation of the legal domain in a context of strategic competition in Legal Operations: The Use of Law as an Instrument of Power in the Context of Hybrid Threats and Strategic Competition.
Brett Sander, a US legal practitioner and principal at Vendor Clearance LLC, provides our final thoughtful article, The Road to Hell is Paved with Bad Contractors: Vendor Vetting is a Better Path.
NATO Legal Gazette Issue 40
Issue 40 of the NATO Legal Gazette Environmental Protection: NATO Policies and National Views returns our practice of publishing thematically organized issues that we adopted in 2013. The intent behind publishing this issue is the same as it was with the other topics that we previously addressed: to provide the readers of the NATO Legal Gazette detailed knowledge about a subject that requires legal attention. As an international organization dedicated to the rule of law, this issue examines Environmental Protection (EP) from the perspective of international law, NATO’s policies and national views.
The 1972 Stockholm Declaration, endorsed by the General Assembly of the United Nations, declared that States have “the responsibility to ensure that activities within their jurisdiction or control do not cause damage to the environment of other States or of areas beyond the limits of national jurisdiction.” The 1992 Rio Declaration in 1992 repeated the prevention principle which the International Court of Justice confirmed in the Gabčíkovo- Nagymaros case. The Court held, “in the field of environmental protection, vigilance and prevention are required on account of the often irreversible character of damage to the environment and of the limitations inherent in the very mechanism of reparation of this type of damage.” The prevention principle is now accepted as a norm of customary international law.4 This approach underlies NATO’s environmental protection policies, doctrine, and standardization agreements.
We present Issue 40 to provide legal advisors and environmental protection specialists a reference for their common use. It starts with four articles offering a comprehensive overview of the rules and policies on environmental protection a legal advisor should know when taking part in an exercise or a mission. Ms. Lisa Weihser, former NATO Legal Intern at the International Military Staff Office of the Legal Advisor, first reviews the events leading to the emergence of environmental protection during international armed conflicts and then analyses this topic through Human Rights norms. Lieutenant-Colonel David J. Burbridge, the SHAPE environmental officer, contributes an article on NATO operational responsibility for environmental protection. He reviews NATO’s evolution in developing current NATO environmental protection policies, standards and regulations. Next, Lieutenant Colonel Ben Valk, the former Deputy Legal Advisor of the International Military Staff, describes how NATO mainstreams environmental protection policies. He also presents an overview of the main documents a Legal Advisor is likely to use during a mission or an operation to ensure compliance with environmental regulations. Finally, Mr. Jeroen Rottink, Head of the Quality, Occupational Safety & Health, Environmental Protection Section (QOSHEP) of the Netherlands Defence Materiel Organization, offers his perspective on What NATO and National Legal Advisors Should Know about the Application of NATO Environmental Protection Policy, Doctrine and Standardization Agreements.
Major Ross Franklin is an Environmental Engineer in the Joint Engineer branch, Canadian Joint Operations Command and the Canadian Head of Delegation to the NATO Environmental Protection and Petroleum Handling Equipment Working Groups. Major Franklin argues in his essay that renewed collective defence measures in Europe are revealing the many capabilities and, sometimes, limitations of the current NATO EP framework in supporting the spirit of the North Atlantic Treaty, the NATO SOFA, and other foundations of the Alliance.
The next two articles are an illustration of national environmental protection framework. As visiting nations have to respect the Host Country’s environmental law when operating in another country, Dr. Jean Rhéaume, environmental law advisor for the Department of National Defence and Canadian Forces, presents a meticulous summary of the Canadian environmental provisions applicable to military activities taking place in Canada to familiarise legal advisors with the environmental law in Canada. Major Shane Drew, Deputy Director Environmental Governance, presents the Australian environmental legislative framework the Australian Defence Force must consider in the planning, conduct and remediation phases of combined and unilateral military exercises to minimise the impact on the environment.
This issue then focuses on specific areas of environmental protection. Colonel Jody M. Prescott, U.S. Army Judge Advocate Corps (retired) Army military attorney and lecturer at the University of Vermont, explores the links between armed conflict, gender and climate change, and addresses gender considerations issues in NATO Environmental Protection doctrine and practice. Mr. Nathaniel L Whelan, Chief of Training Support System Division, 7th Army Training Command, approaches the question of Environmental Protection from a different angle: as a hybrid threat. He describes how some entities use environmental protection and associated regulations to disrupt military operations and handicap NATO’s military training capability. He also suggests a multi-faceted solution set to mitigate this threat.
This issue concludes with current observations from the 2018 Trident Juncture exercise and NATO Resolute Support mission in Afghanistan. Through her experience in NATO-exercise Trident Juncture 2018, Major Marianne R. Bø, engineering officer in the Norwegian Armed Forces posted as Staff Officer Environmental Protection at the Norwegian Joint Headquarters, shares her hands-on perspective on managing the environmental impacts resulting from such a large joint exercise. Despite an intensive preparation and engagement with the visiting countries, this article reports that 1069 cases, 49 complaints and 1020 damage cases, arose during Trident Juncture 2018. This raises the question of how to better ensure respect of environmental regulations and policies in NATO Exercises. Our last article provides insight on the environmental impacts of the NATO Resolute Support mission in Afghanistan. Mr. Chris Ingoe, the NATO Environmental Protection Staff Officer, identifies, with words and pictures, the challenges surrounding the management of these environmental efforts to protect the force the environment and the civilian population.

NATO Legal Gazette Issue 36
The theme of our 36th issue, NATO Training and Exercises, is driven by current events and decisions made by the North Atlantic Council (NAC) at the Chicago Summit in 2012. At that meeting the Heads of State and Government of the Alliance, “confidently set ourselves the goal of NATO Forces 2020: modern, tightly connected forces equipped, trained, exercised and commanded so that they can operate together and with partners in any environment.”
At the 2014 Wales Summit the NAC endorsed the Connected Forces Initiative (CFI) as a key enabler in developing the goal NATO Forces 2020. CFI combines a comprehensive education, training, exercise, and evaluation programme with the use of cutting-edge technology to ensure that Allied forces remain prepared to engage cooperatively in the future. The CFI package approved in Wales included six measures: 1) an updated NATO Education, Training, Exercise and Evaluation (ETEE) Policy; 2) a broader NATO Training Concept 2015-2020; 3) a 2015 high-visability exercise; 4) Major NATO Exercises from 2016 Onwards Programme; 5) Continued progress in implementing the technological aspects of CFI; and 6) A Special Operations Component Command headquarters capability under operational command of SACEUR. As noted by the former Supreme Allied Commander Transformation, General Jean-Paul Palomeros, “The aim of CFI is to help reorient our training and exercises towards more demanding, high intensity operations and manoeuvre warfare while capitalizing on the experience gained through recent operational commitments.”
The consequence of these decisions made by the Alliance has been to increase the number of exercises from 115 in 2014 to 280 in 2015, with NATO’s largest exercise since 2002, Trident Juncture 15, held in October and November in Italy, Portugal, and Spain. More than 36,000 participants from more than 30 nations trained together at 18 exercise locations in a Non- Article V Crisis Response Operation focused on a high intensity modern warfare setting featuring a near peer opponent. And in all of these exercises the role played by legal professionals both as trainers and as members of the exercise audience significantly contributes to the realism of the events and the precision of the Alliance actions.
Thanks to the dedication of the seven authors who contributed articles to this issue: Ms. Victoria Baquerizo Lozano, Commander Svein Lystrup, Mr. Vincent Roobaert, Captain Audun Westgaard, Mr. David Nauta, Commander Wiesław Goździewicz and Colonel Gilles Castel, we are able to produce this 54 page edition offering three articles about training and exercises and one about the topic of self-defence from a French perspective that is consistent with the thematic approach of this issue. Emory International Law Review - Special Edition
NATO’s primary purpose and values are set out in the North Atlantic Treaty, first signed on 4 April 1949 in Washington D.C. by representatives of its twelve founding member nations.
The intervening decades have seen the accession of further members, and a series of changes to the security environment and to the technological means of warfare, to name only a few. Yet, the North Atlantic Treaty with its 14 brief articles remains the bedrock document of the Alliance.
In order to mark the 70th anniversary of the signing of the Washington Treaty, the Legal Offices in NATO Headquarters International Staff, in SHAPE, and in HQ SACT have, in cooperation with Emory Law School, coordinated a publication providing a current commentary to the Washington Treaty.
The publication is a special edition of Emory International Law Review and it would not have been possible without the tireless and meticulous editing and assistance provided by the editorial board of the Emory International Law Review.
The special edition is an Emory International Law Review publication and remains subject to Emory International Law Review copyright and permissions policy. All articles bear a disclaimer and while this is not an official NATO publication or collection of official NATO positions it is regarded to be a welcome contribution to understanding the context of the North Atlantic Treaty and the origins of what we now simply refer to as NATO.
