Iranian threats against American and Israeli leaders have expanded beyond presidents, military commanders, and senior policymakers to include members of their families. The immediate question is how much of the rhetoric represents psychological warfare and how much reflects preparations for actual operations.
For more stories from The Media Line go to themedialine.org
Iranian state television broadcast a three-minute video this week targeting Barron Trump, the 20-year-old son of US President Donald Trump. Titled “Where To Kill Barron Trump?” the video purported to show information about locations associated with him, his security arrangements, and his movements.
Produced by media affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and aired on Iran’s Channel 3, the footage claimed that a $10 million bounty had been offered for his killing.
The purported bounty and alleged surveillance have not been independently verified, and no public evidence has emerged linking the broadcast to an operational Iranian assassination team.
The US Secret Service said Tuesday that it was aware of the footage and investigates anything that could be perceived as a threat to its protectees, while declining to discuss protective intelligence.
Screenshot of channel 3's video explaining how to kill Barron Trump. (credit: Screenshot/X/@GhorbaniiNiyak)Barron Trump assassination threat flanked by threats to Melania, Netanyahu familyThe Barron Trump video followed an earlier production released by the IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency focusing on First Lady Melania Trump. That broadcast, reportedly titled “Where to Kill Melania Trump?” presented alleged details about her movements and potential weaknesses in her security. Reports about the Melania video did not indicate that a comparable multimillion-dollar bounty had been offered.
On Monday, Aug. 24, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu added another allegation.
“Iran targeted one of my sons. Iran tried to kill, to murder one of my sons,” Netanyahu told Israel’s Channel 14.
Netanyahu did not initially identify whether he was referring to Yair or Avner Netanyahu or say when or where the alleged attempt occurred.
Newsmax reported Wednesday that Yair Netanyahu, the prime minister’s 35-year-old elder son, was the alleged target. Citing an unnamed US law enforcement source familiar with the matter, the outlet said Israeli intelligence learned in December 2025 that suspected Iranian operatives were in the Miami area conducting surveillance of his home and movements.
Israeli officials alerted US authorities and instructed Yair Netanyahu to leave Florida immediately, according to Newsmax. He reportedly returned to Israel without collecting his belongings and has remained there. US and Israeli authorities have not publicly confirmed his identification as the alleged target or the operational details in the report.
Israeli media had previously reported that the security establishment had known about the alleged threat for months and that details were subject to military censorship. Iran’s mission to the United Nations did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Netanyahu made the disclosure while responding to reports that the Shin Bet security agency had declined to provide protection for political rival Gadi Eisenkot ahead of Israel’s Oct. 27 election. Netanyahu said the alleged threat against his son demonstrated that security protection was “not a luxury” and that appropriate protection should be provided to every candidate for prime minister.
Iran has a documented history of pursuing targets overseas.
In 2022, the US Justice Department charged IRGC member Shahram Poursafi with attempting to arrange the murder of former US National Security Adviser John Bolton. Prosecutors said the operation was likely intended as retaliation for the January 2020 killing of IRGC Quds Force commander Qasem Soleimani.
European governments have also accused Iran of using criminal networks as intermediaries. Sweden’s security service has accused Tehran of using criminal groups to target Israeli and Jewish interests, while the British government sanctioned the Swedish-based Foxtrot network in 2025 over attacks allegedly carried out on Iran’s behalf.
In June 2026, the UK joined 22 other countries in condemning Iranian state-linked attacks, intimidation, kidnappings, and assassination plots overseas. A British parliamentary briefing published that month said UK security agencies had tracked more than 20 potentially lethal Iran-backed plots during the preceding year and identified dissidents, journalists, Israelis, and Jews among Iran’s targets.
The current US-Israeli war with Iran may have increased Tehran’s incentive for retaliation. The conflict began with large-scale strikes on Feb. 28 that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and senior Iranian military officials, expanding the list of figures Iran may seek to avenge.
Daniel Byman, a professor in Georgetown University’s School of Foreign Service with a concurrent appointment in its Department of Government, told The Media Line that the escalation had increased Iranian incentives for retaliation. He cautioned against treating every public threat as evidence of an imminent attack.
“The current war has greatly increased Iran’s motivation for different forms of terrorism, including assassinations,” Byman said. “Iran attempted several plots in the past in response to the killing of figures like Qasem Soleimani, and the scale of the US and Israeli killings in Iran is far, far greater than what we saw in the past.”
He pointed to a possible countervailing factor: “US and Israeli operations also demonstrate a thorough penetration of Iranian intelligence networks. It is possible that the networks used for foreign assassination attempts are also penetrated...”
Byman said he could not know that for certain.
Open threats decrease likelihood of success, lead to increased security“Highly publicized plotting, such as videos regarding the president’s family, are more likely intimidation and trolling attempts, as this will lead to increased security, making an actual plot harder,” he said.
Public threats, though, are only one part of Iran’s evolving overseas model.
Danny Citrinowicz, a senior researcher in the Iran and the Shi’ite Axis Program at Israel’s Institute for National Security Studies (INSS), said the scale of Iran’s losses means the drive for retaliation is unlikely to disappear even if diplomacy eventually reduces the military confrontation.
“The Iranians are now in the revenge business,” Citrinowicz told The Media Line. “This is not something that is going away. The Iranians, regardless of what will happen in terms of an agreement, yes or no, will seek revenge for Khamenei, I think, for the foreseeable future.”
Citrinowicz said Iran’s increasing reliance on criminals and other intermediaries offers Tehran deniability but also creates vulnerabilities.
“Their modus operandi is very unique. They are using third-party elements because they want to create a distance between them and the operation itself,” he said.
“The good thing for them is that they’re distancing themselves from any activity that happens. The bad thing is that you’re hiring people that are not experienced in this kind of work, and the signature they create helps local authorities discover that,” Citrinowicz said.
“I’m not underestimating their ability to do things, but I think the modus operandi is helping security services to track what the Iranians are trying to do,” he added.
Byman reached a similar conclusion from a different angle.
“Iran’s shift to using criminal networks makes detection harder in some ways, but these networks are also more likely to betray Iran and are more amateurish,” he said. “Most of these plots fail, but at a relatively low cost to Iran.”
Outsourcing allows an operation to be disrupted without exposing large numbers of Iranian intelligence personnel or directly linking Tehran to an attack.
Irina Tsukerman, president of Scarab Rising, said the distinction between propaganda and operations is not absolute. She spoke to The Media Line before Wednesday’s report identified Yair Netanyahu as the alleged target.
“Given Iran’s established record of surveillance, kidnapping plots, assassination attempts, and planned attacks against Israelis abroad, Netanyahu’s claim is plausible enough to warrant serious attention, although there is not enough public information to determine how advanced the alleged operation became,” Tsukerman told The Media Line.
She cautioned that sophisticated-looking targeting videos are not proof of physical surveillance or an active assassination cell.
“Some information presented in state media may originate from social media, commercially available databases, hacking, open-source research, exaggeration, or fabrication, so the existence of an elaborate video does not demonstrate that an assassination team has been deployed,” she said.
The danger, Tsukerman argued, can develop after the material is released.
“Criminals can respond to the prospect of money, ideological sympathizers can volunteer assistance, and Iranian intelligence can later identify useful individuals who began acting without receiving instructions from Tehran,” she explained.
“Under those circumstances, propaganda can become part of an operational environment even when the original broadcast was produced primarily for intimidation.”
That distinction also complicates the frequently used concept of Iranian “sleeper cells.”
Tsukerman said the term can suggest organized teams living covertly in Western countries while awaiting direct instructions from Tehran. Recent investigations instead point to looser systems in which intelligence officers, criminals, locally recruited individuals, foreign nationals, and other intermediaries perform separate tasks.
Such networks can still leave detectable traces. Surveillance of a target, unusual financial transfers, recruitment attempts, weapons acquisition, and communications with known Iranian intermediaries can form an identifiable pattern when intelligence and law enforcement agencies combine information across jurisdictions.
_source.movement_title: 伊朗针对美以领导人亲属升级暗杀威胁与监视行动
_source.movement_abstract: 【美国The Media Line 2026 年 8 月 27 日报道】伊朗国家电视台及伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）附属媒体近期发布视频，针对美国总统特朗普之子巴伦及第一夫人梅拉尼娅进行公开威胁，声称提供 1000 万美元悬赏并展示其行踪与安保漏洞。以色列总理内塔尼亚胡指控伊朗曾试图暗杀其子雅伊尔，据称 2025 年 12 月伊朗特工曾在迈阿密对其住所进行监视，导致其紧急撤离。美国特勤局已关注相关视频并展开调查，但尚未证实具体暗杀小组的存在。分析指出，当前美以与伊朗的冲突加剧了德黑兰的报复动机，特别是针对 2026 年 2 月伊朗最高领袖哈梅内伊遇袭身亡的回应。伊朗正转向利用犯罪网络和第三方中介实施海外行动，以获取行动否认权，但此举也增加了被情报机构追踪的风险。专家警告，此类公开威胁虽可能旨在心理战，但可能诱发激进分子自发行动，且伊朗利用松散网络进行监视、资金转移和武器获取的模式已形成可识别的情报特征。

Netanyahu said the alleged threat against his son demonstrated that security protection was “not a luxury” and that appropriate protection should be provided to every candidate for prime minister.
Iran has a documented history of pursuing targets overseas.
In 2022, the US Justice Department charged IRGC member Shahram Poursafi with attempting to arrange the murder of former US National Security Adviser John Bolton. Prosecutors said the operation was likely intended as retaliation for the January 2020 killing of IRGC Quds Force commander Qasem Soleimani.
European governments have also accused Iran of using criminal networks as intermediaries. Sweden’s security service has accused Tehran of using criminal groups to target Israeli and Jewish interests, while the British government sanctioned the Swedish-based Foxtrot network in 2025 over attacks allegedly carried out on Iran’s behalf.
In June 2026, the UK joined 22 other countries in condemning Iranian state-linked attacks, intimidation, kidnappings, and assassination plots overseas. A British parliamentary briefing published that month said UK security agencies had tracked more than 20 potentially lethal Iran-backed plots during the preceding year and identified dissidents, journalists, Israelis, and Jews among Iran’s targets.
The current US-Israeli war with Iran may have increased Tehran’s incentive for retaliation. The conflict began with large-scale strikes on Feb. 28 that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and senior Iranian military officials, expanding the list of figures Iran may seek to avenge.
Daniel Byman, a professor in Georgetown University’s School of Foreign Service with a concurrent appointment in its Department of Government, told The Media Line that the escalation had increased Iranian incentives for retaliation. He cautioned against treating every public threat as evidence of an imminent attack.
“The current war has greatly increased Iran’s motivation for different forms of terrorism, including assassinations,” Byman said. “Iran attempted several plots in the past in response to the killing of figures like Qasem Soleimani, and the scale of the US and Israeli killings in Iran is far, far greater than what we saw in the past.”
He pointed to a possible countervailing factor: “US and Israeli operations also demonstrate a thorough penetration of Iranian intelligence networks. It is possible that the networks used for foreign assassination attempts are also penetrated...”
Byman said he could not know that for certain.
Open threats decrease likelihood of success, lead to increased security“Highly publicized plotting, such as videos regarding the president’s family, are more likely intimidation and trolling attempts, as this will lead to increased security, making an actual plot harder,” he said.
Public threats, though, are only one part of Iran’s evolving overseas model.
Danny Citrinowicz, a senior researcher in the Iran and the Shi’ite Axis Program at Israel’s Institute for National Security Studies (INSS), said the scale of Iran’s losses means the drive for retaliation is unlikely to disappear even if diplomacy eventually reduces the military confrontation.
“The Iranians are now in the revenge business,” Citrinowicz told The Media Line. “This is not something that is going away. The Iranians, regardless of what will happen in terms of an agreement, yes or no, will seek revenge for Khamenei, I think, for the foreseeable future.”
Citrinowicz said Iran’s increasing reliance on criminals and other intermediaries offers Tehran deniability but also creates vulnerabilities.
“Their modus operandi is very unique. They are using third-party elements because they want to create a distance between them and the operation itself,” he said.
“The good thing for them is that they’re distancing themselves from any activity that happens. The bad thing is that you’re hiring people that are not experienced in this kind of work, and the signature they create helps local authorities discover that,” Citrinowicz said.
“I’m not underestimating their ability to do things, but I think the modus operandi is helping security services to track what the Iranians are trying to do,” he added.
Byman reached a similar conclusion from a different angle.
“Iran’s shift to using criminal networks makes detection harder in some ways, but these networks are also more likely to betray Iran and are more amateurish,” he said. “Most of these plots fail, but at a relatively low cost to Iran.”
Outsourcing allows an operation to be disrupted without exposing large numbers of Iranian intelligence personnel or directly linking Tehran to an attack.
Irina Tsukerman, president of Scarab Rising, said the distinction between propaganda and operations is not absolute. She spoke to The Media Line before Wednesday’s report identified Yair Netanyahu as the alleged target.
“Given Iran’s established record of surveillance, kidnapping plots, assassination attempts, and planned attacks against Israelis abroad, Netanyahu’s claim is plausible enough to warrant serious attention, although there is not enough public information to determine how advanced the alleged operation became,” Tsukerman told The Media Line.
She cautioned that sophisticated-looking targeting videos are not proof of physical surveillance or an active assassination cell.
“Some information presented in state media may originate from social media, commercially available databases, hacking, open-source research, exaggeration, or fabrication, so the existence of an elaborate video does not demonstrate that an assassination team has been deployed,” she said.
The danger, Tsukerman argued, can develop after the material is released.
“Criminals can respond to the prospect of money, ideological sympathizers can volunteer assistance, and Iranian intelligence can later identify useful individuals who began acting without receiving instructions from Tehran,” she explained.
“Under those circumstances, propaganda can become part of an operational environment even when the original broadcast was produced primarily for intimidation.”
That distinction also complicates the frequently used concept of Iranian “sleeper cells.”
Tsukerman said the term can suggest organized teams living covertly in Western countries while awaiting direct instructions from Tehran. Recent investigations instead point to looser systems in which intelligence officers, criminals, locally recruited individuals, foreign nationals, and other intermediaries perform separate tasks.
Such networks can still leave detectable traces. Surveillance of a target, unusual financial transfers, recruitment attempts, weapons acquisition, and communications with known Iranian intermediaries can form an identifiable pattern when intelligence and law enforcement agencies combine information across jurisdictions.", "url": "https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/iran-news/article-906753", "source": null, "publish_time": 1787834812000, "update_time": 1787839170234, "gather_time": 1787839170234, "insert_time": 1787839170234, "picture_urls": ["https://images.jpost.com/image/upload/f_auto,fl_lossy/q_auto/c_fill,g_faces:center,h_720,w_1280/734968", "https://images.jpost.com/image/upload/f_auto,fl_lossy/c_fill,g_faces:center,h_537,w_822/734969"], "video_urls": null, "audio_urls": null, "file_urls": null, "picture_paths": null, "video_paths": null, "audio_paths": null, "file_paths": null, "site_id": "ef9567c55c620bfb79e4da9e3c480be0", "site_name": "以色列耶路撒冷邮报", "site_region": "以色列", "board_id": null, "board_name": "中东", "source_tasks": ["002@091@20250515@10000001@15202"], "project_id": "", "task_id": "", "target_id": ""}

伊朗对美国和以色列领导人的威胁已经扩大到总统、军事指挥官和高级决策者之外，还包括他们的家庭成员。最直接的问题是，有多少言论代表了心理战，又有多少反映了实际行动的准备工作。
更多来自媒体热线的故事，请访问themedialine.org
伊朗国家电视台本周播放了一段3分钟的视频，目标是美国总统唐纳德·特朗普20岁的儿子巴伦·特朗普。这段名为“在哪里杀死巴伦·特朗普？”的视频旨在展示与他有关的地点、他的安全安排和他的行动。
这段视频由隶属于伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）的媒体制作，并在伊朗第三频道播出。视频中称，有人悬赏1000万美元要杀死他。
所谓的赏金和所谓的监视尚未得到独立证实，也没有公开证据将广播与伊朗暗杀小组联系起来。
美国特勤局周二表示，他们已经注意到了这段视频，并调查了任何可能被视为对其受保护者构成威胁的事情，但拒绝讨论保护性情报。
第三频道解释如何杀死巴伦·特朗普的视频截图。（来源：截图/X/@Ghorbaniiniyak）巴伦·特朗普的暗杀威胁与梅拉尼娅和内塔尼亚胡家人的威胁相呼应巴伦·特朗普的视频是在伊斯兰革命卫队下属的塔斯尼姆通讯社早些时候发布的一段关于第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普的视频之后发布的。据报道，该节目名为“在哪里杀死梅拉尼娅·特朗普？”，展示了关于她的行动和潜在安全弱点的所谓细节。关于梅拉尼娅视频的报道并没有表明提供了类似的数百万美元的赏金。
8月24日，星期一，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡又增加了一项指控。
伊朗袭击了我的一个儿子。内塔尼亚胡告诉以色列第14频道：“伊朗试图杀害我的一个儿子。”
内塔尼亚胡最初没有说明他指的是亚伊尔还是阿夫纳·内塔尼亚胡，也没有说明所谓的企图发生的时间和地点。
Newsmax周三报道称，以色列总理35岁的长子亚伊尔·内塔尼亚胡（Yair Netanyahu）是所谓的目标。该媒体援引一位不愿透露姓名的美国执法部门知情人士的话称，以色列情报部门在2025年12月获悉，疑似伊朗特工在迈阿密地区对他的住所和行动进行监视。
据Newsmax报道，以色列官员向美国当局发出警报，并指示亚伊尔·内塔尼亚胡立即离开佛罗里达州。据报告，他没有收拾自己的物品就返回了以色列，并一直留在那里。美国和以色列当局没有公开确认他是所谓的目标，也没有公开确认报告中的行动细节。
以色列媒体此前报道称，安全机构几个月前就知道所谓的威胁，细节受到军方审查。伊朗驻联合国代表团没有回应路透社的置评请求。
内塔尼亚胡是在回应辛贝特安全局拒绝在10月27日以色列大选前为政治对手艾森科特提供保护的报道时透露这一消息的。内塔尼亚胡说，针对他儿子的所谓威胁表明，安全保护“不是一种奢侈品”，应该为每一位总理候选人提供适当的保护。
伊朗有追踪海外目标的历史记录。
2022年，美国司法部指控伊斯兰革命卫队成员沙赫拉姆·普尔萨菲企图安排谋杀前美国国家安全顾问约翰·博尔顿。检察官表示，此次行动可能是为了报复伊斯兰革命卫队圣城部队指挥官卡西姆·苏莱马尼于2020年1月被杀。
欧洲各国政府也指责伊朗利用犯罪网络作为中间人。瑞典安全部门指控德黑兰利用犯罪集团针对以色列和犹太人的利益，而英国政府在2025年制裁了总部位于瑞典的狐步舞网络，据称该网络代表伊朗发动了袭击。
2026年6月，英国与其他22个国家一起谴责与伊朗国家有关的袭击、恐吓、绑架和海外暗杀阴谋。当月发布的一份英国议会简报称，英国安全机构在前一年追踪了20多起可能致命的伊朗支持的阴谋，并将持不同政见者、记者、以色列人和犹太人确定为伊朗的目标。
目前美国和以色列与伊朗的战争可能增加了德黑兰报复的动机。这场冲突始于2月28日的大规模空袭，最高领袖哈梅内伊和伊朗军方高级官员在空袭中丧生，扩大了伊朗可能寻求报复的人物名单。
乔治敦大学（Georgetown University）外交学院（School of Foreign Service）教授丹尼尔·拜曼（Daniel Byman）同时兼任乔治敦大学政府系（Department of Government）教授，他告诉媒体，事态升级增加了伊朗报复的动机。他警告说，不要把每一个公开的威胁都当作即将发生袭击的证据。
拜曼说：“目前的战争大大增加了伊朗实施不同形式恐怖主义的动机，包括暗杀。”“针对卡西姆·苏莱曼尼（Qasem Soleimani）这样的人物被杀，伊朗过去曾尝试过几次阴谋，而美国和以色列在伊朗的杀戮规模远远超过我们过去所看到的。”
他指出了一个可能的抵消因素：美国和以色列的行动也显示了对伊朗情报网络的彻底渗透。用于外国暗杀企图的网络也可能被渗透……
拜曼说他不能确定这一点。
公开威胁降低了成功的可能性，导致安全措施加强。“高度公开的阴谋，比如关于总统家人的视频，更有可能是恐吓和恶意中伤，因为这将导致安全措施加强，使实际阴谋更加困难，”他说。
不过，公开威胁只是伊朗不断演变的海外模式的一部分。
以色列国家安全研究所（INSS）伊朗和什叶派轴心项目的高级研究员丹尼·西特里诺维茨（Danny Citrinowicz）说，伊朗的损失规模意味着，即使外交手段最终减少了军事对抗，报复的动力也不太可能消失。
“伊朗人现在正在复仇，”西特里诺维茨告诉媒体热线。这不是正在消失的东西。我认为，在可预见的未来，无论协议达成与否，伊朗人都将寻求对哈梅内伊的报复。
Citrinowicz说，伊朗对犯罪分子和其他中间人的日益依赖为德黑兰提供了否认的机会，但也造成了漏洞。
他们的作案手法非常独特。他说：“他们正在使用第三方元素，因为他们想在他们和行动本身之间建立一种距离。”
对他们来说，好的一面是他们正在远离发生的任何活动。西特里诺维茨说：“糟糕的是，你雇佣的人没有这方面的工作经验，而他们创造的签名有助于地方当局发现这一点。”
“我没有低估他们做事的能力，但我认为他们的作案手法是在帮助安全部门追踪伊朗人试图做什么，”他补充说。
拜曼从另一个角度得出了类似的结论。
他说：“伊朗转向使用犯罪网络在某些方面使侦查变得更加困难，但这些网络也更有可能背叛伊朗，而且更加业余。”“这些阴谋大多以失败告终，但伊朗付出的代价相对较低.”
外包允许在不暴露大量伊朗情报人员或直接将德黑兰与袭击联系起来的情况下中断行动。
圣甲虫崛起的主席伊琳娜·楚克曼说，宣传和行动之间的区别并不是绝对的。在周三的报道指出亚伊尔·内塔尼亚胡是所谓的目标之前，她接受了媒体的采访。
“鉴于伊朗已有的监视、绑架阴谋、暗杀企图和针对海外以色列人的袭击计划的记录，内塔尼亚胡的说法是可信的，值得认真关注，尽管没有足够的公开信息来确定所谓的行动进展到什么程度，”楚克曼告诉媒体热线。
她提醒说，看起来很复杂的目标视频并不是物理监视或活跃的暗杀小组的证据。
她说：“国家媒体提供的一些信息可能来自社交媒体、商业数据库、黑客、开源研究、夸张或捏造，因此精心制作的视频的存在并不表明已经部署了暗杀小组。”
楚克曼认为，危险可能会在材料释放后发展。
她解释说：“犯罪分子可以对金钱的前景做出反应，意识形态的同情者可以自愿提供援助，伊朗情报部门随后可以识别那些在没有收到德黑兰指示的情况下开始行动的有用的个人。”
“在这种情况下，宣传可以成为行动环境的一部分，即使最初的广播主要是为了恐吓而制作的。”
这一区别也使经常使用的伊朗“潜伏组织”的概念复杂化。
楚克曼说，这个词可以指秘密居住在西方国家的有组织的团队，同时等待来自德黑兰的直接指示。相反，最近的调查表明，情报官员、罪犯、当地招募的个人、外国公民和其他中间人执行不同的任务的系统更加松散。
这样的网络仍然可以留下可检测的痕迹。对目标的监视、不寻常的资金转移、招募企图、武器获取以及与已知的伊朗中间商的通信，在情报和执法机构综合各管辖区的信息时，可以形成一种可识别的模式。

ERBIL, Kurdistan Region - The spokesperson for Iran’s armed forces on Wednesday threatened journalists working for several Persian-language media outlets abroad, describing them as “soldiers” of Israel and the United States and saying they could be treated as military targets.
Brigadier General Abolfazl Shekarchi made the remarks during a visit to Defa Press, a media outlet linked to Iran’s defense establishment, explicitly naming Iran International, BBC Persian, Manoto and Radio Farda and accusing their employees of working on behalf of Tehran’s enemies.
“Media outlets such as BBC, Iran International and Radio Farda are directly connected to [the Israeli intelligence agency] Mossad, the [US’s Central Intelligence Agency] CIA and hostile intelligence organizations, and receive their operational direction and support from them,” Shekarchi said.
“Those who work for these outlets are considered soldiers of Zionism and the criminal [United States of] America, and they could even be included in the military target bank, because from our perspective, these are not media organisations.”
The remarks represent an unusually direct threat against journalists working for Persian-language media outside Iran and come amid the continuing conflict between Tehran and Washington.
Iranian authorities have for years portrayed Persian-language broadcasters based overseas as part of a wider foreign campaign against the Islamic Republic, often framing their reporting as part of a wider psychological warfare or a national security threat.
Moreover, Iran has previously used financial pressure against journalists working for Persian-language broadcasters abroad. In 2017, Iranian authorities imposed an asset-freezing injunction on 152 current and former BBC Persian staff and contributors, preventing them from buying, selling or inheriting property in Iran.
Journalists inside Iran have also repeatedly been detained over their work, particularly during periods of unrest and political crisis.
Earlier this month, Iranian photojournalist Yalda Moaiery was sentenced to 15 years in prison under legislation introduced after the 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June of last year. The charges included giving interviews to media deemed hostile by the authorities and providing photographs to organizations linked to the US and Israel. Reporters Without Borders said 16 journalists had been detained in Iran so far this year.
Iran has also detained foreign and dual nationals on espionage and national security charges. Western governments and rights groups have repeatedly criticized such arrests as politically motivated, allegations Tehran denies.
BBC Persian and other outlets have previously reported pressure on journalists’ relatives inside Iran, while Tehran has imposed legal and financial restrictions on journalists working for foreign-based Persian-language media.
Shekarchi’s Wednesday remarks however, go further by placing media workers directly within the language of military targeting, blurring the distinction between journalism and participation in hostilities.
_source.movement_title: 伊朗军方威胁将境外波斯语媒体记者列为军事打击目标
_source.movement_abstract: 【伊拉克库尔德斯坦埃尔比勒报道】2026 年 8 月 26 日，伊朗武装部队发言人阿博尔法兹尔·谢卡奇准将在访问德法通讯社时发表言论，明确威胁在境外工作的波斯语媒体记者。谢卡奇点名伊朗国际电视台、BBC 波斯语频道、Manoto 和自由电台，指控这些机构与以色列摩萨德及美国中央情报局直接关联，接受其行动指令。他宣称这些媒体员工是“犹太复国主义”和“美国”的士兵，并非新闻机构，因此可能被列入军事目标库。此举标志着伊朗对境外波斯语媒体威胁升级，将新闻工作直接等同于参战行为。伊朗当局长期将境外波斯语广播视为心理战和国家安全威胁，曾于 2017 年冻结 152 名 BBC 波斯语员工资产。今年 6 月伊朗与以色列冲突后，伊朗通过新立法，本月内已有 16 名记者被拘，摄影记者瓦尔达·莫艾里因向被指敌对的媒体提供采访和照片，被判处 15 年监禁。西方政府及人权组织批评此类逮捕具有政治动机，但德黑兰予以否认。

Iranian authorities have for years portrayed Persian-language broadcasters based overseas as part of a wider foreign campaign against the Islamic Republic, often framing their reporting as part of a wider psychological warfare or a national security threat.
Moreover, Iran has previously used financial pressure against journalists working for Persian-language broadcasters abroad. In 2017, Iranian authorities imposed an asset-freezing injunction on 152 current and former BBC Persian staff and contributors, preventing them from buying, selling or inheriting property in Iran.
Journalists inside Iran have also repeatedly been detained over their work, particularly during periods of unrest and political crisis.
Earlier this month, Iranian photojournalist Yalda Moaiery was sentenced to 15 years in prison under legislation introduced after the 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June of last year. The charges included giving interviews to media deemed hostile by the authorities and providing photographs to organizations linked to the US and Israel. Reporters Without Borders said 16 journalists had been detained in Iran so far this year.
Iran has also detained foreign and dual nationals on espionage and national security charges. Western governments and rights groups have repeatedly criticized such arrests as politically motivated, allegations Tehran denies.
BBC Persian and other outlets have previously reported pressure on journalists’ relatives inside Iran, while Tehran has imposed legal and financial restrictions on journalists working for foreign-based Persian-language media.

埃尔比勒，库尔德斯坦地区-周三，伊朗武装部队发言人威胁为几家海外波斯语媒体工作的记者，称他们是以色列和美国的“士兵”，并称他们可能被视为军事目标。
Abolfazl Shekarchi准将在访问与伊朗国防机构有关的媒体DEFA Press时发表了上述言论，明确点名伊朗国际、BBC波斯语、Manoto和Radio Farda，并指责他们的雇员为德黑兰的敌人工作。
谢卡尔奇说：“英国广播公司、伊朗国际和法尔达电台等媒体与（以色列情报机构）摩萨德、（美国中央情报局）中央情报局和敌对情报组织有直接联系，并从他们那里获得行动指导和支持。”
“那些为这些媒体工作的人被认为是犹太复国主义和犯罪（美国）的士兵，他们甚至可能被列入军事目标银行，因为从我们的角度来看，这些不是媒体机构。”
这番言论是对伊朗境外波斯语媒体记者的一种不同寻常的直接威胁，而且正值德黑兰和华盛顿之间的冲突持续之际。
多年来，伊朗当局一直将海外波斯语广播公司描述为针对伊朗伊斯兰共和国的更广泛的外国行动的一部分，经常将其报道说成是更广泛的心理战或国家安全威胁的一部分。
此外，伊朗此前曾对在海外为波斯语广播公司工作的记者施加财政压力。2017年，伊朗当局对152名现任和前任BBC波斯语工作人员和撰稿人实施了资产冻结禁令，禁止他们在伊朗购买、出售或继承财产。
伊朗境内的记者也多次因其工作而被拘留，特别是在动乱和政治危机期间。
本月早些时候，伊朗摄影记者Yalda Moaiery被判处15年监禁，这是去年6月伊朗和以色列之间12天战争后出台的法律规定的。这些指控包括接受被当局视为敌对的媒体的采访，以及向与美国和以色列有关的组织提供照片。记者无国界组织表示，今年到目前为止，已有16名记者在伊朗被拘留。
伊朗还以间谍和国家安全罪名拘留了外国和双重国籍人士。西方政府和人权组织一再批评这种逮捕是出于政治动机，德黑兰否认这种指控。
英国广播公司波斯语频道和其他媒体此前报道称，记者在伊朗境内的亲属受到压力，而德黑兰则对为外国波斯语媒体工作的记者施加了法律和财务限制。
然而，谢卡尔奇周三的讲话更进一步，将媒体工作者直接置于军事目标的语言中，模糊了新闻和参与敌对行动之间的区别。

The Trump administration has announced unspecified plans to further tighten sanctions on Iran, threatening other countries, including China, in the process. We speak to sanctions expert Nicholas Mulder about what he calls the “rhetorical” and “psychological warfare” of the announcement. For Iran, says Mulder, the announcement was not “really materially all that meaningful. And to the extent that they are, they hurt ordinary Iranians and not the government.” The impact on the U.S. relationship with China, however, could be much greater. If the U.S. does place secondary sanctions on Iran’s trading partners, the “U.S.-China trade truce might be unraveling,” warns Mulder. “The space for maneuver that the U.S. has in using these tools of very coercive economic statecraft has narrowed.”
The Trump administration has outlined plans to tighten sanctions on Iran, warning that businesses, banks and other nations could lose access to the U.S. financial system if they continue doing business with Tehran. On Monday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced “Operation Economic Outcast,” which includes secondary sanctions on trade related to Iran’s oil, shipping, cryptocurrency, gold and aviation industries. Bessent said countries have a defined timeline to sever ties with Iran, but provided no details on which countries would be targeted, or when.
After Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent finished his remarks, he took questions from reporters.
Iran has threatened to retaliate against the U.S. in a, quote, “seismic” manner. Iranian officials have said that any country supporting the new U.S. economic restrictions would be considered an enemy. This is Iran’s economy minister, Ali Madanizadeh.
To talk more about the U.S. economic war against Iran, we are joined now by Nicholas Mulder. He’s an associate professor of history at Cornell University and a specialist in sanctions. He’s the author of
.
Nicholas Mulder, welcome to
Your response to this announcement yesterday? There’s not a lot of details on enforcement. And what does this mean for China? China is Iran’s largest economic trading partner, buys over 80% of its oil, and President Trump is set to meet with the Chinese premier next month.
Yeah. Thank you for having me.
I think that this announcement really shows that the United States is trying to increase the pressure on Iran, but is primarily doing so at the moment by rhetorical means and a kind of psychological warfare. Of course, Iran has been under a naval blockade imposed by the United States since June. The Iranian economy is feeling the pressure of that. And the announcement yesterday was very short, as you mentioned, on details. There was a hint that a major global financial institution might be designated under the sanctions soon, but that, too, was left very vague. It could have been a veiled threat towards China. It could have been a sort of general attempt to create a chilling effect around these transactions.
The reality is that at this point there are relatively few sanctions that the United States can take that directly affect Iran. There were some things thrown in to the announcement and to the designations by the Treasury, such as a ban on all remaining remittances to Iran, a ban on remaining academic and sports exchanges. But these really just seem gratuitous ways to try and show that this is an attempt to isolate Iran even further. They weren’t really materially all that meaningful. And to the extent that they are, they hurt ordinary Iranians and not the government.
The real way that the U.S. is going to try and enforce these sanctions is by putting pressure on third countries trading with Iran, and I think that’s where it’s going to be an open question whether these sanctions will be as forceful as Bessent wants them to be. The big trading partner, as you already mentioned, is China, but we’re also talking about Pakistan, Turkey, India and a number of other countries that trade a lot with Iran and, you know, that see that they have every right to, that these are, at the end of the day, just American sanctions — they’re not international legal measures. And these countries claim, and for themselves, the right to sovereign — make sovereign decisions about who they can trade with and who they cannot. The Chinese have already announced that they’re going to not just ignore them, but even make sure that countries and companies within China will not comply with them. And recently Chinese courts have also begun to put sanctions on companies that complied with American sanctions. So, I think that this is no longer an empty counterthreat, either.
And the stakes are pretty high when it comes to the relationship with China, because, of course, the United States is in a very fragile truce, if you could still call it that, on the trade war. So, any excessive pressure on China, I think, is going to be very likely to reopen that. And there’s already been a tit-for-tat spate of measures in the last few weeks dealing with tariffs about overcapacity, restrictions on drone exports and imports, that suggests that this U.S.-China trade truce might be unraveling. And I think this Iran sanctions episode is really likely to further unravel that if the U.S. goes through with secondary sanctions enforcement.
And, Professor Mulder, about this issue of potential sanctions on large financial institutions, most people are not aware that about four of the 10 largest banks in the world are headquartered — are Chinese banks headquartered in China. If you include
, which is in Hong Kong, it’s half of the largest financial institutions of the world have direct ties with China. So, what would be the impact of any attempt to sanction, for instance, a major Chinese bank or institution?
So, initially, it would depend on what kind of sanctions are placed on that bank, whether this is blocking them from participation in dollar markets or whether it’s done through a full blocking order. There’s a different range of sanctions that the U.S. could take. The impact for the Chinese would be that they would have difficulty immediately accessing the U.S. financial system, but that cuts both ways. They have a lot of reserves saved up. And it would almost automatically also have a major effect on Asian financial markets. These Chinese banks hold large amounts of reserves in Hong Kong, but also in Singapore and other markets, and that will cause liquidity issues there. So, I think that this is something that can’t really be sized up that quickly.
Like you mentioned, the the largest bank, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China,, it’s the the single largest financial institution by assets, and so we’re dealing really with hundreds of billions of dollars in assets. I very much doubt that the American government, at this particular moment, would choose to put sanctions on China’s largest bank, given that the Chinese have also shown that they will immediately retaliate with rare earth export controls. They could retaliate by taking measures against all kinds of U.S. foreign investments in China. There is still, of course, a significant degree of American capital in China. So, they could counter-freeze, and that could very quickly escalate.
And at this moment, of course, we should sketch the broader picture here, which is that the United States has entered a period where its own sovereign debt, the Treasury market, is no longer as stable as it once was. The rates are very high. And Bessent has spent the last two weeks desperately trying to talk down the Treasury yields, trying to make sure that American government debt remains an attractive asset class to invest in. But bigger question marks have really emerged over that.
So, if he puts really aggressive sanctions on Iran, it will very quickly tend to backfire against American economic conditions. And there’s two ways. One of them could be through the China channel. The other one could be by further removing oil from global markets. If there is a significant oil importer — say, India — that is immediately and quickly cut off by American secondary sanctions, then what you might see is an immediate pass-through into U.S. inflation, expectations that interest rates are going to go up. We’re coming up against the Federal Reserve meeting soon, in the coming week, and an announcement by Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole symposium about interest rates, and that is certain to feed into the Treasury market immediately, and that would be exactly the opposite of what Bessent is trying to achieve.
So, I see that announcement of him yesterday and the way that he handled the questions as of a piece with his broader attempt to talk the bond market into submission, or at least a kind of quietude, to try and get the bond vigilantes off the back of the American Treasury. The issue is, of course, here that, you know, the bond market, as well as other countries, get a vote, as well, and the space for maneuver that the U.S. has in using these tools of very coercive economic statecraft has narrowed.
And I’m wondering also, the issue of the United Arab Emirates. Just before Bessent’s announcement, the
announced that it was ending trade relations with Iran. Can you talk about the significance of this? And in fact, while all these hostilities have been going on, trade across the Persian Gulf between the
and Iran has continued for all of these months.
Yes, so, the
has always been an important trading partner for Iran. There’s also a very large Iranian diasporic community there and people who move back and forth between Iran and the Emirates. And it has long been a hub for a lot of commercial companies, but that also includes the
, Iranian state companies, as well as private entities. So, that’s long been the case.
It’s also been the case that the Emirates, of course, was a major target of the initial Italian — sorry, Iranian retaliation against the American and Israeli attack after February. But then, in the last six to eight weeks, Iranian attacks on the Emirates really fell off dramatically, and there’s been quite plausible speculation that this was because there was an arrangement that was reached between the Emirates and the Iranian government, and a certain modicum of trade was reallowed in exchange, perhaps, also for Emirati payments or unfreezing of frozen Iranian assets there.
Now, if the Trump administration, as the Emiratis appear to signal, has now reimposed these sanctions, and the Emiratis at least want to suggest that they are complying, two things can be happening: Either they have reimposed this, these restrictions, in which case they would invite pretty prompt Iranian retaliation, or they’re trying to take action against a certain big headline set of commercial activities, while allowing, under the surface, some of it to continue.
I think one should not underestimate the fact that the Gulf countries have been forced in recent months to really recalibrate their relationships, both to the United States but also to China and to a number of other countries. And they realize that the United States is less able to protect them, that American actions against Iran expose them to retaliation, that that means both increased assertiveness on their own part militarily and geopolitically, but also developing their own relations with regional powers. And that includes, eventually, I think, some kind of
with Iran.
So, there’s definitely been, I think, a lot of signaling, but we cannot take the Emirati announcement completely at face value, either. The proof will have to be in analyzing commercial data and trade data in the months to come, and only in time can we tell if this is really what’s happening.
Nicholas Mulder, how is this playing out in Iran? I mean, yesterday, the Iranian rial dropped to a record low of nearly 2 million to the dollar. But Iranian government officials continue to dismiss the Trump administration sanctions announcement. Is there a disconnect between the political defiance we’re seeing from the Iranian government and the actual impact of the sanctions on the ground?
Well, the sanctions have definitely had an impact, and the U.S. naval blockade, to be more specific, more still, since the beginning of June. For ordinary Iranians, of course, this war, which did not spare them in the least, has been horrific. On top of that, there’s major reconstruction costs that are now very difficult to finance because of Iran’s relative isolation. And what exports had been getting out of Iran, in the form of oil and other exports, now have also dropped off. So, Iran is no longer as free to trade as it wants. There are a number of overland routes that have been activated with neighboring countries, but those have a much reduced volume in terms of what they can sustain.
And I do think you’re right to suggest that the Iranian government — certainly, the people that now seem to be having the most influence over decision-making, a number of
and military figures — believe that this economic blockade shows that the Americans are out of military options, and that actually they interpret this as a sign of American weakness. So, they’re not afraid to up the ante further and to threaten retaliation. And they seem also quite capable of carrying it out, if they so choose.
The question is: Whose negotiating position is going to strengthen further by that kind of escalation? Will time be on the side of the Trump administration, or is the Trump administration actually itself racing against the economic clock with, like I said, rising inflation in the U.S., a deteriorating bond market, midterms coming up? In Iran, the government seems determined to ride this out, even if it means that the population will continue to suffer further in the near term. So, yeah, that’s how I see the lay of the land as it stands right now.
Nicholas Mulder is an associate professor of history at Cornell University and a specialist in sanctions, is the author of
. Thank you so much for joining us.
Coming up, we look at how local officials in Illinois are collaborating with federal immigration agents despite a state law barring the practice. Stay with us.
[break]
“El Hielo/
,” by La Santa Cecilia in our
studio.

_source.movement_abstract: 特朗普政府宣布启动'经济孤立行动'，计划进一步收紧对伊朗的制裁，威胁切断与伊朗在石油、航运、加密货币、黄金及航空领域有业务往来的国家、企业及银行进入美国金融系统的渠道。美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特表示，相关国家需在限定时间内切断与伊朗联系，但未公布具体目标国及时间表。伊朗方面威胁将采取'地震式'报复，并将支持新制裁的国家视为敌人。制裁专家尼古拉斯·穆尔德分析指出，该公告缺乏具体执行细节，实质为'修辞性'和'心理战'手段，对伊朗政府实质性影响有限，主要伤害普通民众。然而，若美国对伊朗贸易伙伴实施二级制裁，将严重冲击中美贸易休战局面。中国作为伊朗最大贸易伙伴，进口其超80%石油，已明确表示不遵守美国制裁，并可能通过稀土出口管制等措施反制。穆尔德警告，针对中国大型金融机构的制裁可能引发亚洲金融市场流动性危机及通胀反弹，反噬美国经济。此外，阿联酋虽宣布终止与伊朗贸易，但实际执行情况存疑，海湾国家正重新调整与美、中及地区大国的关系。伊朗里亚尔兑美元汇率跌至近200万的历史低点，但伊朗政府视美国封锁为军事选项耗尽的软弱表现，意图通过升级对抗维持谈判地位。

So, if he puts really aggressive sanctions on Iran, it will very quickly tend to backfire against American economic conditions. And there’s two ways. One of them could be through the China channel. The other one could be by further removing oil from global markets. If there is a significant oil importer — say, India — that is immediately and quickly cut off by American secondary sanctions, then what you might see is an immediate pass-through into U.S. inflation, expectations that interest rates are going to go up. We’re coming up against the Federal Reserve meeting soon, in the coming week, and an announcement by Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole symposium about interest rates, and that is certain to feed into the Treasury market immediately, and that would be exactly the opposite of what Bessent is trying to achieve.
So, I see that announcement of him yesterday and the way that he handled the questions as of a piece with his broader attempt to talk the bond market into submission, or at least a kind of quietude, to try and get the bond vigilantes off the back of the American Treasury. The issue is, of course, here that, you know, the bond market, as well as other countries, get a vote, as well, and the space for maneuver that the U.S. has in using these tools of very coercive economic statecraft has narrowed.
And I’m wondering also, the issue of the United Arab Emirates. Just before Bessent’s announcement, the
announced that it was ending trade relations with Iran. Can you talk about the significance of this? And in fact, while all these hostilities have been going on, trade across the Persian Gulf between the
and Iran has continued for all of these months.
Yes, so, the
has always been an important trading partner for Iran. There’s also a very large Iranian diasporic community there and people who move back and forth between Iran and the Emirates. And it has long been a hub for a lot of commercial companies, but that also includes the
, Iranian state companies, as well as private entities. So, that’s long been the case.
It’s also been the case that the Emirates, of course, was a major target of the initial Italian — sorry, Iranian retaliation against the American and Israeli attack after February. But then, in the last six to eight weeks, Iranian attacks on the Emirates really fell off dramatically, and there’s been quite plausible speculation that this was because there was an arrangement that was reached between the Emirates and the Iranian government, and a certain modicum of trade was reallowed in exchange, perhaps, also for Emirati payments or unfreezing of frozen Iranian assets there.
Now, if the Trump administration, as the Emiratis appear to signal, has now reimposed these sanctions, and the Emiratis at least want to suggest that they are complying, two things can be happening: Either they have reimposed this, these restrictions, in which case they would invite pretty prompt Iranian retaliation, or they’re trying to take action against a certain big headline set of commercial activities, while allowing, under the surface, some of it to continue.
I think one should not underestimate the fact that the Gulf countries have been forced in recent months to really recalibrate their relationships, both to the United States but also to China and to a number of other countries. And they realize that the United States is less able to protect them, that American actions against Iran expose them to retaliation, that that means both increased assertiveness on their own part militarily and geopolitically, but also developing their own relations with regional powers. And that includes, eventually, I think, some kind of
with Iran.
So, there’s definitely been, I think, a lot of signaling, but we cannot take the Emirati announcement completely at face value, either. The proof will have to be in analyzing commercial data and trade data in the months to come, and only in time can we tell if this is really what’s happening.
Nicholas Mulder, how is this playing out in Iran? I mean, yesterday, the Iranian rial dropped to a record low of nearly 2 million to the dollar. But Iranian government officials continue to dismiss the Trump administration sanctions announcement. Is there a disconnect between the political defiance we’re seeing from the Iranian government and the actual impact of the sanctions on the ground?
Well, the sanctions have definitely had an impact, and the U.S. naval blockade, to be more specific, more still, since the beginning of June. For ordinary Iranians, of course, this war, which did not spare them in the least, has been horrific. On top of that, there’s major reconstruction costs that are now very difficult to finance because of Iran’s relative isolation. And what exports had been getting out of Iran, in the form of oil and other exports, now have also dropped off. So, Iran is no longer as free to trade as it wants. There are a number of overland routes that have been activated with neighboring countries, but those have a much reduced volume in terms of what they can sustain.
And I do think you’re right to suggest that the Iranian government — certainly, the people that now seem to be having the most influence over decision-making, a number of
and military figures — believe that this economic blockade shows that the Americans are out of military options, and that actually they interpret this as a sign of American weakness. So, they’re not afraid to up the ante further and to threaten retaliation. And they seem also quite capable of carrying it out, if they so choose.
The question is: Whose negotiating position is going to strengthen further by that kind of escalation? Will time be on the side of the Trump administration, or is the Trump administration actually itself racing against the economic clock with, like I said, rising inflation in the U.S., a deteriorating bond market, midterms coming up? In Iran, the government seems determined to ride this out, even if it means that the population will continue to suffer further in the near term. So, yeah, that’s how I see the lay of the land as it stands right now.
Nicholas Mulder is an associate professor of history at Cornell University and a specialist in sanctions, is the author of
. Thank you so much for joining us.
Coming up, we look at how local officials in Illinois are collaborating with federal immigration agents despite a state law barring the practice. Stay with us.

特朗普政府宣布了进一步加强对伊朗制裁的计划，但没有具体说明，在此过程中威胁到包括中国在内的其他国家。我们与制裁专家尼古拉斯·穆德（Nicholas Mulder）谈到了他所谓的声明中的“修辞”和“心理战”。穆德说，对伊朗来说，这一声明实际上并没有那么大的意义。在某种程度上，他们伤害了普通伊朗人，而不是政府。然而，这对美中关系的影响可能要大得多。穆德警告说，如果美国真的对伊朗的贸易伙伴实施次级制裁，“美中贸易休战可能会瓦解”。“美国在使用这些极具强制性的经济治国工具方面的回旋余地已经缩小。”
特朗普政府概述了加强对伊朗制裁的计划，并警告说，如果企业、银行和其他国家继续与德黑兰做生意，他们可能会失去进入美国金融系统的机会。周一，财政部长斯科特·贝森特（Scott Bessent）宣布了“经济弃儿行动”（Operation Economic Outcast），其中包括对伊朗石油、航运、加密货币、黄金和航空业相关贸易的二级制裁。贝森特说，各国与伊朗断绝关系有一个明确的时间表，但没有提供有关哪些国家将成为目标或何时成为目标的细节。
财政部长斯科特·贝森特结束讲话后，回答了记者的提问。
伊朗威胁要以“地震般”的方式对美国进行报复。伊朗官员表示，任何支持美国新经济限制措施的国家都将被视为敌人。这是伊朗经济部长阿里·马达尼扎德。
为了更多地讨论美国对伊朗的经济战争，我们现在请来了尼古拉斯·穆德。他是康奈尔大学的历史学副教授，也是制裁方面的专家。他是的作者
.
尼古拉斯·穆德欢迎来到。
你对昨天的公告有何回应？没有太多关于执行的细节。这对中国意味着什么？中国是伊朗最大的经济贸易伙伴，购买了伊朗80%以上的石油，特朗普总统将于下月与中国总理会面。
是啊。谢谢你邀请我。
我认为，这一声明确实表明，美国正在试图增加对伊朗的压力，但目前主要是通过修辞手段和一种心理战来这样做。当然，自6月以来，伊朗一直处于美国的海上封锁之下。伊朗经济正感受到这种压力。正如你所提到的，昨天的公告在细节上非常简短。有迹象表明，一家主要的全球金融机构可能很快就会受到制裁，但这一点也非常模糊。这可能是对中国的一种含蓄的威胁。这可能是一种围绕这些交易制造寒蝉效应的普遍企图。
现实情况是，在这一点上，美国可以采取的直接影响伊朗的制裁相对较少。在宣布和财政部的指定中有一些内容，比如禁止所有剩余的汇款到伊朗，禁止剩余的学术和体育交流。但这些似乎只是试图表明这是企图进一步孤立伊朗的毫无理由的方式。它们在物质上并不是那么有意义。在某种程度上，他们伤害了普通伊朗人，而不是政府。
美国试图实施这些制裁的真正方式是对与伊朗进行贸易的第三国施加压力，我认为这将是一个悬而未决的问题，这些制裁是否会像贝森特希望的那样有力。正如你已经提到的，最大的贸易伙伴是中国，但我们也在谈论巴基斯坦、土耳其、印度和其他一些与伊朗进行大量贸易的国家，你知道，这些国家认为他们完全有权这样做，归根结底，这些只是美国的制裁——它们不是国际法律措施。这些国家声称，并为他们自己，有主权-作出主权决定，谁可以与他们进行贸易，谁不能。中国人已经宣布，他们不仅会忽视它们，甚至会确保中国境内的国家和公司不会遵守它们。最近，中国法院也开始对遵守美国制裁的公司实施制裁。所以，我认为这也不再是一个空洞的反威胁。
当涉及到与中国的关系时，风险是相当高的，因为，当然，美国在贸易战上处于非常脆弱的休战状态，如果你还可以这么说的话。因此，我认为，对中国的任何过度压力都很可能会重新开启这一进程。在过去的几周里，已经有一系列针锋相对的措施来处理产能过剩的关税，限制无人机的出口和进口，这表明美中贸易休战可能正在瓦解。我认为，如果美国实施二级制裁，伊朗制裁事件很可能会进一步破坏这一点。
穆德教授，关于对大型金融机构的潜在制裁问题，大多数人都不知道，世界上最大的10家银行中有4家是总部设在中国的中国银行。如果你包括
在香港，世界上最大的金融机构中有一半与中国有直接联系。那么，如果试图制裁中国的一家大型银行或机构，会产生什么影响呢？
因此，最初，这将取决于对该银行实施何种制裁，是阻止他们参与美元市场，还是通过全面封锁令来完成。美国可以采取不同的制裁措施。对中国人的影响是，他们将难以立即进入美国金融体系，但这是双向的。他们存了很多储备金。它几乎会自动地对亚洲金融市场产生重大影响。这些中资银行在香港、新加坡和其他市场持有大量储备，这将导致那里的流动性问题。所以，我认为这是一件不能那么快评估的事情。
就像你提到的，最大的银行，中国工商银行，它是资产最大的单一金融机构，所以我们正在处理数千亿美元的资产。我非常怀疑美国政府，在这个特殊的时刻，会选择对中国最大的银行实施制裁，因为中国也已经表明，他们将立即以稀土出口管制进行报复。他们可以通过对美国在中国的各种外国投资采取措施进行报复。当然，美国资本在中国仍有很大的份额。所以，他们可以反冻结，这可能会很快升级。
当然，此时此刻，我们应该勾勒出更广阔的图景，那就是美国已经进入了一个其主权债务——国债市场——不再像以前那样稳定的时期。利率非常高。过去两周，贝森特一直在拼命压低美国国债收益率，试图确保美国政府债券仍然是一个有吸引力的投资资产类别。但更大的问号确实出现了。
因此，如果他对伊朗实施非常严厉的制裁，很快就会对美国的经济状况产生反作用。有两种方法。其中一个可能是通过中国渠道。另一种可能是进一步将石油从全球市场上移除。如果有一个重要的石油进口国——比如印度——立即被美国的二级制裁迅速切断，那么你可能会看到美国的通货膨胀立即传递，预期利率将会上升。在接下来的一周里，我们即将迎来美联储会议，以及凯文·沃什（Kevin Warsh）在杰克逊霍尔研讨会（Jackson Hole Symposium）上关于利率的声明，这肯定会立即影响到美国国债市场，而这将与贝森特（Bessent）试图实现的目标完全相反。
所以，我认为他昨天的声明和他处理问题的方式与他试图说服债券市场屈服的更广泛的尝试是一致的，或者至少是一种平静，试图让债券义警摆脱美国财政部的支持。当然，这里的问题是，你知道，债券市场，以及其他国家，也有投票权，美国在使用这些非常强制性的经济治国工具方面的回旋空间已经缩小。
我也想知道，阿拉伯联合酋长国的问题。就在贝森特发表声明之前，
宣布结束与伊朗的贸易关系。你能谈谈这件事的意义吗？事实上，当所有这些敌对行动一直在进行时，波斯湾两岸的贸易
伊朗在这几个月里一直在继续。
是的，所以，那个
一直是伊朗重要的贸易伙伴。那里还有一个非常大的伊朗散居社区，人们在伊朗和阿联酋之间来回流动。长期以来，它一直是许多商业公司的中心，但也包括
伊朗国营公司以及私营实体。所以，这种情况一直存在。
当然，阿联酋也是意大利最初的主要目标——对不起，伊朗在2月后对美国和以色列的袭击进行报复。但是，在过去的六到八周里，伊朗对阿联酋的袭击确实急剧减少，有相当可信的猜测认为，这是因为阿联酋和伊朗政府之间达成了一项安排，并重新进行了少量的贸易，以换取阿联酋的付款或解冻被冻结的伊朗资产。
现在，如果特朗普政府，就像阿联酋所暗示的那样，现在重新实施这些制裁，并且阿联酋至少想要表明他们正在遵守，那么可能会发生两件事：要么他们重新实施这些限制，在这种情况下，他们会招致伊朗相当迅速的报复，要么他们试图对某一系列重大商业活动采取行动，同时在表面之下，其中一些要继续。
我认为，人们不应低估这样一个事实，即近几个月来，海湾国家被迫重新调整与美国、中国和其他一些国家的关系。他们意识到美国保护他们的能力下降，美国对伊朗的行动使他们面临报复，这意味着他们在军事和地缘政治上更加自信，同时也发展自己与地区大国的关系。这包括，最终，我认为，某种
与伊朗。
所以，我认为，肯定有很多信号，但我们也不能完全相信阿联酋的声明。证据必须在未来几个月的商业数据和贸易数据中进行分析，只有时间才能告诉我们这是否是真正发生的事情。
尼古拉斯·穆德，这事在伊朗进展如何？我的意思是，昨天，伊朗里亚尔跌至近200万美元兑1美元的历史低点。但伊朗政府官员继续驳斥特朗普政府的制裁声明。我们从伊朗政府那里看到的政治挑衅与制裁的实际影响之间是否存在脱节？
嗯，制裁确实产生了影响，美国的海上封锁，更具体地说，更具体地说，自6月初以来。当然，对于普通伊朗人来说，这场丝毫没有放过他们的战争是可怕的。最重要的是，由于伊朗的相对孤立，主要的重建费用现在很难筹措。以石油和其他出口形式从伊朗获得的出口现在也减少了。因此，伊朗不再像它希望的那样自由贸易。有一些与邻国之间的陆路通道已经启用，但就其所能维持的流量而言，这些通道的流量大大减少。
我确实认为你的建议是正确的，伊朗政府——当然，现在似乎对决策有最大影响力的人，
军方人士认为，这种经济封锁表明美国人没有军事选择，实际上他们认为这是美国软弱的表现。所以，他们并不害怕进一步提高赌注和威胁报复。如果他们愿意的话，他们似乎也很有能力执行。
问题是：这种升级会进一步加强谁的谈判地位？时间会站在特朗普政府一边，还是特朗普政府本身就在与经济时钟赛跑，就像我说的，美国通胀上升，债券市场恶化，中期选举即将到来？在伊朗，政府似乎决心渡过这一难关，即使这意味着民众在短期内将继续遭受进一步的痛苦。所以，是的，这就是我对目前形势的看法。
尼古拉斯·穆德（Nicholas Mulder）是康奈尔大学（Cornell University）的历史学副教授，也是制裁方面的专家。
.非常感谢你加入我们。
接下来，我们来看看伊利诺伊州的地方官员是如何与联邦移民机构合作的，尽管该州法律禁止这种做法。和我们呆在一起。
[休息]
埃尔希埃洛/
，由La Santa Cecilia在我们的
工作室。

Kashmiri Pandit employees working in the Valley have sought immediate security measures from the Jammu and Kashmir administration after a fresh threat poster circulated on social media allegedly under the banner of a shadow outfit calling itself the United Liberation Council (ULC).
The All PM Package Employees Forum Kashmir has submitted a representation to the Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir, seeking urgent security enhancements for migrant Kashmiri Pandit employees amid a growing cyber threat environment.
The representation refers to a poster dated August 23, 2026, which, unlike generic threat messages, allegedly contains sensitive personal information of individual employees. The details reportedly include full names, residential addresses and vehicle registration numbers, raising concerns over how such information may have been obtained and circulated.
Security agencies are yet to establish the authenticity and provenance of the document. However, the forum has argued that the appearance of targeted lists itself has created considerable anxiety among employees and their families.
The concerns are particularly acute among Kashmiri Pandit employees because of the community’s history of targeted attacks in the Valley. Previous killings of minority employees and civilians have left many families apprehensive about threats that identify individuals by name or location.
The forum has called for an immediate investigation into the origin of the poster and a comprehensive review of security arrangements at places of posting, residential quarters and along daily transit routes. It has also sought targeted security cover and clearly defined safety protocols for employees whose addresses, vehicle details or other personal records have appeared in the alleged threat material.
According to top Indian intelligence sources, agencies are examining the ULC’s emergence and its possible links to established Pakistan-backed terror networks, including Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT). Intelligence assessments suggest that such shadow outfits can be used to issue threats and conduct psychological operations while providing established terror handlers with a layer of deniability.
Investigators are also examining whether any local administrative databases or other sources of personal information may have been compromised or accessed to obtain precise residential addresses, vehicle details and other identifying information.
Security officials are increasingly viewing such digital campaigns as a form of low-cost psychological warfare. Beyond threatening individuals, the objective could be to generate fear among minority employees, disrupt government rehabilitation and employment initiatives, and pressure vulnerable groups into withdrawing from postings in the Valley.
For Kashmiri Pandit employees, the latest episode has therefore revived an old fear in a new form: threats that travel through social media but can have very real consequences on the ground.

_source.movement_abstract: 【印度情报部门8月25日报道】2026年8月23日，印控克什米尔地区出现一张疑似由名为‘联合解放委员会’（ULC）的地下组织发布的威胁海报，导致当地工作的克什米尔教派（Kashmiri Pandit）员工面临安全危机。该海报包含多名员工的姓名、家庭住址及车辆注册号码等敏感个人信息。‘全PM包员工论坛克什米尔分会’已向查谟和克什米尔首席秘书提交请愿书，要求立即加强安保措施。安全机构正在核实文件真实性，并调查信息泄露源头，怀疑当地行政数据库可能遭入侵。印度情报部门评估认为，ULC可能与巴基斯坦支持的‘虔诚军’（LeT）等恐怖网络存在关联，此类组织常被用于实施心理战以制造恐慌。安全官员指出，此类低成本数字行动旨在恐吓少数族裔员工，破坏政府安置计划，迫使相关人员撤离。鉴于该社区历史上曾遭受针对性袭击，此次事件引发强烈焦虑，论坛呼吁对受威胁员工实施针对性安保覆盖并审查通勤路线安全。

_source.trans_cont:
在山谷中工作的克什米尔潘迪特员工要求查谟和克什米尔政府立即采取安全措施，此前社交媒体上流传着一张新的威胁海报，据称是打着一个自称联合解放委员会（ULC）的影子组织的旗号。
克什米尔所有总理一揽子雇员论坛已向查谟和克什米尔首席秘书提交了一份陈述，寻求在日益增长的网络威胁环境中为克什米尔潘迪特移民雇员加强紧急安全措施。
该陈述提到了一张日期为2026年8月23日的海报，与一般的威胁信息不同，该海报据称包含个别员工的敏感个人信息。据报道，这些细节包括全名、居住地址和车辆登记号码，这引起了人们对这些信息可能是如何获得和传播的担忧。
安全机构尚未确定该文件的真实性和出处。然而，该论坛认为，目标名单的出现本身就在员工及其家人中造成了相当大的焦虑。
克什米尔潘迪特员工的担忧尤为严重，因为该社区曾在山谷中发生过有针对性的袭击事件。以前对少数族裔雇员和平民的杀害使许多家庭对通过姓名或地点识别个人的威胁感到担忧。
论坛呼吁立即调查海报的来源，并全面检讨张贴地点、住宅区和日常交通路线的保安安排。它还为其地址、车辆详细信息或其他个人记录出现在所谓的威胁材料中的雇员寻求有针对性的安全保护和明确界定的安全协议。
据印度高级情报来源称，各机构正在调查ULC的出现及其与巴基斯坦支持的恐怖网络的可能联系，包括虔诚军（LET）。情报评估表明，这种影子部队可以用来发出威胁和进行心理战，同时为已有的恐怖分子提供一层可否认性。
调查人员还在检查是否有任何地方行政数据库或其他个人信息来源可能已被泄露或访问，以获取准确的居住地址、车辆详细信息和其他身份信息。
安全官员越来越多地将这种数字活动视为一种低成本的心理战。除了威胁个人外，其目的还可能是在少数族裔雇员中制造恐惧，破坏政府的恢复和就业举措，并迫使弱势群体从山谷的岗位上退出。
因此，对于克什米尔潘迪特的员工来说，最新的事件以一种新的形式重新唤起了一种旧的恐惧：通过社交媒体传播的威胁，但可能在当地产生非常真实的后果。

Security and intelligence agencies in Jammu and Kashmir have raised alarms over a renewed wave of intimidation directed at minority Kashmiri Hindu families and government employees living in the region.
The emergence of purported online threat letters and notices—which explicitly publish sensitive personal data, residential addresses, and contact numbers—has been classified by security experts as a calculated tactic of psychological warfare.
The circulation of these circulars, reportedly attributed to shadow groups and fringe outfits operating in the Valley, marks an escalation from generic threats to targeted intimidation.
By singling out specific individuals and government personnel, the campaign seeks to exploit personal vulnerabilities and foster an atmosphere of panic.
Intelligence assessments indicate that the primary objective of publishing such details is not merely physical confrontation, but psychological destabilization—aiming to resurrect deep-seated anxieties and fracture the fragile sense of normalcy among minority communities.
In response to the growing unease, community forums and employee associations have urgently appealed to the administration for heightened safety protocols and comprehensive threat evaluations.
Law enforcement and administrative bodies have initiated rigorous digital audits to track the origin of these notices, verify their authenticity, and assess potential data leaks.
Security grids across sensitive districts have been reinforced, with authorities emphasizing a zero-tolerance approach toward elements attempting to disrupt communal harmony and terrorize civilians through digital propaganda.
_source.movement_title: 印控克什米尔安全机构警示针对少数族裔的数字化恐吓升级
_source.movement_abstract: 印控查谟和克什米尔地区安全与情报机构发出警报，指出针对当地少数族裔克什米尔印度教家庭及政府雇员的恐吓活动出现新一轮升级。安全专家将此类行为定性为精心策划的心理战战术，其核心特征是发布包含敏感个人数据、家庭住址及联系方式的在线威胁信件。情报评估显示，这些通告据称由山谷地区活动的影子团体及边缘组织发布，标志着威胁手段从泛化恐吓转向针对特定个人的精准施压。该行动旨在利用个人脆弱性制造恐慌氛围，其首要目标并非直接引发肢体冲突，而是通过心理 destabilization 手段重燃少数族裔深层焦虑，破坏当地脆弱的正常生活秩序。面对日益加剧的不安情绪，社区论坛及员工协会已紧急呼吁行政当局加强安全协议并开展全面威胁评估。执法与行政机构随即启动严格的数字审计程序，以追踪通告源头、核实真实性并评估潜在数据泄露风险。当局已在敏感地区强化安全网格部署，并强调对试图通过数字宣传破坏社区和谐、恐吓平民的行为采取零容忍态度。

_source.content:
Republican or Democrat, I don't necessarily like writing about politicians' kids, especially those who don't choose to put themselves out there. As we all know, 20-year-old Barron Trump lives a fairly private life, especially compared to his parents and siblings.
But the Iranian regime is not so kind. As a matter of fact, what it did recently is some of the worst propaganda I've seen in a while.
From what I understand, Iranian state TV (Channel 3) played a three-minute video called "Where to kill Barron Trump." That alone should give you an idea of just how gruesome it was. And as if that wasn't bad enough, it also allegedly offered a $10 million reward for his death. I don't think that's confirmed in the video, but it's being widely reported. I should also note that the original video did not appear anywhere online in an official capacity, so we're stuck with what's being passed around on social media.
I saw some of the AI-generated video on anti-regime London-based journalist Niyak Ghorbani's X account, and it has English subtitles, so I'm going by those since I do not speak the language. But it starts out claiming that a girl was able to get past the Secret Service protocols and have a private meeting with Barron, and she apparently handed the regime or whoever made the video the information about his day-to-day life.
It then goes on to explain where and how Barron spends his days in New York and Washington, D.C., both at home and at school, as well as how he gets around in a convoy of Secret Service vehicles. It even talks about the classes he takes, how his "bodyguards" are always around and he's never alone, and how those Secret Service members ditch their suits and dress casually like students to blend in with his classmates. It also shows some NYU dorm rooms.
But then it claims there's a loophole in Barron's, whom the video calls "reclusive," online presence. It says he does not give out his phone number to friends, but that the regime has uncovered some of his other personal accounts that aren't so secure, such as his Xbox, FIFA video games, and Discord, as well as the accounts for some of his friends.
It also mentions that his friends have low-security digital footprints and posts what appears to be screenshots of their profiles. It even names at least one of them. At some point, it apparently says, "This is just the beginning! Barron Trump, wait for us!"
I debated whether or not to embed the video here, and I ultimately decided against it. Our managing editor Chris Queen suggested I link it for those who want to see it, and while it's not graphic, I will say that it's very disturbing, or, at least, it was to me.
— it's easy to find on X as well if you're curious.
Of course, this isn't the first time the Trump family has dealt with such threats from the regime. The president himself has been the target of several, as has the first lady, and some of Donald Trump's other children. There was even a "Where to Kill Melania" video circulating last month.
"The U.S. Secret Service is aware of the video and investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees," a spokesperson for the Secret Service
. "Out of concern for operational security, we do not discuss matters of protective intelligence."
Experts say this is simply psychological warfare or propaganda, and there is likely no real immediate threat to Barron's life, although I have to say: I can be a little hot-headed at times, but if I had the power and this was my kid, I'd just have to finish them.
_source.movement_title: 伊朗国家电视台发布针对特朗普之子的威胁视频
_source.movement_abstract: 伊朗国家电视台第三频道播放一段名为'在哪里杀死巴伦·特朗普'的三分钟视频，内容涉及对美国总统唐纳德·特朗普之子巴伦·特朗普的暗杀威胁。视频声称一名女子突破特勤局安保协议，获取了巴伦在纽约和华盛顿特区的日常生活、学校课程及出行路线等详细信息，并指出其特勤局特工伪装成学生混入校园。视频进一步声称发现巴伦在Xbox、FIFA游戏及Discord等数字平台存在安全漏洞，并展示其部分朋友的低安全数字足迹截图，甚至点名至少一名朋友。视频结尾宣称'这只是开始'，并暗示将实施行动。另有报道指该视频可能提供1000万美元悬赏，但尚未得到官方证实。美国特勤局发言人确认已注意到该视频，并表示正在调查任何可能构成威胁的情报，但出于行动安全考虑不讨论具体细节。专家分析认为此举属于心理战或宣传手段，目前暂无证据表明存在直接现实威胁。此前，特朗普家族其他成员也曾遭遇类似威胁视频。

I should also note that the original video did not appear anywhere online in an official capacity, so we're stuck with what's being passed around on social media.
I saw some of the AI-generated video on anti-regime London-based journalist Niyak Ghorbani's X account, and it has English subtitles, so I'm going by those since I do not speak the language. But it starts out claiming that a girl was able to get past the Secret Service protocols and have a private meeting with Barron, and she apparently handed the regime or whoever made the video the information about his day-to-day life.
It then goes on to explain where and how Barron spends his days in New York and Washington, D.C., both at home and at school, as well as how he gets around in a convoy of Secret Service vehicles. It even talks about the classes he takes, how his "bodyguards" are always around and he's never alone, and how those Secret Service members ditch their suits and dress casually like students to blend in with his classmates. It also shows some NYU dorm rooms.
But then it claims there's a loophole in Barron's, whom the video calls "reclusive," online presence. It says he does not give out his phone number to friends, but that the regime has uncovered some of his other personal accounts that aren't so secure, such as his Xbox, FIFA video games, and Discord, as well as the accounts for some of his friends.
It also mentions that his friends have low-security digital footprints and posts what appears to be screenshots of their profiles. It even names at least one of them. At some point, it apparently says, "This is just the beginning! Barron Trump, wait for us!"
I debated whether or not to embed the video here, and I ultimately decided against it. Our managing editor Chris Queen suggested I link it for those who want to see it, and while it's not graphic, I will say that it's very disturbing, or, at least, it was to me.
— it's easy to find on X as well if you're curious.
Of course, this isn't the first time the Trump family has dealt with such threats from the regime. The president himself has been the target of several, as has the first lady, and some of Donald Trump's other children. There was even a "Where to Kill Melania" video circulating last month.
"The U.S. Secret Service is aware of the video and investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees," a spokesperson for the Secret Service
. "Out of concern for operational security, we do not discuss matters of protective intelligence."
Experts say this is simply psychological warfare or propaganda, and there is likely no real immediate threat to Barron's life, although I have to say: I can be a little hot-headed at times, but if I had the power and this was my kid, I'd just have to finish them.", "url": "https://pjmedia.com/sarah-anderson/2026/08/24/what-the-iranian-regime-did-to-barron-trump-will-make-your-blood-boil-n4956509", "source": null, "publish_time": 1787652378000, "update_time": 1787654581402, "gather_time": 1787654581402, "insert_time": 1787654581402, "picture_urls": ["https://media.townhall.com/cdn/hodl/2024/311/79fc7a25-315b-431b-bdfd-f5d4cb51071f.jpg"], "video_urls": null, "audio_urls": null, "file_urls": null, "picture_paths": null, "video_paths": null, "audio_paths": null, "file_paths": null, "site_id": "bfff154f86499943be9f3e65798b5d53", "site_name": "美国PJ媒体", "site_region": "美国", "board_id": null, "board_name": "news and politics", "source_tasks": ["002@091@20250515@10000001@1867"], "project_id": "", "task_id": "", "target_id": ""}

不管是共和党还是民主党，我都不一定喜欢写政客的孩子，尤其是那些不愿意站出来的人。众所周知，20岁的巴伦·特朗普过着相当私密的生活，尤其是与他的父母和兄弟姐妹相比。
但伊朗政权就没那么仁慈了。事实上，它最近所做的是一段时间以来我所见过的最糟糕的宣传。
据我所知，伊朗国家电视台（第三频道）播放了一段三分钟的视频，名为“在哪里杀死巴伦·特朗普”。光这一点就能让你知道它有多可怕。似乎这还不够糟糕，据称它还为他的死亡提供了1000万美元的赏金。我不认为这在视频中得到了证实，但它被广泛报道。我还应该注意到，原始视频并没有以官方身份出现在网上的任何地方，所以我们被困在了社交媒体上传播的内容中。
我在伦敦的反政府记者Niyak Ghorbani的X账户上看到了一些人工智能生成的视频，它有英文字幕，所以我用了这些，因为我不会说英语。但它一开始声称，一个女孩能够通过特勤局的协议，与巴伦进行私人会面，她显然向政权或制作视频的人提供了有关他日常生活的信息。
它接着解释了巴伦在纽约和华盛顿特区的时间和地点，包括家里和学校，以及他如何在特勤局车队中四处走动。它甚至谈到了他上的课，他的“保镖”总是在他身边，他从不孤单，以及那些特工人员如何脱下西装，像学生一样穿着随意，与他的同学打成一片。它还展示了一些纽约大学的宿舍。
但随后它声称《巴伦周刊》（Barron s）有一个漏洞，视频中称其为“隐士”。它说，他没有把自己的电话号码给朋友，但当局发现了他的其他一些不太安全的个人账户，如他的Xbox、FIFA视频游戏和Discord，以及他的一些朋友的账户。
它还提到，他的朋友们有低安全性的数字足迹，并发布了似乎是他们个人资料的截图。它甚至至少说出了其中一个名字。在某种程度上，它显然是说，这只是一个开始！巴伦·特朗普，等等我们！
我考虑过是否要在这里嵌入视频，但我最终决定不这么做。我们的主编克里斯·奎恩建议我为那些想看它的人链接它，虽然它不是图形，但我要说它非常令人不安，或者至少对我来说是这样。
-如果你好奇的话，在X上也很容易找到。
当然，这不是特朗普家族第一次应对来自政权的这种威胁。总统本人一直是几个人的目标，第一夫人和唐纳德·特朗普的其他一些孩子也是。上个月甚至流传着一段“在哪里杀死梅拉尼娅”的视频。
特勤局发言人说：“美国特勤局知道这段视频，并调查任何可能对我们的受保护者构成威胁的事情。”
.“出于对行动安全的考虑，我们不讨论保护情报的问题。”
专家表示，这只是一场心理战或宣传，可能不会对巴伦的生命构成真正的直接威胁，尽管我不得不说：我有时会有点头脑发热，但如果我有权力，而且这是我的孩子，我就必须完成他们。
_source.trans_title: 伊朗政权对巴伦·特朗普的所作所为会让你热血沸腾。

_source.movement_title: 台湾汉光演习强化军民整合动员应对中国威胁
_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾联合新闻网报道】台湾防务部门近期结束年度汉光演习，演习范围扩展至资安、能源、交通、电信等民间领域，实现军政民跨界整合。演习不仅验证军事作战能力，更侧重战时社会韧性及民间基础设施持续运作能力，标志着汉光演习向全民防卫转型。国际媒体如《纽约时报》关注台湾民防运动发展，报道数千名普通民众参与民防训练，学习急救、疏散及人质营救技能。受中国灰色地带战术及军事胁迫影响，台湾涌现三十多个民间志愿团体，其中黑熊学院通过军事科普、资讯作战、卫生救护及避难规划等课程，提升公众防卫意志。国防安全研究院调查显示，71.6%民众愿意接受民防训练，主要兴趣集中在避难求生及自我保护技能。赖清德成立全社会防卫韧性委员会，旨在推动全民自我防护能力。演习与民防建设凸显台湾社会在应对地缘政治风险时的挑战与准备，强调维持日常生活及自救互救是对前线及社会的重要支持。

TEHRAN — President Donald Trump has turned to psychological warfare and media fabrications in a desperate attempt to distract from the failure of the US military and economic war against Iran.
Such underhanded attempts became even more apparent after Trump reposted a link on Truth Social from the US conservative news outlet Newsmax, which grossly distorted comments made by Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf during his recent diplomatic trip to Iraq.
Newsmax sensationalized the story under the title "Iran Parliament Speaker: 'We Are Hungry, We Cannot Survive,'" attempting to cook up a false narrative of Iranian vulnerability by deliberately twisting Qalibaf’s words. Misquoting the Iranian Parliament speaker, the outlet wrote that no matter how strong military power becomes, if people are hungry, they will not be able to endure. Western outlets immediately spun the story to suggest that Iran is on the verge of collapse and that the US war against Iran, coupled with Washington’s unrelenting economic pressure, could bring down the Islamic Republic.
Nonetheless, a look at Qalibaf’s actual speech delivered in Persian tells a completely different story and sheds light on what was truly said. In a high-level meeting with Iraqi and Iranian economic activists, Qalibaf spoke strategically about the vital need for sovereign nations to maintain both military and economic strength. In this section of his address, the Parliament speaker stressed that alongside formidable military power, economic growth, robust domestic production, and dynamic financial activity are essential pillars to maintaining a country’s overall strength and national resilience. He emphasized that military power alone cannot guarantee a country’s long-term survival if the domestic economy is neglected. In fact, Qalibaf firmly believes that alongside continuously strengthening its defense capabilities, Iran must also bolster its economic foundation and overcome its internal financial challenges precisely to withstand hostile foreign economic pressure.
The media deception occurs against the backdrop of the aggressive US-Israeli war launched on February 28, a joint assault intended to cripple the Islamic Republic that ultimately backfired on its aggressors. When launching the operation, Trump openly declared an intent to force regime change, directly telling the Iranian population to take over their government. Yet, far from achieving its maximalist objectives or collapsing the government, the conflict resulted in the rapid depletion of the US military arsenal, exposing the logistical limits and strategic overreach of American hegemony.
Detailed technical assessments and reports from major American military outlets confirm that months of high-intensity operations have severely drained US weapons stocks—expending nearly two-thirds of its Patriot air defense interceptor inventory, roughly 40 percent of its THAAD interceptors, and a third of its Tomahawk cruise missile supply, while virtually exhausting its precision strike ballistic missiles like ATACMS and PrSM. American military analysts have been forced to admit that Washington simply lacks the industrial manufacturing pace to replenish these advanced systems, proving that claims of having completely wiped out Iranian military power are detached from reality. Iranian military officials have repeatedly dismissed these US proclamations, noting that Iran's defense apparatus remains fully operational, integrated, and capable of sustained deterrence.
Despite these clear tactical setbacks, Trump has continued to operate under extreme geopolitical delusions. Chief among them is his absurd, repeated assertion that the Strait of Hormuz—one of the world's most vital maritime choke points—is now sovereign American territory. Trump has publicly voiced this bizarre claim at least three times. He first floated the idea to a campaign crowd in Long Island, saying that after defeating Iran, he would declare the Strait a territory of the United States. He then doubled down during a press interaction at Joint Base Andrews, claiming the US possessed total control over the region and treated it as American ground. Shortly after, he amplified the delusion by sharing maps on Truth Social depicting the international waterway explicitly tagged as new US territory.
Iranian officials and regional observers were quick to point out the unhinged nature of these statements. Officials in Tehran noted that the vast distance between Washington's military capability and its land-grab fantasies exposes the White House's complete detachment from realities on the ground. The Strait remains an international waterway bordered by sovereign nations, and no amount of Truth Social posts can grant Washington legal or physical ownership over foreign territorial waters.
Trump's unfulfilled claims extend directly to his cycle of military threats, which have repeatedly collapsed into abrupt strategic retreats. This recurring pattern has become so glaring that analysts, financial markets, and international media outlets now widely refer to it as the TACO pattern, an acronym for "Trump Always Chickens Out". Time and again, Trump has issued dramatic ultimatums—threatening to bomb Iranian power plants, target critical energy infrastructure on Kharg Island, or send the country back to the Stone Age if his demands were not met within tight deadlines. Yet every single time the deadline expired and Tehran refused to submit, Trump backed away, offering unilateral extensions, claiming a deal was near, or citing requests from foreign leaders to pause military action.
Having failed to secure a decisive victory on the battlefield, facing a depleted arsenal, and caught in a cycle of empty threats, Washington attempted to shift its focus back to financial strangulation. Trump orchestrated an "economic D-Day" plan against Iran—an aggressive economic warfare operation aimed at crushing the nation’s commercial lifelines and starving its people into submission.
Yet, as Iran’s steadfast endurance neutralizes these hostile measures, Trump’s declared "economic D-Day" has crumbled into another total failure, exposing the utter limits of American coercive leverage. Facing structural defeat on both the military and financial fronts, the White House has resorted to a classic plan to divide and rule—using media fabrications, psychological manipulations on Truth Social, and false narratives about figures like Qalibaf to sow division and disguise Washington's growing impotence on the global stage.
_source.movement_title: 特朗普政府炮制伊朗经济崩溃假象掩盖军事行动失败
_source.movement_abstract: 美国总统特朗普为掩盖对伊朗军事与经济战失败，利用社交媒体及保守派媒体Newsmax歪曲伊朗议长加利巴夫言论，炮制伊朗面临生存危机的虚假叙事。加利巴夫原意强调军事与经济双强对国家韧性的重要性，旨在应对外部压力。自2月28日美以联合军事行动以来，美军库存严重消耗，爱国者拦截弹消耗近三分之二，THAAD拦截弹消耗约40%，战斧巡航导弹消耗三分之一，精确打击弹道导弹几近耗尽，工业产能无法及时补充。特朗普多次宣称霍尔木兹海峡为美国领土，被伊朗及地区观察家驳斥。分析指出特朗普呈现“TACO”模式，即多次发出轰炸伊朗能源设施等最后通牒后均因未获屈服而退缩。其策划的“经济D日”封锁计划亦告失败。目前白宫转向心理战与媒体操纵，试图通过虚假信息掩盖战略无力。

德黑兰——唐纳德·特朗普总统已经转向心理战和媒体捏造，绝望地试图转移人们对美国对伊朗军事和经济战争失败的注意力。
在特朗普转发了美国保守派新闻媒体Newsmax在Truth Social上的一个链接后，这种秘密企图变得更加明显，该链接严重歪曲了伊朗议会议长穆罕默德·巴吉尔·卡利巴夫（Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf）在最近的伊拉克外交之旅中发表的评论。
Newsmax以“伊朗议会议长：'我们饿了，我们无法生存' ”为题对这篇报道进行了耸人听闻的报道，试图通过故意歪曲卡利巴夫的话来编造关于伊朗脆弱性的虚假叙述。该媒体错误地引用伊朗议会议长的话写道，无论军事力量变得多么强大，如果人民挨饿，他们将无法忍受。西方媒体立即编造了这个故事，暗示伊朗正处于崩溃的边缘，美国对伊朗的战争，加上华盛顿无情的经济压力，可能会拖垮这个伊斯兰共和国。
尽管如此，看一看卡利巴夫用波斯语发表的实际演讲，就会发现一个完全不同的故事，并揭示出他真正说了什么。在与伊拉克和伊朗经济活动人士举行的一次高级别会议上，卡利巴夫从战略角度谈到了主权国家保持军事和经济实力的迫切需要。在讲话的这一部分，议会议长强调，除了强大的军事力量，经济增长、强劲的国内生产和活跃的金融活动也是维持国家整体实力和国家复原力的重要支柱。他强调，如果忽视国内经济，仅靠军事力量不能保证一个国家的长期生存。事实上，卡利巴夫坚信，在不断加强国防能力的同时，伊朗还必须巩固其经济基础，克服内部金融挑战，以抵御敌对的外国经济压力。
媒体欺骗是在2月28日发动的美以侵略战争的背景下发生的，这场联合攻击旨在削弱伊斯兰共和国，但最终事与愿违。在发起行动时，特朗普公开宣布了迫使政权更迭的意图，直接告诉伊朗人民接管他们的政府。然而，这场冲突非但没有实现其最大目标或瓦解政府，反而导致美国军火库迅速枯竭，暴露了美国霸权的后勤限制和战略过度扩张。
详细的技术评估和来自美国主要军事媒体的报告证实，几个月的高强度行动已经严重消耗了美国的武器库存——消耗了近三分之二的爱国者防空拦截弹库存，大约40%的萨德拦截弹，以及三分之一的战斧巡航导弹供应，同时几乎耗尽了其精确打击弹道导弹，如ATACMS和PRSM.美国军事分析人士不得不承认，华盛顿只是缺乏工业制造速度来补充这些先进系统，这证明彻底消灭伊朗军事力量的说法与现实脱节。伊朗军方官员一再驳斥美国的这些声明，指出伊朗的国防机构仍在全面运作、整合并具有持续威慑能力。
尽管有这些明显的战术挫折，但特朗普继续在极端的地缘政治错觉下运作。其中最主要的是他荒谬地反复断言霍尔木兹海峡——世界上最重要的海上咽喉要道之一——现在是美国的主权领土。特朗普至少三次公开发表这种奇怪的言论。他首先向长岛的竞选人群提出了这一想法，称在击败伊朗后，他将宣布该海峡为美国领土。然后，他在安德鲁斯联合基地的一次媒体互动中加倍下注，声称美国对该地区拥有完全的控制权，并将其视为美国的领土。不久后，他通过在Truth Social上分享地图放大了这种错觉，这些地图将国际航道明确标记为新的美国领土。
伊朗官员和地区观察员很快指出了这些言论的疯狂本质。德黑兰的官员指出，华盛顿的军事能力与其攫取土地的幻想之间的巨大差距，暴露了白宫完全脱离了当地的现实。该海峡仍然是一条与主权国家接壤的国际航道，再多的真相和社会帖子也不能授予华盛顿对外国领海的法律或实际所有权。
特朗普未兑现的主张直接延伸到他的军事威胁循环，这些威胁一再陷入突然的战略撤退。这种反复出现的模式已经变得如此引人注目，以至于分析师、金融市场和国际媒体现在广泛将其称为墨西哥玉米卷模式，即“特朗普总是临阵脱逃”的首字母缩写。一次又一次，特朗普发出了戏剧性的最后通牒——威胁要轰炸伊朗的发电厂，瞄准哈格岛的关键能源基础设施，或者如果他的要求不能在紧迫的期限内得到满足，就把伊朗送回石器时代。然而，每当最后期限到期而德黑兰拒绝提交时，特朗普就会退缩，提出单方面延期，声称协议即将达成，或援引外国领导人暂停军事行动的要求。
由于未能在战场上取得决定性胜利，面对耗尽的武器库，并陷入空洞威胁的循环，华盛顿试图将其重点重新转移到金融扼杀上。特朗普精心策划了一项针对伊朗的“经济诺曼底登陆日”计划，这是一场激进的经济战行动，旨在摧毁国家的商业命脉，让人民忍饥挨饿。
然而，随着伊朗的坚忍不拔抵消了这些敌对措施，特朗普宣布的“经济诺曼底登陆日”又一次彻底失败，暴露了美国强制手段的绝对局限性。面对军事和金融方面的结构性失败，白宫采取了经典的分裂和统治计划——利用媒体捏造、对社会真相的心理操纵以及对卡利巴夫等人物的虚假叙述来制造分裂，掩盖华盛顿在全球舞台上日益增长的无能。
