_source.movement_title: 美国等41国发布联合声明关切太平洋导弹试射及区域安全
_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾中央社8月12日报道】美国、日本、韩国、马绍尔群岛、帕劳、菲律宾、澳大利亚、新西兰等41国于8月11日发布联合声明，关切近期太平洋地区导弹试射未遵循多数国家通行的标准通报及协调做法。声明指出，中国今年7月6日向太平洋试射潜射导弹时未提供充分且适当的事前通知，呼吁各国建立透明且常态化的事前通报机制，以降低误判及意外升高情势的风险。美国官员同日在日内瓦举行的裁军谈判会议上进一步表达关切。台湾外交部表示，欢迎并肯定国际社会共同发声表达对印太区域安全的关切，再次谴责中国罔顾区域稳定的各种威胁行径。外交部指出，中国持续大幅扩张军力，通过军事恫吓、经济胁迫、认知战及军机舰侵扰等灰色地带手法，企图片面改变台海及印太区域现状，对台湾及区域整体安全构成严峻挑战。外交部强调，维护台海及印太地区和平稳定已是国际社会共识，台湾将作为国际社会负责任的一员，持续与美国及理念相近伙伴紧密合作，共同维护台海及印太地区的和平、稳定与繁荣。

《經濟學人》近日刊登「挾持台灣民主」（Taking Taiwan’s democracy hostage）專文，批評台灣政治人物只顧私利，讓國家變得越來越難以治理，中國成為唯一贏家。文中痛斥反對黨引發一連串憲政危機，包含凍結對美軍購預算、阻擋大法官人事案，甚至阻擋以無人機訂單扶植本土產業的計畫，民主自由原本是台灣的防衛優勢，卻可恥地遭到內部背叛。文章指出，外界研究台海區域情勢時，通常關注中國入侵或封鎖的風險，以及美國介入後兩個核武強權開戰的風險。但另一種情境也值得關注，如果台灣被誘使「不戰而降」，這雖是中國最想看到的情況，但中國國家主席習近平將面臨一連串艱難的抉擇，北京可能必須以殘酷手段鎮壓台灣的自由，全世界都在看。請繼續往下閱讀...
文中提到，台灣的民主不只是蔣介石獨裁體制的改進，本身也是一種威懾力量，台灣迫切需要更多讓中國國家主席習近平忌憚的籌碼，民進黨試圖推動延宕已久的軍事現代化，傳統的保護者美國則是不可靠的朋友，美國總統川普雖同意對台軍售，卻對外嘲笑台灣在中國面前微不足道，5月川習會後還呼應中方論述，稱賴清德是可能引發戰爭的莽撞之人。該文批評，只顧自身利益的台灣政治人物非但沒有珍惜台灣的民主，反而正在摧毀民主。2024年大選後，民進黨掌握總統職位及行政部門，以國民黨為首的反對黨則控制立法院，黨派內鬥自此讓政府運作陷入癱瘓。該文痛斥，許多國家都有惡劣的政治人物，台灣政治人物的不負責任尤其突出，賴清德總統態度固執，不像前總統蔡英文一樣與國民黨溫和派磋商；但反對黨引發了一連串憲政危機，國民黨立委及盟友凍結政府預算數月，包括對美軍購經費，同時阻擋司法院大法官人事任命。文章提到，反對黨還採取一項劇烈的自毀行動，阻擋以21萬架空海無人機訂單扶植本土產業的計畫。國民黨高層曾告訴作者「噢，我們支持製造無人機，這是政治問題。」一名黨內大老更直言，國民黨立委擔心政府會把無人機資金流向捐款給民進黨的企業；被問到親國民黨企業是否可以製造無人機時，這名大老說：「親國民黨的企業通常在中國有投資，因此不敢投入生產」，而國民黨寧願不去正視這個兩難境地。該文提到，國民黨主席鄭麗文宣稱台灣不能依賴美國，因此需要加強對中關係，4月與習近平會晤時，也引發民進黨不滿，鄭宣稱自己的目標是避免戰爭、不是賣台，但民進黨人士指控，國民黨內某些人實際上充當中國的「代理人」。該文認為，毫無疑問，台灣是中國認知作戰的目標，這些手段是否奏效仍未知，但台灣年輕一代對政治越來越失望，投票意願也在降低，同時不斷接觸中國資助、嘲弄台灣民主一片混亂的社群媒體內容。該文強調，從獨裁走向開放社會的歷程，改變了台灣的國際地位，但政治失能正在傷害台灣，外界不可能比台灣的政治人物更珍視台灣民主。台灣的自由本應是一種優勢，讓中國接管台灣付出更多代價，可恥的是，這些自由正遭到內部背叛。
_source.movement_title: 《经济学人》批评台湾政治内斗削弱民主防御优势
_source.movement_abstract: 【英国《经济学人》近日报道】英国《经济学人》近日刊登专文，批评台湾政治人物因党派私利导致国家治理困难，使中国成为最大赢家。文章指出，台湾民主制度本身构成对中国的威慑力量，但当前政治内斗正在削弱这一优势。2024年大选后，民进党掌握行政权，国民党控制立法院，两党对立引发宪政危机。国民党冻结对美军购预算、阻挠大法官人事任命，并反对以21万架无人机订单扶持本土产业计划。国民党高层承认支持无人机制造，但担忧资金流向支持民进党的企业，且亲国民党企业因在中国有投资而不敢投入生产。文章批评台湾政治人物不珍惜民主，反而通过内部背叛摧毁民主。外界关注台海局势时，通常聚焦中国入侵或封锁风险，以及美国介入后核战争风险，但文章提出另一种情境：台湾可能因内部混乱被诱使“不战而降”。文章强调，台湾年轻一代对政治失望，投票意愿降低，且不断接触中国资助的嘲弄台湾民主的社交媒体内容。文章认为，台湾政治失能正在伤害国家，自由本应是优势，却遭到内部背叛。

_source.movement_abstract: 【英国《经济学人》6月报道】英国《经济学人》6月刊登专文，批评台湾政治人物因党派私利导致国家治理困难，使中国成为唯一赢家。文章指出，台湾民主本为防御优势，却因内部政治斗争遭到背叛。2024年大选后，民进党掌握行政权，国民党控制立法院，两党对立引发宪政危机。国民党冻结包括对美军购预算在内的政府预算数月，并阻挠司法院大法官人事任命。此外，国民党还阻挡了价值21万架海空无人机订单以扶植本土产业的计划，部分国民党高层担忧资金流向捐款给民进党的企业，或因亲国民党企业在大陆有投资而不敢投入生产。文章认为，台湾政治人物的不负责任正在摧毁民主，削弱对中国的威慑力量。外界关注台海局势时，除中国入侵或封锁风险外，台湾被诱使“不战而降”的情境亦值得警惕。文章强调，台湾自由本应增加中国接管成本，但政治失能正使这一优势受损。

《經濟學人》近日刊登「挾持台灣民主」（Taking Taiwan’s democracy hostage）專文，批評台灣政治人物只顧私利，讓國家變得越來越難以治理，中國成為唯一贏家。文中痛斥反對黨引發一連串憲政危機，包含凍結對美軍購預算、阻擋大法官人事案，甚至阻擋以無人機訂單扶植本土產業的計畫，民主自由原本是台灣的防衛優勢，卻可恥地遭到內部背叛。
文章指出，外界研究台海區域情勢時，通常關注中國入侵或封鎖的風險，以及美國介入後兩個核武強權開戰的風險。但另一種情境也值得關注，如果台灣被誘使「不戰而降」，這雖是中國最想看到的情況，但中國國家主席習近平將面臨一連串艱難的抉擇，北京可能必須以殘酷手段鎮壓台灣的自由，全世界都在看。
請繼續往下閱讀...
文中提到，台灣的民主不只是蔣介石獨裁體制的改進，本身也是一種威懾力量，台灣迫切需要更多讓中國國家主席習近平忌憚的籌碼，民進黨試圖推動延宕已久的軍事現代化，傳統的保護者美國則是不可靠的朋友，美國總統川普雖同意對台軍售，卻對外嘲笑台灣在中國面前微不足道，5月川習會後還呼應中方論述，稱賴清德是可能引發戰爭的莽撞之人。
該文批評，只顧自身利益的台灣政治人物非但沒有珍惜台灣的民主，反而正在摧毀民主。2024年大選後，民進黨掌握總統職位及行政部門，以國民黨為首的反對黨則控制立法院，黨派內鬥自此讓政府運作陷入癱瘓。
該文痛斥，許多國家都有惡劣的政治人物，台灣政治人物的不負責任尤其突出，賴清德總統態度固執，不像前總統蔡英文一樣與國民黨溫和派磋商；但反對黨引發了一連串憲政危機，國民黨立委及盟友凍結政府預算數月，包括對美軍購經費，同時阻擋司法院大法官人事任命。
文章提到，反對黨還採取一項劇烈的自毀行動，阻擋以21萬架空海無人機訂單扶植本土產業的計畫。國民黨高層曾告訴作者「噢，我們支持製造無人機，這是政治問題。」一名黨內大老更直言，國民黨立委擔心政府會把無人機資金流向捐款給民進黨的企業；被問到親國民黨企業是否可以製造無人機時，這名大老說：「親國民黨的企業通常在中國有投資，因此不敢投入生產」，而國民黨寧願不去正視這個兩難境地。
該文提到，國民黨主席鄭麗文宣稱台灣不能依賴美國，因此需要加強對中關係，4月與習近平會晤時，也引發民進黨不滿，鄭宣稱自己的目標是避免戰爭、不是賣台，但民進黨人士指控，國民黨內某些人實際上充當中國的「代理人」。
該文認為，毫無疑問，台灣是中國認知作戰的目標，這些手段是否奏效仍未知，但台灣年輕一代對政治越來越失望，投票意願也在降低，同時不斷接觸中國資助、嘲弄台灣民主一片混亂的社群媒體內容。
該文強調，從獨裁走向開放社會的歷程，改變了台灣的國際地位，但政治失能正在傷害台灣，外界不可能比台灣的政治人物更珍視台灣民主。台灣的自由本應是一種優勢，讓中國接管台灣付出更多代價，可恥的是，這些自由正遭到內部背叛。

國軍第四作戰區教召部隊本月8日在台南市區迅速完成砲陣地佔領演練。（記者方瑋立攝，資料照）
外媒《華爾街日報》訪問5名不同世代、背景與立場的台灣民眾，有人已做好上前線的準備，也有人認為避免戰爭才是首要選擇。對此，美國聖湯瑪斯大學國際研究講座教授葉耀元發文指出，若要「守住現有生活且極力避免戰火」，核心在於展現防衛決心。他提出3大關鍵做法，首要是強化國防實力以有效嚇阻中國人民解放軍犯台，這是維持台海和平不可或缺的首要基石，必須全力落實。葉耀元今日於臉書粉專「葉教授的國際事務學院」
發文
指出，「這是我的專長，我跟大家說要『守住現有生活、極力避免戰火』要怎麼做」。首先，除了硬體與軍事防禦，軟性防線同樣至關重要；再者，全台上下必須嚴加防範中共對台發動的認知作戰以及潛伏在內部的第五縱隊威脅。第3點，更要建立一套全國人民都願意展現保家衛國姿態的整體氛圍，唯有展現強烈防衛意志，中共才不敢輕舉妄動。請繼續往下閱讀...
葉耀元強調，唯有透過強化嚇阻，才能真正保護台灣現有的自由民主生活。他痛批，任何親中態度或協助中國進行統戰的言行，都只是在逐步蠶食台灣的主權與民主制度，更不要說那些宣揚投降主義的壞人了。
_source.movement_title: 台湾学者叶耀元提出强化国防实力与认知防御以遏制解放军犯台
_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾《华尔街日报》报道】美国圣托马斯大学国际研究讲座教授叶耀元于社交媒体发文指出，台湾若要守住现有生活并极力避免战火，核心在于展现防卫决心。其提出三大关键做法：首要任务是强化国防实力以有效威慑中国人民解放军犯台，这是维持台海和平不可或缺的基石；其次，除硬件防御外，必须严加防范中共对台发动的认知作战及内部潜伏的第五纵队威胁；第三，需建立全民展现保家卫国姿态的整体氛围，通过强烈防卫意志使对手不敢轻举妄动。叶耀元强调，唯有透过强化威慑才能真正保护台湾现有的自由民主生活，并批评任何亲中态度或协助中国进行统战的言行都在逐步蚕食台湾的主权与民主制度。

_source.author_name: By John Murray, Dr. Elise Annett, and Dr. James Giordano
_source.content:
The functions of observation and orientation, central components of the OODA (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act) loop posited by Colonel John Boyd, U.S. Air Force fighter pilot, military strategist, and influential theorist of decision-making, have long been used to explain the cognitive processes that underpin military leadership and
. Within this framework, military advantage has historically been associated with the ability to observe, orient, decide, and act more skillfully and rapidly than an
. As operational environments become increasingly information-intensive and AI-enabled, however, achieving such decisional advantage depends upon the interaction of veridical information, information assimilation and analysis, decision velocity, contextual fidelity, and temporal synchronization. Together, the integrative dynamics of these elements enable commanders to attain and preserve operational initiative by ensuring that decisions are informed by accurate information, produced with sufficient speed, and remain aligned with an evolving operational environment.
Boyd’s original construct has been broadened to account for this alignment by capturing the dispositions, biases, and operational consequences for the decision-making process, as well as the cumulative effects of biological, psychological, social, cultural, institutional, and environmental factors that shape cognition before
. The resulting Disposition, Observe, Orient, Decide, Act, consequence (dOODAc) framework, introduced during a 2011 Strategic Multilayer Assessment (SMA), further recognizes that military actions generate immediate, intermediate, and enduring effects that recursively shape future decision cycles through reflexive
. Decision-making therefore emerges as an adaptive and self-reinforcing process in which operational experience shapes subsequent cognition, institutional understanding, tactical action, and strategic adaptation.
Although Boyd's original conception accounted for adaptation within successive decision cycles, we contend that AI-enabled cognitive warfare, introduces an additional analytical dimension by accelerating the velocity at which the cognitive ecosystem itself evolves. As a result, the operational environment thus becomes an active determinant of the decision process, evolving concurrently with institutional cognition rather than serving solely as the object of
. This relationship broadens both the conceptual basis and practical articulation of command by positioning continuous cognitive synchronization as an imperative condition of effective adaptation.
Although the dOODAc framework effectively characterizes adaptation across successive decision cycles, AI-enabled information ecosystems increasingly evolve during the execution of each cycle. Persistent sensing, algorithmically mediated information exchange, autonomous influence operations, and distributed human-machine interactions continuously alter the operational environment independently of
. Consequently, observations acquired at the outset of a decision cycle capture only an episodic representation of a cognitive environment that continues to evolve through multifactorial and multidimensional (i.e., informational, behavioral, psychological, and social) processes before an action is
.
These developments indicate that, as the operational environment has become increasingly contested within the cognitive domain, competitive advantage has come to depend on preserving the speed and quality of decision-making, as well as the coherence between institutional cognition and continuously evolving
. This extends traditional theories of command by introducing temporal synchronization as an operational variable alongside speed, adaptation, and learning. Decision superiority, in this context, reflects both the quality and velocity of institutional decision-making and the extent to which those decisions remain synchronized with the cognitive environment they are intended to influence.
characterize the evolution of the cognitive environment through the analogy of a starling murmuration, in which coherent system behavior emerges from the continuous interaction of numerous individual agents. Applied to the context of cognitive warfare, this analogy illustrates how the cognitive environment can exhibit intrinsic velocity independent of institutional decision processes. Human beliefs, social relationships, information flows, and adversarial influence activities continue to evolve regardless of the rate at which command-and-control (C2) systems execute a decision cycle. The result is a persistent divergence between the tempo of the cognitive environment and the tempo at which institutional cognition observes and acts upon it.
Figure 1 (below) conceptualizes this relationship by situating the dOODAc framework within the broader cognitive ecosystem of institutional influences and environmental interactions that shape each stage of military decision-making. Within this architecture, biopsychosocial dispositions inform observations, orientation integrates information across multiple cognitive dimensions, and consequences recursively shape future dispositions. Superimposed upon these recursive decision processes is a continuously evolving cognitive ecosystem, represented by the dynamic agent model proposed by Wilcox and Walters.
The upper panel situates the dOODAc decision cycle within the broader cognitive ecosystem, in which biopsychosocial dispositions inform the OODA loop and consequences recursively shape future dispositions. The lower panel represents the continuously evolving cognitive environment as a dynamic agent model, within which the cross-sections at Time A and Time B illustrate that, although institutional decision processes remain internally coherent, the operational environment continues to diverge throughout execution.
The implications of this relationship become apparent in the comparison of Time A and Time B shown in Figure 1. Although institutional decision processes remain internally coherent, the operational environment remains subject to a state of dynamicity throughout execution. This divergence reflects the challenge of applying institutional decision processes within an environment that continues to evolve during execution. Operational advantage in the cognitive domain should therefore be understood as a function of the interaction between decision velocity, that is, the speed at which command completes a decision cycle, and the alignment of institutional understanding with the evolving cognitive environments.
As noted above, decisions predicated upon a single, episodic assessment of the operational environment risk misalignment because the environment may have already diverged by the time a decision is
. Conversely, a deliberately slower decision process intended to preserve alignment with environmental evolution risks inaction, as the temporal window during which the observed environment remains actionable may close before the decision is finalized. From this perspective, a central challenge of cognitive warfare lies in governing the relationship between institutional cognition and an operational environment in which informational, behavioral, and social dynamics evolve continuously and often independently of military decision timelines.
The views and opinions expressed in this essay are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect those of the United States government, Department of War, or the National Defense University.
Mr. John Murray is a Research Intern in the Program for Disruptive Technology and Future Warfare at the Institute for National Strategic Studies at the National Defense University and a graduate candidate in the Master of Public Administration program at Auburn University.
Dr. Elise Annett is a Research Fellow in the Program for Disruptive Technology and Future Warfare of the Institute for National Strategic Studies at the National Defense University.
Dr. James Giordano is Head of the Center for Strategic Deterrence and Weapons of Mass Destruction Studies of the Institute for National Strategic Studies at the National Defense University and serves as NDU Special Advisor to the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War (CBRN).

_source.movement_abstract: 【美国国防大学国家战略研究所报道】美国国防大学国家战略研究所研究人员约翰·默里、伊莉丝·阿内特和詹姆斯·乔尔达诺发表文章，提出扩展博伊德上校OODA循环的dOODAc（Disposition-Observe-Orient-Decide-Act-consequence）框架，用于解析人工智能赋能下的认知域作战决策机制。文章指出，随着作战环境日益信息密集和人工智能化，决策优势取决于真实信息、信息同化分析、决策速度、情境保真度和时间同步的交互作用。dOODAc框架强调生物、心理、社会、文化、制度和环境因素对认知的影响，以及行动产生的即时、中期和持久效应如何递归塑造未来决策周期。研究认为，人工智能引入额外分析维度，加速认知生态系统自身演变，使作战环境成为决策过程的主动决定因素，而非单纯被观察对象。文章通过椋鸟群飞类比说明认知环境具有内在速度，独立于机构决策进程演变，导致机构认知与认知环境之间出现持续分歧。研究强调，认知域作战优势取决于决策速度与机构理解同演化认知环境对齐程度的交互作用，指出单一时点评估风险错配，而刻意缓慢决策可能导致错失行动窗口。文章观点仅代表作者，不一定反映美国政府、国防部或国防大学立场。

. Within this framework, military advantage has historically been associated with the ability to observe, orient, decide, and act more skillfully and rapidly than an
. As operational environments become increasingly information-intensive and AI-enabled, however, achieving such decisional advantage depends upon the interaction of veridical information, information assimilation and analysis, decision velocity, contextual fidelity, and temporal synchronization. Together, the integrative dynamics of these elements enable commanders to attain and preserve operational initiative by ensuring that decisions are informed by accurate information, produced with sufficient speed, and remain aligned with an evolving operational environment.
Boyd’s original construct has been broadened to account for this alignment by capturing the dispositions, biases, and operational consequences for the decision-making process, as well as the cumulative effects of biological, psychological, social, cultural, institutional, and environmental factors that shape cognition before
. The resulting Disposition, Observe, Orient, Decide, Act, consequence (dOODAc) framework, introduced during a 2011 Strategic Multilayer Assessment (SMA), further recognizes that military actions generate immediate, intermediate, and enduring effects that recursively shape future decision cycles through reflexive
. Decision-making therefore emerges as an adaptive and self-reinforcing process in which operational experience shapes subsequent cognition, institutional understanding, tactical action, and strategic adaptation.
Although Boyd's original conception accounted for adaptation within successive decision cycles, we contend that AI-enabled cognitive warfare, introduces an additional analytical dimension by accelerating the velocity at which the cognitive ecosystem itself evolves. As a result, the operational environment thus becomes an active determinant of the decision process, evolving concurrently with institutional cognition rather than serving solely as the object of
. This relationship broadens both the conceptual basis and practical articulation of command by positioning continuous cognitive synchronization as an imperative condition of effective adaptation.
Although the dOODAc framework effectively characterizes adaptation across successive decision cycles, AI-enabled information ecosystems increasingly evolve during the execution of each cycle. Persistent sensing, algorithmically mediated information exchange, autonomous influence operations, and distributed human-machine interactions continuously alter the operational environment independently of
. Consequently, observations acquired at the outset of a decision cycle capture only an episodic representation of a cognitive environment that continues to evolve through multifactorial and multidimensional (i.e., informational, behavioral, psychological, and social) processes before an action is
.
These developments indicate that, as the operational environment has become increasingly contested within the cognitive domain, competitive advantage has come to depend on preserving the speed and quality of decision-making, as well as the coherence between institutional cognition and continuously evolving
. This extends traditional theories of command by introducing temporal synchronization as an operational variable alongside speed, adaptation, and learning. Decision superiority, in this context, reflects both the quality and velocity of institutional decision-making and the extent to which those decisions remain synchronized with the cognitive environment they are intended to influence.
characterize the evolution of the cognitive environment through the analogy of a starling murmuration, in which coherent system behavior emerges from the continuous interaction of numerous individual agents. Applied to the context of cognitive warfare, this analogy illustrates how the cognitive environment can exhibit intrinsic velocity independent of institutional decision processes. Human beliefs, social relationships, information flows, and adversarial influence activities continue to evolve regardless of the rate at which command-and-control (C2) systems execute a decision cycle. The result is a persistent divergence between the tempo of the cognitive environment and the tempo at which institutional cognition observes and acts upon it.
Figure 1 (below) conceptualizes this relationship by situating the dOODAc framework within the broader cognitive ecosystem of institutional influences and environmental interactions that shape each stage of military decision-making. Within this architecture, biopsychosocial dispositions inform observations, orientation integrates information across multiple cognitive dimensions, and consequences recursively shape future dispositions. The upper panel situates the dOODAc decision cycle within the broader cognitive ecosystem, in which biopsychosocial dispositions inform the OODA loop and consequences recursively shape future dispositions. The lower panel represents the continuously evolving cognitive environment as a dynamic agent model, within which the cross-sections at Time A and Time B illustrate that, although institutional decision processes remain internally coherent, the operational environment continues to diverge throughout execution.
The implications of this relationship become apparent in the comparison of Time A and Time B shown in Figure 1. Although institutional decision processes remain internally coherent, the operational environment remains subject to a state of dynamicity throughout execution. This divergence reflects the challenge of applying institutional decision processes within an environment that continues to evolve during execution. Operational advantage in the cognitive domain should therefore be understood as a function of the interaction between decision velocity, that is, the speed at which command completes a decision cycle, and the alignment of institutional understanding with the evolving cognitive environments.
As noted above, decisions predicated upon a single, episodic assessment of the operational environment risk misalignment because the environment may have already diverged by the time a decision is
. Conversely, a deliberately slower decision process intended to preserve alignment with environmental evolution risks inaction, as the temporal window during which the observed environment remains actionable may close before the decision is finalized. From this perspective, a central challenge of cognitive warfare lies in governing the relationship between institutional cognition and an operational environment in which informational, behavioral, and social dynamics evolve continuously and often independently of military decision timelines.

Kaohsiung, Aug. 11 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) on Tuesday presided over the launch ceremony for two new marine survey vessels, reiterating the government's resolve to uphold maritime governance and national security through surveys of Taiwan's surrounding waters.
At the launch ceremony in Kaohsiung, Lai named the 100-ton-class and 300-ton-class survey vessels "Blue Ocean 101" and "Blue Ocean 102," respectively.
The vessels were built by CSBC Corp., Taiwan, following an open tender initiated by the National Academy of Marine Research (NAMR) under the Ocean Affairs Council (OAC).
Lai said that after entering service, the two vessels will collect hydrographic and biological data in the shallow coastal waters off Taiwan's main island and outlying islands to bolster the country's maritime governance and disaster response capabilities.
He noted that the ocean is a crucial domain in Taiwan's efforts to ensure national security.
"In recent years, China has used research vessels, coast guard vessels and cognitive warfare to carry out various gray-zone incursions, affecting regional peace and stability," he said.
"These developments repeatedly remind us that only by having a more complete understanding of the environment of our own waters can we safeguard national security and jointly protect the maritime order with the international community."
The government will continue establishing a national marine radar observation network to strengthen maritime security monitoring and support decision-making, Lai said.
It will also actively pursue a project to construct a 4,000-ton survey vessel to build a comprehensive survey fleet covering waters from coastal areas to the open ocean, he said.
At the ceremony, OAC Minister Kuan Bi-ling (管碧玲) also underscored the importance of maritime research in efforts to safeguard national security.
"In recent years, China's research vessels have frequently entered Taiwan's surrounding waters to conduct maritime surveys and collect data, bordering on incursion and harassment," Kuan said.
"When we ask, 'What are they doing in our neighborhood?' we must also ask, 'How much do we know about our ocean?'" she said.
"Seabed topography, hydrology, ocean currents, and long-term accumulated marine data are the foundation of marine scientific research in peacetime, but they are also an important basis for the country to understand the maritime situation when facing security challenges."
The NAMR said the 4,000-ton survey vessel is scheduled to be completed in 2029, and the three vessels will cost a total of NT$6.32 billion (US$196 million).
The NAMR said the 100-ton-class survey vessel has a range of 500 nautical miles and is equipped with scientific instruments including a shallow-water multibeam echosounder, single-beam echosounder, acoustic Doppler current profiler, conductivity-temperature-depth (CTD) profiler and deployment systems.
The 300-ton-class survey vessel has a range of 1,500 nautical miles and is equipped with a deep-water multibeam echosounder, sub-bottom profiler and scientific three-frequency fish finder, according to the NAMR.
_source.movement_title: 台湾当局启动海洋调查船项目强化海域管控与国家安全能力
_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾中央社8月11日报道】2026年8月11日，台湾当局在高雄举行两艘新型海洋调查船下水仪式，总统赖清德出席并强调通过海洋调查维护海域治理与国家安全。两艘调查船分别为100吨级'蓝洋101'号和300吨级'蓝洋102'号，由台湾造船公司承建，隶属于海洋委员会下属国家海洋研究院。投入使用后，两船将采集台湾本岛及离岛周边浅海海域的水文与生物数据，提升海洋治理与灾害应对能力。赖清德指出，近年来中国大陆利用科研船、海警船及认知战手段在周边海域开展灰色地带行动，影响区域和平稳定，强调需深化对己方海域环境认知以保障国家安全。台湾当局计划建立国家海洋雷达观测网络，并推进4000吨级调查船建设项目，预计2029年完工，三艘船总造价为新台币63.2亿元（约1.96亿美元）。100吨级船续航500海里，配备浅水多波束测深仪、单波束测深仪、声学多普勒流速剖面仪及温盐深仪等设备；300吨级船续航1500海里，配备深水多波束测深仪、海底剖面仪及三频探鱼仪等科学仪器。海洋委员会主委管碧玲表示，中国大陆科研船频繁进入台湾周边海域开展调查，接近侵扰行为，凸显掌握海洋数据对应对安全挑战的重要性。

Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel speaks during the opening of the 1st International Colloquium "Fidel: Legacy and Future" at Havana Convention Palace in Cuba on Monday. The conference marks the centenary of the birth of Fidel Castro and runs from through Thursday.
Aug. 10 (UPI) --
Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel accused the United States of waging "psychological warfare" against Cuba and linked recent reports of increased CIA operations on the island to what he described as an attempt by Washington to destabilize the Cuban government.
Díaz-Canel made the remarks Saturday during the closing session of the 24th International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties, held at the Palace of Conventions in Havana.
"We are living through the most dangerous period since the October Crisis," Díaz-Canel said, using Cuba's name for the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis.
He said that, in addition to economic pressure, Cuba is facing a "high-intensity unconventional war" that he said includes "digital subversion," funding for "internal mercenaries," media smear campaigns and influence networks.
Díaz-Canel directly linked those accusations to recent reports published by U.S. media outlets about an alleged increase in CIA operations involving Cuba.
"We are not at all surprised by the revelations in recent days by major U.S. media outlets about an increase in CIA operations in Cuba to subvert the internal order," he said.
"These are not random leaks, as they are being portrayed, but part of the deliberate plan by the U.S. regime to wage psychological warfare against Cuba," he added.
Díaz-Canel also accused the U.S. government of intensifying military threats and maintaining a policy of "regime change" toward Cuba. He also criticized the island's continued inclusion on the U.S. list of state sponsors of terrorism.
During the
speech
, the president cited recent remarks by Secretary of State
Marco Rubio
about sanctions against Cuba and said Washington is seeking to prevent the Cuban government from finding ways to ease economic pressure.
The remarks come as Cuba faces a prolonged economic and energy crisis that has led to power outages that, according to Díaz-Canel, can exceed 20 hours a day in some parts of the country. The president attributed much of the situation to U.S. sanctions and difficulties importing fuel and other resources.
Díaz-Canel said about 1,400 megawatts of distributed generation capacity remain offline because of a lack of diesel and fuel oil. He said that if the capacity were available every day, power outages could be reduced to about three hours.
The president also described difficulties in Cuba's healthcare system. According to figures he presented, 98,500 patients are awaiting surgery, including 12,000 children, while only 30% of the country's basic medicines are available. He also said the technical availability of ambulances stands at 22%.
Díaz-Canel said U.S. sanctions and other measures are intended to increase social discontent to bring about political change in Cuba and called on the communist parties and allied movements gathered in Havana to intensify their opposition to U.S. policy toward the island.
The president also urged those organizations to use digital platforms to counter what he called a "fascist media siege" and a "disinformation machine," as well as to mobilize parliaments, labor unions and social movements against U.S. sanctions.

_source.movement_abstract: 【美国UPI通讯社8月10日报道】古巴总统迪亚斯-卡内尔在哈瓦那举行的第24届共产党和工人党国际会议闭幕式上发表讲话，指控美国对古巴发动“心理战”及“高强度非传统战争”。迪亚斯-卡内尔将近期美国媒体披露的中央情报局（CIA）在古巴增加行动的报道，定性为华盛顿旨在颠覆古巴内部秩序、制造社会不满并推动政权更迭的蓄意计划。他指出，古巴正面临自1962年导弹危机以来最危险的时期，美国通过经济制裁、数字颠覆、资助内部代理人及媒体抹黑等手段施压。受制裁及燃料短缺影响，古巴约1400兆瓦分布式发电能力停摆，部分地区每日停电超20小时。医疗系统面临严峻挑战，约98500名患者等待手术，其中12000名为儿童，基本药物仅30%可用，救护车可用率仅为22%。迪亚斯-卡内尔呼吁与会政党及盟友利用数字平台反击美国“法西斯媒体围剿”，动员议会、工会及社会运动反对美国制裁政策。

Aug. 10 (UPI) --
Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel accused the United States of waging "psychological warfare" against Cuba and linked recent reports of increased CIA operations on the island to what he described as an attempt by Washington to destabilize the Cuban government.
Díaz-Canel made the remarks Saturday during the closing session of the 24th International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties, held at the Palace of Conventions in Havana.
"We are living through the most dangerous period since the October Crisis," Díaz-Canel said, using Cuba's name for the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis.
He said that, in addition to economic pressure, Cuba is facing a "high-intensity unconventional war" that he said includes "digital subversion," funding for "internal mercenaries," media smear campaigns and influence networks.
Díaz-Canel directly linked those accusations to recent reports published by U.S. media outlets about an alleged increase in CIA operations involving Cuba.
"We are not at all surprised by the revelations in recent days by major U.S. media outlets about an increase in CIA operations in Cuba to subvert the internal order," he said.
"These are not random leaks, as they are being portrayed, but part of the deliberate plan by the U.S. regime to wage psychological warfare against Cuba," he added.
Díaz-Canel also accused the U.S. government of intensifying military threats and maintaining a policy of "regime change" toward Cuba. He also criticized the island's continued inclusion on the U.S. list of state sponsors of terrorism.
During the
speech
, the president cited recent remarks by Secretary of State
Marco Rubio
about sanctions against Cuba and said Washington is seeking to prevent the Cuban government from finding ways to ease economic pressure.
The remarks come as Cuba faces a prolonged economic and energy crisis that has led to power outages that, according to Díaz-Canel, can exceed 20 hours a day in some parts of the country. The president attributed much of the situation to U.S. sanctions and difficulties importing fuel and other resources.
Díaz-Canel said about 1,400 megawatts of distributed generation capacity remain offline because of a lack of diesel and fuel oil. He said that if the capacity were available every day, power outages could be reduced to about three hours.
The president also described difficulties in Cuba's healthcare system. According to figures he presented, 98,500 patients are awaiting surgery, including 12,000 children, while only 30% of the country's basic medicines are available. He also said the technical availability of ambulances stands at 22%.
Díaz-Canel said U.S. sanctions and other measures are intended to increase social discontent to bring about political change in Cuba and called on the communist parties and allied movements gathered in Havana to intensify their opposition to U.S. policy toward the island.
The president also urged those organizations to use digital platforms to counter what he called a "fascist media siege" and a "disinformation machine," as well as to mobilize parliaments, labor unions and social movements against U.S. sanctions.

_source.content:
As an Iranian journalist in close contact with people across Iran, I have witnessed a reality often overlooked by outside observers.
Through conversations with Iranians from different regions and backgrounds, people who do not know one another, I have repeatedly encountered a growing trust in Israel. This sentiment is shaped not by external campaigns, but by years of experience with the Islamic Republic’s repression, regional aggression, and the consequences of its policies.
Many Iranians view Israel as the only actor with the determination and strategic clarity to confront the core of the regime’s power, targeting not only military capabilities and nuclear ambitions but also the leadership and networks behind them.
They see Israel’s approach as fundamentally different from powers that can leave the region: a strategy focused on confronting threats at their source.
This deep trust is a strategic asset for the Jewish state that must be continuously protected, defended, and nurtured against deliberate campaigns of subversion.
Today, this priceless capital of mutual trust faces a sophisticated threat – not just from the overt propaganda machines in Tehran, but from reckless media narratives that inadvertently serve the Islamic Republic’s strategic goals.
More importantly, it acts as a devastating psychological operation that directly targets the trust ordinary Iranians place in the State of Israel.
To suggest that Jerusalem would favor elevating one of Iran’s most brutal oppressors as a viable alternative is an insult to the Iranian people. It is a narrative that risks fracturing a strategic friendship that has survived decades of clerical dictatorship.
To understand why this narrative is so damaging, one must look at who Mahmoud Ahmadinejad truly is to the Iranian nation. He is not a standard political figure; he is a symbol of domestic terror and democratic betrayal.
In 2009, Ahmadinejad “won” re-election through a blatantly rigged and fraudulent vote. This political farce was orchestrated by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) mafia with the absolute backing of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.
When millions of ordinary Iranians poured into the streets during the Green Movement, demanding “Where is my vote?” the regime responded with savage, bloody suppression. Thousands of peaceful protesters were beaten, imprisoned, tortured, and killed. Ahmadinejad was the smiling face of that murderous crackdown.
He is a deeply despised figure among the vast majority of Iranians, who view his tenure as the dark era when the IRGC completely hijacked the state’s economy, politics, and social fabric. Furthermore, Ahmadinejad’s global infamy rests heavily on his grotesque denial of the Holocaust.
By hosting international conferences of Holocaust deniers and spewing vile antisemitic rhetoric, he sought to isolate Iran and position the country as the vanguard of global antisemitism. This behavior added immense fuel to the rage of the Iranian people.
The citizens of Iran, who view themselves as proud inheritors of a culture defined by tolerance, were deeply ashamed of this state-sponsored bigotry. Iranians are friends of the Jewish people. They saw Ahmadinejad’s antics for what they were: a desperate attempt by an illegitimate regime to legitimize itself by weaponizing hatred.
Therefore, when reports surface suggesting Israel wanted to bring this tyrant to power as an alternative, the Iranian public is left asking a painful question: How could Israel, the nation built as a sanctuary for Holocaust survivors, ever wish to empower a Holocaust denier?
How could Jerusalem wish to elevate a man under whose watch the IRGC solidified its total iron grip over Iran?
The answer is simple: Israel would not. The narrative is a toxic distortion. However, the mere existence of these media reports plays directly into the hands of the Islamic Republic’s hard core.
The ruling clerics in Tehran are terrified of the profound affection and trust that exists between the Iranians and Israel. They recognize that this grassroots friendship represents a massive existential threat to their ideological legitimacy. If the Iranian people view Israel not as an enemy, but as a historic ally, the regime’s foundational pillar of “Death to Israel” completely crumbles.
Consequently, the Islamic Republic’s overt and covert agents are working overtime to damage this trust by manufacturing elaborate conspiracy theories.
In recent regional conflicts, the regime’s propaganda machine aggressively weaponized a highly sensitive historical trauma. They spread systematic rumors claiming that Israel planned to use Kurdish separatist forces from outside the borders to invade western Iran.
This line of propaganda is a calculated psychological trap designed to trigger memories of the painful period immediately following the 1979 revolution, when armed separatist Kurdish factions occupied and besieged cities in Western Iran, pushing the nation to the brink of balkanization.
Crucially, this psychological warfare causes the greatest outrage among Iran’s patriotic Kurdish majority. These patriotic Kurds fought against the separatists after 1979, sacrificing their lives to keep Iran whole.
Historically, Iran’s Kurdish population has been a bedrock of Iranian national identity and cultural heritage, consistently rejecting the regime’s attempts to question their loyalty to Iran’s territorial integrity.
By manufacturing accusations of territorial division, spreading rumors about a Kurdish-led invasion, and validating absurd theories about Israel trying to bring Ahmadinejad back to power as an alternative, the regime is directing a multi-part psychological script.
These are not separate events; they are coordinated scenes of a singular narrative born entirely out of the Islamic Republic’s absolute terror of the deep trust between ordinary Iranians and Israel.
On January 8 and 9, 2026, following a direct call to action by Pahlavi, millions of brave Iranians defied the regime and flooded the streets across Iran. The historic scale of those protests proved that the Iranian people’s desire for a secular, democratic future is a powerful, organic grassroots reality, not a digital illusion created by computers.
When media outlets play domestic politics with national security and international alliances, the consequences are measured in human lives.
The path to a peaceful Middle East relies entirely on the inevitable collapse of the Islamic Republic and the rebirth of a free, democratic Iran. Israeli media and strategic analysts must remain fiercely vigilant against narratives that alienate their greatest geopolitical asset.
They must write and analyze with a clear, unwavering understanding: the Iranian nation and the Israeli nation have no better, truer friends in the region than each other.
The friendship between our peoples is biblical, tracing its roots back to Cyrus the Great. It is a timeless alliance that no modern media distortion can erase.
Free Iranians and Israelis must stand together, ensuring that the cornerstone of tomorrow’s peace is never sacrificed for sensationalist headlines.
_source.movement_title: 伊朗民众视以色列为战略盟友，德黑兰政权利用虚假叙事破坏互信
_source.movement_abstract: 伊朗记者基于广泛接触指出，伊朗民众对以色列存在深厚信任，视其为对抗伊斯兰共和国政权压迫及地区扩张的唯一战略力量。该信任源于民众对伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队及最高领袖哈梅内伊镇压政策的长期不满，以及对以色列战略决心的认可。德黑兰政权视此民间互信为生存威胁，正通过宣传机器制造虚假叙事进行心理战，包括散布以色列企图扶持前总统内贾德复辟、支持库尔德分裂势力入侵伊朗西部等谣言，旨在利用1979年革命后库尔德分离主义的历史创伤煽动民族对立。2026年1月8日至9日，伊朗爆发大规模反政府抗议，民众要求世俗民主未来，证明该反政权情绪为有机草根现实。分析认为，媒体若传播损害伊以民间友谊的叙事，将直接服务于伊朗政权战略目标，削弱以色列地缘政治资产。中东和平路径依赖于伊斯兰共和国崩溃及民主伊朗重生，以色列与伊朗民众基于古波斯居鲁士大帝时期的历史渊源，构成地区内最稳固的盟友关系，需警惕并抵御旨在破坏该关系的宣传攻势。

Crucially, this psychological warfare causes the greatest outrage among Iran’s patriotic Kurdish majority. These patriotic Kurds fought against the separatists after 1979, sacrificing their lives to keep Iran whole.
Historically, Iran’s Kurdish population has been a bedrock of Iranian national identity and cultural heritage, consistently rejecting the regime’s attempts to question their loyalty to Iran’s territorial integrity.
By manufacturing accusations of territorial division, spreading rumors about a Kurdish-led invasion, and validating absurd theories about Israel trying to bring Ahmadinejad back to power as an alternative, the regime is directing a multi-part psychological script.
These are not separate events; they are coordinated scenes of a singular narrative born entirely out of the Islamic Republic’s absolute terror of the deep trust between ordinary Iranians and Israel.
On January 8 and 9, 2026, following a direct call to action by Pahlavi, millions of brave Iranians defied the regime and flooded the streets across Iran. The historic scale of those protests proved that the Iranian people’s desire for a secular, democratic future is a powerful, organic grassroots reality, not a digital illusion created by computers.
When media outlets play domestic politics with national security and international alliances, the consequences are measured in human lives.
The path to a peaceful Middle East relies entirely on the inevitable collapse of the Islamic Republic and the rebirth of a free, democratic Iran. Israeli media and strategic analysts must remain fiercely vigilant against narratives that alienate their greatest geopolitical asset.
They must write and analyze with a clear, unwavering understanding: the Iranian nation and the Israeli nation have no better, truer friends in the region than each other.
The friendship between our peoples is biblical, tracing its roots back to Cyrus the Great. It is a timeless alliance that no modern media distortion can erase.

民進黨立委王定宇。（資料照）
繼台中市政府社宅宣傳公告上誤用「中國國徽」後，本報披露，交通部觀光署日月潭風景區管理處8日在車埕火車站鐵道廣場舉辦「鐵道音樂嘉年華」，其中站長體驗活動，竟提供多頂中共五星國徽的車長帽供民眾配戴拍照。對此，民進黨立委王定宇要求各級單位加強辨識能力，公務體系中部分人員，缺乏敵我觀念，對於這種國家的界線沒有戒心，導致從中央到地方都發生類似情形。王定宇指出，台中市政府社宅的宣傳出現了中國五星旗的徽章，集集的火車音樂節，讓民眾佩戴的帽子上面竟然也出現中共五星旗的徽章。中華人民共和國是中華民國台灣唯一而且最大的威脅，該威脅不僅僅是經濟的、安全的，更是要消滅我們的國家，「讓我們失去主權，讓我們自由民主的生活方式全部被消滅。」
請繼續往下閱讀...
王定宇批評，當五星旗徽章在公務體系裡面，竟毫無知覺地拿來當作展示宣傳的用途，顯示我國面對敵情威脅的敵我意識非常的模糊。這樣的模糊，唯一得利的是中共可以利用這樣模糊的界線進行滲透、分化、敵我界線的去除，對台灣的安全當然是有影響。至於發生的原因，王定宇分析，現在AI時代，在運用AI時，可能忽略了AI的資料庫裡面，中國可能占了中文體系裡面的多數資料庫，所以用AI去設計東西或者寫文案時，若沒有給予適當的指令，很容易就跑出這樣的東西；加上在公務體系裡面部分人員，缺乏敵我觀念，對於這種國家的界線沒有戒心，導致從中央到地方都發生類似情形。「我們會要求相關各級單位加強辨識能力！」王定宇表示，運用AI時，如何給予適當指令，出來的結果如何要檢核；對於失職，讓中華人民共和國的國徽竟然出現在我國公辦的活動上面，或公家的官署的宣傳上面，也應該給予適當的懲處，以儆效尤。王定宇強調，台灣面對中國越來越大的威脅，不管是軍事上的、經濟上的、灰色地帶上的，中共對台灣社會的認知作戰、分化也無所不用其極之際，對於這種動輒用中華人民共和國的國徽放在我國政府的活動上，不能輕忽這樣子的影響。這一些動輒引用中國圖騰來模糊我國國家主權的做法呢，台灣必須更小心謹慎的因應。
_source.movement_title: 台湾民进党立委王定宇批评公务体系误用中共国徽暴露敌我意识模糊
_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾中央社报道】台湾民进党立委王定宇指出，台中市政府社宅宣传及交通部观光署日月潭风景区管理处举办的铁道嘉年华活动中，出现误用中华人民共和国国徽及五星旗徽章的情况。王定宇批评公务体系部分人员缺乏敌我观念，对国家界线缺乏戒心，导致从中央到地方发生类似情形。他强调，中华人民共和国是台湾唯一且最大的威胁，涉及经济、安全及主权层面。王定宇分析，AI时代运用AI设计或撰写文案时，若未给予适当指令，易因数据库中文体系多数为中国内容而产出错误结果。他要求各级单位加强辨识能力，对失职行为给予适当惩处，以儆效尤。王定宇强调，面对中共日益增大的军事、经济及灰色地带威胁，以及认知作战与分化手段，台湾必须谨慎应对，避免引用中国图腾模糊国家主权。

（中央社記者
楊堯茹
台北9日電）日本戰略研究論壇與福和會舉行首次台日美政經模擬推演，參與的美國退役海軍少將蒙哥馬利今天於記者會表示，各國應事前規劃互通性，確保溝通順、制定計畫，尤其是確保海上安全航行；台灣社會韌性所面臨挑戰已超越國內範疇，須和美日盟友緊密合作。日本戰略研究論壇與福和會今天舉行「民主之盾：台日美三邊合作機制倡議第一次政經模擬推演」記者會，這次一天半的政經模擬推演聚焦全社會防衛韌性，包括能源、人道救援、運輸交通、醫療及因應認知作戰，包括台日國會議員、總統府全社會防衛韌性委員會委員及各界專家、學者等參與。出席的蒙哥馬利（Mark Montgomery）表示，此次推演重要性不在部隊運用，而是各種想定與需求的事前準備，再由政府各部門共同建構互通性，讓彼此在危機時能溝通順暢並制定計畫。蒙哥馬利強調，受脅迫地區在運送食物或水等物資時，海上部隊最為重要，也有接近95%貿易是經由海運，因此維持安全航行的能力至關重要，包括引導商船、提供救援，這通常是由海岸警衛隊或海軍負責，事前規劃跨國互通性在推演中引起熱烈討論。蒙哥馬利也提到，總統賴清德及其行政團隊在建構社會韌性方面表現卓越，致力確保在遭受可能的能源、通訊或金融危機時，台灣仍能維持運作，民間社會也能應對其他干擾。台灣社會韌性所面臨挑戰已超越國內範疇，必須和夥伴、美日盟友緊密合作。美國空軍退役軍官吉耐獅（Guermantes Lailari）則說，在國際間建立社會各層面的連結至關重要，讓各國在人為災害或自然災害時，能立即向外求助且對方也瞭解情況、提供協助。此連結的推動必須有連續性，超越政府或立法機關的民意變遷，持續保持對話。日本眾議員長島昭久認為，日本國會議員長期推動國會交流，試圖彌補政府間溝通管道的不足，希望互動不僅止於友好氣氛上。在可能突發情況發生時，日本、美國與台灣在援助時間點的共識達成較困難，因此這種民間對話機制至關重要。長島昭久提到，資訊戰讓社會陷入混亂且日夜不斷，日本與美國同樣受到此類挑戰，台灣在這方面能提供許多經驗，而日本則是在能源儲備、供應鏈多元化上稍微進步一些。日本眾議員神田潤一指出，日台任何一方陷入困境，都可能面對嚴峻局面，此類對話的面對面溝通，讓各項課題逐漸浮現；日本眾議員鹿嶋祐介也點到，此次推演凸顯資訊共享重要性。前日本海上自衛隊幕僚長武居智久則說，這次推演沒有劇本想定，每位參與者都是自行設定獨立情境、展開討論，其中的事前準備、日美台如何達成有效溝通都非常重要，希望與會者將討論內容帶回國作為檢討素材。#賴清德

_source.movement_title: 台日美举行首次政经模拟推演 退役美将强调跨域互通与海上安全
_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾中央社2026年8月9日报道】2026年8月9日，日本战略研究论坛与福和会在台北举行首次台日美政经模拟推演，主题为“民主之盾：台日美三边合作机制倡议第一次政经模拟推演”。推演为期一天半，聚焦全社会防卫韧性，涵盖能源、人道救援、运输交通、医疗及认知作战等领域。美国退役海军少将蒙哥马利（Mark Montgomery）在记者会上表示，推演重点在于事前规划互通性与沟通顺畅，确保危机时能制定计划。他强调，全球约95%贸易依赖海运，维持安全航行能力至关重要，需由海岸警卫队或海军负责引导商船及提供救援。蒙哥马利指出，台湾社会韧性面临的挑战已超越国内范畴，须与美日盟友紧密合作。美国空军退役军官吉耐狮（Guermantes Lailari）强调国际间建立社会各层面连结的重要性，确保灾害发生时能立即求助并获得协助。日本众议员长岛昭久表示，日本长期推动国会交流以弥补政府间沟通不足，民间对话机制在突发情况下至关重要。日本众议员神田润一、鹿嶋祐介及前日本海上自卫队幕僚长武居智久均指出，推演凸显信息共享与事前准备的重要性，参与者将讨论内容带回国内作为检讨素材。台湾总统赖清德及其行政团队在构建社会韧性方面表现卓越，致力确保在能源、通讯或金融危机时台湾仍能维持运作。

台北9日電）日本戰略研究論壇與福和會舉行首次台日美政經模擬推演，參與的美國退役海軍少將蒙哥馬利今天於記者會表示，各國應事前規劃互通性，確保溝通順、制定計畫，尤其是確保海上安全航行；台灣社會韌性所面臨挑戰已超越國內範疇，須和美日盟友緊密合作。
日本戰略研究論壇與福和會今天舉行「民主之盾：台日美三邊合作機制倡議第一次政經模擬推演」記者會，這次一天半的政經模擬推演聚焦全社會防衛韌性，包括能源、人道救援、運輸交通、醫療及因應認知作戰，包括台日國會議員、總統府全社會防衛韌性委員會委員及各界專家、學者等參與。
出席的蒙哥馬利（Mark Montgomery）表示，此次推演重要性不在部隊運用，而是各種想定與需求的事前準備，再由政府各部門共同建構互通性，讓彼此在危機時能溝通順暢並制定計畫。
蒙哥馬利強調，受脅迫地區在運送食物或水等物資時，海上部隊最為重要，也有接近95%貿易是經由海運，因此維持安全航行的能力至關重要，包括引導商船、提供救援，這通常是由海岸警衛隊或海軍負責，事前規劃跨國互通性在推演中引起熱烈討論。
蒙哥馬利也提到，總統賴清德及其行政團隊在建構社會韌性方面表現卓越，致力確保在遭受可能的能源、通訊或金融危機時，台灣仍能維持運作，民間社會也能應對其他干擾。台灣社會韌性所面臨挑戰已超越國內範疇，必須和夥伴、美日盟友緊密合作。
美國空軍退役軍官吉耐獅（Guermantes Lailari）則說，在國際間建立社會各層面的連結至關重要，讓各國在人為災害或自然災害時，能立即向外求助且對方也瞭解情況、提供協助。此連結的推動必須有連續性，超越政府或立法機關的民意變遷，持續保持對話。
日本眾議員長島昭久認為，日本國會議員長期推動國會交流，試圖彌補政府間溝通管道的不足，希望互動不僅止於友好氣氛上。在可能突發情況發生時，日本、美國與台灣在援助時間點的共識達成較困難，因此這種民間對話機制至關重要。
長島昭久提到，資訊戰讓社會陷入混亂且日夜不斷，日本與美國同樣受到此類挑戰，台灣在這方面能提供許多經驗，而日本則是在能源儲備、供應鏈多元化上稍微進步一些。
日本眾議員神田潤一指出，日台任何一方陷入困境，都可能面對嚴峻局面，此類對話的面對面溝通，讓各項課題逐漸浮現；日本眾議員鹿嶋祐介也點到，此次推演凸顯資訊共享重要性。
前日本海上自衛隊幕僚長武居智久則說，這次推演沒有劇本想定，每位參與者都是自行設定獨立情境、展開討論，其中的事前準備、日美台如何達成有效溝通都非常重要，希望與會者將討論內容帶回國作為檢討素材。（編輯：蘇志宗）1150809

_source.author_name: 自由時報電子報 記者黃靖媗／台北報導
_source.content:
民進黨立委陳培瑜今在「『民主之盾』台日美三邊合作機制倡議‧第一次政經模擬推演記者會」發言。（記者叢昌瑾攝）
福和會與日本戰略研究論壇合辦的「民主之盾」台美日三邊合作機制倡議論壇圓滿落幕。民進黨立委陳培瑜今（9）日在會後記者會說明，希望能藉由論壇向國際社會傳達，台灣正努力在全社會防衛韌性積極做準備，也期望讓台灣人民知道，無論政黨意識、價值觀為何，國內保持團結、持續進步最為重要。福和會與日本戰略研究論壇（JFSS）昨於台北舉辦「福和會『民主之盾』台美日三邊合作機制倡議論壇」，共同研討面對災難時，台、日、美各項關鍵基礎設施防護、民生供應韌性及跨部門危機應變合作機制。今日舉辦「『民主之盾』台日美三邊合作機制倡議‧第一次政經模擬推演記者會」。請繼續往下閱讀...
陳培瑜表示，民進黨立委在不同的論壇、座談中，都希望向美國、日本等好朋友傳達希望持續保持溝通、交流、對話的重要訊息，同時，也想向國際社會傳達，台灣正努力在全社會防衛韌性積極做好準備，涵蓋各式物資、運輸、醫療、認知作戰、人道救援等，政府希望帶領台灣人民對國際社會保持溝通、交流，同時提升台灣能力至最佳狀態。陳培瑜坦言，台灣目前面臨的困境一部分來自立法院，希望持續透過對話、政黨協商、政黨對話，讓更多台灣人民知道，無論政黨意識為何、選擇的價值觀是什麼，讓台灣國內保持團結、持續進步才是最重要的。陳培瑜指出，面對中國共產黨的威脅，相信台灣人民有各自對中共不同的解讀，但是若中共持續在台灣散播敵對訊息，甚至干擾國際外交，相信如同今日活動的民間交流有其必要性，同時邀請國會議員或各層級民意代表，表達出台灣在這件事情上，無論中央、地方都在努力。她也期望，能透過與各種民間單位合作，邀請更多台灣人一起參與、關心議題，與更多國際組織交流。
_source.movement_title: 民进党立委陈培瑜出席台日美三边合作机制论坛强调社会防卫韧性
_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾中央社 2026年8月9日报道】2026年8月9日，台湾福和会与日本战略研究论坛（JFSS）在台北联合举办“民主之盾”台美日三边合作机制倡议论坛暨第一次政经模拟推演。民进党立委陈培瑜在会后记者会表示，论坛旨在向国际社会传达台湾正积极提升全社会防卫韧性，涵盖物资储备、运输保障、医疗支援、认知作战应对及人道救援等领域。陈培瑜强调，台湾需持续与美国、日本等友好国家保持沟通对话，同时呼吁国内各政党超越意识形态差异，维持团结以应对挑战。针对中国大陆的威胁，陈培瑜指出中共持续在台湾散播敌对讯息并干扰外交，认为通过民间交流及各级民意代表参与，加强国际组织合作至关重要。她呼吁台湾社会各界共同参与，提升整体应对能力至最佳状态，以强化关键基础设施防护及跨部门危机应变机制。

_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾中央社 2026年8月9日报道】台湾国防部于2026年8月5日至14日实施汉光42号实兵演习，首次引入随军记者机制，旨在验证战时信息发布效率与战场传播管理。该机制不同于传统媒体邀访，选定少数媒体记者跟随一线部队深入操演现场。国防部智库国防安全研究院学者苏紫云指出，随军采访核心在于行动安全（OPSEC），记者未参与行动时享有完全报道自由，但一旦随军即须接受部队集体指挥管制，以确保战场防护与军事安全。苏紫云表示，此举参考美军与北约成熟经验，通过事前源头管理、制定明确基本规则、要求配合集体指挥管制及限制素材检视等手段，防止敌对势力透过媒体报道掌握部队精确位置或关键敏感情报。演习期间，军方在确保不泄露作战部署及机密前提下，测试民间媒体如何第一时间传递国军实况至国际社会，以反制敌方认知作战与假讯息宣传。苏紫云强调，随军采访制度象征国军思维跨越，旨在建立兼顾国防安全与新闻自由的制度环境，促进跨组织文化相互操作性。

Independent journalist David Hundeyin has exposed the Pentagon’s new psychological operations unit targeting Africa, “Drongo Company”. Tasked with “expanding the military’s ability to influence foreign audiences” across the continent, its heavily hyped launch occurs against a backdrop of dramatically and irreversibly waning Western influence and power in every sphere across the continent. As Africans steadily rid themselves of unwelcome foreign occupiers and oppressors, the US is forced to rely on strategies of manipulation to stem the tide, which have already failed spectacularly. They will surely misfire yet again.
Based in Fort Bragg, North Carolina – home to AFRICOM – Drongo Company’s nickname is inspired by a bird native to Africa, known for precisely imitating other species’ warning calls, and using other deception tactics to drive other animals away from food. The Pentagon reportedly “selected the name to reflect the unit’s focus on influencing perceptions and behavior.” Fittingly, a May 2014 Science paper found the drongo can mimic other species’ sounds and manipulate adversaries with unparalleled, almost human sophistication.
Task & Purpose notes Drongo Company’s creation “comes amid a shift in US military strategy in Africa,” which is quite an understatement. Washington is on the run across the continent, with combat units and occupation forces being withdrawn from multiple countries over recent years. In September 2024, over 1,000 soldiers departed Niger, while a $100 million drone base was abandoned. An anti-ISIS mission in Nigeria controversially launched this March was abruptly terminated in July, due to a cataclysmic inability to achieve its objectives.
Drongo Company is an attempt by the Empire to reassert narrative dominance over Africa, as its military capabilities across the continent and beyond constantly shrink in size and potency. An official US Army report openly states, “the art of psyops relies on persuasion rather than physical force.” This entails the exploitation of “mental factors…to evoke specific emotions, attitudes and behaviors.” The ultimate goal “is to persuade enemy, neutral and friendly nations and forces to take favorable actions toward the US and its allies.”
Drongo Company’s official launch ceremony
An AFRICOM factsheet on psyops claims local campaigns are targeted at militant groups, such as Al Qaeda, Boko Haram, and ISIS. Parenthetical mention is also made to “malign state actors” being targets, in the context of advancing “US interests.” As a Military.com report acknowledges, this is a reference to “competition with foreign governments.” Specifically, “Russia and China have expanded their political, economic and security activities across Africa” in recent years, which the Empire has been singularly unable to counter via military force.
Drongo Company is thus being deployed for “an information contest that extends beyond conventional battlefields.” The Pentagon is extremely sensitive, however, to “skeptical audiences” seeing through their psyops. Military.com further notes while AFRICOM claims its psychological operations adhere strictly to US law and Pentagon policies prohibiting targeting US citizens, these prohibitions only apply to intended audiences. There are no mechanisms in place preventing Stateside spectators being deluged – theoretically illegally – with Drongo Company’s sophisticated, clandestine military psychological warfare offensives, especially online.
Quite some informational assault is planned. Drongo Company will wage its psyops campaigns via “both established and emerging communication technologies…[including] print media, radio broadcasts, text messaging, direct engagement, television programming, social media platforms, and online resources.” These information sources will be blitzed with “persuasive messages intended to change how selected audiences think or act.” The need to “ensure targeted audiences consider…messages credible” is of paramount importance. After all, “adversaries or skeptical audiences” will reflexively dismiss obvious “American propaganda”:
“Drongo Company’s effectiveness will depend on more than its ability to produce messages. Its soldiers will need regional and cultural knowledge, language skills, accurate intelligence and credible African partners capable of reaching communities that may distrust communications associated with the US military.”
‘Role Players’
Strikingly, Drongo Company is formally part of the US Army’s notorious 7th Psychological Operations Battalion. The Pentagon’s premier psychological warfare unit, since May 2022 7th POB has released a series of disturbing, abstract recruitment videos. In the first, dramatic, rapid cut scenes are interspersed with eerie, monochrome cartoon clips, backed by an aggressive soundtrack. All along, text on the screen proclaims:
“You’ll find us in the shadows, at the tip of the spear. War is evolving, and all the world’s a stage. Anything we touch is a weapon. We can deceive, persuade, change, influence, inspire…We are everywhere.”
Despite such ominous hype, Drongo Company’s activation suggests a longstanding, initially much-vaunted 7th POB unit previously “forged for Africa” operational from 2017 onwards fell far short of its bold objectives. In February that year, the US Army published an essay celebrating the new psyops division’s launch. It revealed how the unit’s operatives were deployed “into the gray zones of Africa where alliances can be fluid and the people are as diverse as the many landscapes,” following elaborate training exercises in Florida:
“Influencing a population to create lasting change when you don’t look, sound, or dress like that population is a tricky proposition. Cultural training, language proficiency, and an indigenous approach can go pretty far towards closing the gap, but true effectiveness is only achieved through airtight relationships with host nation partners.”
Hence, training saw 7th Psychological Operations Battalion operatives deployed to simulated environments in the fictional African nation of Conch Republic. Under the exercise’s auspices, “the government of Conch had requested support from the US Embassy” to combat “a bevy of societal problems from drug trafficking to domestic terrorism, to combat these ills.” It featured live-action components, in which US police and Navy operatives and African “civic leaders” were “role players”, with detailed characters.
Their roles included “local radio disc jockeys, roving reporters, and even the police” in the fictional African country, who “would ambush teams in broad daylight and attempt to gain information, curry favor, or even solicit a bribe to make a tough situation disappear.” A synthetic local social media infrastructure was also constructed – “a dynamic, reactive and proactive environment…with analogs to Facebook, Twitter, and even Craigslist.” Through this online nexus, the Battalion could “affect and inform” different Conch Republic audiences.
A role-played Conch Republic border security ‘interrogates’ 7th POB operative
The social media simulation reportedly “provided an invaluable feedback mechanism that showed which messages were heard and to what extent they were understood.” Elsewhere, “the unit broke new ground…through the use of new communications equipment and series development software,” utilising a variety of “information transmission devices…useful in influence campaigns.” Resultantly, 7th POB operatives could supposedly “hit the ground” when deployed to Africa, delivering “cogent, impactful” psyops “aimed right at the heart of the population”:
“By all accounts, the juice is worth the squeeze. Community leaders take pride in supporting a high caliber exercise, the partnered agencies have found unique ways to meet their own training objectives through the scenarios, and the teams heading out the door are better prepared; prepared to amplify African solutions to African challenges, and prepared to survive if the world falls down around them.”
‘Indigenous Approach’
The US Army essay on 7th POB’s then-new African assignment revealed, “there’s a saying in the PSYOP community” – “[Army Special Operations Forces] makes change happen. PSYOP makes change last.” A senior military advisor to the division boasted how 7th POB’s activities represented the apotheosis of US psychological operations – “a place where science and technique blend.” The essay bombastically concluded by characterising psyops as “the long game, where changes in behavior are measured not over a deployment, but often over years.”
Judged by this metric, the “long game” played by 7th POB throughout the continent over the past decade has been decisively lost. In May, AFRICOM commander Dagvin Anderson laid bare in Congressional testimony how a “75% reduction” in US military and intelligence “posture” regionally during this time – “coupled with a drawdown of allies in the region” – has produced a “black hole” in Africa. He lamented at length how this gaping chasm in Western dominance has been rapidly filled by China, Iran and Russia.
Beijing’s “aggressive investments” in Africa’s “mining, infrastructure, and transportation sectors” have supplanted Western control over “critical minerals and strategic infrastructure.” On top of major profit hits and supply chain disruption, China’s increasing domination in industrial fields reliant on these resources – ranging from “electric vehicles, consumer electronics, and advanced military technologies” – represents “a structural vulnerability for the US Defense Industrial Base.” Meanwhile, Russia’s rising economic and military footprint on the continent is “undermining US influence and limiting NATO’s reach on its southern flank.”
Anderson claimed Russian paramilitary forces “insulate and protect regimes” in Africa with which Moscow has close relations, “under the guise of counter-terrorism operations.” However, the AFRICOM chief contradictorily acknowledged the threat of extremist militancy throughout the region Russian military advisors seek to deter was very real. In particular, Anderson cited how Al Qaeda-affiliate JNIM aims to destabilise the revolutionary governments of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, to the “extent of securing the resources and trappings of a nation state” in the manner of ISIS.
AFRICOM’s commander neglected to mention how France and Ukraine have heavily supported JNIM’s counter-revolutionary activities in the Sahel. An April essay published by Militarnyi, Kiev’s most prominent military news site, makes clear the objective of these military and intelligence machinations is out-and-out regime change, explicitly in service of furthering the Empire’s interests in Africa. Drongo Company must be understood as the psychological warfare component of this proxy assault on the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), and continent more widely.
Evidently, Africans must remain vigilant. Counter-revolutionary forces seen and unseen are perpetually on the offensive, determined to shatter national and continental unity, strangle sovereignty, and ensure the region remains dominated by pliant and brutal puppet regimes facilitating untrammelled Western economic rape and pillage. Yet, 7th POB’s supposed “cultural training, language proficiency, and indigenous approach” from 2017 onwards soundtracked an absolutely extraordinary collapse in the Empire’s clout throughout Africa. Drongo Company’s repeat attempt may end with Washington’s final, long-overdue retreat from the continent entirely.

_source.movement_abstract: 【Kit Klarenberg Substack 2026年8月报道】独立记者David Hundeyin披露，美国国防部在非洲司令部（AFRICOM）下设新心理战单位“Drongo Company”，旨在通过心理行动扩大对非洲大陆受众的影响力。该单位隶属于陆军第7心理战营，总部位于北卡罗来纳州布拉格堡。其命名灵感源自非洲长尾伯劳鸟，象征利用模仿与欺骗战术驱离对手。该单位成立背景为美军在非洲军事存在大幅缩减，2024年9月超1000名士兵撤离尼日尔，并放弃价值1亿美元无人机基地。官方文件指出，心理战核心在于利用心理因素引发特定情绪、态度和行为，目标包括激进组织及“敌对国家行为体”，实质指向俄罗斯与中国在非洲的政治经济活动。Drongo Company将利用传统媒体、社交媒体及新兴通信技术传播说服性信息，强调需具备区域文化知识与语言能力以确保信息可信度。AFRICOM指挥官Dagvin Anderson在国会证词中承认，过去十年美军在非洲态势缩减75%，导致影响力真空被中俄填补。该单位被视为美国试图在军事力量衰退背景下，通过信息战重夺叙事主导权的举措。

Independent journalist David Hundeyin has exposed the Pentagon’s new psychological operations unit targeting Africa, “Drongo Company”. Tasked with “expanding the military’s ability to influence foreign audiences” across the continent, its heavily hyped launch occurs against a backdrop of dramatically and irreversibly waning Western influence and power in every sphere across the continent. As Africans steadily rid themselves of unwelcome foreign occupiers and oppressors, the US is forced to rely on strategies of manipulation to stem the tide, which have already failed spectacularly. They will surely misfire yet again.
Based in Fort Bragg, North Carolina – home to AFRICOM – Drongo Company’s nickname is inspired by a bird native to Africa, known for precisely imitating other species’ warning calls, and using other deception tactics to drive other animals away from food. The Pentagon reportedly “selected the name to reflect the unit’s focus on influencing perceptions and behavior.” Fittingly, a May 2014 Science paper found the drongo can mimic other species’ sounds and manipulate adversaries with unparalleled, almost human sophistication.
Task & Purpose notes Drongo Company’s creation “comes amid a shift in US military strategy in Africa,” which is quite an understatement. Washington is on the run across the continent, with combat units and occupation forces being withdrawn from multiple countries over recent years. In September 2024, over 1,000 soldiers departed Niger, while a $100 million drone base was abandoned. An anti-ISIS mission in Nigeria controversially launched this March was abruptly terminated in July, due to a cataclysmic inability to achieve its objectives.
Drongo Company is an attempt by the Empire to reassert narrative dominance over Africa, as its military capabilities across the continent and beyond constantly shrink in size and potency. An official US Army report openly states, “the art of psyops relies on persuasion rather than physical force.” This entails the exploitation of “mental factors…to evoke specific emotions, attitudes and behaviors.” The ultimate goal “is to persuade enemy, neutral and friendly nations and forces to take favorable actions toward the US and its allies.”
Drongo Company’s official launch ceremony
An AFRICOM factsheet on psyops claims local campaigns are targeted at militant groups, such as Al Qaeda, Boko Haram, and ISIS. Parenthetical mention is also made to “malign state actors” being targets, in the context of advancing “US interests.” As a Military.com report acknowledges, this is a reference to “competition with foreign governments.” Specifically, “Russia and China have expanded their political, economic and security activities across Africa” in recent years, which the Empire has been singularly unable to counter via military force.
Drongo Company is thus being deployed for “an information contest that extends beyond conventional battlefields.” The Pentagon is extremely sensitive, however, to “skeptical audiences” seeing through their psyops. Military.com further notes while AFRICOM claims its psychological operations adhere strictly to US law and Pentagon policies prohibiting targeting US citizens, these prohibitions only apply to intended audiences. There are no mechanisms in place preventing Stateside spectators being deluged – theoretically illegally – with Drongo Company’s sophisticated, clandestine military psychological warfare offensives, especially online.
Quite some informational assault is planned. Drongo Company will wage its psyops campaigns via “both established and emerging communication technologies…[including] print media, radio broadcasts, text messaging, direct engagement, television programming, social media platforms, and online resources.” These information sources will be blitzed with “persuasive messages intended to change how selected audiences think or act.” The need to “ensure targeted audiences consider…messages credible” is of paramount importance. After all, “adversaries or skeptical audiences” will reflexively dismiss obvious “American propaganda”:
“Drongo Company’s effectiveness will depend on more than its ability to produce messages. Its soldiers will need regional and cultural knowledge, language skills, accurate intelligence and credible African partners capable of reaching communities that may distrust communications associated with the US military.”
‘Role Players’
Strikingly, Drongo Company is formally part of the US Army’s notorious 7th Psychological Operations Battalion. The Pentagon’s premier psychological warfare unit, since May 2022 7th POB has released a series of disturbing, abstract recruitment videos. In the first, dramatic, rapid cut scenes are interspersed with eerie, monochrome cartoon clips, backed by an aggressive soundtrack. All along, text on the screen proclaims:
“You’ll find us in the shadows, at the tip of the spear. War is evolving, and all the world’s a stage. Anything we touch is a weapon. We can deceive, persuade, change, influence, inspire…We are everywhere.”
Despite such ominous hype, Drongo Company’s activation suggests a longstanding, initially much-vaunted 7th POB unit previously “forged for Africa” operational from 2017 onwards fell far short of its bold objectives. In February that year, the US Army published an essay celebrating the new psyops division’s launch. It revealed how the unit’s operatives were deployed “into the gray zones of Africa where alliances can be fluid and the people are as diverse as the many landscapes,” following elaborate training exercises in Florida:
“Influencing a population to create lasting change when you don’t look, sound, or dress like that population is a tricky proposition. Cultural training, language proficiency, and an indigenous approach can go pretty far towards closing the gap, but true effectiveness is only achieved through airtight relationships with host nation partners.”
Hence, training saw 7th Psychological Operations Battalion operatives deployed to simulated environments in the fictional African nation of Conch Republic. Under the exercise’s auspices, “the government of Conch had requested support from the US Embassy” to combat “a bevy of societal problems from drug trafficking to domestic terrorism, to combat these ills.” It featured live-action components, in which US police and Navy operatives and African “civic leaders” were “role players”, with detailed characters.
Their roles included “local radio disc jockeys, roving reporters, and even the police” in the fictional African country, who “would ambush teams in broad daylight and attempt to gain information, curry favor, or even solicit a bribe to make a tough situation disappear.” A synthetic local social media infrastructure was also constructed – “a dynamic, reactive and proactive environment…with analogs to Facebook, Twitter, and even Craigslist.” Through this online nexus, the Battalion could “affect and inform” different Conch Republic audiences.
A role-played Conch Republic border security ‘interrogates’ 7th POB operative
The social media simulation reportedly “provided an invaluable feedback mechanism that showed which messages were heard and to what extent they were understood.” Elsewhere, “the unit broke new ground…through the use of new communications equipment and series development software,” utilising a variety of “information transmission devices…useful in influence campaigns.” Resultantly, 7th POB operatives could supposedly “hit the ground” when deployed to Africa, delivering “cogent, impactful” psyops “aimed right at the heart of the population”:
“By all accounts, the juice is worth the squeeze. Community leaders take pride in supporting a high caliber exercise, the partnered agencies have found unique ways to meet their own training objectives through the scenarios, and the teams heading out the door are better prepared; prepared to amplify African solutions to African challenges, and prepared to survive if the world falls down around them.”
‘Indigenous Approach’
The US Army essay on 7th POB’s then-new African assignment revealed, “there’s a saying in the PSYOP community” – “[Army Special Operations Forces] makes change happen. PSYOP makes change last.” A senior military advisor to the division boasted how 7th POB’s activities represented the apotheosis of US psychological operations – “a place where science and technique blend.” The essay bombastically concluded by characterising psyops as “the long game, where changes in behavior are measured not over a deployment, but often over years.”
Judged by this metric, the “long game” played by 7th POB throughout the continent over the past decade has been decisively lost. In May, AFRICOM commander Dagvin Anderson laid bare in Congressional testimony how a “75% reduction” in US military and intelligence “posture” regionally during this time – “coupled with a drawdown of allies in the region” – has produced a “black hole” in Africa. He lamented at length how this gaping chasm in Western dominance has been rapidly filled by China, Iran and Russia.
Beijing’s “aggressive investments” in Africa’s “mining, infrastructure, and transportation sectors” have supplanted Western control over “critical minerals and strategic infrastructure.” On top of major profit hits and supply chain disruption, China’s increasing domination in industrial fields reliant on these resources – ranging from “electric vehicles, consumer electronics, and advanced military technologies” – represents “a structural vulnerability for the US Defense Industrial Base.” Meanwhile, Russia’s rising economic and military footprint on the continent is “undermining US influence and limiting NATO’s reach on its southern flank.”
Anderson claimed Russian paramilitary forces “insulate and protect regimes” in Africa with which Moscow has close relations, “under the guise of counter-terrorism operations.” However, the AFRICOM chief contradictorily acknowledged the threat of extremist militancy throughout the region Russian military advisors seek to deter was very real. In particular, Anderson cited how Al Qaeda-affiliate JNIM aims to destabilise the revolutionary governments of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, to the “extent of securing the resources and trappings of a nation state” in the manner of ISIS.
AFRICOM’s commander neglected to mention how France and Ukraine have heavily supported JNIM’s counter-revolutionary activities in the Sahel. An April essay published by Militarnyi, Kiev’s most prominent military news site, makes clear the objective of these military and intelligence machinations is out-and-out regime change, explicitly in service of furthering the Empire’s interests in Africa. Drongo Company must be understood as the psychological warfare component of this proxy assault on the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), and continent more widely.
Evidently, Africans must remain vigilant. Counter-revolutionary forces seen and unseen are perpetually on the offensive, determined to shatter national and continental unity, strangle sovereignty, and ensure the region remains dominated by pliant and brutal puppet regimes facilitating untrammelled Western economic rape and pillage. Yet, 7th POB’s supposed “cultural training, language proficiency, and indigenous approach” from 2017 onwards soundtracked an absolutely extraordinary collapse in the Empire’s clout throughout Africa. Drongo Company’s repeat attempt may end with Washington’s final, long-overdue retreat from the continent entirely.

_source.content:
Though Sony and Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” had the second-biggest global opening weekend and made over NT$32.25 billion (US$1 billion) within its first six days the industry faces a profound corporate reckoning.
Five years prior, “Spider-Man: No Way Home” triggered an international standoff when Sony Pictures refused Beijing’s ultimatum to erase the Statue of Liberty. Sony CEO Tom Rothman stood firm, walking away from up to NT$10.97 billion in Chinese box-office revenue to safeguard a US icon.
However, 20th Century Fox’s “Bohemian Rhapsody” (2018) scrubbed more than two minutes of key LGBTQ+ content to satisfy Chinese gatekeepers. This contrast exposes Hollywood’s systemic habit of trading creative independence for access to large totalitarian markets — capitulating by default unless an executive draws a line.
As documented in PEN America’s landmark report, “Made in Hollywood, Censored by Beijing,” creative storytelling wields outsized influence over global culture by directly shaping public imagination.
Allowing a censorious regime to dictate what can be shown grants a hostile foreign power an invisible veto over global mass media. When filmmakers preemptively integrate a made-in-Beijing blueprint into creative development to secure Chinese capital and market quotas, severe commercial, artistic and expressive trade-offs must be dragged into open public debate.
This corporate posture creates a pipeline of compliance, where the CCP uses revenue-based extended deterrence to enforce widespread self-censorship. To preserve market access, Western studios systematically strip away LGBTQ+ identity and eliminate sensitive geopolitical topics like Tibet or sovereign symbols like the Taiwan flag.
Once distributed globally, these sanitized blockbusters provide soft-power validation to an expansionist, totalitarian regime executing severe human rights abuses. For audiences in Taiwan, this structural surrender is not merely a matter of compromised artistic integrity, it represents an active component of Beijing’s psychological and cognitive warfare.
Blueprint for surrender
By systematically scrubbing Taiwan’s sovereignty and distinct democratic identity from global screens, Hollywood subtly conditions the international community to accept the CCP’s narrative of territorial ownership before a single kinetic shot is ever fired.
The historical blueprint for this surrender was forged in the 1930s, when US studios prioritized German interests. As documented in Ben Urwand’s “The Collaboration,” studio moguls normalized a partnership with Nazi consul Georg Gyssling, actively weaponizing “Article 15” to kill anti-fascist projects, fire Jewish sales representatives and scrub Jews from film credits to protect European revenue.
This optimized pipeline resurfaced in late 1997, when TriStar’s “Seven Years in Tibet” and Disney’s “Kundun” challenged Beijing. Faced with retaliatory state bans and threats to its future theme park plans, Hollywood corporate boards resolved never again to fund mainstream pictures challenging Chinese state sovereignty.
This institutional freeze triggered an insidious ideological flip among icons who once championed democratic ideals. Former democracy advocate Jackie Chan declared, “Chinese people need to be controlled,” while Donnie Yen accepted a political appointment to the CPPCC and publicly labeled the 2019 Hong Kong pro-democracy movement a “riot.”
This co-optation serves as a stark cautionary tale for Taiwan regarding Beijing’s broader united front strategies, exposing how economic dependence converts celebrated cultural icons into vocal authoritarian surrogates. Western stars face equal public humiliation, exemplified by John Cena issuing a video apology in Mandarin on Weibo after referring to Taiwan as a “country” to protect “F9” (2021) revenues.
Consequently, the modern film industry institutes absolute self-censorship, treating the “Three Ts” (Taiwan, Tibet, Tiananmen) as unfinanceable liabilities. This compliance is managed by Beijing’s Central Propaganda Department and enforced directly within Los Angeles by private equity firms like Silver Lake and TPG Capital.
Self-censorship
Through their financial control of top talent agencies these equity funds preemptively kill sensitive scripts before they can ever trigger Chinese state retaliation. This manufactured climate permanently restricts the creative boundaries of the genre, while abandoning the millions of Chinese who want to hear authentic stories regardless of the political cost.
Through international relations theory, this self-censorship represents a textbook failure of extended deterrence. Since the CCP maintains a credible threat of economic punishment, frontline democracies like Taiwan receive a dangerous signal that Western economic dependency far outweighs ideological commitments.
Furthermore, when Taiwanese theatergoers witness powerful Western cultural institutions instantly folding to authoritarian financial pressure, it actively feeds insidious “America skepticism” and erodes public confidence in international democratic alliances.
The physical scars of this filter span decades of blockbusters: Marvel’s “Doctor Strange” (2016) whitewashed a Tibetan monk, and “Red Dawn” (2012) digitally swapped Chinese invaders for North Koreans. Most egregiously, the worldwide cut of “World War Z” (2013) scrubbed its Chinese virus origin to clear censors, rewriting it to originate in Taiwan.
In doing so, Hollywood completely erased author Max Brooks’ central, prophetic political thesis — modeled on the real-world 2000s SARS outbreak — that warned authoritarian press censorship creates the dark spaces required for local epidemics to morph into global pandemics. For Taiwan, which acted as the global community’s transparent whistleblower during real-world health crises while Beijing suppressed the truth, Hollywood’s script change was a malicious historical inversion.
Yet public blowback can force a reversal. Following intense domestic backlash and investor Tencent’s exit over the removal of Taiwan and Japan flags from Tom Cruise’s jacket in the initial “Top Gun: Maverick” (2022) trailer, Paramount restored the flags and grossed NT$48.38 billion globally without China, proving dependency is an illusion.
Liberalism vanishes
This pivotal victory demonstrates that the democratic ecosystem possesses the capacity to break free from authoritarian leverage, directly countering defeatist narratives within frontline societies. Similarly, “South Park” creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone successfully used counter-deterrence, mocking self-censorship in their episode “Band in China” (2019) and refusing to apologize when Beijing banned the show.
Domestically, Hollywood celebrates social justice and political resistance through figureheads like Mark Ruffalo and Steven Spielberg. Yet, facing Beijing, their vaunted liberalism vanishes under the weight of financial reward.
Spielberg co-founded DreamWorks SKG to master China’s censorship rules, while Disney spent US$5.5 billion to build the Shanghai Disney Resort. To protect that physical infrastructure, Disney systematically sanitized its global slate, culminating in tailoring “Mulan” (2020) to Chinese state-approved nationalism and explicitly offering “special thanks” in the credits to the very government bureaus operating the mass-internment camps in Xinjiang.
Stars who refuse the payday face harsh consequences: Richard Gere, Harrison Ford and Keanu Reeves were all systematically blacklisted, banned or scrubbed from streaming networks for voicing solidarity with Tibet. Native creators face equal censorship; when Chloe Zhao won the Best Director Oscar for “Nomadland” (2021), nationalists unearthed a 2013 interview where she called China a place of “lies everywhere,” prompting a total state media blackout and market blacklist.
Blueprint for change
The film industry requires aggressive structural reform to reverse Chinese censorship. First, Western governments must mandate annual SEC disclosures detailing all script changes made for foreign states. At the same time, creative unions must contractually bar studios from altering a film’s political framework for secondary markets.
Second, G7 nations should launch democratic cultural endowments and pooled cinematic credit facilities, offering low-interest production loans to blockbuster studios that commit to uncompromised global cuts.
Third, antitrust enforcers must separate talent agencies from cross-border private equity funds, stopping agents from preemptively sanitizing scripts.
Finally, streaming platforms must integrate interactive metadata tags detailing altered content, overseen by an independent cinematic auditing body applying public consumer warning labels to altered films to introduce an immediate reputational cost.
In the 1930s, studio heads rationalized working with the Nazi regime to protect commerce. Today, Hollywood’s supreme loyalty remains tied to foreign box-office returns that fund generous executive bonuses.
Hollywood’s capitulation to Chinese communists demonstrates that progressive values stop where authoritarian market barriers begin. Until policy and labor unions force financial transparency, the final cut of global mass media will belong to autocrats rather than artists. Free speech cannot survive in an industry that willingly “drinks poison to quench its thirst,” as the Chinese saying goes.
_source.movement_title: 好莱坞系统性自我审查迎合北京审查制度引发台湾主权认知战担忧
_source.movement_abstract: 文章指出好莱坞电影产业为进入中国市场，长期实施系统性自我审查，删除涉及台湾主权、西藏及LGBTQ+等敏感内容。索尼影业在《蜘蛛侠：崭新之日》中拒绝北京要求删除自由女神像的指令，与20世纪福克斯在《波西米亚狂想曲》中删减LGBTQ+内容形成对比。文章分析称，这种审查机制源于北京通过经济惩罚实施的延伸威慑，迫使西方制片厂在剧本开发阶段即剔除敏感议题，包括台湾、西藏和天安门等“三T”禁忌。历史案例显示，1930年代好莱坞曾为保护欧洲收入与纳粹德国合作，1997年后为规避中国禁令，迪士尼等公司主动调整内容。文章列举《奇异博士》《红色黎明》《僵尸世界大战》等影片修改内容以迎合中国审查，导致台湾主权叙事被抹除。文章警告，这种自我审查构成北京认知战的一部分，削弱国际社会对台湾民主身份的认知。文章建议西方政府强制披露剧本修改情况，G7国家设立民主文化基金，反垄断机构分离人才机构与跨境私募股权基金，流媒体平台引入内容修改元数据标签及消费者警告标签，以恢复创作自由并遏制中国审查影响。

Blueprint for change
The film industry requires aggressive structural reform to reverse Chinese censorship.
