_source.evidence: 文章核心内容是台湾AI实验室创办人杜奕瑾针对‘川习会’后台湾部分媒体舆论现象的分析。文章指出，部分台湾媒体在报道中美高层互动时，未依据白宫官方摘要，而是照搬中国官媒叙事，将美国的‘战略模糊’曲解为‘美国放弃台湾’，从而在认知层面配合了中国的舆论攻势。这属于典型的认知域对抗行动，即通过操控信息传播、利用媒体作为工具进行心理战和舆论战，属于具体的‘舆论攻击行动’或‘认知对抗动向’。虽然涉及台湾（非中国大陆），但在中国大陆认知域视角下，这属于外部势力（或内部渗透）针对中国核心利益（台湾问题）进行的认知域行动/动向，符合‘行动动向’中关于‘具体的舆论攻击行动’的定义。它不是单纯的理论政策发布，也不是军事演习或技术武器研发，更不是中国大陆作为被攻击方遭受的直接敌情事件（虽然涉及台湾，但文章重点在于描述一种舆论操作行为/动向），因此归类为‘行动动向’最为贴切。

_source.content:
印太戰略智庫執行長矢板明夫。(資料照)
近日中國旅外知名軍事博主「說真話的徐某人」在X平台爆料,過去曾收到來自中共情報單位派出的「中間人」招募,在網路打輿論戰攻擊台灣,還放出證據錄音檔,引發外界熱議。對此,印太戰略智庫執行長矢板明夫得知整件事後,得出「3個結論」,教大家如何判斷哪些KOL已經被中共收買!
矢板明夫21日深夜在臉書發文,「一名長期旅居海外、以軍事與國際評論聞名的華語網紅 『說真話的徐某人』公開了一段錄音,揭露曾有中國方面的中間人接觸過他,對方開出『每月4萬歐元』(約合新台幣148萬元)的條件,希望他配合進行對外宣傳。錄音內容相當直白。在某些議題上,可以『小罵大幫忙』,也就是在枝節問題上適度批評中國並不成問題,但有一道絕對不能碰的『紅線』,就是『不准批評習近平』。這則報導引發社會高度關注,也讓人不得不正視背後的現實。」
請繼續往下閱讀...
他接著說:「我認為至少可以得出三個結論。第一個結論,台灣網紅圈內一定早就有不少人被接觸過。這其實不難理解。中國連對歐洲網紅都願意砸下重金經營輿論,對於認知作戰最關鍵的戰場台灣,不可能什麼都不做。台灣與中國語言相通,而台灣又長期被北京視為核心利益之一。從成本效益來看,台灣網紅對中國而言,吸引力只會更高。」
「第二個結論,是金錢本身的誘惑。148萬元台幣一個月,在台灣網紅圈幾乎是神話級的收入。現實情況是,多數台灣網紅若能月收突破15萬,就已經足以被視為成功者。當報酬放大十倍,再搭配『又不是不能罵中國』這種話術,必然會有人失守。於是,我們開始看到一些網紅,在關鍵議題上,立場總是與北京保持高度一致。也有人在小事上偶爾批評中國,但一旦涉及台灣主權、民主價值或國際立場,立刻選邊站隊。這種『小罵大幫忙』的操作,若觀眾缺乏警覺,很容易被包裝所迷惑。」
「第三個結論,也是最重要的辨識線索:如何判斷誰可能已被收買?答案很簡單,就『看他敢不敢罵習近平』。中國是一個高度集權的體制,許多人的前途與命運,牢牢掌握在習近平一個人手中。已被收買的海外御用文人,若公開批評習近平,真正承擔風險的,往往不是他本人,而是其背後的『上線』。」
最後矢板明夫直言,「因此,當一個人能夠公開直指習近平志大才疏、目光短淺、沉迷個人崇拜、擅長整人卻不擅長治國,甚至毫不掩飾地給出最嚴厲的道德評價時,反而構成了一種清楚的判斷依據。『紅線』這麼清楚,希望有助於讓更多人分辨出哪些是在配合中共宣傳的聲音。」

_source.movement_abstract: 中國旅外軍事博主「說真話的徐某人」爆料曾遭中共情報單位招募，以每月 4 萬歐元條件要求配合輿論戰，並設定「不准批評習近平」為紅線。印太戰略智庫執行長矢板明夫針對此事提出三點結論：首先，台灣因語言相通且被視為核心利益，網紅圈內早有不少人被接觸；其次，高額報酬結合「小罵大幫忙」的話術，易使部分網紅在關鍵議題上選邊站隊；最後，判斷是否被收買的最重要線索在於是否敢公開批評習近平。矢板明夫指出，若有人能嚴厲評價習近平，反而證明其未被收買，此標準有助於公眾辨識配合中共宣傳的聲音。
_source.title: 誰被中共收買？ 矢板明夫教用「一條紅線」秒辨網紅親中勢力
_source.trans_cont:
印太战略智库执行长矢板明夫。（资料照）
近日，中国旅外知名军事博主「说真话的徐某人」在X平台爆料，过去曾收到来自中共情报单位派出的「中间人」招募，在网络上进行舆论战攻击台湾，还放出证据录音档，引发外界热议。对此，印太战略智库执行长矢板明夫得知整件事后，得出「3个结论」，教大家如何判断哪些KOL已经被中共收买！
矢板明夫21日深夜在脸书发文，「一名长期旅居海外、以军事与国际评论闻名的华语网红『说真话的徐某人』公开了一段录音，揭露曾有中国方面的中间人接触过他，对方开出『每月4万欧元』（约合新台币148万元）的条件，希望他配合进行对外宣传。录音内容相当直白。在某些议题上，可以『小骂大帮忙』，也就是在枝节问题上适度批评中国并不成问题，但有一道绝对不能碰的『红线』，就是『不准批评习近平』。这则报道引发社会高度关注，也让人不得不正视背后的现实。」
请继续往下阅读...
他接着说：「我认为至少可以得出三个结论。第一个结论，台湾网红圈内一定早就有人被接触过。其实并不难理解。中国连对欧洲网红都愿意砸下重金经营舆论，对于认知作战最关键战场台湾，不可能什么都不做。台湾与中国语言相通，而台湾又长期被北京视为核心利益之一。从成本效益来看，台湾网红对于中国而言，吸引力只会更高。」
「第二个结论，是金钱本身的诱惑。148万元台币一个月，在台湾网红圈几乎是神话级的收入。现实情况是，多数台湾网红若能月收突破15万，就足以被视为成功者。当报酬放大十倍，再搭配『又不是不能骂中国』这种话术，必然有人失守。于是，我们开始看到一些网红，在关键议题上，立场总是与北京保持高度一致。也有人在小事上偶尔批评中国，但一旦涉及台湾主权、民主价值或国际立场，立刻选边站队。这种『小骂大帮忙』的操作，若观众缺乏警觉，很容易被包装所迷惑。」
「第三个结论，也是最重要的辨识线索：如何判断谁可能已被收买？答案很简单，就『看他敢不敢骂习近平』。中国是一个高度集权的体制，许多人的前途与命运，牢牢掌握在习近平一个人手中。已被收买海外御用文人，若公开批评习近平，真正承担风险的，往往不是他本人，而是其背后的『上线』。」
最后矢板明夫直言，「因此，当一个人能够公开直指习近平志大才疏、目光短浅、沉迷个人崇拜、擅长整人却不擅长治国，甚至毫不掩饰地给出最严厉的道德评价时，反而构成了一种清楚的判断依据。『红线』这么清楚，希望有助于让更多人分辨出哪些是在配合中共宣传的声音。」

_source.content:
The timing is almost too perfect to ignore.
The very week Congress is preparing to reopen MKUltra — one of the darkest chapters in American intelligence history — reports claim documents tied to MKUltra and the
suddenly became the center of a fight involving the CIA, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, and Congress.
According to
, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence denied claims that the CIA “raided” Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard’s office.
But the denial did not erase the larger question. Rep.
, who chairs the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets,
connected to JFK and MKUltra were taken from ODNI’s possession. The DNI’s office disputed the word “raid.”
Fine. Let Washington argue over the word.
Was it a raid? Was it a transfer? Was it a seizure? Was it “routine handling of documents?”
Call it whatever you want. If records tied to JFK and MKUltra were removed, disputed, returned, preserved, or fought over behind closed doors, the American people deserve to know exactly what happened, because we are not talking about ordinary records.
We are talking about files connected to the assassination of an American president and a CIA mind-control program that used drugs, psychological manipulation, and human experimentation.
And again, the timing is almost too perfect to ignore.
Luna’s task force exists to examine long-buried federal secrets. Reporting from
said she had announced a May hearing on MKUltra. So the same week Congress is preparing to put MKUltra under a microscope, documents connected to MKUltra reportedly become the center of a fight involving the CIA, the DNI, and Congress?
What are the chances?
Seriously. What are the chances?
MKUltra was not a fever dream from a man in a tinfoil hat. It was real. The CIA really did experiment on the human mind. The government really did explore drugs, hypnosis, psychological manipulation, chemical testing, and behavior modification.
Americans were told for years that only crazy people believed stories like that.
Then the documents came out.
Then the Senate investigated it.
Then the conspiracy theory became a government record.
In 1977, the Senate held hearings titled “Project MKULTRA, The CIA’s Program of Research in Behavioral Modification.”
That alone should stop every American in their tracks. This was not some harmless Cold War research project tucked away in a dusty archive. This was the intelligence world exploring the manipulation of consciousness itself.
People were drugged. People were studied. People were used. Some did not consent. Some did not even know they had become test subjects in experiments tied to the intelligence world.
That should chill every American to the bone.
And now, decades later, while Congress tries to drag these secrets back into the light, we are hearing about documents connected to MKUltra being fought over again?
Excuse me?
I thought this was all ancient history. I thought the files were mostly destroyed. I thought there was nothing left to see. I thought everyone still asking questions was just a “conspiracy theorist.”
So why are there allegedly boxes of records still floating around inside the intelligence system?
That is the question.
And it is not just about history. It is about power.
The Director of National Intelligence is supposed to sit over the intelligence community. Tulsi Gabbard is not some random citizen filing a FOIA request. This is the top intelligence office in the country.
So if documents connected to the CIA, JFK, and MKUltra were in that orbit while Congress was demanding transparency, why would anyone inside the system think those records should be moved, hidden, controlled, or disputed?
Who is really in charge here?
Is the president in charge? Is Congress in charge? Is the DNI in charge? Or do these agencies operate like permanent governments unto themselves, deciding what gets released, what gets buried, what gets “lost,” and what gets quietly moved when the heat gets too close?
This is why Americans do not trust these institutions anymore.
It is not because people are stupid. It is not because everyone has lost their minds. It is because every time the public gets close to the truth, suddenly there is another denial, another classification excuse, another missing file, another destroyed record, and another official telling us, “You do not need to know that.”
No. We do need to know.
Because MKUltra proved something many Americans never wanted to believe: Powerful institutions are absolutely capable of lying to the public while doing horrifying things behind closed doors.
And once that truth settles in, it changes how you look at everything.
It changes how you look at government secrecy.
It changes how you look at intelligence agencies.
It changes how you look at the phrase “trust the experts.”
And it should absolutely change how Christians view the modern push toward psychedelics.
President Donald Trump recently signed an
accelerating research and access pathways for psychedelic drugs as potential treatments for serious mental illness. The White House order specifically mentions psychedelic drugs, including ibogaine compounds, and directs federal agencies to facilitate access under Right to Try pathways.
The FDA has also
actions following the order to support the development of perception-altering psychedelic medications.
The official language sounds compassionate. It talks about veterans, trauma, serious mental illness, research, treatment, and hope.
I am not attacking veterans who are hurting. I am not saying people with trauma should be abandoned. I am not saying every doctor or researcher involved in this field is evil.
But I am saying this: The federal government does not get to act naïve about the power of psychedelics on the human mind.
They know.
They know because they studied them.
They know because they tested them.
They know because they used them.
MKUltra was not a theory. It was a warning.
So when the same federal system that once explored psychedelics for control, interrogation, manipulation, and behavior modification now tells Americans, “Trust us, this is about healing,” Christians should not check their brains at the door.
We should remember history.
If psychedelics were powerful enough for intelligence agencies to study them for control decades ago, why would we pretend they are spiritually neutral now?
Why would we assume they only open the door to healing and never to deception?
Why would a nation that has rejected Christ now look for salvation through chemicals, altered states, clinical mysticism, and government-approved spiritual experiences?
That is the deeper issue.
This is not just about medicine. It is about the human mind. It is about consciousness. It is about spiritual vulnerability.
And Christians had better wake up.
The Bible tells believers to be sober-minded and watchful. That command matters in a generation being told that altered consciousness is healing, enlightenment, revelation, and progress.
Compassion for suffering people is good. Blind trust in powerful systems is not.
And this story gets even bigger when you look at the world we are living in now.
MKUltra happened in an age of primitive tools. Today, we live under artificial intelligence, facial recognition, biometric surveillance, algorithmic manipulation, behavioral prediction, digital currencies, psychological profiling, and smartphones that track nearly every movement, location, purchase, and interaction of billions of people.
That is not science fiction.
That is infrastructure.
If intelligence agencies were experimenting on consciousness in the 1950s, 1960s, and 1970s, what should we assume modern governments, corporations, and military systems are capable of now with AI?
Every major technology eventually gets weaponized.
The airplane became a bomber. Television became propaganda. The internet became surveillance. Social media became psychological warfare. Smartphones became tracking devices.
And now artificial intelligence is being handed to governments, corporations, and unelected global systems with almost no restraint.
So forgive me if I do not automatically believe, “Don’t worry, everything is fine.”
Everything is not fine.
If MKUltra taught us anything, it is that powerful agencies will hide horrifying things from the American people when they believe the mission justifies the crime.
So yes, Americans should ask hard questions.
What is in those documents?
Why were they allegedly taken?
Who ordered it?
Who knew?
Why now?
And why does transparency only seem to happen when Congress threatens a subpoena?
This is not normal. This is not boring. This is not some dusty history lesson from the Cold War.
This is a living example of how secrecy protects power.
And if the same machine that buried the truth yesterday is still fighting over documents today, then Christians and Americans should not yawn.
We should demand answers.
Because a nation that refuses to learn from MKUltra is a nation ready to be manipulated again.
And this time, the tools are far more powerful.

_source.movement_title: MKUltra 文件争议再起：警惕情报机构隐瞒真相与迷幻药风险
_source.movement_abstract: 文章指出，在国会准备重启对 MKUltra 计划的审查之际，与该计划及 JFK 暗杀相关的文件突然成为 CIA、国家情报总监办公室（ODNI）与国会之间争议的焦点。尽管 ODNI 否认了“突袭”说法，但文件被移除、争夺或转移的事实引发了公众对情报机构隐瞒真相的强烈质疑。文章强调 MKUltra 是真实存在的意识操控实验，涉及药物与人体实验，并警示当前政府推动迷幻药合法化用于治疗的精神风险，认为历史表明权力机构可能利用此类物质进行控制。结合现代 AI 与监控技术的飞速发展，作者警告若缺乏透明度和问责，强大的情报系统可能再次掩盖恐怖行径，呼吁民众保持警惕，要求政府交代文件去向及事件真相，防止历史重演。
_source.title: Op-Ed: Tulsi Gabbard, the CIA, And the MKUltra Files - What Are They Hiding?
_source.trans_cont:
时机几乎完美到让人无法忽视。
就在国会准备重新审视MKUltra——美国情报史上最为黑暗的篇章之一——的那周，有报道称与MKUltra和
的文件突然成为CIA、国家情报总监办公室和国会之间争执的中心。
据
报道，国家情报总监办公室否认了CIA“突袭”国家情报总监图尔西·加巴德办公室的说法。
但这种否认并没有消除更大的疑问。众议员
，主持国会解密联邦机密特别监督委员会，
称与肯尼迪和MKUltra相关的文件是从国家情报总监办公室手中被拿走的。国家情报总监办公室则质疑“突袭”这个词的准确性。
好吧，让华盛顿的人们争论这个词吧。
这是突袭吗？是转移吗？是没收吗？还是“文件的常规处理”？
叫它什么都可以。如果与肯尼迪和MKUltra相关的记录被移走、争议、归还、保存或在幕后被争夺，美国人民有权利知道到底发生了什么，因为我们谈论的不是普通的文件。
我们谈论的是与一位美国总统遇刺和一个使用药物、心理操控和人体实验的CIA思想控制计划相关的文件。
再次强调，时机几乎完美到让人无法忽视。
卢娜的特别委员会旨在审查长期被掩盖的联邦机密。据
报道，她宣布将在5月举行关于MKUltra的听证会。因此，当国会准备将MKUltra置于显微镜下时，与MKUltra相关的文件却据报道再次成为CIA、国家情报总监和国会之间的争斗中心？
这可能性有多大？
认真地说，这可能性有多大？
MKUltra并不是一个戴锡箔帽的人的幻想。它是真实的。CIA确实对人类大脑进行了实验。政府确实研究了药物、催眠、心理操控、化学测试和行为改造。
多年来，美国人被告知只有疯子才会相信这样的故事。
然后文件被公开了。
然后参议院对此进行了调查。
然后阴谋论变成了政府记录。
1977年，参议院举行了名为“MKULTRA项目，CIA的行为改造研究计划”的听证会。
仅这一点就足以让每个美国人都停下脚步。这不是一个藏在尘封档案中的无害冷战研究项目。这是情报界在探索意识本身的操控。
人们被下药了。人们被研究了。人们被利用了。有些人没有同意。有些人甚至不知道自己成为了与情报界相关的实验对象。
这应该让每个美国人都感到寒意。
而现在，几十年后，当国会试图将这些秘密重新带入阳光之下时，我们又听说与MKUltra相关的文件再次成为争斗的焦点？
请原谅？
我以为这一切都是过去的事了。我以为这些文件大多已经被销毁了。我以为已经没有什么可看了。我以为还在问问题的人只是“阴谋论者”。
那么，为什么据说仍有大量文件在情报系统内部游荡？
这就是问题所在。
这不仅仅关乎历史，更关乎权力。
国家情报总监应该监督整个情报界。图尔西·加巴德并不是一个随意的公民提交信息公开请求的人。这是这个国家最高级别的情报机构。
因此，如果与CIA、肯尼迪和MKUltra相关的文件在国会要求透明度时处于这个体系中，为什么有人会认为这些文件应该被移动、隐藏、控制或争议？
到底谁真正掌权？
是总统？是国会？是国家情报总监？还是这些机构像独立的政府一样运作，决定什么信息可以发布、什么信息可以埋藏、什么信息可以“丢失”，什么信息在压力逼近时可以悄悄转移？
这就是为什么美国人不再信任这些机构。
并不是因为人们愚蠢，也不是因为每个人都失去了理智。而是因为每当公众接近真相时，突然又出现另一个否认、另一个分类借口、另一个失踪的文件、一个被销毁的记录，以及另一个官员告诉我们：“你不需要知道这些。”
不，我们需要知道。
因为MKUltra证明了很多人不愿相信的事实：强大的机构完全有能力在幕后做可怕的事情，同时对公众撒谎。
一旦这个真相深入人心，它会改变你对一切的看法。
它会改变你对政府保密的看法。
它会改变你对情报机构的看法。
它会改变你对“相信专家”这句话的看法。
它也应该彻底改变基督徒对现代向迷幻药物推进的态度。
唐纳德·特朗普总统最近签署了一项
，加速迷幻药物作为治疗严重精神疾病潜在疗法的研究和获取途径。白宫的命令特别提到了迷幻药物，包括伊博格aine化合物，并指示联邦机构在“右试”途径下促进获取。
食品药品监督管理局（FDA）也
采取了行动，以支持感知改变型迷幻药物的发展。
官方语言听起来充满同情。它谈论了退伍军人、创伤、严重精神疾病、研究、治疗和希望。
我不是在攻击那些正在受苦的退伍军人。我不是在说有创伤的人应该被抛弃
_source.trans_title: MKUltra 文件争议再起：警惕情报机构隐瞒真相与迷幻药风险
_source.evidence: 文章主要讨论美国国内关于CIA MKUltra计划文件的争议、国会听证会以及特朗普政府关于致幻剂研究的行政命令。虽然文章涉及了心理战、意识控制等与认知域相关的概念，但其核心事件完全发生在美国国内，属于美国内部的政治丑闻、历史解密争议及政策讨论。文章并未涉及中国大陆（作为被攻击对象或相关方）的敌情事件，也没有描述针对中国的认知域行动、演习、力量建设或技术武器化。根据标签定义，[涉我事件]要求涉及中国大陆，[行动动向]通常指具体的对抗行动，而本文属于美国内部事务。因此，该文章虽然属于广义的认知域话题（心理战历史），但不符合针对中国大陆的具体分类标签，应归为[其他]。

_source.content:
The landmark 2016 arbitral ruling on the West Philippine Sea observed its 10th anniversary, with senior military officials and security experts warning that the country is already facing a “political and informational war” marked by cyberattacks, disinformation, and foreign influence operations tied to tensions in the disputed waters.
The warnings came during a forum organized by Stratbase Institute and Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung on AFP modernization, where the experts urged expanding military modernization beyond traditional weapons platforms to include cyber defense, intelligence, strategic communications, and cognitive warfare capabilities.
AFP chief of staff Gen. Romeo Brawner, through his acting deputy chief of staff Lt. Gen. Arvin Lagamon, said in his keynote address that the Philippines must adopt a mindset that “we are already at war. Not yet a kinetic war, but the political war, the economic war, and more importantly, the cyber and informational war are already going on,” Lagamon said.
Constant bullying
He noted that the Philippines continued to confront China’s “daily illegal, coercive, aggressive, deceptive, destructive, and bullying” activities in the West Philippine Sea, alongside “their use of sharp power through their United Front Works and their malign information and foreign influence information.”
His remarks echoed growing concern over the role of disinformation and cognitive warfare in the country’s maritime dispute with China, which continues to dismiss the 2016 arbitral ruling that invalidated its sweeping claims over the South China Sea.
“Every day, efforts to undermine and discredit the ruling persist,” Stratbase president Victor Andres “Dindo” Manhit said.
“In recent years, the country has faced sustained asymmetric gray zone challenges across multiple domains: Water cannons and ramming incidents in the maritime space, dangerous maneuvers and flares in the airspace, and information warfare in the digital domain.”
_source.movement_title: 菲军方警告南海争端已演变为政治与认知战争
_source.movement_abstract: 2016 年南海仲裁案裁决十周年之际，菲律宾军方高层与安全专家发出警告，指出菲中争端已演变为涵盖网络攻击、虚假信息及外国干预的政治与认知战争。在由 Stratbase 研究所与康拉德·阿登纳基金会举办的关于菲律宾武装部队现代化论坛上，专家呼吁将军事现代化扩展至网络防御、情报及战略传播领域。菲律宾武装部队副总参谋长拉加蒙少将强调，尽管尚未爆发动能战争，但政治、经济、网络及信息战已全面展开。菲方持续面临中国在南海的非法、胁迫及霸凌行为，并遭受“锐实力”及恶意信息活动的冲击。战略基地研究所总裁曼希特指出，各方每日都在努力削弱仲裁案效力，菲律宾正面临海空域及数字领域的多重不对称灰色地带挑战。
_source.title: Arbitral ruling turns 10, ‘war’ ongoing
_source.trans_cont:
具有里程碑意义的2016年南海仲裁裁决迎来十周年纪念，高级军事官员和安全专家警告称，该国已面临一场以网络攻击、虚假信息和与争议海域紧张局势相关的外国影响力行动为特点的“政治与信息战争”。这些警告出现在由战略研究所和孔拉德-阿登纳基金会组织的关于菲律宾武装部队现代化论坛上，专家们敦促将军事现代化扩展至传统武器平台之外，包括网络安全、情报、战略传播和认知战能力。

菲律宾武装部队参谋长罗梅奥·布拉诺将军通过其代理副参谋长阿尔文·拉加蒙少将表示，在主旨演讲中指出，菲律宾必须树立“我们已处于战争中”的思维模式。拉加蒙表示：“我们尚未进入动能战争，但政治战争、经济战争，更重要的是网络和信息战争，已经展开。”

他指出，菲律宾持续面临中国在南海的“每日非法、强制、侵略、欺骗、破坏和欺凌”行为，以及“通过统一战线工作实施的强硬手段和有害信息及外国影响力信息”的使用。他的言论呼应了日益增长的担忧，即虚假信息和认知战在菲律宾与中国海上争端中的作用，而中国仍拒绝承认2016年裁决所否定的其对南海的广泛主张。

“每天，企图削弱和诋毁裁决的努力仍在持续，”战略研究所所长维克多·安德烈斯·“丁多”·马尼特说。

“近年来，该国在多个领域面临持续的非对称灰色地带挑战：在海洋空间的水炮和冲撞事件，在空域的危险机动和闪光弹，以及在数字领域的信息战。”
_source.trans_title: 菲军方警告南海争端已演变为政治与认知战争
_source.evidence: 文章核心内容围绕2016年南海仲裁案十周年，重点描述了菲律宾军方及专家对中国在南海及认知域（信息战、虚假信息、认知战）所采取的‘日常’对抗行动的指控。文中明确提到中国使用‘统一战线工作’、‘恶意信息’、‘外国影响力行动’以及‘水炮、冲撞’等具体手段进行‘政治战、经济战、网络和信息战’。这符合‘涉我事件’的定义，即涉及中国大陆作为被攻击对象或相关方（在此语境下是被指控的发起方，但属于针对中国的敌情/对抗事件描述），且内容聚焦于具体的对抗行动和敌情态势，而非单纯的演习、理论发布或机构成立。虽然涉及‘认知战’概念，但文章主旨是描述针对中国的持续性对抗行动（Action/Incident），而非单纯的技术研发或理论探讨。

_source.content:
Peter Thiel, image Wikipedia.
General Michael Flynn, Trump’s former National Security advisor, boasted to the Young America Foundation soon after Trump’s first election victory in 2016, that the President’s campaign had been a quasi-military “insurgency” run by “digital soldiers”.
That same year the NATO Strategic Communications Centre of Excellence’s official journal
published a paper entitled ‘It’s Time to Embrace Memetic Warfare’.
Its author was Jeff Giesea, an investor and political operative, who had run companies on behalf of pro-Trump billionaire Peter Thiel, co-founder of defence surveillance giant Palantir and
of convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
At the time Giesea defined memetic warfare, a term he coined, as “a subset of information operations or psychological warfare tailored to social media”.
To illustrate its applications, he drew on the expertise of a co-contributor he described as “an annoying gadfly or guerrilla warrior, depending on one’s perspective”: far-right activist and disinformation operator Charles C. Johnson.
The paper proposed methods by which to undermine ISIS: “systematically lure and entrap”  recruiters; subvert its messaging via “fake ‘sockpuppet’ accounts” – online personas manufactured to simulate grassroots support or opposition – and “expose and harass people” within its funding network, “including their family members”.
To the editors of the NATO journal, these may have appeared as novel strategic prescriptions. In fact, they had already appeared – in a different context entirely.
In 2011, hackers breached the servers of HBGary Federal, a private US intelligence contractor, and leaked internal documents revealing a proposed operation – developed with involvement from Thiel’s data company Palantir – to deploy near-identical tactics against trade unions, journalists and left-wing activists on American soil.
This reporter was among those who covered the breach at the time, and who first drew public attention to Palantir’s role in it — the beginning of more than a decade tracking the network this piece describes.
The proposal included fabricating fake online personas, planting false information, and running coordinated harassment campaigns to discredit targets. Palantir suspended the employees involved and issued an apology, but the documents had already established that this tactical repertoire existed, was operational, and ran through Thiel’s own firm.
Those tactics had been developed and deployed over years by a loose network of far-right organisations – funded, in part, by figures directly connected to Thiel.
That infrastructure centred on a cluster of white supremacist and hard-right online platforms – among them the neo-Nazi publication
— covertly funded, according to participants, by Giesea. The same platforms served as testing grounds for the harassment campaigns, disinformation operations and memetic tactics that Giesea would later present to a NATO-affiliated journal as a respectable strategic toolkit.
Connecting those platforms to Thiel’s wider network was a single figure: Andrew Auernheimer, a hacker and neo-Nazi provocateur known online as “Weev”. His ties to Thiel had been rumoured in leaked Epstein correspondence, but had never previously been corroborated. They can now be established — through Auernheimer’s own private statements and a decade of documented network activity — for the first time.
Auernheimer was, in effect, a bridge. He moved between the anarchic image-board subcultures of the early internet and organised white supremacist movements. He connected the PayPal and Palantir milieu around Thiel to the alt-right he helped create and harness. And he linked the first generation of online harassment operations to the contemporary influence networks that today increasingly shape mainstream political discourse.
In Discord server logs – a messaging platform used widely by gaming and political communities – as
by journalist Luke O’Brien in his 2020 investigation into Thiel’s development of the alt-right, Auernheimer described Giesea as “a major investor providing help to racists”. O’ Brien reported that an online alias used by Giesea had encouraged donors to give money to white nationalist and neo-Nazi organizations.
Giesea initially denied this. When confronted with evidence of a $5,000 donation to the white supremacist organisation led by notorious neo-Nazi Richard Spencer, he replied: “No comment.”
Giesea’s financial support for the neo-Nazi platform
along with other associated projects run by Auernheimer and Johnson has since been claimed by other participants in those far-right networks.
One identified Epstein attorney Alan Dershowitz as another Epstein associate involved in the Giesea project during his producing role on Mike Cernovich’s 2016 documentary
– a film featuring Auernheimer, Johnson and Milo Yiannopoulos.
Giesea denied the claims by participants in these neo-Nazi networks, telling
: “I have never supported Weev or the Daily Stormer. I have always found the Daily Stormer and its orbit vile and reprehensible.”
However, he confirmed that he had engaged with Aurnheimer. He said that this was limited to a single occasion: “My only interaction with Weev was a single, brief exchange while conducting research for a NATO paper on memetic warfare. At the time, I barely knew who he was, only that he was a notorious internet troll. I asked how he would approach trolling ISIS. That was the full extent of it. There was no funding, no relationship, and no alignment of any kind.”
Like Johnson, Weev served as an operational connector, moving between overlapping worlds that were, in other contexts, kept separate – the anarchic image-board subcultures of the early internet, white supremacist organising, the investment and intelligence networks around Thiel, and the broader influence ecosystems that shaped the 2016 political cycle and its aftermath.
Auernheimer’s elevation was made possible by such things as 4chan, the image-board platform that served as an incubator of memes, organised harassment campaigns known as “raids”, and novel forms of information warfare.
He was also a prolific editor of
, a wiki that catalogued 4chan-era internet culture and its developing repertoire of tactics.
Auernheimer gained early notoriety for using an Amazon exploit to flag LGBT materials as inappropriate in what he characterised as a strike against “the hypocracy [sic] of the gay community” – and for founding trolling collectives from which he recruited operatives for more consequential ventures.
After being indicted by the Department of Justice (DOJ) for exploiting a vulnerability in AT&T’s systems to extract exposed data of more than 100,000 customers, which he shared with the outlet
, he became a temporarily useful ersatz hero of civil liberties campaigners.
As with much else involving Thiel’s network, Aurenheimer’s role was initially concealed until referenced in leaked correspondence.
On 17 November 2014, the technologist Vincenzo Iozzo emailed the financier Jeffrey Epstein, alerting him that a novel hedge fund strategy he and Epstein had been developing was already being executed by Auernheimer, reportedly funded by Thiel:
“I’ve heard rumors that Thiel (who I believe you know) was bankrolling this dude: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weev to do similar things.”
Auernheimer had effectively confirmed his relationship with Thiel six months earlier in what he believed to be a private conversation.
“I have run a hedge fund, I am starting another one, and it is not nearly as regulated,” Weev stated, having separately referenced “a meeting with Peter Thiel’s right hand this week”.
In the same exchange, he spoke warmly of the eBay founder Pierre Omidyar, who played a central role in PayPal’s creation alongside Thiel: “I’ve met Pierre, I like Pierre, and he’s a friend of a close friend.”
In November 2011, Boris Nikolic – a biotech investor later named as a trustee in Epstein’s will – wrote to Epstein linking to a
article on 4chan’s political influence, noting: “The potential for manipulation is huge.”
The email followed Epstein’s first meeting with Chris Poole, 4chan’s founder. Days later, 4chan launched its /pol/ board – a “Politically Incorrect” forum that would become a central organising space for online far-right radicalisation.
The /pol/ board subsequently served as a primary incubator for GamerGate, the 2014 online harassment campaign directed primarily at women in the games industry. Auernheimer and Yiannopoulos were both instrumentally involved in driving elements of that campaign.
Auernheimer came from the same 4chan ecosystem that had given rise to Anonymous, but from an ideologically opposite direction: he played no part in its broadly leftist anti-authoritarian campaigns.
Soon after he was released from prison – his chest now adorned with a massive swastika tattoo – in 2014.
GamerGate and the constituency it mobilised later migrated to 8chan, the image-board founded by Auernheimer’s associate Frederick Brennan, who also contributed to
. 8chan went on to function as a central dissemination space for QAnon as it continued to embed itself in mainstream Republican politics.
By 2016, Auernheimer was writing to an associate that he was “working on facial recognition, specifically about black people”. In 2017, Charles Johnson announced on Facebook that he was “building algorithms to ID all the illegal immigrants for the deportation squads”.
Clearview AI – the facial recognition company that subsequently expanded the capabilities of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) – launched in 2018, seed-funded by Thiel, operating under Johnson’s Giesea-funded software framework WeSearchr, and represented in legal matters by Aurenheimer’s longtime lawyer, Tor Ekeland.
Johnson, Auernheimer, Giesea, Yiannopoulos, Dershowitz and Thiel did not respond to requests for comment.
Ekeland objected to the allegation that Auernheimer used an “exploit” on AT&T, telling
: “All that happened was his alleged co-conspirator Daniel Spitler wrote a script to access non password protected, publicly facing information – email addresses, on an unsecured server.”
In 2016, Jeffrey Epstein wrote to Peter Thiel summarising what he saw as the political opportunity opened by the Brexit vote: “return to tribalism. counter to globalisation. amazing new alliances.” This, he concluded, was “just the beginning.”
What the documented record shows across a decade is a consistent pattern.
Tactics developed in far-right corners of internet culture – harassment campaigns, disinformation operations, sockpuppet networks, memetic influence campaigns – were progressively absorbed into elite political and strategic discourse, sometimes through the same operators who first deployed them.
Far from an anomaly, the NATO
paper Giesea co-authored with Johnson was a culmination of this activity.
As General Flynn’s son, Michael Flynn Jr., boasted last year: “The public has no idea how massive our Digital Army is.”
_source.movement_title: 蒂尔网络与极右翼：模因战如何渗透美国政治
_source.movement_abstract: 文章揭露了彼得·蒂尔（Peter Thiel）及其关联网络在塑造美国政治话语中的角色。前国家安全顾问迈克尔·弗林曾将特朗普竞选比作准军事“叛乱”，而北约战略传播中心期刊发表的一篇关于“模因战”的论文，其作者杰夫·吉西亚曾受雇于蒂尔。该论文提出的针对ISIS的战术，实则在2011年已被蒂尔的数据公司帕兰提尔（Palantir）用于针对工会和左翼活动家的类似行动。黑客安德鲁·奥恩海默（Weev）作为关键连接点，将蒂尔的资本与极右翼平台（如4chan、Daily Stormer）及“游戏门”等骚扰运动联系起来。文章指出，从极右翼的骚扰、虚假信息到后来的Clearview AI人脸识别技术，这些战术逐渐被精英政治战略吸收，形成了从网络亚文化向主流政治渗透的十年模式。
_source.title: The Neo-Nazi Enforcer Who Helped Build Peter Thiel’s Online Influence Empire
_source.trans_cont:
彼得·蒂尔，图片来自维基百科。
特朗普的前国家安全顾问迈克尔·弗林在特朗普2016年首次当选总统后不久，向青年美国基金会吹嘘称，总统的竞选活动是一场由“数字士兵”领导的准军事“游击战”。
同年，北约战略传播卓越中心的官方期刊发表了一篇题为《是时候拥抱模因战争了》的文章。
作者是杰夫·吉塞亚，一位投资者和政治操盘手，他曾代表支持特朗普的亿万富翁彼得·蒂尔（彼得·蒂尔是国防监控巨头帕兰蒂尔的联合创始人）以及被定罪的性侵者杰弗里·爱泼斯坦运营公司。
当时，吉塞亚将模因战争定义为“信息行动或心理战的一个子集，专门针对社交媒体”。
为了说明其应用，他引用了一位合著者的专业知识，这位合著者被他描述为“一个令人讨厌的苍蝇或游击战士，取决于你的视角”：极右翼活动家和虚假信息操作者查尔斯·C·约翰逊。
该论文提出了削弱“伊斯兰国”（ISIS）的方法：“系统地引诱并诱捕”招募者；通过“假‘傀儡’账户”颠覆其信息传播——这些在线身份是制造出来的，以模拟基层支持或反对；并“揭露并骚扰”其资金网络中的人，“包括他们的家人”。
对于该北约期刊的编辑来说，这些可能看起来像是新颖的战略建议。实际上，这些方法早已出现——只是在完全不同的背景下。
2011年，黑客入侵了HBGary联邦公司的服务器，泄露了内部文件，揭示了一项由蒂尔的数据公司帕兰蒂尔参与制定的计划，该计划提议在美国本土对工会、记者和左翼活动人士使用几乎相同的战术。
这位记者当时曾报道过这次入侵，并首次引起了公众对帕兰蒂尔在其中作用的关注——这标志着追踪本文所描述网络的十多年旅程的开始。
该提案包括制造虚假的在线身份、散布虚假信息，并开展协调的骚扰活动以损害目标。帕兰蒂尔暂停了涉及的员工并发表了道歉，但文件已经表明，这种战术手段存在、运作，并且贯穿于蒂尔自己的公司。
这些战术是由一个松散的极右翼组织网络多年发展和部署的——部分资金来自与蒂尔直接相关的个人。
这一基础设施以一群白人至上主义和强硬右翼的在线平台为中心——其中包括据参与者称由吉塞亚秘密资助的极右翼出版物。这些平台也成为骚扰活动、虚假信息操作和模因战术的试验场，吉塞亚后来将这些战术呈现在北约相关期刊上作为一种值得尊敬的战略工具。
将这些平台与蒂尔的更广泛网络联系起来的是一个人：安德鲁·奥尔纳海默，一位黑客和极右翼挑衅者，网名为“韦夫”（Weev）。他的与蒂尔的联系曾在泄露的爱泼斯坦通信中被传闻，但此前从未得到证实。现在，通过奥尔纳海默自己的私人声明和十年的文档网络活动，这些联系首次得到了确认。
奥尔纳海默实际上是一座桥梁。他穿梭于早期互联网的无政府主义图像板亚文化与组织化的白人至上主义运动之间。他将蒂尔周围的PayPal和帕兰蒂尔圈子与他帮助创建和利用的另类右翼联系起来。他还连接了第一代在线骚扰行动与今天日益塑造主流政治话语的当代影响力网络。
在Discord服务器日志——一个被游戏和政治社区广泛使用的即时通讯平台——中，记者卢克·奥布莱恩在其2020年关于蒂尔发展另类右翼的调查中提到，奥尔纳海默将吉塞亚描述为“一位主要投资者，为种族主义者提供帮助”。奥布莱恩报告称，吉塞亚使用的在线别名鼓励捐赠者向白人至上主义者和新纳粹组织捐款。
吉塞亚最初否认了这一点。当被出示向臭名昭著的新纳粹理查德·斯宾塞领导的白人至上主义组织捐赠5000美元的证据时，他回答说：“不予评论。”
吉塞亚对新纳粹平台的资金支持，以及奥尔纳海默和约翰逊其他相关项目的资金支持，后来被这些极右翼网络的其他参与者声称。
一位被确认的爱泼斯坦律师艾伦·德肖维茨被指出是参与吉塞亚项目的另一位爱泼斯坦关联人士，他在制作迈克·辛诺维奇2016年纪录片《》时担任制作人——这部影片包括奥尔纳海默、约翰逊和米洛·伊亚诺普洛斯。
吉塞亚否认了这些极右翼网络参与者提出的
_source.trans_title: 彼得蒂尔网络如何推动极右翼战术渗透美国主流政治
_source.evidence: 文章主要描述了美国右翼势力（如Peter Thiel、Jeff Giesea、Andrew Auernheimer等）利用网络水军、虚假信息、深度伪造技术（如Clearview AI人脸识别）、以及‘模因战’（Memetic Warfare）理论进行舆论操纵和认知对抗的具体行动。文中详细列举了针对特定目标（如ISIS、工会、左翼活动人士）的骚扰、渗透和舆论攻击战术，以及这些战术如何从网络亚文化演变为被NATO等机构采纳的战略工具。虽然涉及了技术（人脸识别）和理论（模因战），但文章的核心在于描述这些力量如何被组织起来并实际执行了具体的认知域对抗行动（如GamerGate、针对特定群体的骚扰等），属于具体的作战、对抗行动及其动向。

(中央社記者
台北15日電)央廣和烏克蘭的利維夫媒體論壇(LMF)深度合作,央廣與外交部、美國國家民主基金會同是LMF的策略夥伴,他們舉辦「台灣專場」,展現台烏媒體合作在抗衡威權擴張與資訊戰上的緊密連結。
2026年烏克蘭最大媒體盛事「利維夫媒體論壇」(Lviv Media Forum, LMF)14日正式揭幕,據新聞稿,央廣與台灣外交部、美國國家民主基金會(NED)並列為LMF 2026年會之策略夥伴,並於論壇開幕首日舉辦「台灣專場」(Taiwan Session),吸引超過70名國際與烏克蘭媒體專業人士參與。
這場台灣專場(Taiwan Session),以「Distant Borders, Common Threats: How Can Global Media Partnerships Disrupt Authoritarian Infowars(遙遠邊界,共同威脅:全球媒體合作如何反制威權資訊戰)」為題。此次論壇由央廣副總台長劉嘉偉主持,邀集台灣與烏克蘭多位資訊戰、媒體研究與開源情報領域專家,共同探討威權國家的認知作戰、平台治理與全球媒體合作等議題。
論壇有台烏專家對談,台灣戰略模擬學會研究員黃柏叡分析中國如何透過社群媒體、敘事操作與灰色地帶手段,形成輿論戰、心理戰以及法律戰,以影響台灣民主社會與認同。
曾任烏克蘭資訊政策副部長的佐洛圖欽(Dmytro Zolotukhin)則從政策制定角度,回顧國際社會如何從「宣傳」逐步發展出「錯誤資訊」與「外國資訊操縱與干預(FIMI)」等概念。
佐洛圖欽認為,各國應從「防禦假訊息」轉向「建構自身敘事」,強化國家身分認同與民主價值。他並特別點出台灣面臨的挑戰,指出包括TikTok、抖音等平台,可能在選舉期間影響資訊環境,但目前仍缺乏足夠法律監管平台演算法與責任機制。
台灣專場成為論壇中少數聚焦亞洲民主防衛與跨區域資訊戰合作的主題活動,也讓台灣與烏克蘭之間進一步超越物質援助,而成為深層次的媒體技術與經驗共享關係,為共同對抗威權主義擴張,攜手合作。(編輯:張銘坤)1150515
_source.movement_title: 央廣與台外交、NED 成利維夫論壇策略夥伴 共抗威權資訊戰
_source.movement_abstract: 2026 年烏克蘭利維夫媒體論壇於 14 日揭幕，央廣與台灣外交部、美國國家民主基金會並列為策略夥伴，並舉辦「台灣專場」。該場次以「遙遠邊界，共同威脅」為題，探討全球媒體合作如何反制威權資訊戰。活動由央廣副總台長劉嘉偉主持，邀請台烏專家對談，分析中國透過社群媒體進行的認知作戰，以及國際社會從防禦假訊息轉向建構自身敘事的趨勢。佐洛圖欽指出台灣面臨 TikTok 等平台在選舉期間的資訊環境挑戰，呼籲強化法律監管。此活動標誌著台烏關係超越物質援助，深化為媒體技術與經驗共享，共同對抗威權擴張。
_source.title: 深化台烏媒體合作 央廣攜手烏克蘭辦「台灣專場」
_source.trans_cont:
（中央社记者 台北15日电）央广与乌克兰利维夫媒体论坛（LMF）展开深度合作，央广与外交部、美国国家民主基金会同为LMF的策略伙伴，他们举办“台湾专场”，展现台乌媒体合作在抗衡威权扩张与信息战上的紧密联系。

2026年乌克兰最大媒体盛事“利维夫媒体论坛”（Lviv Media Forum, LMF）14日正式开幕，据新闻稿，央广与台湾外交部、美国国家民主基金会（NED）并列为LMF 2026年会之策略伙伴，并于论坛开幕首日举办“台湾专场”（Taiwan Session），吸引超过70名国际与乌克兰媒体专业人士参与。

这场“台湾专场”以“遥远边界，共同威胁：全球媒体合作如何反制威权信息战”为主题。此次论坛由央广副总台长刘嘉伟主持，邀请台湾与乌克兰多位信息战、媒体研究与开源情报领域专家，共同探讨威权国家的认知作战、平台治理与全球媒体合作等议题。

论坛设有台乌专家对谈，台湾战略模拟学会研究员黄柏睿分析中国如何通过社交媒体、叙事操作与灰色地带手段，形成舆论战、心理战以及法律战，以影响台湾民主社会与认同。

曾任乌克兰信息政策副部长的佐洛图钦（Dmytro Zolotukhin）则从政策制定角度，回顾国际社会如何从“宣传”逐步发展出“错误信息”与“外国信息操纵与干预（FIMI）”等概念。

佐洛图钦认为，各国应从“防御假信息”转向“构建自身叙事”，强化国家身份认同与民主价值。他特别指出台湾面临的挑战，包括TikTok、抖音等平台可能在选举期间影响信息环境，但目前仍缺乏足够的法律监管平台算法与责任机制。

“台湾专场”成为论坛中少数聚焦亚洲民主防卫与跨区域信息战合作的主题活动，也使台湾与乌克兰进一步超越物质援助，建立深层次的媒体技术与经验共享关系，共同携手对抗威权主义扩张。（编辑：张铭坤）1150515
_source.trans_title: 2026 年乌媒论坛：台乌深化合作共抗信息战
_source.evidence: 文章核心描述的是央广（台湾）与乌克兰媒体论坛合作举办'台湾专场'，探讨'威权扩张与资讯战'、'认知作战'等议题。虽然文中多次提及'中国'、'威权国家'作为被讨论的负面对象（如分析中国如何透过社群媒体进行舆论战），但这属于第三方（台乌）对中国的认知域攻击或防御策略的讨论，而非中国大陆作为主体发起的行动，也不是中国大陆作为被攻击方发生的直接敌情事件（如具体的网络攻击、舆论抹黑行动）。文章主要聚焦于'媒体合作'、'论坛研讨'、'政策制定角度'以及'防御假讯息'等理论、策略和框架层面的交流。根据标签定义，[涉我事件]通常指针对中国大陆的具体敌情事件，而此处是台乌联合举办的论坛，属于外部势力（含台独势力）的动向。然而，从中国大陆视角看，这是外部势力（台乌）针对'威权扩张'（暗指中国）进行的认知域对抗活动，属于外部针对中国的认知域行动动向。但更精准地看，文章重点在于'论坛'、'研讨'、'政策制定'、'理论探讨'（如从宣传到错误信息的概念发展）。对比标签：[行动动向]通常指具体的作战或对抗行动（如舆论攻击），而此处是'论坛'和'研讨'，更偏向于策略和理论层面的交流。[理论政策]涉及理论、政策、法规、战略框架。文中提到'从政策制定角度'、'回顾国际社会如何从宣传逐步发展出错误信息...等概念'、'建构自身叙事'等，符合理论政策特征。但考虑到这是'台乌媒体合作'对抗'威权'（中国），这实际上是一种针对中国的认知域'行动'（舆论战、心理战）的策划和展示。不过，文章本身描述的是'论坛'这一事件，而非具体的攻击行动。再看[涉我事件]：涉及中国大陆（作为被攻击对象或相关方，非发起方）的敌情事件。文中明确提到'抗衡威权扩张'、'分析中国如何...形成舆论战'，中国是被攻击/被分析的对象。这符合[涉我事件]的定义：涉及中国大陆作为被攻击对象的相关事件。虽然形式是论坛，但内容是针对中国的认知战策略。因此，[涉我事件]比[理论政策]更贴切，因为核心是'针对中国的敌情'（台乌联合反华认知战）。

Concerns are rising across southern Syria amid reports of systematic land acquisitions by foreign actors and a shifting military landscape along the border. While claims of large-scale land purchases by Israeli-linked businessmen have circulated widely, local investigations and legal experts suggest the narrative may be part of a broader psychological and strategic campaign aimed at reshaping the region’s geography.
Unpacking the Real Estate Narrative
In recent months, rumors have alleged that individuals of various nationalities and Jewish descent have acquired more than 200,000 dunams of agricultural land in the Dara’a governorate. Yet activists and local residents—including Amjad al-Hajji—say they have seen no evidence of unusual or large-scale transactions.
Legal specialists note that Syrian law strictly prohibits foreign ownership of agricultural land, especially in sensitive border areas. Any property transfer in these zones requires high-level security approvals and complex administrative procedures. Observers argue that the “land-sale” narrative may be a deliberate distraction—drawing public attention to hypothetical real estate deals while Israel advances concrete military operations and engineering works in the Yarmouk Basin and the Quneitra countryside.
The “Yellow Line” Strategy
A recent assessment by the Arab Center for Research and Policy Studies points to a more tangible development: the implementation of what it calls the “Yellow Line” strategy. This doctrine involves establishing defensive buffer zones in Gaza, southern Lebanon, and now southern Syria—effectively dismantling the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.
Since late 2024, Israeli forces have moved to seize control of the demilitarized buffer zone, framing the occupation as a temporary measure to protect settlements in the occupied Golan Heights and curb weapons smuggling. However, satellite imagery from early 2026 suggests a more permanent intent. Reports indicate that Israeli agricultural aircraft have sprayed unidentified chemical agents across the Quneitra countryside, resulting in near-total vegetation loss. Analysts view this scorched-earth tactic as a means to clear lines of sight and establish long-term surveillance and military outposts.
Strategic and Demographic Pressures
Beyond military expansion, analysts warn that Israel may be attempting to fracture the region’s social fabric. The Arab Center’s report suggests a strategy aimed at displacing local populations, degrading infrastructure, and potentially encouraging separatist tendencies among minority groups to create a loyalist buffer zone.
What is unfolding in southern Syria is increasingly seen not as a localized security issue but as a direct contest over sovereignty. As Damascus attempts to reassert full authority and rebuild a state battered by fifteen years of conflict, it confronts an Israeli strategy of “gradual erosion”—a blend of psychological warfare and incremental military expansion designed to impose a new, irreversible reality on the ground.
For now, the future of the Syrian south remains precariously suspended between advancing military lines and the resilience of its communities.

_source.movement_title: 以色列推进叙利亚南部缓冲区战略实施心理与军事双重施压
_source.movement_abstract: 【叙利亚观察家网站2026年6月报道】叙利亚南部地区近期出现关于外国势力系统性土地收购及军事态势变化的报告。尽管有传言称以色列关联商人收购了德拉省超过20万杜纳亩农业用地，但当地居民及法律专家指出，叙利亚法律严格禁止外国人拥有边境敏感地区农业用地，相关土地交易传闻可能为心理战策略。阿拉伯研究与政策研究中心评估指出，以色列正在实施所谓“黄线”战略，旨在加沙、黎巴嫩南部及叙利亚南部建立防御缓冲区，实质上瓦解1974年脱离接触协议。自2024年底以来，以色列军队已控制非军事缓冲区，将其定性为保护戈兰高地定居点的临时措施。2026年初卫星图像显示，以色列农业飞机在库奈特拉乡村喷洒不明化学制剂，导致植被近乎完全消失，分析人士认为这是焦土战术，旨在清除视线并建立长期监视及军事前哨。除军事扩张外，以色列试图通过破坏基础设施、制造人口流离失所及鼓励少数族裔分离倾向，建立效忠缓冲区。大马士革方面将此视为主权争夺，试图在经历十五年冲突后重建国家权威，而以色列则采取“渐进侵蚀”策略，结合心理战与军事扩张在地面强加不可逆转的新现实。
_source.title: Israeli Activity in Southern Syria: Between Real Estate Rumors and Military Encroachment - The Syrian Observer
_source.trans_cont:
人们对南部叙利亚的担忧正在上升，随着有关外国势力系统性土地收购的报道以及边境地区军事形势的变化。尽管有关与以色列有关的商人进行大规模土地购买的传言广泛流传，但当地调查和法律专家表示，这一说法可能是更广泛的心理和战略行动的一部分，旨在重塑该地区的地理格局。

解析房地产叙事
最近几个月，传言称来自不同国籍和犹太血统的人士在德拉省收购了超过20万杜纳姆的农业用地。然而，活动人士和当地居民，包括阿姆贾德·哈吉，表示他们并未看到任何异常或大规模交易的证据。

法律专家指出，叙利亚法律严格禁止外国对农业用地的所有权，尤其是在敏感的边境地区。这些地区的任何财产转让都需要高级别的安全批准和复杂的行政程序。观察人士认为，“土地销售”这一叙事可能是一种故意的分散注意力的手段——将公众注意力引向假设的房地产交易，而以色列则在亚尔穆克盆地和库奈特拉乡村推进具体的军事行动和工程作业。

“黄线”战略
阿拉伯研究中心和政策研究所最近的一项评估指出，一个更切实的发展是所谓“黄线”战略的实施。这一战略包括在加沙、南部黎巴嫩以及现在南部叙利亚建立防御缓冲区，实际上是在拆解1974年的脱离协议。

自2024年底以来，以色列部队已开始夺取非军事化缓冲区的控制权，并将占领描述为一项临时措施，以保护被占领戈兰高地的定居点并遏制武器走私。然而，2026年初的卫星图像表明，以色列的意图可能更加永久。据报道，以色列农业飞机在库奈特拉乡村喷洒了未知的化学物质，导致植被几乎完全消失。分析人士认为，这种焦土战术是为了清除视线并建立长期的监视和军事据点。

战略与人口压力
除了军事扩张，分析人士警告称，以色列可能试图破坏该地区的社会结构。阿拉伯研究中心的报告指出，这可能是一种旨在驱逐当地人口、破坏基础设施，并可能鼓励少数族裔群体产生分离倾向，以建立一个忠诚的缓冲区的战略。

目前在叙利亚南部发生的事情，越来越被视为不仅仅是局部安全问题，而是一场直接的主权争夺。随着大马士革试图重新确立完全的权威并重建一个经历了十五年冲突而遭受重创的国家，它面临着以色列“渐进式侵蚀”战略的挑战——这是一种心理战和逐步军事扩张的结合，旨在在地面上施加一种新的、不可逆转的现实。

目前，叙利亚南部的未来仍然悬而未决，处于不断推进的军事前线和当地社区的韧性之间。

_source.trans_title: 以色列在叙利亚南部的活动：在房地产传闻与军事扩张之间——叙利亚观察者
_source.evidence: 文章主要描述了以色列在叙利亚南部（特别是德拉省和库奈特拉地区）进行的军事渗透、土地收购传闻背后的心理战策略、以及具体的军事行动（如喷洒化学剂、建立缓冲区）。虽然涉及心理战（认知域），但核心内容是具体的军事对抗行动和地缘政治动向，且事件发生地为中国大陆以外的地区（叙利亚），不涉及中国大陆作为被攻击对象或相关方，因此不属于[涉我事件]。文章未提及中国相关的演习、部队组建、技术研发或政策发布。根据定义，该文章属于认知域相关（心理战、舆论战），但具体标签中无完全匹配的非涉我国际冲突类标签，且不属于中国自身的行动或发展。然而，根据标签定义，[行动动向]涵盖“相关领域的具体作战、对抗等行动及其动向”，虽然通常指涉我，但在无涉我情况下，若必须归类，其描述的是敌对势力的具体行动。但严格审视标签定义，[涉我事件]明确限定为“涉及中国大陆...的敌情事件”，本文不涉及中国。[行动动向]通常指我方或相关领域的行动。鉴于文章描述的是国际冲突中的认知战/心理战行动，且非中国相关，最准确的分类应为[其他]，因为现有标签主要针对中国视角下的认知域活动（涉我、我方演习、我方力量、我方技术、我方政策）。若强行归类，其描述的是“敌情”（以色列行动），但非“涉我”。因此归为[其他]。

_source.content:
US President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing on Wednesday for a state visit and scheduled talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, with trade, rare earths, Taiwan, artificial intelligence, and the Iran war expected to dominate the agenda. The visit may produce visible deliverables, but the larger test is whether either side can gain leverage while leaving the deepest disputes unresolved.
For more stories from The Media Line go to themedialine.org
The two leaders are expected to hold bilateral talks on Thursday, with the summit focused on stabilizing economic relations, possible Chinese purchases of US agricultural goods and aircraft, rare earths, advanced chips, and the wider impact of the Iran war.
The visit follows the Busan summit in October 2025, where Trump and Xi agreed to pause the sharpest phase of their trade war. The Guardian and The Washington Post reported that tariffs on Chinese goods reached as high as 145% during the escalation leading up to the October truce. That truce reduced immediate pressure but did not settle the underlying disputes over technology controls, supply chains, market access, or strategic influence.
Taken together, the issues on the table point to a summit built around tactical bargains rather than strategic settlement: limited trade relief, managed language on Iran, guarded signals on Taiwan, and attempts by both governments to preserve leverage for the next round.
A foreign policy analyst who works on US-China strategic competition and spoke with The Media Line on condition of anonymity framed the summit as a likely continuation of Busan rather than a break from it.
US President Donald Trump shakes hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping as they hold a bilateral meeting at Gimhae International Airport, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, in Busan, South Korea, October 30, 2025. (credit: REUTERS/EVELYN HOCKSTEIN)“What we can realistically expect from this meeting is basically a second round of Busan,” the analyst said. “Both sides will walk out with some deliverables, a tariff extension, a rare earth license, maybe a good photo, and call it a historic result.”
“That is not stabilization of the relationship, it is calendar management,” the analyst added.
Beijing, the analyst said, is treating the talks as part of a phased negotiation, with commitments kept reversible and timed against the US political calendar. The closer Washington gets to the 2026 midterm elections, the analyst argued, the more valuable a visible diplomatic win becomes for Trump.
Dr. Elizabeth Freund Larus, a Taiwan Fellow with the Republic of China Ministry of Foreign Affairs and an adjunct senior fellow at the Pacific Forum, said she did not expect a “big climactic summit” or breakthrough. Presidential visits, she told The Media Line, usually formalize work done earlier by lower-level officials.
For Larus, the summit should be understood through the practical interests of both governments. China wants tariff relief and market stability, while Trump wants Chinese purchases of American goods and proof that his pressure campaign has delivered. Substantively, she said, the result is more likely to extend the same unresolved bargaining pattern.
“I honestly see it as more of the same rather than a breakthrough,” Larus said.
Guy Burton, author of China and Middle East Conflicts and visiting fellow at Lancaster University, also said the Beijing talks should not be mistaken for a decisive turning point in the relationship. High-level summits, he told The Media Line, are often treated as historic moments, but the main forces shaping US-China relations are structural, long-term, and already in motion.
US President Donald Trump, accompanied by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, attends a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, accompanied by Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, in South Korea, October 30, 2025. (credit: REUTERS/EVELYN HOCKSTEIN)Burton identified Taiwan, trade, rare earths, and Iran as central issues, but argued that the wider challenge for Washington lies in the ambiguity of its own strategic messaging. He said “the current US position often appears internally inconsistent,” making it difficult for both allies and adversaries to determine Washington’s priorities.
That inconsistency is especially visible on Iran. The war has moved from being a Middle Eastern crisis into a global pressure point affecting energy markets, sanctions enforcement, maritime security, and China’s relationship with both Tehran and Washington. Iran is expected to feature prominently in the Beijing talks, with US officials pressing China to use its influence with Tehran as the conflict strains regional diplomacy and global energy flows.
For Burton, the question is not only whether Beijing can influence Tehran, but whether Washington’s own Iran policy is clear enough to persuade China that cooperation would serve a defined objective. He said US policy has moved among several stated aims, including preventing nuclear escalation, weakening Iran’s regional influence, and broader regime-change signals, creating uncertainty for allies and adversaries.
Burton said Trump’s statements matter because he remains the American president, but Washington’s frequent shifts make US signaling harder to interpret.
Iran is one of the clearest examples of how the summit’s formal agenda and its strategic subtext overlap. China has economic interests in continued energy access from Iran, while Washington wants Beijing to help restrain Tehran or at least avoid undercutting sanctions pressure. Reuters reported that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said China buys 90% of Iran’s energy, while public reporting on oil-tracking data has also pointed to China’s continuing role as a major buyer of Iranian crude.
The foreign policy analyst said Beijing is likely to present itself as a useful interlocutor on Iran while avoiding sanctions enforcement that would harm its access to discounted Iranian oil. In that reading, China’s contribution would be diplomatic language and process rather than concrete pressure on Tehran.
“What is going to happen is China offers diplomatic language and process, not actual enforcement,” the analyst said. “And the final communiqué will make that legible as cooperation.”
Beyond Iran, the conflict has given Beijing a fresh military reference point as it weighs US capabilities, Taiwan contingencies, sanctions pressure, and energy security. Dennis Wilder, former senior director for East Asia in the George W. Bush administration and professor of the practice at Georgetown University, framed the Iran conflict as a demonstration of American military reach and operational capacity.
“The conflict in Iran presents a complicated picture for China,” Wilder told The Media Line. “Militarily, Xi must now realize that Trump is not reluctant to employ the US military’s formidable offensive power for distant force projection when he deems it in the best interest of the United States.”
Wilder said the Iran war would be studied closely by the People’s Liberation Army because it showcased US and Israeli use of artificial intelligence, cyber capabilities, space-based sensors, drones, satellites, and integrated battlefield data. He argued that the Chinese military is still far from matching those capabilities in real combat conditions.
“The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is far from having the kind of informationalized joint force warfare capabilities - using artificial intelligence, cyber, space-based sensors, etc. - exhibited by the US and Israeli militaries,” Wilder said.
China's Gulf relationships more valuable than Iranian tiesFor Beijing, Iran is both an opportunity and a constraint. China has benefited from discounted Iranian oil, but its economic relationships with Gulf states are far more valuable than its ties with Tehran. Wilder said this has limited China’s willingness to openly support Iran during the conflict.
“The wars in Iran and Gaza have demonstrated the limits of China’s influence in the Middle East,” Wilder said. “Pakistan, not China, is the mediator in the Iran conflict, and China had no role in mediating the resolution of the conflict in Gaza.”
Beijing’s caution, Wilder said, reflects its larger commercial stake in the Gulf. China’s trade with the Gulf Cooperation Council reached roughly $300 billion last year, compared with an estimated $10 billion to $40 billion in trade with Iran. Chinese firms have also been expanding their presence in Saudi Arabia under the “comprehensive strategic partnership” agreement signed with Riyadh in 2023.
Taiwan remains the most sensitive strategic issue between the two powers, even if it does not formally appear in the economic negotiations. Beijing considers Taiwan part of its territory and has not ruled out the use of force, while Taiwan rejects Beijing’s claim and says only its people can decide its future.
China’s Foreign Ministry said after a November 2025 Trump-Xi call that Xi told Trump: “Taiwan’s return to China is an integral part of the post-war international order.”
For Burton, Taiwan is precisely where US ambiguity becomes most consequential. He said one of Beijing’s likely red lines will be preventing any formal strengthening of US commitments toward Taiwanese sovereignty or security guarantees beyond Washington’s traditional framework of strategic ambiguity.
“Chinese leaders will be especially attentive to whether Trump might casually concede rhetorical ground, improvise unexpectedly, or alter longstanding diplomatic formulations in ways that create instability,” Burton said.
Larus, speaking from Taipei, said concern over China remains present but should not be confused with panic. She argued that the threat environment has changed, but life in Taiwan continues without the sense of imminent crisis often suggested in Western media coverage.
“The people in Taiwan have been facing this threat from China for a very long time. It’s just that China was not able to make good on it until recently,” Larus said.
She added that people in Taiwan still question US commitments, especially in academic and government circles, and some are watching closely to see whether Trump says anything in Beijing about Taiwan independence or Washington’s position on the island’s future.
Larus also argued that Xi may have reasons to avoid military action for now, especially given Taiwan’s internal political divisions, China’s own military uncertainties, and the high risks of war.
“Xi Jinping knows he doesn’t have to strike Taiwan. He doesn’t have to. Taiwan’s not going anywhere. It’s an island. It can’t go anywhere. Its population is declining. People aren’t having kids here,” Larus said.
She said China may see less risk from political pressure and influence operations than from an invasion. Larus warned that Beijing remains skilled at cognitive warfare, social media influence, media penetration, and the cultivation of sources inside Taiwan’s military.
“China is very good, very, very good at cognitive warfare,” Larus said.
Taiwan unlikely to appear in trade text, but will affect talksThe foreign policy analyst said Taiwan is unlikely to appear in any trade text, but will still affect the atmosphere of the talks. Chinese cooperation on trade or Iran, the analyst argued, is likely to become harder when US arms sales to Taiwan or technology export controls accelerate.
“It will not appear that way in any agreement text, but it will show up in the timing of concessions,” the analyst added.
Trade, tariffs, and critical minerals form the most visible area for potential deliverables. China dominates several parts of the rare earth and critical mineral supply chain, giving Beijing leverage over industries ranging from electric vehicles and consumer electronics to defense production. The International Energy Agency’s 2025 Global Critical Minerals Outlook warned that China is the dominant refiner for 19 of the 20 strategic minerals analyzed, with an average market share of around 70%.
Those vulnerabilities became visible in 2025, when Chinese exports of rare earth magnets reportedly plunged 74% year over year in May after export licensing restrictions, according to a Wall Street Journal analysis cited by Automotive World. Ford was among the manufacturers affected by rare earth magnet supply constraints, with the Ford-focused industry reporting that some plants were temporarily shut down over the shortage.
For Burton and the foreign policy analyst, rare earths are a powerful source of leverage but not a weapon Beijing can use without cost. Burton said China wants to preserve stability and predictability, while the analyst said aggressive use of export controls could permanently accelerate allied diversification, as happened with Japan after 2010.
“That is why China uses the threat intermittently rather than going for a full cutoff,” the analyst said. “Some new US magnet production capacity is expected to start coming online in summer 2026, which would marginally reduce exposure, but real self-sufficiency is still years away.”
Beyond rare earths, trade remains central to the summit. Trump’s tariff policy has been one of the most visible features of his China strategy, but its stated objectives have ranged from industrial protection and revenue generation to retaliation against unfair trade practices. Both sides are expected to discuss a possible extension of the October truce, potential tariff relief, and Chinese purchases of US goods, including agricultural products and aircraft.
Burton said Trump’s tariff policy has mixed several objectives - protecting industry, raising revenue, and punishing unfair trade practices - that do not always point in the same direction. He added that legal challenges over presidential tariff authority could narrow the administration’s room to maneuver compared with what appeared possible a year ago.
Wilder, meanwhile, placed the summit in a broader military and strategic context. For China, the Iran war is a warning about US capabilities, but also a lesson about vulnerabilities in energy supply chains. The closure or disruption of the Strait of Hormuz reinforces long-standing Chinese fears about the Strait of Malacca, through which a large share of China’s Middle Eastern oil imports travel. China depends heavily on Middle Eastern energy flows, and any disruption in the Strait of Hormuz carries direct energy-security implications for Beijing.
A closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Wilder said, would remind China of the fragility of oil supply chains and deepen long-standing concerns about the United States’ ability to disrupt Chinese oil imports from the Middle East during a Taiwan contingency by blockading the Strait of Malacca.
He added that China is likely to look for alternative energy sources, a shift that could benefit US liquefied natural gas exporters if Beijing seeks to diversify away from vulnerable maritime chokepoints.
For Larus, China’s longer-term strategic movement may be most visible not only around Taiwan but also in the South China Sea and Central Asia. She said Beijing is building naval reach while expanding land routes to reduce exposure to US-controlled maritime chokepoints.
The summit’s importance may lie less in its formal conclusions than in the balance of leverage each side accumulates, even as major disputes remain unresolved. For Beijing, time can be an asset if negotiations are managed through temporary extensions and controlled concessions. For Washington, the challenge is to convert pressure into enforceable outcomes without giving China symbolic wins on Taiwan, sanctions, technology, or supply chains.
Final test: Which side leaves with more leverage?Burton said the broader global order is already undergoing a structural shift, with deeper changes taking place through trade measures, military positioning, technological competition, and the erosion of the wider international order. Still, the final test of the Beijing talks may be narrower and more immediate: Which side leaves with more leverage for the next round?
The foreign policy analyst framed the issue as a question of strategic clarity.
“At the end of the day, this meeting is not about resolving the specific disputes. It is about who accumulates position while the disputes stay open,” the analyst said.
“The Americans arrive in Beijing with a transactional agenda, wanting to close line items, and the Chinese arrive knowing exactly what they are willing to concede and what they are not,” the analyst added. “That asymmetry in strategic clarity is the most important variable in the room, and it will not appear in any press release.”
_source.movement_title: 特朗普访华与习近平会谈聚焦贸易稀土伊朗及台湾问题
_source.movement_abstract: 【美国The Media Line 2026年6月报道】美国总统特朗普于2026年6月29日抵达北京进行国事访问，计划与习近平主席举行双边会谈。议程涵盖贸易关税、稀土供应链、伊朗战争影响及台湾问题。双方预计就延长2025年10月釜山峰会达成的关税休战期、中国采购美国农产品及飞机、稀土出口许可等达成战术性协议，但深层战略分歧难以解决。伊朗战争成为关键议题，美方施压中方利用影响力约束德黑兰，但中方更关注能源安全及海湾地区贸易利益，预计仅提供外交辞令而非实质性制裁配合。台湾问题虽可能不列入正式文本，但仍是核心红线，中方警惕美方改变战略模糊立场。稀土领域，中国掌握约70%战略矿产精炼份额，美方担忧供应链脆弱性，预计2026年夏季部分美国产能上线。伊朗战争展示了美军远程投送及AI、网络战能力，引发解放军关注。分析人士指出，此次峰会旨在管理分歧而非解决争端，核心在于双方如何在保留各自战略筹码的同时，为下一轮博弈积累优势。
_source.title: Trump-Xi Beijing summit tests leverage on trade, Taiwan, Iran - analysis
_source.trans_cont:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于周三抵达北京进行国事访问并计划与中华人民共和国主席习近平举行会谈，贸易、稀土、台湾、人工智能以及伊朗战争等问题预计将成为会谈的主要议题。这次访问可能会产生一些可见的成果，但更大的考验是双方是否能在不解决最深层次分歧的情况下获得筹码。
欲了解更多来自The Media Line的故事，请访问themedialine.org
两位领导人预计于周四举行双边会谈，峰会将聚焦于稳定经济关系、可能的中国购买美国农产品和飞机、稀土、先进芯片以及伊朗战争的更广泛影响。
此次访问是在2025年10月的釜山峰会之后进行的，当时特朗普和习近平同意暂停他们贸易战最激烈的阶段。《卫报》和《华盛顿邮报》报道，在10月停火之前，中国商品的关税一度高达145%。这次停火减少了即时压力，但并未解决技术控制、供应链、市场准入或战略影响力等根本性分歧。
综合来看，桌面上的问题表明，峰会将围绕战术性妥协而非战略解决展开：有限的贸易救济、对伊朗的措辞谨慎、对台湾的信号谨慎，以及两国政府试图为下一轮谈判保留筹码。
一位专注于美国-中国战略竞争的外交政策分析师，在匿名的情况下与The Media Line交谈，将此次峰会描述为对釜山的延续，而不是对其的突破。
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普与中华人民共和国主席习近平在韩国釜山举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）峰会期间，在 Gimhae 国际机场举行双边会谈。 (信用: REUTERS/EVELYN HOCKSTEIN)“我们能从这次会议中现实地期待的是基本上是釜山的第二轮。”这位分析师表示。“双方都会带着一些成果、关税延期、稀土许可，也许一张好照片，称之为历史性成果。”
“这不是关系的稳定，这是日程管理。”这位分析师补充道。
分析师表示，北京将会谈视为分阶段谈判的一部分，承诺保持可逆，并与美国政治日程相协调。随着华盛顿接近2026年中期选举，分析师认为，对特朗普来说，一个可见的外交胜利变得更有价值。
台湾事务研究员、中华民国外交部的Elizabeth Freund Larus博士，以及太平洋论坛的高级顾问，表示她不期待“重大高潮的峰会”或突破。她告诉The Media Line，总统访问通常会正式化较低级别官员之前的工作。
对Larus来说，峰会应从双方政府的务实利益来理解。中国希望关税减免和市场稳定，而特朗普希望中国购买美国商品并证明他的压力行动已取得成效。实质上，她说，结果更可能延续同样的未解决的讨价还价模式。
“我坦率地认为，这更像是同样的事情而不是突破。”Larus说。
中国与中东冲突的作者、兰开斯特大学的访问学者Guy Burton也表示，北京的会谈不应被误认为是关系中的决定性转折点。他告诉The Media Line，高层峰会通常被视为历史性时刻，但塑造美中关系的主要力量是结构性的、长期的，并且已经处于进行中。
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普与国务卿马可·鲁比奥和商务部部长霍华德·卢特尼克在韩国与中华人民共和国主席习近平举行双边会谈。 (信用: REUTERS/EVELYN HOCKSTEIN)Burton指出台湾、贸易、稀土和伊朗是核心问题，但认为华盛顿面临的更广泛挑战在于其战略信息的模糊性。他表示，“当前美国立场经常显得内部不一致”，这使得盟友和对手难以确定华盛顿的优先事项。
这种不一致性在伊朗问题上尤为明显。战争已从中东危机演变为影响能源市场、制裁执行、海上安全以及中国与德黑兰和华盛顿关系的全球压力点。伊朗预计将在北京会谈中占据重要位置，美国官员敦促中国利用其对德黑兰的影响，以缓解地区外交和全球能源流动的压力。
对于Burton来说，问题不仅在于北京是否能影响德黑兰，还在于华盛顿自身的伊朗政策是否足够清晰，以说服中国合作能实现明确目标。他表示，美国政策在多个明确目标之间摇摆，包括防止核升级、削弱伊朗的地区影响力以及更广泛的政权更迭信号，这给盟友和对手带来了不确定性。
Burton表示特朗普的言论很重要，因为特朗普仍然是美国总统，但华盛顿频繁的转变使得美国的信号更难解读。
伊朗是峰会正式议程和战略潜台词重叠的最清晰例子之一。中国在伊朗持续获得能源方面有经济利益，而华盛顿希望北京帮助遏制德黑兰或至少避免削弱制裁压力。路透社报道称，财政部部长Scott Bessent表示，中国购买了伊朗90%的能源，而公开的石油追踪数据也指出中国继续作为伊朗原油的主要买家。
这位外交政策分析师表示，北京很可能将自己呈现为伊朗问题上的有用对话者，同时避免执行制裁，这会损害其获得折扣伊朗石油的渠道。在这种解读中，中国的贡献将是外交语言和程序，而不是对德黑兰的实际压力。
“将会发生的是，中国提供外交语言和程序，而不是实际执行。”这位分析师说。“最终公报将使这一点看起来像合作。”
除了伊朗，冲突还为北京提供了一个新的军事参考点，使其权衡美国能力、台湾局势、制裁压力和能源安全。前乔治·W·布什政府东亚事务高级主任、乔治城大学实践教授Dennis Wilder将伊朗冲突描述为展示美国军事能力和作战能力的示范。
“伊朗冲突对中国的复杂图景。”Wilder告诉The Media Line。“军事上，习近平现在必须意识到特朗普并不不愿在他认为符合美国最佳利益时，使用美国军队强大的进攻力量进行远距离力量投射。”
Wilder表示，伊朗战争将被中国人民解放军密切关注，因为它展示了美国和以色列在人工智能、网络能力、基于太空的传感器、无人机、卫星和集成战场数据方面的使用。他指出，中国军队在实际战斗条件下仍远未达到这些能力。
“中国人民解放军（PLA）在使用人工智能、网络、基于太空的传感器等进行信息化联合作战能力方面，远未达到美国和以色列军队所展示的水平。”Wilder说。
对中国来说，海湾关系比伊朗关系更有价值
对于北京来说，伊朗既是机会也是限制。中国从折扣的伊朗石油中受益，但其与海湾国家的经济关系比与德黑兰的关系更有价值。Wilder表示，这限制了中国在冲突期间公开支持伊朗的意愿。
“伊朗和加沙的战争展示了中国在中东影响力有限。”Wilder说。“巴基斯坦，而不是中国，是伊朗冲突的调解者，中国在调解加沙冲突解决中没有发挥作用。”
Wilder表示，北京的谨慎反映了其在海湾更大的商业利益。中国与海湾合作委员会的贸易额去年达到约3000亿美元，而与中国伊朗的贸易额估计在100亿到400亿美元之间。中国公司还在沙特阿拉伯扩大其存在，这是2023年与利雅得签署的“全面战略伙伴关系”协议的一部分。
台湾仍然是两国之间最敏感的战略问题，即使它不会正式出现在经济谈判中。北京认为台湾是中国领土的一部分，没有排除使用武力，而台湾拒绝北京的主张，并表示只有台湾人民才能决定其未来。
中国外交部在2025年11月特朗普与习近平通话后表示，习近平告诉特朗普：“台湾回归中国是战后国际秩序的重要组成部分。”
对于Burton来说，台湾正是美国模糊性变得最关键的地方。他表示，北京可能的红线之一是防止任何正式加强美国对台湾主权或安全承诺的行为，超越华盛顿传统的战略模糊框架。
“中国领导人将特别关注特朗普是否可能随意让步，即兴发挥，或以可能造成不稳定的方式改变长期外交表述。”Burton说。
Larus从台北表示，对中国的担忧仍然存在，但不应被误认为恐慌。她认为威胁环境已经改变，但台湾的生活并未感受到西方媒体常提到的迫近危机。
“台湾人民已经面临来自中国的威胁很长时间了。只是中国直到最近才未能兑现承诺。”Larus说。
她补充说，台湾人民仍然质疑美国的承诺，尤其是在学术界和政府界，一些人密切关注特朗普在北京是否对台湾独立或华盛顿对台湾未来立场发表任何言论。
Larus还指出，习近平可能有理由暂时避免军事行动，特别是考虑到台湾内部的政治分歧、中国的军事不确定性以及战争的高风险。
“习近平知道他不需要攻击台湾。他不需要。台湾不会消失。它是一个岛屿。它不能消失。人口正在减少。人们在这里不生孩子。”Larus说。
她说，中国可能认为从政治压力和影响力行动中获得的风险比从入侵中更小。Larus警告说，北京在认知战、社交媒体影响、媒体渗透以及培养台湾军队内部消息来源方面非常擅长。
“中国在认知战方面非常擅长，非常非常擅长。”Larus说。
台湾不太可能出现在贸易文本中，但会影响会谈氛围
这位外交政策分析师表示，台湾不太可能出现在任何贸易文本中，但仍然会影响会谈的氛围。分析师认为，中国在贸易或伊朗方面的合作，可能会在美对台军售或技术出口管制加速时变得更加困难。
“它不会以任何协议文本的形式出现，但会在让步的时间安排上体现出来。”分析师补充道。
贸易、关税和关键矿物是潜在成果最明显的领域。中国主导了稀土和关键矿物供应链的几个部分，使北京在从电动汽车和消费电子产品到国防生产等多个行业拥有筹码。国际能源署2025年全球关键矿物展望警告称，中国是分析的20种战略矿物中的19种的主要精炼商，平均市场份额约为70%。
这些脆弱性在2025年变得明显，当时据《华尔街日报》引用《汽车世界》的分析，由于出口许可限制，中国5月稀土磁体出口同比下降了74%。福特是受稀土磁体供应限制影响的制造商之一，福特相关行业报告称，由于短缺，一些工厂暂时关闭。
对于Burton和这位外交政策分析师来说，稀土是强大的筹码来源，但不是北京可以无代价使用的武器。Burton表示，中国希望维持稳定和可预测性，而分析师表示，使用出口管制的激进手段可能会永久加速盟友的多元化，正如2010年后日本的情况一样。
“这就是为什么中国间歇性地使用威胁，而不是完全切断。”分析师说。“预计新的美国磁体生产能力将在2026年夏季开始上线，这将略微减少暴露，但真正的自给自足仍需多年。”
除了稀土，贸易仍然是峰会的核心。特朗普的关税政策是他对中国战略中最具可见性的特征之一，但其声明目标从工业保护和收入生成到对不公平贸易做法的报复不等。双方预计会讨论10月停火的可能延长、潜在的关税减免以及中国购买美国商品，包括农产品和飞机。
Burton表示，特朗普的关税政策结合了几个目标——保护产业、增加收入和惩罚不公平的贸易做法——这些目标并不总是指向同一个方向。他补充说，对总统关税权力的法律挑战可能会限制政府的行动空间，与一年前相比有所缩小。
与此同时，Wilder将峰会置于更广泛的军事和战略背景下。对中国来说，伊朗战争是一个关于美国能力的警告，但也是一堂关于能源供应链脆弱性的课程。霍尔木兹海峡的关闭或中断强化了中国长期对马六甲海峡的担忧，因为大量中国从中东进口的石油通过该海峡运输。中国严重依赖中东的能源流动，霍尔木兹海峡的任何中断都对北京的能源安全有直接影响。
Wilder表示，霍尔木兹海峡的关闭将提醒中国石油供应链的脆弱性，并加深其对美国在台湾局势下通过封锁马六甲海峡干扰中国从中东进口石油能力的长期担忧。
他补充说，中国可能会寻找替代能源来源，如果北京寻求摆脱脆弱的海上瓶颈，这可能对美国液化天然气出口商有利。
对Larus来说，中国长期的战略动向可能不仅在台湾，也在南海和中亚最为明显。她说，北京正在扩大海军能力，同时扩展陆路以减少对美国控制的海上瓶颈的依赖。
峰会的重要性可能不在于其正式结论，而在于双方积累的筹码平衡，即使主要分歧仍未解决。对北京来说，时间可以成为资产，如果谈判通过临时延长和受控让步进行管理。对华盛顿来说，挑战是将压力转化为可执行的结果，而不会在台湾、制裁、技术或供应链上给中国带来象征性胜利。
最终考验：哪一方离开时拥有更多筹码？
Burton表示，更广泛的全球秩序已经经历了结构性转变，更深层次的变化通过贸易措施、军事部署、技术竞争以及更广泛国际秩序的削弱而发生。然而，北京会谈的最终考验可能更狭窄且更直接：哪一方在下一轮中拥有更多筹码？
这位外交政策分析师将问题描述为战略清晰度的问题。
“归根结底，这次会议并不是解决具体争端。它关乎谁在争端仍然开放的情况下积累地位。”这位分析师说。
“美国人带着交易议程来到北京，希望关闭条目，而中国人清楚自己愿意让步和不愿意让步的内容。”这位分析师补充道。“这种战略清晰度的不对称性是房间内最重要的变量，它不会出现在任何新闻稿中。”
_source.trans_title: 特朗普-习近平北京峰会考验贸易、台湾、伊朗等议题的影响力——分析

Peraton is aiming to give soldiers an edge in fast-moving cognitive warfare with its new Interactive Realtime Information System (IRIS), an AI platform designed to convert large volumes of data into usable intelligence.
IRIS integrates five AI models with mission data, domain context, and analytical workflows, enabling users to process complex information into actionable insights.
It provides advanced semantic search, natural language querying, sentiment trend analysis, and AI-assisted narrative tracking.
Read the full story on NextGen Defense: Peraton Targets Cognitive Warfare With New AI Platform

artificial intelligence cyber cyber attacks cybersecurity Cyberspace hybrid warfare technology United States
_source.movement_title: 美国Peraton推出IRIS平台强化认知战情报处理能力
_source.movement_abstract: 美国Peraton公司推出交互式实时信息系统（IRIS），旨在提升士兵在快速变化的认知战环境中的作战优势。该平台整合五个AI模型、任务数据、领域上下文及分析工作流，将海量数据转化为可操作情报。系统提供高级语义搜索、自然语言查询、情感趋势分析及AI辅助叙事追踪功能，支持用户将复杂信息转化为可执行洞察。该平台聚焦于提升情报处理效率与认知域作战能力，体现美国在人工智能与认知战融合领域的技术发展方向。

_source.content:
[
Army Mad Scientist welcomes T2COM G2 analyst, Mr. Dorsel “Flip” Boyer as today’s guest blogger. Mr. Boyer expertly lays out how our adversaries view cognitive warfare, the emerging technologies impacting its transformation, and how the U.S. can respond! — Enjoy!]
Data science and behavioral psychology have rapidly evolved since the dawn of the information age. Advanced computational models and ubiquitous data collection allow precise cognitive targeting that would have been previously impossible. Current tools and techniques enable adversaries to:
1) rapid synthesis of personalized disinformation created from machine enabled analysis of digital footprints
2) algorithmic manipulation of information environments
3) lower technical barriers for proxy actors to execute sophisticated psychological warfare.
Existing Western military frameworks often lack steady-state operational mechanisms for identifying or countering continuous cognitive campaigns. While information operations are integrated into tactical and operational planning, they are frequently treated as episodic for defined effects rather than continuous defensive and offensive measures. Western organizations often segregate cyber, psychological operations, and public affairs. This die-integration creates friction that malign actors readily exploit.
Addressing this operational asymmetry requires adaptation across the DOTMLPF-P framework to incorporate proactive measures against cognitive threats. This modernization may involve several core elements:
A clarified definition of the Cognitive Domain (Doctrine): Doctrine requires revision to recognize the cognitive sphere as an independent domain of warfare, parallel to land, air, sea, space, and cyber. Integrating cognitive security as a steady-state Phase 0 operation limits an adversary’s ability to shape the operational environment.
Persistent Organizational Structures (Organization & Personnel): Transitioning from ad-hoc information task forces to persistent, dedicated organizational structures may present new opportunities to monitor and counter ad
versary cognitive campaigns. These organizations might include data scientists, cognitive psychologists, and cultural analysts in addition to traditional Cyber, PSYOPs, and Public Affairs professionals.
Technologically Advanced Materiel Solutions (Materiel): Countering AI-driven cognitive attacks requires the acquisition and deployment of advanced detection tools. Suites must be capable of identifying synthetic media, algorithmic manipulation, and coordinated inauthentic behavior in real-time.
Evolving Training and Leadership Models (Training & Leadership): Preparing the force for a contested cognitive domain will necessitate updating training to include realistic simulations of targeted cognitive attacks. Building cognitive resilience in commanders and Soldiers is critical for decision-making integrity under persistent psychological pressure.
Decision Advantage: Adapting to the cognitive domain fortifies decision-making by reducing ambiguity generated by adversary disinformation.
Force Protection: These adaptations help ensure that military formations are shielded from micro-targeted psychological subversion, preserving morale, unit cohesion, and overall readiness.
Allied Interoperability: Harmonized cognitive defense standards facilitate intelligence sharing, joint narrative planning, and coalition resilience against wedge-driving operations.
Strategic Deterrence: Demonstrating a robust capability to defend the cognitive domain and counter-manipulate adversary perceptions signals readiness.
_source.movement_title: 美军建议改革框架以应对对手认知战及新兴技术威胁
_source.movement_abstract: 文章指出，随着数据科学与行为心理学的演进，对手利用先进计算模型和 ubiquitous 数据收集，实现了前所未有的精准认知 targeting。当前工具使对手能快速合成个性化虚假信息、操纵信息环境并降低代理执行心理战的门槛。现有西方军事框架缺乏应对持续认知战役的稳态机制，且常将网络、心理战与公共事务割裂，易被恶意利用。为应对这一不对称性，需通过 DOTMLPF-P 框架进行现代化改革：明确认知域为独立作战域；建立包含数据科学家和心理学家在内的持久组织架构；部署能实时识别合成媒体和算法操纵的先进探测工具；更新训练模式以增强指挥官和士兵在心理压力下的决策韧性；并强化决策优势、部队保护、盟友互操作性及战略威慑能力，以构建全面的认知防御体系。
_source.title: Cognitive Warfare – The Human Mind is the Decisive Terrain of Future Conflicts
_source.trans_cont:
欢迎T2COM G2分析师多尔赛“翻转”博耶先生作为今天的客座博主。博耶先生专业地阐述了我们的对手如何看待认知战、影响其转型的新兴技术，以及美国应如何应对！——尽情享受吧！

自信息时代开始以来，数据科学和行为心理学迅速发展。先进的计算模型和广泛的数据收集能力使得精确的认知定向成为可能，这在以前是无法实现的。当前的工具和技术使对手能够：
1）快速合成基于机器分析数字足迹而创建的个性化虚假信息；
2）对信息环境进行算法操控；
3）降低代理行动者执行复杂心理战的技术门槛。

现有的西方军事框架通常缺乏稳定状态的操作机制，以识别或应对持续的认知行动。虽然信息行动已被纳入战术和作战计划，但它们通常被当作特定效果的临时行动，而不是持续的防御和进攻措施。西方组织往往将网络、心理战和公共事务分开，这种分割导致摩擦，而恶意行为者则轻易地利用这些摩擦。

应对这种操作上的不对称性，需要在DOTMLPF-P框架内进行适应，以主动应对认知威胁。这种现代化可能涉及几个核心要素：

A. 认知领域的明确定义（条令）：条令需要修订，以承认认知领域作为独立的战争领域，与陆地、空中、海上、太空和网络领域并列。将认知安全作为稳定状态的第0阶段行动，可以限制对手塑造作战环境的能力。

B. 持续的组织结构（组织与人员）：从临时的信息任务部队向持续、专门的组织结构转变，可能为监控和应对对手的认知行动提供新的机会。这些组织可能包括数据科学家、认知心理学家和文化分析人员，以及传统的网络、心理战和公共事务专业人员。

C. 先进的物资解决方案（物资）：应对由人工智能驱动的认知攻击，需要获取和部署先进的检测工具。这些工具必须能够实时识别合成媒体、算法操控和协调的不真实行为。

D. 演进的培训和领导模式（培训与领导）：为应对竞争性的认知领域做好准备，需要更新培训内容，包括对目标认知攻击的现实模拟。在持续的心理压力下，提升指挥官和士兵的认知韧性对于保持决策的完整性至关重要。

E. 决策优势：适应认知领域有助于决策，通过减少对手虚假信息带来的模糊性。

F. 部队保护：这些适应措施有助于确保军事单位免受有针对性的心理颠覆，保持士气、单位凝聚力和整体战备状态。

G. 同盟互操作性：统一的认知防御标准有助于情报共享、联合叙事规划和联盟对楔形行动的抵御能力。

H. 战略威慑：展示强大的能力以防御认知领域并反制对手的操控，表明了准备就绪的状态。
_source.trans_title: 认知战新威胁与 DOTMLPF-P 框架现代化改革路径
_source.evidence: 文章主要讨论了认知战（Cognitive Warfare）的概念、现状以及应对策略。核心内容集中在呼吁更新军事条令（Doctrine）、建立专门的组织结构（Organization）、研发技术装备（Materiel）以及改进训练模式（Training），即围绕DOTMLPF-P框架提出的理论框架和政策建议。文章并未描述具体的针对中国的敌情事件（排除涉我事件），也没有描述具体的作战行动或演习（排除行动动向、演习演训），虽然提到了技术，但重点在于技术作为应对手段的理论规划而非具体的武器化研发进展（排除技术武器）。文章本质上是关于认知域作战的理论构建、条令修订和战略规划，因此最符合[理论政策]标签。
