New Delhi: India’s military is planning major changes under the Defence Forces Vision 2047 released by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The long-term plan aims to prepare for future wars that may not be limited to land, sea and air but could also involve space, cyber networks and digital systems.
The plan includes building a dedicated drone force, creating space and cyber commands, strengthening air defence through the Mission Sudarshan Chakra and expanding indigenous weapons production under the ‘Make in India’ push.
The armed forces are also planning new data and cognitive warfare units, which means the forces will rely more on technology and digital systems in future wars.
Add Zee News as a Preferred Source
A dedicated drone force in the making
One of the biggest elements of the Vision 2047 plan is the creation of a large and dedicated drone force. Training centres are being developed across 19 major military institutions. The Indian Military Academy in Dehradun is expected to play an important part, while Officers Training Academy in Chennai and Gaya (Bihar) will also host drone training centres.
Soldiers will be trained to operate nano, micro and medium drones. The Army is planning to deploy between 8,000 and 10,000 drones in every corps, which could expand battlefield surveillance and strike capabilities.
The Indian Air Force (IAF) is also moving ahead with a Rs 39,000-crore plan for indigenous stealth drones. In addition, Rs 10,000 crore has been approved to develop six stealth fighter prototypes. Once development is completed, production of more than 60 stealth drones is expected to follow.
These drones are built to carry out precision strikes, surveillance missions and swarm attacks, giving commanders faster decision-making and greater operational flexibility.
Space and cyber commands for future wars
India’s future military structure will also include dedicated space and cyber commands. These new formations are expected to handle satellite operations, surveillance, cyber defence and offensive digital capabilities.
A data warfare force is also planned, which will depend on artificial intelligence and advanced cyber tools to analyse battlefield information. At the same time, a cognitive warfare force will handle information and psychological operations.
The space command will oversee satellite-based intelligence, communication and surveillance systems. The cyber command will monitor and respond to cyber threats and digital attacks targeting military networks and infrastructure.
To accelerate development, the government is planning to bring in experts from the private sector. Adjustments to the Agniveer scheme may also be considered to meet future technology requirements.
Mission Sudarshan Chakra – a multi-layer air defence
Between 2030 and 2040, India’s air defence system is expected to expand under the Mission Sudarshan Chakra. The programme aims to create a multi-layered shield capable of intercepting ballistic missiles, drones and aerial attacks.
The plan is aimed at strengthening ballistic missile defence systems and preparing for swarm drone attacks. The objective is to protect major cities, military bases and critical infrastructure.
The emphasis across the programme is on indigenous systems, with domestic defence manufacturing playing a central role in long-term planning.
Challenges ahead
Experts have pointed to several challenges that could affect the pace of implementation. The plan will require sustained political support, closer operational coordination among the Army, the Navy and the Air Force and faster execution of indigenous defence projects.
Delays in domestic defence programmes have been identified as a main concern. Faster development timelines and better integration between the three services are expected to be essential for meeting the Vision 2047 targets.
A technology-driven military by 2047
The Defence Forces Vision 2047 describes a future where drones, satellites, cyber capabilities and artificial intelligence become an important part of military planning. With drone forces, space command, cyber units and Mission Sudarshan Chakra, India is working toward building a technology-driven military designed for modern warfare.
_source.movement_title: 印度国防部发布2047愿景计划推进无人机与太空网络作战体系建设
_source.movement_abstract: 【印度Zee News报道】印度国防部发布《国防力量2047愿景》长期规划，旨在构建适应未来多维战争形态的军事体系。该计划由国防部长拉杰纳特·辛格发布，核心内容包括组建专用无人机部队、设立太空与网络司令部、强化防空系统及推进本土武器制造。规划提出在德hradun、金奈和加亚等19所主要军事院校建立无人机训练中心，培养士兵操作纳米、微型及中型无人机能力。陆军计划每个军部署8000至10000架无人机，以增强战场监视与打击能力。印度空军推进3900亿卢比本土隐身无人机计划，并批准1000亿卢比用于开发6架隐身战斗机原型机，预计后续量产超60架隐身无人机。新设太空司令部将负责卫星情报、通信与监视系统，网络司令部将应对针对军事网络的数字攻击。数据战部队将利用人工智能分析战场信息，认知战部队负责心理作战。'Sudarshan Chakra'任务计划在2030至2040年间构建多层防空系统，拦截弹道导弹与无人机群攻击，重点保护主要城市、军事基地及关键基础设施。规划强调本土国防制造的核心作用，并考虑调整'Agniveer'计划以吸纳私营部门专家。专家指出实施面临政治支持持续性、三军协同及本土项目执行延迟等挑战。
_source.title: Space and cyber commands to transform warfare, India to become ‘war machine’ by 2047, ‘drone storm’ to rain from the sky
_source.trans_cont:
新德里：印度军方正在根据国防部长拉简纳特·辛格发布的《国防力量2047愿景》计划进行重大改革。长期计划旨在为未来可能不限于陆、海、空领域的战争做准备，还可能涉及太空、网络和数字系统。

该计划包括组建专门的无人机部队、创建太空和网络指挥机构、通过“苏达什兰卡行动”强化防空能力，并在“印度制造”倡议下扩大本土武器生产。军方还计划组建新的数据和认知战单位，这意味着未来战争将更加依赖技术与数字系统。

添加Zee新闻为首选来源
正在组建的专门无人机部队
《国防力量2047愿景》计划中最大的组成部分之一是组建一支规模庞大的专门无人机部队。培训中心正在19所主要军事院校中建设。德里哈德大学印度军事学院将发挥重要作用，而金奈和加雅（比哈尔）的军官训练学院也将设立无人机培训中心。

士兵将接受操作纳米、微型和中型无人机的培训。陆军计划在每个军区部署8000至10000架无人机，这将扩大战场监视和打击能力。

印度空军（IAF）也正在推进一项价值3900亿卢比的本土隐身无人机计划。此外，已批准1000亿卢比用于开发六架隐身战斗机原型。一旦研发完成，预计将生产超过60架隐身无人机。

这些无人机将执行精确打击、监视任务和蜂群攻击，为指挥官提供更快的决策和更大的作战灵活性。

未来战争的太空和网络指挥
印度未来的军事结构还将包括专门的太空和网络指挥机构。这些新单位将负责卫星操作、监视、网络安全和数字攻击能力。

计划还包含一支数据战部队，将依赖人工智能和先进网络工具分析战场信息。同时，一支认知战部队将负责信息和心理战行动。

太空指挥将负责卫星情报、通信和监视系统。网络指挥将监控并应对针对军事网络和基础设施的网络威胁和数字攻击。

为加快发展，政府计划引入私营部门专家。调整“阿格尼维尔”计划也可能考虑以满足未来技术需求。

苏达什兰卡行动——多层防空体系
在2030至2040年间，印度的防空系统将在“苏达什兰卡行动”下扩展。该计划旨在建立多层防护体系，能够拦截弹道导弹、无人机和空中攻击。

该计划旨在强化弹道导弹防御系统，并应对蜂群无人机攻击。目标是保护主要城市、军事基地和关键基础设施。

该计划的重点是本土系统，国内国防制造在长期规划中发挥核心作用。

面临的挑战
专家指出了一些可能影响实施进度的挑战。该计划需要持续的政治支持、陆军、海军和空军之间更紧密的作战协调，以及本土国防项目的更快执行。

国内国防项目进展缓慢被列为主要担忧。更快的开发时间表和三军之间更好的整合预计是实现2047愿景目标的关键。
_source.trans_title: 太空与网络司令部将重塑战争，印度到2047年将成为“战争机器”，“无人机风暴”将从天而降

_source.content:
NATO’s eastern flank faces a transformed operational environment defined by persistent hybrid threats that expose critical gaps in intelligence fusion and response timelines. Airspace incursions, undersea-cable sabotage, cyber intrusions, information campaigns, and targeted GPS jamming are not just isolated events, but elements of a sustained Russian strategy to probe defenses, test resolve, and impose continuous strain on a NATO systems architecture designed for episodic crises rather than persistent, multi-domain competition below the threshold of armed conflict.
The Alliance’s core challenge is not sensing capacity. NATO and its members field capable Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) platforms across all domains. The problem lies in speed, integration, and trust. Data remains fragmented across national systems, shared selectively, and processed through architectures ill-suited for today’s tempo of operations. Without corresponding investments in shared infrastructure, paired with clear standards, adopting emerging technologies and modernizing systems risk amplifying friction rather than reducing it.
The June 2025 NATO commitment to invest 5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) annually in defense and security-related spending by 2035 could address some of these issues. However, absent deliberate guidance, new resources may be absorbed by legacy platforms and approaches, producing fragmentation at greater scale.
This paper argues that cloud-enabled ISR aligns with NATO’s federated political reality, enabling infrastructure for effective modernization. Rather than attempting to centralize intelligence collection, investments in cloud infrastructure could match desires for interoperability with technical reality, while enabling allies to retain data ownership and facilitating shared processing, fusion, and controlled dissemination. By the 2029 NATO-wide reassessment of the trajectory and balance of spending,
as outlined in the June 2025 Hague Summit Declaration, NATO should mandate interoperability standards for all new ISR acquisitions. It also should articulate firm requirements for all cloud vendors, allocate meaningful portions of increased defense spending toward shared digital infrastructure, and rely on rigorous trust frameworks based on verifiable technical measures.
NATO’s eastern flank is under persistent pressure across multiple domains. Airspace incursions, maritime sabotage, cyber intrusions, and deliberate information operations all occurred last year and have become routine. These are not isolated incidents, but part of a sustained Russian strategy to probe Alliance defenses, test political resolve, and impose continuous operational and cognitive strain on NATO and its member states.
In the final months of 2025, there were at least thirteen days marked by distinct, attributable airspace incursions across NATO’s eastern flank.
Additional developments have included the November 2024 to January 2025 wave of subsea cable incidents in the Baltics
, with at least seven cable cuts in three months, combined with sustained GPS jamming affecting 85 percent of flights into and out of Estonia
, along with 2,732 recorded incidents in Poland
during January 2025. While NATO has responded, most notably through Operations Baltic Sentry
and Eastern Sentry
, recent incidents have exposed weaknesses in the Alliance’s ability to rapidly integrate forces and information in order to quickly respond to the evolving nature of warfare.
These incursions have triggered airport closures
and fighter aircraft sorties, while stress-testing and revealing inefficiencies in NATO’s ISR architecture. More consequentially, beyond their immediate operational impact and response, these incursions reinforce the hybrid nature of modern warfare, in which shaping public perception and societal resilience is as strategically significant as military effects. NATO’s ability to defend and respond in the future will be defined as much by processing power and systems design as by F-35 sortie speed.
The core challenge is not a lack of sensing capacity. NATO and its members field a wide array of advanced ISR platforms across all domains. Rather, the problem lies in speed, integration, and trust. Rather, the problem lies in speed, integration, and trust. This challenge extends beyond the Alliance level. Even national militaries struggle to integrate data from diverse sensing platforms into unified observation capabilities—as recent efforts to track submarine activity in the Baltic demonstrate.
Alliance data remains fragmented across national systems, shared selectively, and processed through architectures that are ill-suited for persistent, multi-domain competition below the threshold of armed conflict. Enhancing interoperability through advanced computing technologies is central to NATO’s ability to counter not only airborne and maritime incursions, but also increasingly sophisticated cyber and cognitive attacks. Equally important, cloud infrastructure offers resilience that traditional architectures cannot match, such as distributed storage and redundant processing to ensure that critical intelligence remains available even when individual nodes are compromised.
Ukraine has become the most consequential laboratory for cloud-enabled warfare, and its experience offers critical lessons for NATO. The central lesson is that the tempo, scale, and character of modern conflict is changing. The country’s Delta battlefield management system, which integrates satellite imagery, radar, and drone reconnaissance into a unified operational picture, has decreased detect-to-engage timelines from approximately seventy-two hours to roughly two minutes.
This compression has altered battlefield decision-making by enabling near-real-time sensing to become accessible on the battlefield across dispersed units. The effect was driven by the fusion of data from different sources rather than by a single exquisite platform.
The lesson for NATO is not Delta’s technical configuration, but its implementation and architecture.
The commercial technology ecosystem has also proven operationally useful. AI-driven targeting technology that further enables integration
, commercial synthetic aperture radar (SAR) constellations, and low-cost AI vision modules improving first-person view (FPV) drone accuracy
all demonstrate the changing possibilities in ISR. As proof, Ukraine’s military leadership attributes much of its defensive success to a similar technology stack.
NATO should not replicate Ukraine’s model wholesale. Ukraine operates as a unitary command with existential urgency and accepts commercial dependencies that Alliance governance structure would constrain. Their approach prioritized operational speed over security hardening—a rational choice under existential threat, but one that has left aspects of its cloud infrastructure vulnerable. The Alliance requires federated architectures that respect national classification authorities while achieving comparable fusion speeds, while still prioritizing data security and availability. NATO’s Multi-Domain Operations concept recognizes this reality, calling for “converging effects at the speed of relevance,”
but achieving that tempo within such a federated structure requires investment in architectures explicitly designed for selective sharing, distributed control, and verifiable trust.
NATO must strive to find convergence in shared and trustworthy infrastructure. No single vendor will be able to provide all that each member of the Alliance requires, but NATO can articulate clear and common technical standards which, in turn, will enforce meaningful interoperability. Cloud-enabled warfare is not only a technical transformation, but an institutional one that requires NATO to reconcile operational speed with collective governance, and technological advantage with political reality.
The NATO alliance of thirty-two countries does not possess an organic, centralized intelligence agency. Instead, the Alliance relies on thirty-two different intelligence production cycles and voluntary sharing. Each state determines what intelligence to share, when to share it, and with whom. While this federated model has many benefits, such as protection of sources and methods, it also presents challenges to conglomerate timely, actionable intelligence that can then be acted upon. Any effort to modernize NATO’s ISR capabilities therefore must be nested in the current structure of existing intelligence sourcing, which also defines the boundaries within which any cloud-enabled ISR solutions must operate.
Perhaps the Alliance’s most developed effort to aggregate and analyze intelligence is the NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre (NIFC). Established following operations in the Balkans and the War on Terror, the NIFC was created “to facilitate the sharing and fusion of intelligence, contribute to filling intelligence gaps within Allied Command Operations, and to support the planning and execution of operations.”
While the NIFC has certainly improved coordination and situational awareness, its effectiveness has remained constrained by national caveats and trust dynamics within the Alliance.
In practice, intelligence sharing within the Alliance remains uneven and selective. NATO has recognized this problem and has taken marginal steps to improve intelligence sharing through the Joint Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (JISR) system, which stresses a “responsibility to share” relevant information over only sharing information on a “need to know” basis.
While JISR has attempted to establish common procedures and a shared vocabulary for intelligence cooperation, its implementation remains voluntary. While NATO continues to lack the authority to compel allies to contribute sensitive intelligence, it is taking steps in the right direction to promote data standardization and information assurance. Additionally, internal timelines targeting 2030 for full cloud transition risk misalignment with both the threat trajectory and the pace of technological evolution.
These structural limitations are particularly consequential in today’s operational environment on NATO’s eastern flank, where the threat is defined by both persistent gray-zone activity and episodic crises. Airspace incursions, maritime sabotage, cyber operations, and information campaigns often unfold simultaneously and below the threshold of armed conflict. Responding effectively, often in multiple domains simultaneously, requires that decision makers and operational forces have rapid access to the best intelligence. Yet NATO’s underlying intelligence architecture remains ill-suited to respond to continuous competition, leaving the Alliance with less decision space in times of elevated activity.
NATO’s existing ISR architecture was largely designed for episodic crises involving significant force movements, not for persistent, multi-domain competition below the threshold of armed conflict. NATO allies have no shortage of specialized platforms, but the Alliance struggles to ingest, fuse, and analyze streams of information from multiple countries and across multiple domains. Rather than attempting to centralize organic capability, cloud-enabled ISR supports a federated approach uniquely suited for NATO. Allies would retain ownership and control of their data and platforms, while NATO infrastructure would enable conglomeration, shared processing, a standardized tagging system, and controlled selective dissemination. NATO would need to enable this functionality with updated and secure cross-domain solutions and policies. This cloud-computing model would acknowledge the political reality of the Alliance and would operate inside that space to improve the speed and utility of intelligence sharing.
In this cloud computing model, “service providers offer metered, on-demand access to computing resources. Instead of operating their own servers and facilities, customers specify workloads—sets of defined computing tasks, utilizing computing resources—for which cloud providers handle implementation and execution,” according to research by the Atlantic Council.
While readers may find a variety of terms used by companies marketing cloud services to describe clouds that are “dedicated,” “commercial,” “mission-focused,” and so on, these are largely distinctions in rhetoric or sales intent rather than substance. It is also material to acknowledge that buying and building cloud infrastructure is capital-intensive and the four largest cloud providers, often collectively referred to as the “hyperscalers,” bring in revenues well in excess of their competitors, which can influence where and how they operate.
Cloud-enabled ISR architecture also could facilitate the integration of generative AI and commercial-sensing systems that are becoming increasingly proliferated and accurate. When fused with retained allied ISR capabilities and organic NATO feeds in a trusted cloud environment, these commercial sources can reduce costs and enhance redundancy. Generative AI systems can provide more effective machine reasoning over large and rapidly changing datasets. However, integrating these systems presents risks. Commercial and open-source data are vulnerable to manipulation, misinformation, and adversarial deception, reinforcing the need for rigorous data validation and human oversight. Generative AI systems remain in their commercial infancy—and harnessing the effects of a large language model inside a software system takes time, experience, and tolerance for failure. These technologies don’t solve NATO’s ISR challenges, but they do present a cost-effective path that acknowledges the political reality of the Alliance and strengthens collective defense.
As NATO faces growing pressure to adopt emerging commercial technologies, its reliance on cloud services will deepen, and how it procures this capability will be vital. Procurement guidance should specify requirements in operational terms such as latency, throughput, and availability, rather than privileging particular vendors or national frameworks. Conflicting trust regimes risk undermining interoperability across NATO’s thirty-two-nation cloud ecosystem, reducing collaboration without delivering meaningful security gains. Harmonizing verifiable, outcome-based trust criteria would better reflect Alliance realities while preserving flexibility and resilience. When France requires SecNumCloud while Germany applies C5 attestation and the US mandates FedRAMP, interoperability suffers without improving security.
NATO should move toward trust criteria that are verifiable, meaningful, and collaborative rather than imposing unilateral entity-based exclusions.
Waterfall techniques, where many states’ security requirements can reference a common standard or satisfy the same certification, can be useful but should be approached with caution. The interplay of national standards risks conflating related terms without their underlying differentiated meaning or associated compliance mechanisms. How something is being audited and verified in real time is often as important as the requirement itself.
NATO’s digital transformation agenda has generated genuine policy momentum, yet implementation continues to lag behind both operational necessity and technological availability. The April 2025 adoption of an AI-enabled, cross-domain technology platform represents a meaningful inflection point.
For the first time, all thirty-two allies can access a common environment capable of federated data access, handling multiple classification levels. Equally important, the acquisition was framed around capability requirements rather than vendor identity, which is a precedent NATO should preserve.
Certain cloud providers can already meet many, if not most, of the requirements of the technologies discussed here. These requirements are also not the last word in what NATO and its member states need, but rather the best public representation of that use case. One reasonable requirement for NATO’s classified cloud deployments is security protocols that are sufficient to protect NATO workloads from cloud-provider staff viewing them.
Some use cases or specific requirements might only be met by a small handful of providers, and that should be weighed against locality but not held in opposition. As stated in past Atlantic Council research, “Artificially constraining cloud providers, mandating technology transfer, and rewarding regulatory arbitrage do nothing to advance national sovereignty objectives and incentivize lax security practices instead of proactive, systemic monitoring.”
NATO’s 2022 Digital Transformation Vision articulated the ambition of a shared digital backbone and data ecosystem. The 2024 Digital Transformation Implementation Strategy sought to operationalize that vision.
Progress, however, remains incremental. Given the operational environment on NATO’s eastern flank, incrementalism is no longer sufficient. 2026 should mark the transition from voluntary compliance to mandatory implementation for core digital standards.
This urgency is magnified by the Alliance’s June 2025 commitment to invest 5 percent of GDP annually in defense and security-related spending by 2035. As NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte noted, this decision resolves a transatlantic imbalance that has persisted since the 1950s.
However, this opportunity is not without risk. Absent deliberate guidance and clear standards, new resources will be absorbed by legacy platforms or national stovepipes, producing fragmentation at an even greater scale.
The opportunity is to invest a meaningful portion of this funding in shared civilian/military infrastructure with firm requirements for meaningful Allied interoperability. Dual-use infrastructure amortizes the costs across defense and civilian budgets, making cloud-infrastructure investment (to include data centers, energy-grid upgrades, and telecom improvements) more palatable politically and more resilient. NATO cannot afford slow, uneven implementation while the threat environment continues to accelerate.
This paper has argued that NATO’s core ISR challenge resides not in collection but in fusion, and that the new 5 percent target presents opportunities for collective investment with firm and vendor-agnostic interoperability standards. Whether this produces collective advantage or simply amplifies existing fragmentation depends on the Alliance. Below are some steps that NATO should consider taking:
Taken together, these recommendations support a principled and pragmatic path toward cloud infrastructure and the potential it supports for adopting AI and other emerging technologies to support NATO’s ISR mission. The paper prioritizes interoperability, which will allow allies to retain control over sensitive assets while enabling faster, more coherent collective action. The threat environment is evolving, and the operational consequences of inaction are already becoming visible on NATO’s eastern flank. The Alliance already possesses the sensing capacity. It must now invest in the connective tissue and shared infrastructure to translate data into actionable shared intelligence at speed.

_source.movement_title: 北约数字转型：混合威胁下的云ISR体系构建
_source.movement_abstract: 北约东部防线面临混合威胁挑战，传统情报监视与侦察（ISR）体系难以应对持续多域竞争。尽管北约及其成员国拥有先进ISR平台，但数据碎片化、共享选择性及处理架构滞后导致响应效率不足。2025年6月北约承诺2035年前将防务支出提升至GDP的5%，但若缺乏明确标准，新增资源可能被传统系统吸收加剧碎片化。基于云计算的ISR体系被建议作为解决方案，通过共享基础设施实现数据融合与快速响应，同时保留成员国数据主权。乌克兰Delta系统经验表明，整合卫星、雷达与无人机数据可将情报处理时间从72小时压缩至2分钟，但北约需构建联邦式架构以平衡安全与效率。当前北约数字转型进展缓慢，2024年实施策略虽确立共享数字基础，但2026年前需强制推行核心数字标准。云服务商需满足北约安全要求，避免因单边信任标准损害互操作性。文章强调北约应投资共享民用/军用基础设施，推动AI等技术应用，并制定可验证的互操作标准以应对加速的威胁环境。

_source.title: Fusion on paper or in practice? Making the cloud work for ISR and NATO
_source.trans_cont:
北约东翼面临一个由持续混合威胁定义的转变后的作战环境，这些威胁暴露出情报融合和响应时间上的关键缺口。空域侵入、海底电缆破坏、网络入侵、信息行动和有针对性的GPS干扰不仅仅是孤立事件，而是俄罗斯持续战略的一部分，旨在探测防御、测试决心，并对为应对偶发危机而设计的北约系统架构施加持续压力。
联盟的核心挑战并不在于感知能力。北约及其成员国在所有领域都部署了先进的情报、监视和侦察（ISR）平台。问题在于速度、整合和信任。数据仍然分散在国家系统中，选择性共享，并通过不适合当前作战节奏的架构进行处理。如果没有相应的共享基础设施投资，以及明确的标准，采用新兴技术和现代化系统可能会加剧摩擦，而非减少。
2025年6月北约承诺到2035年每年将国内生产总值（GDP）的5%用于国防和安全支出，这可能解决一些问题。然而，缺乏明确的指导，新资源可能会被传统平台和方法吸收，导致更大规模的碎片化。
本文认为，基于云的ISR与北约的联邦政治现实相一致，能够为有效的现代化提供基础设施。与其试图集中情报收集，投资云基础设施可以匹配对互操作性的愿望与技术现实，同时使盟国能够保留数据所有权，并促进共享处理、融合和受控传播。根据2025年6月海牙峰会宣言中概述的2029年北约整体支出轨迹和平衡评估，北约应强制所有新ISR采购的互操作性标准。同时，应明确对所有云供应商的要求，将增加的国防支出中相当一部分用于共享数字基础设施，并依赖基于可验证技术措施的严格信任框架。
北约东翼正面临多个领域的持续压力。空域侵入、海上破坏、网络入侵和有意识的信息行动去年都发生了，并已成为常态。这些不是孤立事件，而是俄罗斯持续战略的一部分，旨在探测联盟防御、测试政治决心，并对北约及其成员国施加持续的作战和认知压力。
2025年最后几个月，北约东翼至少有十三天发生了可追溯的空域侵入事件。
其他发展包括2024年11月至2025年1月期间波罗的海地区发生的海底电缆事件，三个月内至少有七次电缆被切断，同时持续的GPS干扰影响了85%进出爱沙尼亚的航班，以及2025年1月波兰记录的2732起事件。虽然北约已作出回应，尤其是通过“波罗的海哨兵”和“东方哨兵”行动，但最近的事件暴露了联盟在快速整合力量和信息以应对战争性质变化方面的能力不足。
这些侵入引发了机场关闭和战斗机出动，同时考验并揭示了北约ISR架构的低效。更严重的是，除了其直接的作战影响和应对措施外，这些侵入强化了现代战争的混合性质，其中塑造公众认知和社会韧性与军事效果一样具有战略意义。北约未来防御和应对能力将不仅取决于处理能力和系统设计，还取决于F-35出动速度。
核心挑战并不在于感知能力的缺乏。北约及其成员国在所有领域都部署了广泛的先进ISR平台。问题在于速度、整合和信任。这一挑战不仅限于联盟层面。即使国家军队也难以将来自不同感知平台的数据整合为统一的观察能力——正如最近在波罗的海追踪潜艇活动的努力所显示的那样。
联盟数据仍然分散在国家系统中，选择性共享，并通过不适合持续、多领域竞争的架构进行处理。通过先进计算技术增强互操作性是北约应对不仅空中和海上侵入，还包括日益复杂的网络和认知攻击能力的关键。同样重要的是，云基础设施提供了传统架构无法匹敌的韧性，例如分布式存储和冗余处理，以确保关键情报在个别节点受损时仍然可用。
乌克兰已成为云赋能战争最重要的实验室，其经验为北约提供了关键教训。核心教训是，现代冲突的节奏、规模和性质正在发生变化。该国的Delta战场管理系统将卫星图像、雷达和无人机侦察整合为统一的作战画面，将探测到交战的时间从大约72小时缩短到大约2分钟。
这种压缩改变了战场决策，使近实时感知在分散单位中变得可访问。这种效果是由不同来源数据的融合驱动的，而不是由单一精良平台。
对北约的教训不是Delta的技术配置，而是其实施和架构。
商业技术生态系统也已被证明在操作上是有用的。由人工智能驱动的目标定位技术进一步促进整合，商业合成孔径雷达（SAR）星座，以及低成本的人工智能视觉模块，提高了第一人称视角（FPV）无人机的精度，都展示了ISR的变革可能性。作为证明，乌克兰的军事领导层将大部分防御成功归功于类似的科技堆栈。
北约
_source.trans_title: 纸上谈兵还是实战应用？让云技术为情报、监视与侦察及北约服务
_source.evidence: 文章主要讨论了北约（NATO）在认知域和情报监视侦察（ISR）领域面临的挑战，特别是针对俄罗斯在东翼的混合威胁（包括信息战、网络攻击等）。文章的核心内容是提出一种基于云技术的ISR架构解决方案，并建议北约制定新的政策、标准和战略框架（如2025年海牙峰会宣言、2026年数字转型实施策略等）来应对这些威胁。文章重点在于理论探讨、政策建议、战略框架的构建以及技术标准的制定，而非描述具体的作战行动、部队组建或单纯的武器研发。虽然涉及技术（云、AI），但其落脚点在于如何通过政策和架构设计来整合这些技术以服务于联盟战略。因此，最匹配的标签是[理论政策]。

_source.content:
In response to escalating concerns
about child safety online,
OpenAI has unveiled a blueprint to enhance U.S. child protection efforts amid the AI boom. The
Child Safety Blueprint
, which was released Tuesday, is designed to help with faster detection, better reporting, and more efficient investigation into cases of AI-enabled child exploitation.
The overall goal of the Child Safety Blueprint is to tackle the alarming rise in child sexual exploitation linked to advancements in AI. According to the
Internet Watch Foundation
(IWF), more than 8,000 reports of AI-generated child sexual abuse content were detected in the first half of 2025, a 14% increase from the year prior. This includes criminals using AI tools to generate fake explicit images of children for financial sextortion and to generate convincing messages for grooming.
OpenAI’s blueprint also comes amid increased scrutiny from policymakers, educators, and child-safety advocates, especially in light of
troubling incidents
where young individuals died by suicide after allegedly engaging with AI chatbots.
Last November, the Social Media Victims Law Center and the Tech Justice Law Project filed seven lawsuits in California state courts, alleging that OpenAI released GPT-4o before it was ready. The suits claim the product’s psychologically manipulative nature contributed to wrongful deaths by suicide and assisted suicide. They cite four individuals who died by suicide and three others who experienced severe, life-threatening delusions after extended interactions with the chatbot.
This blueprint was developed in collaboration with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) and the Attorney General Alliance, as well as with feedback from North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson and Utah Attorney General Derek Brown.
The company says that the blueprint focuses on three aspects: updating legislation to include AI-generated abuse material, refining reporting mechanisms to law enforcement, and integrating preventative safeguards directly into AI systems. By doing so, OpenAI aims not only to detect potential threats earlier but also to ensure actionable information reaches investigators promptly.
OpenAI’s new child safety blueprint builds on
previous initiatives
, including updated guidelines for interactions with users under 18, which prohibits the generation of inappropriate content, or encouraging self-harm, and avoiding advice that would help young people conceal unsafe behavior from caregivers. The company recently released a safety blueprint for teens in India.
_source.movement_title: OpenAI发布儿童安全蓝图应对AI生成儿童性剥削内容激增
_source.movement_abstract: 为应对人工智能技术滥用引发的儿童性剥削问题，OpenAI于2025年7月发布《儿童安全蓝图》，旨在提升美国儿童在线保护水平。该蓝图聚焦三大领域：推动立法更新以纳入AI生成的虐待内容、优化向执法部门的举报机制、在AI系统中集成预防性安全措施。据国际反网络色情基金会（IWF）数据，2025年上半年AI生成儿童性虐待内容举报量达8000余起，较前一年增长14%。此举响应了政策制定者、教育界和儿童权益倡导者对AI技术可能危害未成年人的心理健康及安全的担忧，尤其在多起青少年因AI聊天机器人产生自杀念头的事件后。此前，OpenAI已在印度推出青少年安全保护计划，并更新了针对18岁以下用户的交互指南，禁止生成不当内容、鼓励自残行为及提供帮助青少年隐藏危险行为的建议。该蓝图制定过程中获得失踪与受虐儿童国家中心（NCMEC）及总检察长联盟支持，北卡罗来纳州和犹他州检察长也提供了反馈。
_source.title: OpenAI releases a new safety blueprint to address the rise in child sexual exploitation
_source.trans_cont:
针对日益加剧的在线儿童安全担忧，OpenAI发布了蓝图，旨在借助AI热潮提升美国儿童保护工作。周二发布的《儿童安全蓝图》旨在帮助更快发现、更高效报告和调查AI技术助长的儿童性剥削案件。

《儿童安全蓝图》的总体目标是应对与AI技术进步相关的儿童性剥削案件激增问题。据互联网监控基金会（IWF）统计，2025年上半年检测到超过8000份AI生成的儿童性虐待内容报告，比前一年增长14%。这包括犯罪分子利用AI工具生成儿童虚假色情图像进行财务勒索，以及生成具有说服力的对话内容进行诱骗。

OpenAI发布该蓝图也正值政策制定者、教育工作者和儿童安全倡导者对其加强监督之际，尤其在一些令人担忧的事件中，年轻个体因疑似与AI聊天机器人互动后自杀身亡。

去年11月，社交媒体受害者法律中心和科技正义法律项目在加州州法院提起七起诉讼，指控OpenAI在产品准备就绪前就发布了GPT-4o。诉讼称该产品的心理操控性导致了自杀和协助自杀的错误死亡，并引用四名自杀身亡者和三名在与聊天机器人长时间互动后出现严重、危及生命的妄想症的案例。

该蓝图是在与国家失踪和受虐儿童中心（NCMEC）和检察长联盟合作，并征询北卡罗来纳州检察长杰夫·杰克逊和犹他州检察长德里克·布朗意见的基础上制定的。

公司表示，该蓝图聚焦三个方面：更新法律以涵盖AI生成的虐待内容、完善向执法部门报告的机制，以及将预防性安全措施直接整合进AI系统。通过这些措施，OpenAI不仅希望更早发现潜在威胁，还确保可操作信息能及时传达给调查人员。

OpenAI的新儿童安全蓝图延续了此前的举措，包括针对18岁以下用户互动的更新指南，禁止生成不当内容或鼓励自残，以及避免提供可能帮助年轻人隐瞒危险行为的建议。公司最近还发布了针对印度青少年的安全蓝图。
_source.trans_title: OpenAI发布新的安全蓝图 以应对儿童性剥削的上升

_source.content:
Cybercriminals have allegedly stolen a large amount of sensitive internal documents from the Los Angeles Police Department and leaked the data online.
The stolen data included police officer personnel files, internal affairs investigations, and discovery documents that can include unredacted criminal complaints and personal information, such as witness names and medical data,
according to The Los Angeles Times
.
Emma Best, the founder of transparency group Distributed Denial of Secrets, which hosts the data, said
in an online post
that the extortion gang World Leaks is behind the data breach.
Best said she was able to review some of the leaked data when it was posted — and then deleted — on the gang’s leak website, where the group publicizes its breaches in an attempt to pressure its victims into paying a ransom.
It’s not clear for what reason the data is no longer listed on World Leaks’ website.
In a public statement
, the LAPD said it is investigating the breach, which it said did not involve LAPD systems or networks, but rather affected “a digital storage system” belonging to the Los Angeles City Attorney’s Office.
The LAPD said it is “working with the LA City Attorney’s Office to gain access to the impacted files to understand the full scope of the data breach.”
According to The Los Angeles Times, most police officer records under California state law are deemed private. The newspaper said that the leak, if proven authentic, would represent a “stunning breach of police data,” as police records are rarely disclosed or published.
The breach reportedly exposed 7.7 terabytes of data and more than 337,000 files.
A spokesperson for the LA City Attorney’s Office did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment. An LAPD spokesperson declined to comment, referring to the department’s public statement on X.
The hackers could not be reached for comment.
World Leaks started its activities in January 2025 as an apparent rebrand of a previous group known as Hunters International. Since then, the group has compromised organizations across several industries, including healthcare, manufacturing, technology, and others.
According to
cybersecurity firm Halcyon
, the hackers have “demonstrated capability against defense contractors and Fortune 500 organizations.”
Updated to included the LAPD’s response.
_source.movement_title: 洛杉矶警方遭黑客窃取7.7TB敏感数据 World Leaks团伙所为
_source.movement_abstract: 黑客团伙World Leaks涉嫌窃取洛杉矶警方7.7TB敏感数据并在线泄露，涉及警察人员档案、内部调查及刑事投诉等未删减文件。洛杉矶市检察官办公室称数据泄露源于其数字存储系统，与警方系统无关。该事件若属实将构成罕见的警察数据泄露，因加州法律规定大部分警员记录属于隐私范畴。网络安全公司Halcyon指出该团伙具备攻击国防承包商及财富500强企业的能力。World Leaks系2025年1月由Hunters International改名重组，已针对医疗、制造、科技等多个行业实施网络攻击。洛杉矶市检察官办公室和警方均表示正在合作调查数据泄露范围，但未透露具体原因及后续处理措施。
_source.title: Hackers steal and leak sensitive LAPD police documents
_source.trans_cont: 据称，网络犯罪分子从洛杉矶警察局窃取了大量敏感内部文件，并将数据泄露到网上。据《洛杉矶时报》报道，被盗数据包括警察人员档案、内部事务调查文件以及可能包含未删除的刑事指控和个人信息（如证人姓名和医疗数据）的发现文件。透明度组织“分布式拒绝服务”（Distributed Denial of Secrets）的创始人艾玛·贝斯特（Emma Best）在一篇在线帖子中表示，数据泄露事件是由勒索团伙World Leaks所为。贝斯特称，她曾查看过该团伙在其泄露网站上发布并随后删除的部分数据，该网站用于公布其攻击事件，以迫使受害者支付赎金。目前尚不清楚数据为何不再列于World Leaks网站上。洛杉矶警察局（LAPD）在一份公开声明中表示，正在调查此次数据泄露事件，称此次事件并未涉及LAPD的系统或网络，而是影响了洛杉矶市检察官办公室的“一个数字存储系统”。LAPD表示，正在与洛杉矶市检察官办公室合作，以获取受影响文件，了解数据泄露的全部范围。据《洛杉矶时报》报道，根据加利福尼亚州法律，大多数警察人员记录被视为私人信息。该报称，如果此次泄露属实，将代表一次“令人震惊的警察数据泄露”，因为警察记录很少被披露或发布。据报道，此次泄露涉及7.7太字节的数据和超过337,000份文件。洛杉矶市检察官办公室的一名发言人未立即回应TechCrunch的评论请求，LAPD发言人则表示不作评论，转而引用部门在X平台上的公开声明。黑客组织未回应评论请求。World Leaks于2025年1月开始活动，似乎是此前名为Hunters International的组织的重新品牌。此后，该组织已入侵了多个行业的机构，包括医疗、制造、科技等。据网络安全公司Halcyon称，黑客已“展现出针对国防承包商和财富500强企业的攻击能力”。已更新内容，包含LAPD的回应。
_source.trans_title: 黑客窃取并泄露了洛杉矶警察局的敏感文件

_source.content:
Russia has confirmed the deaths of 16 Cameroonian nationals fighting with its army in the invasion of Ukraine, Cameroon’s government said in an internal document obtained Tuesday.
The foreign ministry note acknowledging receipt of a fatality list from the Russian embassy in Yaounde said the “contract soldiers” had been “engaged in the special military operation zone,” using Russia’s phrase for its invasion.
The note, dated Monday, did not give further details on the circumstances of their deaths.
Ukraine says around 1,800 Africans have been enrolled to fight with Russian forces in the war since 2022. Some allege they were lured with fake promises of jobs or educational programs, then forced into the army.
Cameroon had not previously acknowledged officially that it had citizens involved in the conflict, despite local media reports on families’ anguish over their loved ones being enlisted by Russia.
Cameroonian authorities asked the families of the deceased to contact the foreign ministry, in a statement aired on state broadcaster CRTV.
In February, the watchdog group All Eyes on Wagner published the names of 1,417 Africans enlisted by Moscow from January 2023 to September 2025 for its Ukraine campaign. More than 300 had died.
Egypt, Cameroon, and Ghana were the top countries of origin.
Tags
Cameroon Conflict Russia Ukraine

_source.movement_abstract: 俄罗斯确认16名喀麦隆籍雇佣兵在乌克兰冲突中阵亡，相关死亡名单由俄罗斯驻雅温得大使馆提供。喀麦隆外交部在1月18日接收文件中承认这些公民参与了俄罗斯的特别军事行动区域，但未披露死亡细节。乌克兰方面称自2022年以来约有1800名非洲人在俄乌战争中被招募，部分人涉嫌被虚假就业或教育项目引诱后被迫参军。尽管当地媒体曾报道俄罗斯征召喀麦隆公民引发家属担忧，但喀麦隆政府此前未正式承认公民参与冲突。2023年1月统计显示，莫斯科在2023年1月至2025年9月期间共招募1417名非洲籍士兵参与乌克兰行动，其中300余人死亡，埃及、喀麦隆和加纳为主要来源国。喀麦隆政府要求阵亡者家属通过国家电视台CRTV联系外交部。

_source.trans_cont: 俄罗斯确认在入侵乌克兰的行动中阵亡的16名喀麦隆公民，喀麦隆政府在周二获得的一份内部文件中表示。外交部的声明承认收到了俄罗斯驻雅温得大使馆提供的伤亡名单，称这些“合同兵”参与了俄罗斯所谓的“特别军事行动区”的战斗。这份周一发布的声明未提供更多关于他们死亡情况的细节。乌克兰称自2022年以来已有约1800名非洲人被征召加入俄军参战。一些人指控他们被虚假的工作承诺或教育项目所诱骗，随后被强迫入伍。尽管当地媒体报道了家属因亲人被俄军征召而痛苦的情况，喀麦隆此前并未正式承认有本国公民参与冲突。喀麦隆当局在国家广播公司CRTV播放的声明中要求阵亡者的家属联系外交部。2月，监督组织“关注瓦格纳”公布了从2023年1月至2025年9月期间莫斯科招募的1417名非洲人名单，其中超过300人已阵亡。埃及、喀麦隆和加纳是主要来源国。标签：喀麦隆 冲突 俄罗斯 乌克兰

Anthropic will make its new AI model available to some of the world’s biggest cybersecurity and software firms in an effort to slow the arms race ignited by AI in the hands of hackers, Anthropic said Tuesday. Amazon, Apple, Cisco, Google, JPMorgan Chase and Microsoft, among other firms, will now have access to Anthropic’s Mythos model for cyber defense purposes. That includes finding bugs in those firms’ software and testing whether specific hacking techniques work on their products. Mythos (officially dubbed “Claude Mythos Preview”) is not ready for a public launch because of the ways it could be abused by cybercriminals and spies, according to Anthropic — a prospect that has prompted widespread concern in Washington and in Silicon Valley.

_source.content:
UK cyber defense authorities have warned that a Russian state-linked hacking group is exploiting poorly secured internet hardware to conduct credential theft and traffic interception.
The National Cyber Security Centre said attackers are compromising widely used “edge devices” such as home and small office routers.
Once accessed, these devices can silently redirect internet traffic through attacker-controlled infrastructure.
The activity has been attributed to APT28, also known as Fancy Bear, Sofacy, or Sednit, which the UK attributes to Russia’s military intelligence service, specifically the GRU’s Military Unit 26165.
London has previously tied the group to cyber espionage campaigns targeting Western institutions, including logistics networks and technology firms.
Hijacking Through DNS
At the center of the operation is the Domain Name System (DNS), which converts human-readable web addresses into machine-readable IP addresses.
By tampering with DNS, attackers can redirect users to fraudulent websites that mimic legitimate platforms, allowing the attackers to capture login credentials such as usernames, passwords, and authentication tokens.
The operation starts broadly, scanning for vulnerable devices, then narrows to targets of intelligence value once access is gained.
Mitigation Measures
Authorities recommend a set of basic mitigation steps to reduce exposure.
These include restricting access to device management interfaces, applying regular firmware and software updates to address known vulnerabilities, and enabling multi-factor authentication to limit the impact of credential theft.
Additional measures include monitoring for unusual DNS changes and ensuring default passwords are replaced with strong, unique credentials.
Tags

_source.movement_title: 俄罗斯黑客组织利用路由器漏洞实施DNS劫持窃取凭证
_source.movement_abstract: 英国网络安全部门警告称，一个与俄罗斯政府关联的黑客组织正在利用未妥善保护的互联网硬件进行凭证窃取和流量拦截。国家网络安全中心指出，攻击者已入侵广泛使用的边缘设备（如家庭及小型办公室路由器），通过控制这些设备将互联网流量秘密重定向至攻击者掌控的基础设施。此次活动被归因于APT28组织，该组织还被称为Fancy Bear、Sofacy或Sednit，英国将其与俄罗斯军情局（GRU）26165部队关联。此前伦敦已将该组织与针对西方机构的网络间谍行动联系起来，包括物流网络和技术企业。攻击核心手段为篡改域名系统（DNS），通过劫持DNS将用户引导至伪造网站以窃取登录凭证。攻击流程通常从广泛扫描易受攻击设备开始，获取访问权限后转向具有情报价值的目标。官方建议采取限制设备管理界面访问权限、定期更新固件和软件、启用多因素认证、监控异常DNS变更及更换默认密码等基本缓解措施。
_source.title: UK Flags Russian Group Exploiting Vulnerable Routers for Data Interception
_source.trans_cont:
英国网络安全机构警告称，一个与俄罗斯有关联的黑客组织正在利用安全性较差的网络硬件进行凭证窃取和流量拦截。国家网络安全中心表示，攻击者正在入侵广泛使用的“边缘设备”，如家庭和小型办公室路由器。一旦被入侵，这些设备可以悄无声息地将网络流量重定向至攻击者控制的基础设施。该活动被归因于APT28（也称为Fancy Bear、Sofacy或Sednit），英国将其归咎于俄罗斯军情部门格鲁乌的第26165部队。伦敦此前曾将该组织与针对西方机构的网络间谍活动联系起来，包括物流网络和技术公司。

通过DNS劫持
此次行动的核心是域名系统（DNS），它将人类可读的网址转换为机器可读的IP地址。攻击者通过篡改DNS，可将用户重定向至模仿合法平台的欺诈网站，从而捕获用户名、密码和认证令牌等登录凭证。该行动初期广泛扫描漏洞设备，一旦获得访问权限，便聚焦于具有情报价值的目标。

缓解措施
机构建议采取一系列基础缓解措施以降低风险。这些措施包括限制设备管理界面的访问权限、定期更新固件和软件以修复已知漏洞，以及启用多因素认证以减少凭证窃取的影响。其他措施还包括监控异常的DNS变更，并将默认密码替换为强且唯一的凭证。

_source.trans_title: 英国旗标俄罗斯集团利用易受攻击的路由器进行数据拦截
_source.evidence: 文章核心描述了俄罗斯国家关联黑客组织（APT28）利用路由器漏洞进行网络间谍活动和流量拦截的具体行动。虽然涉及技术漏洞利用，但重点在于敌对势力的具体攻击行为（行动），而非单纯的技术研发或武器化探索。该事件针对的是英国及西方机构，并未直接涉及中国大陆作为被攻击对象或相关方，因此不符合[涉我事件]。文章未提及演习、新机构成立、政策发布或理论框架。根据定义，这属于相关领域的具体对抗行动及其动向，故归类为[行动动向]。

_source.content:
Landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely was a clear and compelling demonstration of U.S. technological prowess and might in an era of strategic competition with the Soviet Union. The United States went to the Moon during the Cold War precisely for that reason—to demonstrate to the world the supremacy of capitalism over communism and democracy over autocracy. President John F. Kennedy chose this goal in 1961 because it was the one NASA was most confident it could achieve before the Soviets, and before the decade was out. The United States went to the Moon to win.
And the United States did win. People around the world were captivated by the Moon landing. An estimated one in five people across the planet watched live when Neil Armstrong took his one small step on July 20, 1969. It was a turning point in the Cold War.
Unfortunately, it was also a turning point in the U.S. space program. Instead of building on the United States’ giant leap for all mankind, winning was the end. Apollo missions 18, 19, and 20 were canceled due to declining public interest and shifting political priorities—and no human (let alone American)—has traveled further than low Earth orbit since.
The Artemis program offers an opportunity to change that—beginning with Artemis II, when NASA sends the first humans to lunar orbit since 1972. But the Artemis program is notable not for its repetition of Apollo-era missions, but for its explicit goal of establishing a sustained human presence on another celestial body.
Rather than chasing flags and footprints, NASA is planning to build a Moon base, a feat that will again demonstrate the technological might of the United States—but this time in an enduring way. Establishing a permanent presence on the Moon will push the space economy into cislunar space, creating business opportunities for a new generation of American dreamers and entrepreneurs. It will provide experience in long-duration surface missions, laying the groundwork for humanity’s next giant leap–to Mars. And most importantly, it will extend Western values and democracy to a new foothold in the solar system.
Today, the United States is again in an era of strategic competition, not with the Soviets but with the People’s Republic of China. There is a strong bipartisan consensus in Washington that the United States must return to the Moon before China lands its first taikonauts on the lunar surface. This element of competition helps create the urgency and drive that energizes the nation’s space program and excites the American people with demonstrations of new and novel feats.
But the United States should not recreate a competition it has already won. China almost certainly has a long-term plan to establish a permanent presence on the Moon—one that is oriented around its priorities, its economy, and its values. So yes, the United States should compete with China as a key strategic rationale for the U.S. space program. But the United States should not mistake the sprint to be first with the marathon to stay.
It is time to return to the Moon, and this time, the United States needs to be in it for the long game.
Audrey M. Schaffer is a senior associate (non-resident) at the Aerospace Security Project of the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, D.C. She is a space policy expert with experience across the civil, commercial, and national security space sectors. She previously served in the U.S. government for over 15 years, including on the National Security Council staff, at the Departments of Defense and State, and at NASA.
_source.movement_title: 美国重返月球：从短期竞赛到长期战略
_source.movement_abstract: 文章回顾了美国冷战时期通过阿波罗计划实现登月的历史背景，指出该计划旨在展示资本主义与民主制度对苏联共产主义的科技优势。1969年阿波罗11号登月成为冷战转折点，但随后因公众兴趣下降和政治优先级变化，美国终止了后续登月任务。当前阿尔忒弥斯计划提出重返月球的新目标，重点转向建立长期月球基地，推动地月空间经济发展，并为火星探索积累经验。作者强调中美新一轮太空竞争中，美国应超越短期登月竞赛，制定可持续的长期战略，通过月球基地扩展西方价值观和民主制度。文章指出中国同样可能在推进月球长期计划，建议美国在竞争中注重战略规划而非单纯追求速度。
_source.post_location: 华盛顿特区西北罗德岛大道1616号
_source.site_name: 美国战略与国际问题研究中心
_source.title: We Are Going Back to the Moon to Stay
_source.trans_cont:
将一个人送上月球并安全返回，是美国在与苏联进行战略竞争的时代，展示其科技实力和力量的明确而有力的证明。在冷战期间，美国正是出于这个原因前往月球——向世界展示资本主义优于共产主义，民主优于专制。总统约翰·F·肯尼迪在1961年选择这一目标，是因为他认为NASA最有可能在苏联之前实现这一目标，并在十年内完成。美国前往月球是为了胜利。

美国确实取得了胜利。全球各地的人们都被登月所吸引。据估计，当时地球上每五个人中就有一人观看了尼尔·阿姆斯特朗在1969年7月20日迈出那一步的直播。这是冷战的一个转折点。

不幸的是，这也是美国航天计划的一个转折点。美国没有在人类历史上迈出的一大步上继续前进，胜利就结束了。阿波罗18、19和20号任务因公众兴趣下降和政治优先事项的变化而被取消，自那以后，没有人（更不用说美国人了）去过比近地轨道更远的地方。

阿尔忒弥斯计划提供了改变这一局面的机会——从阿尔忒弥斯二号任务开始，NASA将再次将人类送往自1972年以来的月球轨道。但阿尔忒弥斯计划之所以引人注目，不是因为它重复了阿波罗时代的任务，而是因为它明确的目标是建立在另一个天体上的持续人类存在。

NASA不再追逐旗帜和脚印，而是计划建立一个月球基地，这将再次展示美国的科技实力，但这次是持久的。在月球上建立永久存在将推动航天经济进入地月空间，为新一代美国梦想家和企业家创造商业机会。它将提供长期地表任务的经验，为人类下一步的巨大飞跃——前往火星——奠定基础。最重要的是，它将把西方价值观和民主扩展到太阳系的新立足点。

今天，美国再次处于战略竞争的时代，不是与苏联，而是与中国人民共和国。华盛顿方面存在强烈的两党共识，认为美国必须在中国人首次将宇航员送上月球表面之前重返月球。这种竞争元素有助于创造紧迫感和动力，激发美国的航天计划，并让美国人民为新的、前所未有的成就感到兴奋。

但美国不应重演已经赢得的竞争。中国几乎肯定有一个长期计划，旨在在月球上建立永久存在——这将围绕其优先事项、经济和价值观展开。因此，美国确实应该将与中国竞争作为美国航天计划的一个关键战略理由。但美国不应将赢得竞赛的冲刺误解为赢得长期比赛的马拉松。

现在是时候重返月球了，这次，美国需要为长远目标做好准备。  
奥黛丽·M·沙弗是华盛顿特区战略与国际研究中心航空航天安全项目的一名高级研究员（非驻职）。她是一位空间政策专家，拥有民用、商业和国家安全空间领域的丰富经验。她曾在美政府任职超过15年，包括在国家安全委员会工作人员、国防部和国务院，以及NASA工作。

政戰局文宣心戰處副處長王宜弘上校晉任少將,月底接任文宣處處長一職。(資料照,記者張嘉明攝)
〔記者羅添斌/台北報導〕國防部心戰大隊在2019年曾公開展示戰時軍方的心戰手段,除了心戰喊話車以及心戰作業車之外,外包裝上印有簡體字與我國旗的心戰「投誠食品」成為眾人焦點,更讓老共跳腳,這兩年更點名批評心戰大隊還揚言制裁,當年的心戰大隊長王宜弘上校,本週接受賴總統的授階晉任少將,並將在月底接任國防部政戰局文宣心戰處長,扛起國軍反制共軍認知作戰的文宣重任。
心戰大隊是國防部政戰局所屬的特業部隊,下設多個中隊,是反制共軍認知作戰的責單位,2015年11月也與太平洋司令部第七心戰群簽署「合作協議書」,雙方建立「戰略溝通平台」及推動互訪、輔訓及聯合演訓計畫,未來台灣若遭逢戰亂,資訊傳播管道遭中國封鎖時,即可透過這個管道由美方提供協助,甚至是進一步接替執行任務。

國防部心戰大隊在2019年曾公開展示戰時軍方的心戰手段,除了心戰喊話車以及心戰作業車之外,外包裝上印有簡體字與我國旗的心戰「投誠食品」成為眾人焦點,更讓老共跳腳。(圖:軍聞社提供)
在2019年的心戰能量展示時,軍方展示出包括泡麵、巧克力夾心餅乾、牛奶糖和蛋捲等心戰食品,外包裝上都印上了投誠步驟、投誠地點,像是「中華民國國軍軍原味蛋捲」上頭,印有投誠地點「恆春仁壽派出所」以及地圖,投誠步驟按順序依序為:「放下武器」、「雙手舉高」、「持此蛋捲盒」、「向我軍投誠」、「回家團圓」。又或是牛奶糖盒上印有,「請保留此盒並放下武器投誠,我們將保證你的自由與安全」等字樣。
時任心戰大隊大隊長王宜弘當時表示,戰時心戰文宣品的製作選材是多樣化的,國軍配合戰場實際需求,結合台灣自由民主意涵,從食品外包裝到各種隨處可見的民生用品,都是心戰文宣品可運用的素材,做到植基於平時,運用於戰時。王宜弘表示,美軍在波灣戰爭中也採用相同招降手段,透過創意和巧思,將可運用的物資轉為對敵的心戰品。
賴總統為新任國防部文宣心戰處長王宜弘少將授階。(圖:軍聞社提供)
軍政人士說,王宜弘的思維敏捷,行事相當靈活,經常有新點子來因應共軍日新月異的認知戰招術,王宜弘目前擔任的是國防部政戰局文宣心戰處的副處長,現任處長朱蕙芳少將即將調任為後備指揮部的政戰主任,並由王宜弘直升處長,並且晉任少將,足證國防部各級長官對王宜弘表現的肯定。
值得一提的是政戰局文宣心戰處的副處長一職,近年已成為直升少將的跳板寶座,有些是外放調升為馬防部政戰主任,或是直升少將編制的處長,這種人事晉任的安排,也反映出國軍反制共軍認作戰上,對相人事佈局的重視。

_source.movement_title: 王宜弘晋升少将 将接任台湾国防部文宣心战处处长
_source.movement_abstract: 台湾国防部政战局文宣心战处副处长王宜弘上校近日获总统赖清德授阶晋升为少将，并将于月底接任文宣心战处处长一职。该职位负责主导国军反制共军认知作战的文宣工作。2019年心战大队曾公开展示战时文宣手段，包括印有简体字及台湾国旗的「投诚食品」，如泡面、巧克力夹心饼干等民生用品，外包装印有投诚步骤及地点，引发关注。该部队2015年11月与美军太平洋司令部第七心战群签署合作协议，建立战略沟通平台并推动联合演训。军政人士指出，王宜弘思维灵活，善于应对共军认知战策略，其晋升反映国军对此领域人事布局的重视。近年文宣心战处副处长职位已成为晋升少将的跳板，部分人员调任马防部政战主任或直升处长。
_source.site_name: 台湾自由时报-军事频道
_source.title: 賴總統點將》心戰「投誠食品」讓老共跳腳  王宜弘升少將掌國軍文宣
_source.trans_cont:
政战局文宣心战处副处长王宜弘上校晋升少将，月底将接任文宣处处长一职。（资料照，记者张嘉明摄）
〔记者罗添斌／台北报导〕国防部心战大队在2019年曾公开展示战时军方的心战手段，除了心战喊话车以及心战作业车之外，外包装上印有简体字与我国旗的心战「投诚食品」成为众人焦点，更让老共跳脚，这两年更点名批评心战大队还扬言制裁，当年的心战大队长王宜弘上校，本周接受赖总统的授阶晋升少将，并将在月底接任国防部政战局文宣心战处处长，扛起国军反制共军认知作战的文宣重任。
心战大队是国防部政战局所属的特业部队，下设多个中队，是反制共军认知作战的责任单位，2015年11月也与太平洋司令部第七心战群签署「合作协议书」，双方建立「战略沟通平台」及推动互访、辅训及联合演训计划，未来台湾若遭遇战乱，资讯传播管道遭中国封锁时，即可透过这个管道由美方提供协助，甚至是进一步接替执行任务。

在2019年的心战能量展示时，军方展示了包括泡面、巧克力夹心饼干、牛奶糖和蛋卷等心战食品，外包装上都印上了投诚步骤、投诚地点，例如「中华民国国军军原味蛋卷」上头，印有投诚地点「恒春仁寿派出所」以及地图，投诚步骤按顺序依次为：「放下武器」、「双手举高」、「持此蛋卷盒」、「向我军投诚」、「回家团圆」。又或是牛奶糖盒上印有，「请保留此盒并放下武器投诚，我们将保证你的自由与安全」等字样。
时任心战大队大队长王宜弘当时表示，战时心战文宣品的制作选材是多样化的，国军配合战场实际需求，结合台湾自由民主意涵，从食品外包装到各种随处可见的民生用品，都是心战文宣品可运用的素材，做到植基于平时，运用于战时。王宜弘表示，美军在海湾战争中也采用相同招降手段，透过创意和巧思，将可运用的物资转为对敌的心战品。
赖总统为新任国防部文宣心战处处长王宜弘少将授阶。（图：军闻社提供）
军政人士说，王宜弘的思维敏捷，行事相当灵活，经常有新点子来应对共军日新月异的认知战招术，王宜弘目前担任的是国防部政战局文宣心战处的副处长，现任处长朱蕙芳少将即将调任为后备指挥部的政战主任，并由王宜弘直升处长，并且晋升少将，足证国防部各级长官对王宜弘表现的肯定。
值得一提的是政战局文宣心战处的副处长一职，近年已成为直升少将的跳板宝座，有些是外放调升为马防部政战主任，或是直升少将编制的处长，这种人事晋任的安排，也反映出国军反制共军认知作战上，对人事布局的重视。

_source.content:
For NATO, innovation is only valuable if it equips warfighters with a military advantage. Allied Command Transformation helps make that happen through its Science and Technology Programme of Work, moving promising concepts quickly from experimentation into real operational pathways.
One of the mechanisms that accelerates that journey is the Innovation Continuum. It creates a repeatable cycle of scoping, experimentation, and demonstration that helps NATO test emerging and disruptive technologies with operational users, then transition what works to the commands and agencies that can adopt and sustain it.
The Innovation Continuum is NATO’s fast lane for turning innovation into operational capability, strengthening deterrence and readiness by rapidly translating emerging and disruptive technologies into real military advantage.
– Krzysztof Skurzak, Section Head of Science & Technology and lead of the Innovation Continuum at NATO Allied Command Transformation
As the Innovation Continuum prepares to begin its annual cycle later this month, four recent examples show what a focus on innovation can produce in practical terms: MAINSAIL, the Joint ISR Asset Planner, MDO AI, and Türkiye’s ALFA 2026 national innovation call, inspired by NATO ACT’s Innovation Continuum model.
MAINSAIL: Protecting critical underwater infrastructure
MAINSAIL (Multi Domain Awareness and Insight with AI Layering) is NATO’s maritime situational awareness capability focused on protecting critical underwater infrastructure such as subsea communication cables and energy pipelines. Developed by NATO’s Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation under Allied Command Transformation’s Programme of Work and in conjunction with Allied Maritime Command, it fuses inputs from sensors and other data sources to help operators spot patterns and anomalies tied to seabed security.
Over the past four months, the most significant change has been the integration and alignment of data. MAINSAIL has successfully integrated maritime-relevant information from the SINBAD (Smart Indication and Warning, Broad Area Detection) project, enabling more effective information sharing to enhance maritime situational awareness. This milestone supports NATO’s broader data strategy by leveraging information from different systems.
– LCDR Stefano Aiello, NATO Allied Command Transformation’s MAINSAIL Project Lead
Notably, this integration moved quickly. Since December 2024, Allied Command Operations and Allied Maritime Command have operated MAINSAIL continuously, 24/7, while the system continues to evolve toward full operational capability.
MAINSAIL has also consistently proven its value in real operational contexts. It supported major activity in 2025, including REPMUS and Dynamic Messenger, and it was demonstrated at the capstone “SHINE” event of the NATO Innovation Continuum at the end of 2025. In parallel, NATO is progressing the transition of ownership from Allied Command Transformation to Allied Command Operations and Allied Maritime Command, which is a key step toward wider operational adoption and long-term sustainment.
Joint ISR Asset Planner: Smarter collection management
The Joint ISR Asset Planner helps commanders and staffs plan how to use NATO intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance assets by reducing manual matching of requirements to platforms and sensors. It is being tailored for operational use in close coordination with operational stakeholders, focusing on practical workflows and integration.
Since last autumn, the team has adjusted the application to accommodate requirements from Allied Air Command. A demonstration of the updated version produced very positive feedback, and the project is now operating in a tight user feedback loop with frequent incremental releases.
A key next step is system-to-system integration. The team is defining the interface between INTEL FS SP2 (the Intelligence Functional Services Spiral 2 and the NATO intelligence community’s flagship capability) and the Joint ISR Asset Planner, with implementation and testing planned over the next few weeks. In parallel, lessons identified during SHINE highlighted additional work needed on the AI planning component that would automate deliberative and dynamic ISR asset planning. Importantly, those findings are already being fed straight into rapid updates, so the capability can be refined quickly and made more useful for real world planners.
MDO AI: Decision support for Multi Domain Operations
Last year, the MDO (Multi-Domain Operations) AI prototype demonstrated at the Innovation Continuum SHINE event showed how advanced algorithms can retrieve and process doctrinal and operational information to produce validated, actionable answers for staff decision support. Building on that foundation, the focus is now shifting from a single prototype toward the broader ecosystem required to make AI enabled decision support operational and scalable.
The practical lesson is that integration alone is not enough. Operational staffs need information that is discoverable, accessible on demand, and trustworthy when questions are ad hoc and mission driven. That requires stronger data quality, better search and retrieval, and tighter collaboration between subject matter experts and technical teams, so AI can find the right material, explain what it used, and support human judgement with transparency.
Security remains central as these capabilities mature. As AI systems replicate selected data to improve findability and speed, the same access controls and retention policies must follow that data wherever it resides. This is driving a stronger emphasis on Data Centric Security and Zero Trust principles built in from the start, with access control models evolving toward more granular approaches that reflect role, attributes, relationships, and topic sensitivity.
This year’s work packages reflect that shift: strengthening the foundations that enable trusted AI at scale, not as isolated tools, but as integrated, secure components of NATO’s broader digital transformation.
Türkiye: A national innovation call inspired by the Innovation Continuum
One of the clearest signs the Innovation Continuum is working is that Allies are inspired by the model, not just participating in it. After hosting NATO ACT Innovation Continuum milestones in 2025, Türkiye launched a national effort that mirrors the Continuum’s core logic: scenario-led problem framing, industry teaming for interoperability, and field demonstration under realistic conditions.
Türkiye’s initiative is ALFA 2026 (Artificial Intelligence, Quantum and Autonomous Systems Exercise), led by the Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye Secretariat of Defence Industries (SSB). SSB described the 2025 hosted Continuum events as the catalyst that helped create a national framework where companies can demonstrate capabilities together in integrated consortia rather than in isolation.
Through Türkiye’s ALFA 2026, Companies respond to a Request for Information with technical and performance details, plus how their systems can integrate with others. Feasible solutions will then be selected and moved into demonstration planning.
This is not happening in a national silo. Three consortia have already applied to NATO ACT’s Innovation Continuum 2026 cycle with the same concepts, and Türkiye plans to synchronize its national demonstrations with the broader NATO schedule, with the intent to integrate outputs such as the common operational picture into NATO infrastructure. Early momentum is strong: SSB reports more than 40 companies have already submitted intent to participate.
Through ALFA 2026, Türkiye aims to establish a robust experimentation environment that accelerates the application of Emerging and Disruptive Technologies (EDTs) to operational battlefield requirements. Türkiye views the Innovation Continuum as a key opportunity to test and advance interoperability with NATO Allies’ industries and operational assets.
– Professor Haluk Görgün, Secretary of Defence Industries (SSB)
Driving innovation forward
These stories share the same pattern: start with real operational needs, test in realistic conditions, and move quickly toward adoption. That is the practical value of the Innovation Continuum, and it is why ACT uses it to help turn experimentation into deliverable capability.
Later this month, SPARK will mark the first of four Innovation Continuum milestones for the year. Building on momentum from recent cycles that included dozens of experimentation and demonstration activities and hundreds of participants, SPARK will again focus the community on priority challenges that matter to planners and operators: Arctic ISR (Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance), AI in Audacious Training, the Layered Counter UAS Initiative, Next Generation Targeting, Smart Logistics and Sustainment, Electronic Warfare, AI Next Gen C4SR, Cognitive Warfare, and Cyber Resilience. Together, these topics will shape the scenarios, frame candidate solutions, and set the conditions for a strong SHINE capstone event in the series later this year.

_source.movement_title: 北约盟军转型司令部推进创新连续体加速新兴技术向作战能力转化
_source.movement_abstract: 【北约盟军转型司令部2026年6月报道】北约盟军转型司令部（ACT）通过创新连续体（Innovation Continuum）机制，加速新兴与颠覆性技术从实验阶段向实战能力转化。该机制包含范围界定、实验验证与演示评估的循环流程，旨在快速将技术优势转化为军事优势。近期重点成果包括：MAINSAIL项目通过融合SINBAD等数据源，实现对海底通信电缆及能源管道等关键水下基础设施的态势感知与异常监测，系统已于2024年12月起投入全天候运行；联合情报监视侦察（ISR）资产规划器通过优化平台与传感器匹配流程，提升指挥决策效率，正推进与INTEL FS SP2系统的深度集成；多域作战（MDO）人工智能原型从单一验证转向生态系统构建，强化数据质量与检索能力以支持动态决策。土耳其国防部工业局（SSB）受该模式启发，启动ALFA 2026国家创新计划，聚焦人工智能、量子及自主系统，已有超40家企业参与，旨在建立与北约同步的联合演示环境。2026年6月启动的SPARK活动将作为年度首个里程碑，聚焦北极ISR、认知战、电子战及网络弹性等优先挑战，为后续SHINE年度总结活动奠定基础。
_source.title: Scaling Innovation Across the Alliance: The Innovation Continuum’s Results and Influence
_source.trans_cont:
对北约而言，创新只有在为作战人员提供军事优势时才具有价值。盟军转型司令部通过其科技计划工作，帮助实现这一目标，将有前景的概念迅速从实验阶段转化为实际的作战路径。
加速这一进程的一个机制是创新连续体。它创建了一个可重复的范围界定、实验和演示循环，帮助北约与作战用户测试新兴和颠覆性技术，然后将行之有效的方法过渡到能够采用和持续发展的指挥机构和部门。
创新连续体是北约将创新转化为作战能力的快速通道，通过迅速将新兴和颠覆性技术转化为真正的军事优势，增强威慑力和战备状态。
—— 克日什托夫·斯库尔扎克，北约盟军转型司令部科技与创新连续体负责人
随着创新连续体准备在本月底开始其年度周期，四个最近的例子展示了对创新的关注在实际应用中可以产生什么成果：MAINSAIL、联合情报监视侦察资产规划器、多域作战人工智能（MDO AI）和土耳其的ALFA 2026国家创新呼吁，灵感来源于北约ACT的创新连续体模型。
MAINSAIL：保护关键的水下基础设施
MAINSAIL（多域态势感知与人工智能分层）是北约的海上态势感知能力，专注于保护关键的水下基础设施，如海底通信电缆和能源管道。由北约盟军转型司令部的计划工作和与盟军海上司令部联合开发，它融合了来自传感器和其他数据源的输入，帮助操作人员识别与海底安全相关的模式和异常。
在过去四个月中，最显著的变化是数据的整合和对齐。MAINSAIL成功整合了来自SINBAD（智能指示与预警、广域探测）项目的海上相关信息，使信息共享更加高效，从而增强海上态势感知能力。这一里程碑支持了北约更广泛的数据战略，利用不同系统的相关信息。
—— 大副斯特凡诺·艾利奥，北约盟军转型司令部MAINSAIL项目负责人
值得注意的是，这种整合进展迅速。自2024年12月以来，盟军行动司令部和盟军海上司令部已连续24小时不间断运行MAINSAIL，同时系统仍在向全面作战能力演进。
MAINSAIL在实际作战环境中也持续证明其价值。它支持了2025年的重大活动，包括REPMUS和Dynamic Messenger，并在2025年底北约创新连续体的“SHINE”活动上进行了演示。同时，北约正在推进从盟军转型司令部向盟军行动司令部和盟军海上司令部的过渡，这是向更广泛作战采用和长期维持的重要一步。
联合情报监视侦察资产规划器：更智能的采集管理
联合情报监视侦察资产规划器帮助指挥官和参谋人员规划如何使用北约的情报、监视和侦察资产，通过减少手动将需求与平台和传感器匹配来实现。它正在与作战利益相关者密切合作，针对实际工作流程和集成进行定制。
自去年秋天以来，团队已经调整了应用程序以满足盟军空军司令部的需求。更新版本的演示获得了非常积极的反馈，该项目现在正在与用户保持紧密的反馈循环，并频繁发布增量更新。
下一步的关键是系统间的集成。团队正在定义INTEL FS SP2（情报功能服务螺旋2和北约情报界旗舰能力）与联合情报监视侦察资产规划器之间的接口，并计划在未来几周内进行实施和测试。同时，SHINE期间识别出的教训表明，还需要在人工智能规划组件上进行额外的工作，以实现自动化的审慎和动态情报监视侦察资产规划。重要的是，这些发现已经直接用于快速更新，使能力能够迅速改进并更适用于实际规划者。
多域作战人工智能：多域作战的决策支持
去年，在创新连续体SHINE活动上展示的多域作战（MDO）人工智能原型，展示了先进的算法如何检索和处理条令和作战信息，以产生经过验证、可操作的答案，支持参谋人员的决策。在此基础上，重点正从单一原型转向构建更广泛的生态系统，以实现人工智能支持的决策支持的作战化和可扩展性。
实际的教训是，仅靠集成是不够的。作战参谋需要可发现、按需可访问且在临时和任务驱动的问题中可信赖的信息。这需要更强的数据质量、更好的搜索和检索能力，以及更紧密的领域专家和技术团队之间的协作，以便人工智能能够找到正确的材料，解释其使用情况，并以透明度支持人类判断。
随着这些能力的成熟，安全始终是核心。当人工智能系统复制选定数据以提高查找速度和效率时，必须将相同的访问控制和保留政策应用于这些数据所在的所有位置。这正在推动更强的数据中心安全和零信任原则，从一开始就建立，访问控制模型正向更细粒度的方法演进，以反映角色、属性、关系和主题敏感性。
今年的工作包反映了这一转变：加强使人工智能在大规模上可信赖的基础，而不仅仅是孤立的工具，而是作为北约更广泛数字化转型的集成、安全组件。
土耳其：受创新连续体启发的国家创新呼吁
创新连续体发挥作用的最明显迹象之一是，盟国不仅参与其中，还受到该模型的启发。在2025年主办了北约ACT创新连续体里程碑活动后，土耳其启动了一项国家努力，其逻辑与连续体的核心逻辑一致：以场景为导向的问题界定、行业团队合作以实现互操作性，以及在现实条件下的现场演示。
土耳其的倡议是ALFA 2026（人工智能、量子和自主系统演习），由土耳其共和国总统府国防工业秘书处（SSB）领导。SSB将2025年主办的连续体活动描述为促使创建一个国家框架的催化剂，该框架使公司能够在集成的联合体中展示能力，而不是孤立地进行。
通过土耳其的ALFA 2026，公司对信息请求做出回应，提供技术细节和性能信息，以及他们的系统如何与其他系统集成。可行的解决方案将被选择并进入演示计划。
这并不是在一个国家的孤岛中进行的。已有三个联合体申请参加北约ACT的2026年创新连续体周期，使用相同的概念，土耳其计划将其国家演示与北约的更广泛日程同步，并有意将诸如共同作战画面等输出整合到北约基础设施中。早期势头强劲：SSB报告称已有超过40家公司表达了参与的意向。
通过ALFA 2026，土耳其旨在建立一个强大的实验环境，加速新兴和颠覆性技术（EDTs）在作战战场需求中的应用。土耳其将创新连续体视为与北约盟国工业和作战资产进行互操作性测试和发展的关键机会。
—— 教授哈鲁克·戈尔古恩，土耳其国防工业秘书处（SSB）秘书长
推动创新前进
这些故事有一个共同的模式：从真实的作战需求开始，实现实时条件下的测试，并迅速推进采用。这就是创新连续体的实际价值，这也是为什么ACT使用它来帮助将实验转化为可交付的能力。
本月底，SPARK将标志着今年四个创新连续体里程碑中的第一个。在最近的周期中，包括数十项实验和演示活动以及数百名参与者的基础上，SPARK将再次将社区聚焦于对规划者和操作者至关重要的优先挑战：北极情报、监视与侦察（ISR）、人工智能在大胆训练中的应用、分层反无人机倡议、下一代目标获取、智能后勤与维持、电子战、人工智能下一代C4SR、认知战和网络韧性。这些主题将塑造场景，界定候选解决方案，并为今年晚些时候系列中的强大SHINE活动创造条件。

_source.content:
◎ 廖明輝
美國在美伊戰爭前,Anthropic因拒絕讓AI被使用於大規模國內監控與完全自主武器,遭五角大廈貼上「供應鏈風險」標籤;OpenAI卻選擇在自設紅線下,把模型部署進戰爭部的雲端機密環境。
這件事說明美國不是沒有AI軍事化,而是軍事化發生在企業、政府、法院與輿論的拉鋸之中。
表面上,
企業還能談原則、社會還能論邊界;但一旦國安需求、商業利益與地緣競爭綁在一起,紅線就可能在一次次的「例外」中被侵蝕殆盡
。美國在AI的問題不是沒有煞車,而是煞車未必能踩得住。
請繼續往下閱讀...
美國五角大廈與AI模型開發公司Anthropic,因機密軍事系統中使用AI模型的限制而僵持不下。(路透檔案照)
中國走的則是另一條路。去年八月由國務院印發《關於深入實施「人工智慧+」行動的意見》,
已清楚揭示北京的AI戰略從來不只是拚產值、衝應用,而是同步把AI嵌入公共安全預警、社會治安管理、網路空間治理,並上綱到維護與塑造國家安全能力。
換言之,北京要打造的不是單一產業政策,而是把AI結合經濟發展、社會治理、維穩控場與戰略競爭的國家能力體系。另一面,解放軍又被揭露以Meta Llama為底,開發軍用模型ChatBIT,
顯示中國正把民用模型、資料、算力與軍民融合體系快速轉換成軍事用途。換句話說,美國是在爭辯將AI軍事化,中國則是在體制內整合AI軍事化。
這正是美、中AI治理路線最根本差異。
美國仍保有企業反抗、司法審查與公共辯論空間,因此邊界雖脆弱
,至少還能被挑戰;中國則由國家先定方向,再要求產業、地方與軍方同步落地,效率更高,制衡卻更低。前者的風險是民主制度在國安壓力下節節退讓;
後者的風險則是技術、監控與軍事指管深度合流,最後形成外界難以預測、內部也難以節制的戰爭機器
。台灣現在已不能天真地只談理念,必須回到建軍現實。
國防部規劃未來八年的一.二五兆元特別預算,已把「AI輔助與C5ISR系統」列入重點,目標是打造「台灣之盾」,把感測、指管、情資分享與火力鏈結起來
。這個方向是對的,因為美軍近期對伊朗軍事行動已顯示,AI能把大量情報迅速轉成目標判識、排序與作戰節奏優勢;
若解放軍未來在台海把AI導入跨域感測、指管通聯、無人機蜂群與認知作戰,首先被壓縮的就是我方的決策時間與通訊韌性。
國防部規劃的1.25兆元特別預算,已把「AI輔助與C5ISR系統」列入重點。圖為參謀總長梅家樹日前在總統府記者會上說明該系統建構。(資料照,取自總統府官方直播)
綜上所述,因應AI軍事化趨勢,台灣該加速的,不只是買武器,而是分散式指管、抗干擾通訊、備援資料鏈路、反無人機與電子戰、關鍵基礎設施資安,以及戰時民用通訊備援。
我們要看清AI正在快速成為左右戰場節奏、國安判斷與戰略優勢的核心工具。我們更不能低估威權體制用AI重塑台海戰場規則的速度
。面對美中在這場已經開始的AI競逐,
台灣必須加速建構具韌性的指管通情體系;否則,未來我們失去的不只是戰場上的反應時間,而是決定國家安全與生存方式的主導權。
(作者為中華經濟研究院輔佐研究員)

_source.movement_abstract: 【台湾自由时报2026年6月29日报道】文章分析美国与中国在人工智能军事化路径上的根本差异。美国方面，五角大楼与Anthropic公司因AI模型在机密军事系统中的应用限制产生分歧，Anthropic拒绝将AI用于大规模国内监控与完全自主武器，被贴上供应链风险标签；而OpenAI则选择将模型部署至国防部云端机密环境。美国AI军事化过程伴随企业原则、司法审查与公共辩论，边界虽脆弱但可被挑战。中国方面，国务院印发《关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见》，将AI嵌入公共安全预警、社会治安管理、网络空间治理及国家安全能力体系。解放军被揭露以Meta Llama为底开发军用模型ChatBIT，显示中国正将民用模型、数据、算力与军民融合体系快速转换为军事用途。中国模式由国家定方向，产业、地方与军方同步落地，效率高但制衡低。文章指出，台湾国防部规划1.25兆元特别预算，将“AI辅助与C5ISR系统”列入重点，旨在打造“台湾之盾”，整合感测、指挥、控制、通信、计算机、情报、监视与侦察系统。面对解放军可能利用AI进行跨域感测、无人机蜂群与认知作战，台湾需加速构建具韧性的指挥管制通信情报体系，包括分散式指挥管制、抗干扰通讯、备援资料链路、反无人机与电子战、关键基础设施资安及战时民用通讯备援，以应对AI重塑台海战场规则的速度，确保国家安全与生存方式的主导权。
_source.title: 自由開講》美中AI軍事化分歧 台灣更不能天真
_source.trans_cont:
廖明辉
在美伊战争之前，Anthropic因拒绝让AI用于大规模国内监控和完全自主武器，被五角大楼贴上“供应链风险”标签；而OpenAI则选择在自设红线下，将模型部署到战争部的云端保密环境。
这件事说明美国并非没有AI军事化，而是军事化发生在企业、政府、法院与舆论的拉锯之中。
表面上，
企业还能谈原则、社会还能论边界；但一旦国家安全需求、商业利益与地缘竞争捆绑在一起，红线就可能在一次次的“例外”中被侵蚀殆尽
。美国在AI的问题不是没有刹车，而是刹车未必能踩得住。
请继续往下阅读...
美国五角大楼与AI模型开发公司Anthropic，因在机密军事系统中使用AI模型的限制而僵持不下。（路透档案照）
中国则走的是另一条路。去年八月由国务院印发的《关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见》，
已清楚揭示北京的AI战略从来不只是拼产值、冲应用，而是同步将AI嵌入公共安全预警、社会治安管理、网络空间治理，并上纲到维护与塑造国家安全能力。
换句话说，北京要打造的不是单一产业政策，而是将AI结合经济发展、社会治理、维稳控场与战略竞争的国家能力体系。另一方面，解放军又被揭露以Meta Llama为基础，开发军用模型ChatBIT，
显示中国正把民用模型、数据、算力与军民融合体系快速转化为军事用途。换句话说，美国是在争论将AI军事化，中国则是在体制内整合AI军事化。
这正是美、中AI治理路线最根本的差异。
美国仍保有企业反抗、司法审查与公共辩论空间，因此边界虽脆弱
，至少还能被挑战；中国则由国家先定方向，再要求产业、地方与军方同步落地，效率更高，制衡却更低。前者的风险是民主制度在国安压力下节节退让；
后者的风险则是技术、监控与军事指管深度合流，最后形成外界难以预测、内部也难以节制的战争机器
。台湾现在已不能天真地只谈理念，必须回到建军现实。
国防部规划未来八年的1.25兆元特别预算，已将「AI辅助与C5ISR系统」列入重点，目标是打造「台湾之盾」，将感知、指管、情报分享与火力链接起来
。这个方向是对的，因为美军近期对伊朗的军事行动已显示，AI能把大量情报迅速转化为目标识别、排序与作战节奏优势；
若解放军未来在台海将AI导入跨域感知、指管通联、无人机蜂群与认知作战，首先被压缩的就是我方的决策时间与通讯韧性。
国防部规划的1.25兆元特别预算，已将「AI辅助与C5ISR系统」列入重点。图为中国国民党参謀總長梅家樹日前在總統府記者會上说明该系统建构。（资料照，取自總統府官方直播）
综上所述，因应AI军事化趋势，台湾该加速的，不只是买武器，而是分散式指管、抗干扰通讯、备份数据链路、反无人机与电子战、关键基础设施资安，以及战时民用通讯备份。
我们要看清AI正在快速成为左右战场节奏、国安判断与战略优势的核心工具。我们更不能低估威权体制用AI重塑台海战场规则的速度
。面对美中在这场已经开始的AI竞逐，
台湾必须加速建构具有韧性的指管通情体系；否则，未来我们失去的不只是战场上的反应时间，而是决定国家安全与生存方式的主导权。
（作者为中华经济研究院辅佐研究员）
