_source.content:
A hacking group backed by the Iranian government dubbed “Handala” said on Friday that it has breached the personal email account of FBI director Kash Patel.
In a post on its website, Handala included several pictures of a visibly younger Patel, as well as a link to a cache of files that appear to come from Patel’s personal Gmail account.
TechCrunch confirmed that at least some of the emails leaked by Handala were from Patel’s alleged Gmail account by verifying information contained within the message headers. These message headers contain information from the sender that helps email delivery systems confirm that an email is genuine and not a spoof.
We used a tool to verify several emails in the leaked cache of files that were sent by Patel from his Gmail account. These emails contained cryptographic signatures that matched the messages, which strongly suggests that the emails we checked are authentic. In some cases, Patel appears to have sent emails from his former Justice Department email address in 2014 to his Gmail account. TechCrunch found that the emails sent from Patel’s DOJ account also appeared to be authentic.
The files in the leaked cache appear to date up to about 2019.
The FBI and Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Reuters,
which first reported
the email leaks, said a Justice Department official confirmed the breach.
TechCrunch sent messages seeking confirmation to Patel’s Gmail email address revealed by the hackers, as well as a text message to a cellphone number contained in a resume allegedly belonging to Patel. We did not immediately hear back.
Since the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran started in February, Iran-linked Handala has ramped up its hacks, most notably
claiming responsibility for a destructive attack
against medical tech giant Stryker that
wiped tens of thousands of employee devices
. The hackers have also published the personal details of several people who are allegedly part of the Israeli Defense Forces and local defense contractors.
Following the Stryker hack,
the FBI seized a handful of Handala websites
, which quickly came back online on new domains. U.S. prosecutors have
formally accused
the Iranian ministry of intelligence and security (MOIS) of operating the Handala group.
The hackers did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment sent to a chat account that the hackers publicize on their website, as well as an email address owned by the group that was published by the Justice Department.
Corrected the fourth paragraph to note that the emails were sent from Patel’s DOJ email address, and not his FBI email address.
ZW
.
_source.movement_title: 伊朗支持黑客组织入侵FBI局长邮箱并泄露邮件
_source.movement_abstract: 据路透社报道，一个由伊朗政府支持的黑客组织“Handala”于周五宣布已入侵FBI局长卡什·帕特尔的个人邮箱。该组织在其网站发布的消息中展示了帕特尔年轻时的照片，并附有疑似其个人Gmail账户的文件链接。TechCrunch通过验证邮件头信息确认部分泄露邮件的真实性，这些邮件最早可追溯至2014年帕特尔在司法部任职期间，最晚文件日期约为2019年。司法部官员已证实此次数据泄露事件。自2月美国与以色列对伊朗的军事行动开始以来，Handala黑客组织的攻击活动显著增加，曾对医疗器械巨头施乐百（Stryker）发动破坏性攻击，导致数万员工设备数据被清除。FBI此前已查封该组织多个网站，但黑客迅速改用新域名恢复运营。美国检察官已正式指控伊朗情报安全部门（MOIS）运营Handala组织。TechCrunch尝试通过公开渠道联系黑客组织和帕特尔本人均未获回应。
_source.title: Iranian hackers claim breach of FBI director Kash Patel’s personal email account
_source.trans_cont:
一个据称得到伊朗政府支持的黑客组织“Handala”于周五表示，已入侵了FBI局长卡什·帕特尔的个人电子邮件账户。
在网站上的一篇帖子中，Handala发布了几张明显比帕特尔现在年轻的照片，以及一个链接，指向似乎来自帕特尔个人Gmail账户的文件集合。
TechCrunch通过验证邮件头信息确认，至少部分被泄露的电子邮件确实来自帕特尔的Gmail账户。这些邮件头信息包含发件人信息，有助于电子邮件系统确认邮件的真实性，而非伪造邮件。
我们使用工具验证了泄露文件集合中的一些电子邮件，这些邮件是帕特尔从他的Gmail账户发出的。这些电子邮件包含与邮件内容匹配的加密签名，这强烈表明我们检查的电子邮件是真实的。在一些情况下，帕特尔似乎在2014年曾从他以前的司法部电子邮件地址向他的Gmail账户发送邮件。TechCrunch发现，从帕特尔司法部账户发出的邮件也似乎真实。
泄露文件集合中的文件似乎可追溯至大约2019年。
FBI和司法部尚未对评论请求作出回应。
首先报道电子邮件泄露的路透社称，一名司法部官员确认了此次入侵事件。
TechCrunch向黑客公布的帕特尔Gmail电子邮件地址发送了信息，同时也向一份据称属于帕特尔的简历中包含的手机号码发送了短信，但尚未收到回复。
自2月美国和以色列对伊朗开战以来，与伊朗有关的Handala组织加大了其网络攻击力度，最显著的是声称对医疗科技巨头Stryker发起的破坏性攻击负责，该攻击导致数万台员工设备被毁。黑客还发布了据称属于以色列国防军和本地国防承包商人员的个人资料。
在Stryker事件之后，FBI查封了Handala的一些网站，这些网站很快在新的域名上重新上线。美国检察官已正式指控伊朗情报与安全部（MOIS）运营了Handala组织。
黑客没有回应TechCrunch通过他们在网站上公开的聊天账户以及司法部公布的属于该组织的电子邮件地址发送的评论请求。
修正了第四段，指出电子邮件是从帕特尔的司法部电子邮件地址发送的，而不是他的FBI电子邮件地址。
_source.trans_title: 伊朗黑客声称入侵了FBI局长卡什·帕特尔的个人电子邮件账户

_source.content:
A group of Jeffrey Epstein survivors is suing the Justice Department and Google over the “wrongful disclosure and re-publication” of their personal information in files tied to the federal probe into the convicted sex offender’s crimes.
The class action lawsuit, filed Thursday in the Northern District of California on behalf of Jane Doe and other victims, alleges that the DOJ “outed approximately 100 survivors” in the documents released in late 2025 and early 2026.
“Even after the government acknowledged the disclosure violated the rights of the survivors and withdrew the information, online entities like Google continuously republish it, refusing victims’ pleas to take it down,” the complaint stated.
The Trump administration, namely Attorney General Pam Bondi, has come under intense scrutiny for its handling of the Epstein investigation since the first batch of files was released in December.
Bipartisan groups of lawmakers and Epstein’s victims have accused the federal government of failing to comply with the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which required that victims’ identities be redacted.
The complaint claims that DOJ officials engaged in a “release now, retract later” approach that resulted in “some combination” of names, phone numbers and other victim-identifying information being disclosed to the public.
“The United States, acting through the DOJ, made a deliberate policy choice to prioritize rapid, large-volume disclosure over protection of Epstein survivors’ privacy,” it stated.
Lawyers for Epstein victims filed an emergency request in the Southern District of New York in early February, seeking a court order to shut down the DOJ’s database until proper redactions were made in the 3.5 million released files.
The DOJ moved to fix the errors, blaming the blunder on “technical or human error” when it announced it had taken down the documents and images.
The latest lawsuit also criticizes Google for allegedly refusing to remove or de-index specific content from search results and caches despite having the technological capability to do so.
“Google continues even now to display Plaintiff and Class members’ PII in search results, cached pages, and archived materials, effectively republishing the unlawful disclosure and making it permanently and globally accessible,” the complaint said.
“As a result of Google’s actions, [plaintiff class] remains easily discoverable by anyone with internet access, perpetuating the privacy invasion and enabling ongoing harassment, stalking, and reputational harm,” it continued.
The Justice Department and Google did not immediately respond to The Hill’s requests for comment.
Earlier this month, Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche rebuffed accusations that the department has ignored Epstein’s victims.
“I do defend the work that this department is doing today, right now, which is going after every single perpetrator anywhere. And if there’s a narrative that exists that we’re ignoring Epstein victims, that is false,” he said during an appearance on Katie Miller’s podcast.
_source.movement_title: Epstein性侵案幸存者起诉美司法部和谷歌泄露个人信息
_source.movement_abstract: Jeffrey Epstein性侵案幸存者群体于周四在美国加州北区法院提起集体诉讼，指控美国司法部和谷歌公司非法泄露其个人信息。诉讼称司法部在2025年底和2026年初发布的案件文件中，未对约100名幸存者身份进行遮蔽处理，且在承认违规后，谷歌持续在搜索结果和缓存页面中重复发布这些信息，导致受害者遭受持续骚扰。案件引发两党议员及受害者对政府违反《Epstein文件透明法案》的批评，该法案要求遮蔽受害者身份信息。司法部虽已下架相关文件并归咎于技术或人为失误，但幸存者律师称其采用\"先公开后撤回\"策略，导致350万份文件中出现姓名、电话等敏感信息泄露。本月早些时候，司法部副部长Todd Blanche曾否认部门忽视Epstein案受害者，强调当前正在追查所有涉案人员。司法部和谷歌均未就《Hill》媒体的置评请求作出回应。
_source.title: Epstein survivors sue DOJ, Google over personal information release
_source.trans_cont:
一群杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的幸存者正在起诉美国司法部和谷歌，指控他们在与联邦调查爱泼斯坦犯罪案件相关的文件中“错误地披露并重新发布”了他们的个人信息。这起集体诉讼于周四在加州北部地区法院提起，代表Jane Doe和其他受害者，指控司法部“在2025年底和2026年初发布的文件中泄露了大约100名幸存者的信息”。  
投诉中指出：“即使政府承认披露行为侵犯了幸存者的权利并撤回了信息，像谷歌这样的在线实体仍持续重新发布这些信息，拒绝受害者要求将其删除的请求。”  
特朗普政府，特别是司法部长帕姆·邦迪，自12月首批文件发布以来，一直受到对爱泼斯坦调查处理方式的强烈质疑。两党立法者团体和爱泼斯坦的受害者指责联邦政府未能遵守《爱泼斯坦文件透明法案》，该法案要求对受害者的身份进行遮蔽。  
投诉称，司法部官员采取了“先发布、后撤回”的做法，导致一些姓名、电话号码和其他可识别受害者身份的信息被公开。  
“美国通过司法部做出了一项有意识的政策选择，优先考虑快速大量披露，而非保护爱泼斯坦幸存者的隐私。”  
爱泼斯坦受害者的律师于2月初在纽约南区法院提交了紧急请求，要求法院下令关闭司法部的数据库，直到对已发布的350万份文件进行适当遮蔽。  
司法部表示已采取措施纠正错误，将失误归因于“技术或人为错误”，并宣布已下架相关文件和图片。  
最新诉讼还批评谷歌，指控其在有能力的情况下拒绝从搜索结果和缓存中删除或去索引特定内容。  
“谷歌至今仍在搜索结果、缓存页面和存档材料中显示原告和类成员的个人身份信息（PII），实际上重新发布非法披露的信息，并使其永久且全球可访问。”投诉中写道。  
“由于谷歌的行为，[原告类成员]仍可被任何拥有互联网接入的人轻易发现，持续侵犯隐私并助长持续的骚扰、跟踪和名誉损害。”  
司法部和谷歌尚未对《山岳报》的评论请求作出回应。  
本月早些时候，副司法部长托德·布兰奇驳斥了部门忽视爱泼斯坦受害者指控的说法。  
“我捍卫司法部目前正在进行的工作，即追查每一个犯罪者。如果存在一种说法认为我们忽视了爱泼斯坦受害者，那是错误的。”他在凯蒂·米勒的播客上表示。
_source.trans_title: 埃普斯坦幸存者起诉美国司法部和谷歌，要求披露个人信息

_source.content:
Flick through pro-government Hungarian accounts on TikTok, and you might see an AI-generated version of Volodymyr Zelensky, the president of Ukraine, sitting on a golden toilet, counting his money, snorting cocaine, and barking orders at a Hungarian soldier. You might also find an AI-generated Péter Magyar, the leader of the Hungarian opposition, appearing to say he’s fine with handing Hungarian factories over to foreigners, as long as he’s the one in charge of the country. Keep going, and you will find images of war, violence, and a SpongeBob look-alike declaring that Magyar “wipes up cocaine with me after he accidentally sneezed and it all fell to the floor.”
You won’t find much about Hungary itself, which is not an accident. In recent years political parties around the world have produced surrealist campaigns, comic campaigns, conspiratorial campaigns, even beer-drinking campaigns. But on any list of strange elections, the 2026 parliamentary election in Hungary will stand out—this may be the world’s first post-reality campaign.
In actual reality, the news for Viktor Orbán, the Hungarian prime minister, is not good. After 16 years in office, plus an earlier three-year term, Orbán has made his country the
most
corrupt
in the European Union, one of the
poorest
, and certainly the
least free
. His political party, Fidesz, now controls most universities, the civil service, the high courts, and, through a network of oligarchs, almost all newspapers and broadcasters, as well as about a
fifth of the econom
y
, according to independent economists. General paranoia about Fidesz spies means that Budapest, once again, has become a city where people lower their voices when talking about politics in public.
With that kind of influence, Fidesz, which is well behind in most polls, cannot evade responsibility for Hungarian stagnation, and so neither the party nor its leader are talking much about Hungary, its
falling industrial production
, or its
shrinking population
. Instead—backed by Russian propagandists, the European far right, and now the Trump administration (about which more in a minute)—the party is directing a small fortune’s worth of posters and social-media videos toward a different goal: convincing Hungarians to fear sabotage, thievery, or even a military attack from ... Ukraine.
This is an entirely false, even ludicrous threat. The Ukrainians have enough to do without starting a second war in Hungary. But Orbán, his government, his party, and many outsiders are now focused on making this threat
seem
true. Pay attention, because this may be the future of electoral politics: Multiple politicians from several countries are shoveling propaganda at an electorate in order to build terror of an enemy
that doesn’t exist at all
.
The campaign is not subtle. In Budapest last week, Orbán’s face was almost nowhere to be seen. But posters featuring Zelensky were ubiquitous. Sometimes the Ukrainian president is seen glowering alongside the slogan “Don’t let Zelensky have the last laugh.” Sometimes Zelensky appears with Magyar and Ursula von der Leyen, the president of the European commission, along with the slogan “They are the risk. Fidesz is the safe choice.” Peter Kreko, who runs a Budapest think tank, told me that this is unprecedented. In 2022, Orbán campaigned on keeping Hungary out of the war. Now he’s telling Hungarians that, as Kreko put it, “we are under imminent threat of attack.”
The same threats reach Hungarians on their phones. On TikTok, where new pro-Fidesz accounts appear every day, AI-created videos of Magyar seem to show him slandering his country—“I stay silent because my masters in Brussels have forbidden me from defending the homeland”—or else singing the Ukrainian national anthem. Another
genre of video
shows war violence: a Hungarian girl crying as her blindfolded father, wearing a Hungarian uniform, is executed, apparently in Ukraine. Multiple videos also smear Magyar, making personal, sexual, and financial allegations against him, but the fear-Ukrainian-invasion narrative dominates. During a Fidesz march on March 15, a group in the front of the crowd carried a
banner
declaring
We won’t be a Ukrainian colony!
This language and these images have been backed up by the actions of the Hungarian state, each one designed to reinforce Fidesz propaganda. In February, Orbán sent Hungarian soldiers to guard the country’s oil and gas infrastructure, allegedly to prevent a Ukrainian attack, for which there was no evidence. In March, Hungarian counterterrorism authorities
seized
two trucks, owned by a Ukrainian bank, that were passing through the country on a routine cash-transport run from Vienna. They arrested seven bank employees, one of whom lost consciousness after they injected him with what may have been truth serum. Later they were all released because, again, there was no evidence against them.
András Pethő: Trump’s attempts to muzzle the press look familiar
The Hungarian government nevertheless confiscated $82 million in gold and cash, which it has not returned. The online publication
Direkt36
, one of a tiny number of outlets still doing investigative reporting in Hungary, wrote that Fidesz reckons this ham-handed operation a success: It provoked Zelensky to
half-jokingly threaten Orbán
, which gave the Hungarian leader another few days’ worth of material.
Hungarian state institutions are not the only government bodies seeking to shape Hungarian perceptions of reality. Although Orbán likes to use the word
sovereignty
, he now functions, in practice, as the most important Russian puppet in Europe. According to a
Washington Post
investigation
published last week, Orbán’s foreign minister, Péter Szijjártó, regularly calls his Russian counterpart, Sergei Lavrov, to keep the Russians informed following European Union meetings, and sometimes to ask for favors. During a 2020 call between the two men, according to a transcript
published
by a Hungarian journalist, Szijjártó asked Lavrov to arrange a meeting in Moscow for a pro-Russian Slovak politician, to help him win an election. The meeting did later take place. Other European leaders long ago stopped discussing any security issues in the presence of Orbán himself, who has repeatedly used his veto to block European sanctions on Russia and European aid for Ukraine.
Concerned that a key asset might lose power, the Russians have sent a team of propagandists to Budapest to ensure that Orbán wins. The
Financial Times
has
identified
the influence group as the Social Design Agency, a Kremlin-backed IT company whose activities are well known. In 2023, back when the American government was still interested in unmasking Russian propaganda, the State Department’s now-dismantled Global Engagement Center
exposed
the agency’s role in creating a series of seemingly native pro-Russian websites in Latin America. In Budapest, they were tasked with creating AI videos and using their existing network of trolls and bots to pass them on. One Russian network has circulated doctored screenshots of the English-language website Euronews, with fake quotes attributed to Magyar. The
Washington Post
investigation revealed that the Russians even proposed to stage a fake assassination of Orbán, in order to build more sympathy for him. They called this strategy “Gamechanger.”
Anne Applebaum: The longest suicide note in American history
Tisza, Magyar’s opposition party, is expecting more. Several people close to Tisza told me that they feared a false-flag operation, perhaps an explosion at a Hungarian pipeline or another energy site. I was also told that Tisza has been preparing for a major hack of their internal communications infrastructure, and has built an analog backup system, just in case. Last week, that seemed prudent, since the party’s membership database had already been hacked, with names and private information of members dumped online. Now it seems prescient: This week,
Direkt36
published an
article
, based partly on material from a whistleblower, claiming that this was indeed the Hungarian government’s plan. In response, the Hungarian government said some of the individuals involved were linked to Ukrainian intelligence, and separately
accused
a
Direkt36
journalist of espionage. The
story
continues to twist and turn.
Not long ago, the U.S. government would have vocally defended the democratic process in Hungary, and might have sought to downplay wild claims about fictional Ukrainian invasions. Instead, the Trump administration is doing its best to amplify them. Strange though it sounds, Hungary, although a tiny country in Central Europe, plays an outsize role in the imagination of the American and European far-right: MAGA and its international wing understand that the Hungarian election, the most important in Europe this year, could mark a turning point in the war of ideas that has convulsed the democratic world for the past decade.
Orbán has been actively engaged in this battle, fighting against liberal democracy and the rule of law, advocating for authoritarian populism and one-party rule. He became a beacon for other leaders who seek to alter their own democratic political systems, who also want to twist the rules in order to ensure that they never lose. Kevin Roberts, the head of the Heritage Foundation, once said Orbán’s Hungary was not just “a model for modern statecraft, but
the
model.” Orbán pioneered a form of campaigning too, spending years convincing Hungarians that existential threats—from migrants, from so-called decadence, from the European Union—required the radical institutional changes that have kept his party in power. Americans will be familiar with these tactics, which have been adopted, and adapted, by Trump and Vance.
Now the political leaders who have long admired Orbán’s methods are gathering to help him. Secretary of State Marco Rubio traveled to Budapest in February to
endorse
Orbán, even seeming to
offer
financial support “if you face things that threaten the stability of your country.” Vice President J. D. Vance is set to visit Budapest, probably after Easter. President Trump himself appeared on video at the Budapest meeting last Saturday of CPAC, the formerly mainstream-conservative organization that now organizes pop-up rallies on behalf of the international radical right. In his message, Trump offered his “complete and total endorsement” for Orbán, Russia’s closest European ally.
Other members of the European far right showed up in person. Alice Weidel, head of the far-right Alternative for Germany, made a speech attacking the European Union for allegedly sending billions of euros to Ukraine, “the most corrupt regime on Earth,” as if she were not speaking on a podium inside the most corrupt state in the EU, and were not echoing the rhetoric of Russia, which might authentically be the most corrupt regime on Earth. She was followed by Santiago Abascal, the leader of the Spanish far right, who said that Orbán’s Hungary—repressed and impoverished after years of ersatz populism—is a “shining beam of light in the darkness.” Marine Le Pen of France, Karol Nawrocki of Poland, and Geert Wilders of the Netherlands have also made appearances. Benjamin Netanyahu endorsed Orbán by video. Even the libertarian president of Argentina, Javier Milei, came all the way from South America to laud Orbán, a man who has built one of Europe’s most centralized and repressive societies.
All of them have their own motives. Maybe Weidel is trying to help out the Russians, who
fund
some of her party members and amplify her own online campaigns. Milei may reckon it prudent to back an ally of Trump, who gave him $20 billion to shore up his country’s currency just before his own recent election. Perhaps Abascal or LePen hope for a boost in their campaigns too. But mostly they were there because the return of a different government in Hungary would invalidate the claim that the far-right represents Europe’s future.
Read: Is the end of NATO near?
In Budapest, Orban’s language and tactics already feel like they belong to the past. His old threats aren’t working anymore, perhaps because reality is reasserting itself. There is, in fact, no wave of migration challenging the survival of the Hungarian nation. Brussels doesn’t pose an actual threat to Hungarian health and happiness, but the poor state of the nation’s hospitals very well might. And, of course, Ukraine is not going to invade, but Russia might. Hungary was actually invaded, after all, in living memory—by tanks sent in by Moscow, not Kyiv: In 1956, the Soviet army came to Budapest to crush the anti-Communist Hungarian revolution.
To counter Orbán’s post-reality campaign, Tisza has focused on building a grassroots campaign that reaches actual people in the three-dimensional world. Magyar gives no interviews but instead makes campaign speeches in several different towns and villages every day, mostly on topics people understand: the economy, health, corruption. Usually he stays away from the geopolitical themes Orbán much prefers. But at a large rally in Budapest earlier this month, Magyar did start chanting “Russians go home.”
That chant, and the historical memory behind it, also helps explain why Budapest feels so feverish, and why Orbán’s post-reality campaign is so fraught. To win, Orbán has to corrupt that searing national memory, and to substitute fear of Ukraine. That means waging cognitive warfare on a scale no one else has tried before. Emotions are high because the stakes are high. If he succeeds, he will once again blaze a path that others will follow. And if he loses, an era comes to an end.
_source.movement_title: 匈牙利执政党联合俄美势力发动反乌认知战以应对2026年议会选举
_source.movement_abstract: 【美国华盛顿邮报2026年6月报道】2026年6月，匈牙利执政党青年民主主义者联盟（Fidesz）为应对议会选举，联合俄罗斯宣传机构及美国特朗普政府，发起大规模反乌认知战。该党利用人工智能生成虚假视频，描绘乌克兰总统泽连斯基吸毒、腐败及匈牙利反对派领袖马加日叛国等场景，并在社交媒体广泛传播。政府以防范乌克兰入侵为由，调动军队守卫能源设施，并逮捕乌克兰银行职员、没收8200万美元资产，但缺乏证据。美国特朗普政府高层包括国务卿鲁比奥、副总统万斯及总统特朗普本人公开支持奥班，提供政治背书及潜在资金支持。俄罗斯通过社会设计机构等组织协助制造虚假新闻及深度伪造内容。反对派蒂萨党则揭露政府计划，并加强内部通信备份。此次选举被视为欧洲极右翼势力与民主制度博弈的关键节点，奥班试图通过制造虚假威胁巩固权力，其策略可能影响全球民主政治走向。
_source.title: The First Post-Reality Political Campaign
_source.trans_cont:
翻阅匈牙利亲政府的TikTok账号，你可能会看到由人工智能生成的乌克兰总统泽连斯基坐在金马桶上数钱、吸可卡因，并对匈牙利士兵发号施令。你还会发现人工智能生成的匈牙利反对派领袖彼得·马加尔，似乎在说他愿意将匈牙利工厂交给外国人，只要他能掌控国家。继续浏览，你还会看到战争、暴力的画面，以及一个海绵宝宝的仿制品宣称马加尔“在马加尔不小心打喷嚏后，可卡因洒了一地，他和我一起打扫干净”。

你不会看到太多关于匈牙利本身的内容，这并非偶然。近年来，全球各政党纷纷推出超现实主义、漫画风格、阴谋论或甚至啤酒饮用主题的竞选活动。但在奇怪的选举名单中，2026年匈牙利议会选举将格外突出——这可能是世界上首个脱离现实的竞选活动。

实际上，匈牙利总理欧尔班的处境并不乐观。执政16年加上此前的3年任期，欧尔班使匈牙利成为欧盟最腐败的国家之一，也是最贫穷的国家之一，无疑是最缺乏自由的国家之一。他的政党青民盟（Fidesz）现在控制着大部分大学、文职机构、最高法院，通过一个寡头网络几乎掌控所有报纸和广播媒体，以及约五分之一的经济，根据独立经济学家的说法。对青民盟间谍的普遍猜疑意味着布达佩斯再次成为人们在公开场合谈论政治时压低声音的城市。

凭借这种影响力，尽管在大多数民调中处于落后地位，青民盟无法逃避匈牙利停滞的责任，因此该党及其领导人很少谈论匈牙利、其工业生产的下降或人口的减少。相反，该党在俄罗斯宣传者、欧洲极右翼和现在特朗普政府（稍后将详细说明）的支持下，将大量海报和社交媒体视频用于不同的目标：说服匈牙利人害怕来自……乌克兰的破坏、盗窃，甚至军事攻击。

这是一个完全虚假、甚至荒谬的威胁。乌克兰人没有精力再在匈牙利发动第二次战争。但欧尔班、他的政府、他的政党以及许多外部人士现在正专注于让这一威胁看起来真实。请注意，因为这可能是选举政治的未来：多个国家的多名政客向选民灌输对一个根本不存在的敌人的恐惧。

这场竞选并不隐晦。上周在布达佩斯，欧尔班的面孔几乎无处不在。但印有泽连斯基的海报却随处可见。有时乌克兰总统被描绘成怒视着“别让泽连斯基最后得逞”的标语。有时泽连斯基与马加尔和欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯·德莱恩一起出现，标语写着“他们是风险，青民盟是安全之选”。布达佩斯智库负责人彼得·克雷科告诉我，这在2022年是前所未有的。当时欧尔班竞选时承诺让匈牙利远离战争。现在他却告诉匈牙利人，“我们正面临即将发生的攻击威胁”。

同样的威胁也通过手机传递给匈牙利人。在TikTok上，每天都有新的亲青民盟账号出现，人工智能生成的马加尔视频似乎显示他在诽谤自己的国家——“我保持沉默是因为布鲁塞尔的主子禁止我捍卫祖国”——或者唱乌克兰国歌。另一类视频展示战争暴力：一位匈牙利女孩哭泣，她的盲folded父亲穿着匈牙利军装被处决，似乎是在乌克兰。多段视频还抹黑马加尔，对他进行个人、性及财务指控，但对乌克兰入侵的恐惧叙事占据主导地位。3月15日，青民盟游行时，人群前的团体举着标语“我们不会成为乌克兰的殖民地”。

这些语言和图像得到了匈牙利国家机构的行动支持，每项行动都旨在强化青民盟的宣传。2月，欧尔班派匈牙利士兵守卫国家的石油和天然气基础设施，声称是为了防止乌克兰攻击，尽管没有证据。3月，匈牙利反恐机构扣押了两辆属于乌克兰银行的卡车，这些卡车正在从维也纳进行例行现金运输。他们逮捕了七名银行员工，其中一人在注射可能为真言药剂后失去意识。后来他们都被释放，因为同样没有证据指控他们。

安德拉斯·佩托：特朗普试图压制媒体的尝试看起来很熟悉

匈牙利政府却没收了8200万美元的黄金和现金，至今未归还。匈牙利少数仍在进行调查性报道的媒体之一《Direkt36》称，青民盟认为这次笨拙的操作是成功的：它激怒了泽连斯基，使欧尔班获得了一点额外的宣传材料。

匈牙利国家机构并不是唯一试图塑造匈牙利人对现实认知的政府机构。尽管欧尔班喜欢使用“主权”这个词，但实际上他已成为欧洲最重要的俄罗斯傀儡。据《华盛顿邮报》上周发表的一项调查，欧尔班的外交部长彼得·西吉亚尔托经常致电他的俄罗斯同行谢尔盖·拉夫罗夫，以在欧盟会议后向俄罗斯通报情况，有时还请求帮助。根据一位匈牙利记者发表的一份通话记录，2020年两人通话时，西吉亚尔托请求拉夫罗夫安排一次在莫斯科的会面，帮助一位亲俄的斯洛伐克政客赢得选举。这次会面后来确实发生了。其他欧洲领导人早已不再在欧尔班本人面前讨论任何安全问题，因为他多次动用否决权阻止欧盟对俄罗斯实施制裁和对乌克兰提供援助。

担心关键资产可能失去权力，俄罗斯派了一支宣传团队前往布达佩斯，确保欧尔班获胜。《金融时报》已确认该影响集团是克里姆林宫支持的IT公司“社会设计公司”，其活动众所周知。2023年，当美国政府仍致力于揭露俄罗斯宣传时，国务院已解散的全球参与中心曾揭露该机构在拉丁美洲创建了一系列看似本土的亲俄网站。在布达佩斯，他们被指派制作人工智能视频，并利用其现有的网络水军和机器人传播。一个俄罗斯网络传播了对英文新闻网站Euronews的伪造截图，附有虚假的马加尔引语。《华盛顿邮报》的调查还揭示，俄罗斯甚至提议策划一场假扮的欧尔班遇刺事件，以增加对他的同情。他们称这一策略为“变革者”。

安妮·阿普尔鲍姆：美国历史上最长的自杀信

马加尔的反对党蒂萨预计会看到更多。几位接近蒂萨的人告诉我，他们担心虚假旗手行动，比如匈牙利输油管道或另一处能源设施的爆炸。我也被告知蒂萨已为重大黑客攻击其内部通信基础设施做好准备，并建立了模拟备份系统以防万一。上周，这似乎是有远见的，因为该党的会员数据库已被黑客入侵，成员姓名和私人信息被泄露到网上。现在看来，这预示着未来：本周，《Direkt36》发表了一篇文章，部分内容来自举报人，声称这确实是匈牙利政府的计划。作为回应，匈牙利政府称部分涉案人员与乌克兰情报有关，并单独指责《Direkt36》记者从事间谍活动。这个故事仍在不断变化。

不久之前，美国政府会公开捍卫匈牙利的民主进程，并可能淡化关于虚构乌克兰入侵的夸张说法。相反，特朗普政府正尽其所能放大这些说法。尽管听起来奇怪，匈牙利虽是中欧一个小小的国家，却在美欧极右翼的想象中扮演着不成比例的角色：MAGA及其国际分支理解，今年欧洲最重要的选举——匈牙利选举，可能标志着过去十年席卷民主世界的意识形态战争的一个转折点。

欧尔班积极投身于这场斗争，对抗自由民主和法治，倡导威权民粹主义和一党制。他成为其他希望改变自己民主政治体制的领导人的灯塔，他们也希望扭曲规则以确保自己永远不会失败。赫尔曼基金会的负责人凯文·罗伯茨曾说，欧尔班的匈牙利不仅是“现代国家治理的典范”，更是“典范”。欧尔班还开创了一种竞选方式，花费多年说服匈牙利人，来自移民、所谓的堕落和欧盟的生存威胁需要进行激进的制度变革，以维持其政党的执政地位。美国人会熟悉这些策略，这些策略已被特朗普和范斯所采用。

现在，长期钦佩欧尔班方法的政治领袖们正聚集起来帮助他。国务卿马尔科·鲁比奥2月前往布达佩斯支持欧尔班，甚至似乎提供“如果面临威胁你国家稳定的事物，可以提供财政支持”。副总统J·D·范斯计划在复活节后访问布达佩斯。总统特朗普本人上周六在CPAC会议（一个曾为主流保守派组织，现在为国际极右翼组织举办临时集会）的视频上公开支持欧尔班，称其为俄罗斯最亲密的欧洲盟友。

其他欧洲极右翼成员也亲自到场。德国极右翼“另类选择党”领导人艾丽丝·魏德尔发表演讲，攻击欧盟“据说向乌克兰发送数十亿欧元”，称其为“地球上最腐败的政权”，仿佛她不是在欧盟最腐败的国家的讲台上发言，也不是在重复俄罗斯的言论，而俄罗斯可能确实是地球上最腐败的政权。她之后是西班牙极右翼领导人桑托斯·阿巴卡尔，他说欧尔班的匈牙利——在多年虚假民粹主义之后被压制和贫困化——是“黑暗中的光辉”。法国的玛丽娜·勒庞、波兰的卡罗尔·纳沃克和荷兰的基尔特·威尔德斯也出席了活动。本杰明·内塔尼亚胡通过视频支持欧尔班。甚至阿根廷自由派总统胡里奥·马里亚·米莱也从南美洲远道而来赞扬欧尔班，这位建立了欧洲最集中和压制性社会的领导人。

他们都各有动机。也许魏德尔试图帮助俄罗斯，俄罗斯资助她党内的部分成员并放大她的在线竞选。米莱可能认为支持特朗普的盟友是明智的，因为特朗普在他最近的选举前向他提供了200亿美元以稳定其国家货币。也许阿巴卡尔或勒庞也希望自己的竞选获得提升。但主要原因是，如果匈牙利出现不同的政府，将否定极右翼代表欧洲未来的说法。

阅读：北约的终结是否临近？

在布达佩斯，欧尔班的语言和策略已经显得像是过去的事情。他旧有的威胁不再奏效，也许因为现实正在重新确立。事实上，没有大规模移民挑战匈牙利民族的生存。布鲁塞尔并不真正威胁匈牙利人的健康和幸福，但该国医院的糟糕状况却可能如此。当然，乌克兰不会入侵，但俄罗斯可能会。匈牙利实际上在记忆中曾被入侵——由莫斯科派来的坦克，而不是基辅：1956年，苏联军队来到布达佩斯镇压匈牙利反共革命。

为了对抗欧尔班的后现实运动，蒂萨专注于建立一个基层运动，触及现实世界中的人们。马加尔不接受采访，而是每天在多个城镇和村庄发表竞选演讲，主要谈论人们能理解的话题：经济、健康、腐败。通常他避免涉及欧尔班偏好的地缘政治主题。但在本月早些时候布达佩斯的一次大型集会上，马加尔开始喊道“俄罗斯人回家去”。

这一口号以及其背后的历史记忆也解释了为什么布达佩斯感觉如此紧张，为什么欧尔班的后现实运动如此充满挑战。为了获胜，欧尔班必须腐蚀这种尖锐的民族记忆，并用对乌克兰的恐惧取代它。这意味着在规模上进行前所未有的认知战争。情绪高涨是因为赌注很高。如果他成功，他将再次开辟一条他人将追随的道路。如果他失败，一个时代将结束。
_source.trans_title: 后现实时代的首次政治竞选
_source.evidence: 文章详细描述了匈牙利政府（Orbán/Fidesz）在2026年议会选举期间，利用AI生成虚假视频（如泽连斯基吸毒、乌克兰入侵威胁等）进行大规模认知域攻击和舆论操纵的具体行动。文中提到了具体的对抗手段（AI视频、虚假叙事）、具体的行动目标（恐吓选民、转移国内矛盾）以及外部势力（俄罗斯、美国部分政客）的介入。虽然涉及AI技术（技术武器），但文章的核心在于描述这些技术被用于具体的政治对抗和舆论攻击行动（即‘行动’本身），而非单纯的技术研发。同时，虽然涉及中国立场的专家视角，但事件主体是匈牙利，并非直接针对中国大陆的敌情事件（涉我事件），而是作为认知域对抗的典型案例。根据定义，这属于‘相关领域的具体作战、对抗等行动及其动向（如具体的舆论攻击行动）’，因此归类为[行动动向]。

Elbit Systems’ German subsidiary has signed an agreement with startup Cucuyo GmbH to obtain exclusive rights to adapt the company’s laser-based communication technology for military applications.
Under the deal, Elbit can use and further develop Cucuyo’s technology specifically for defense purposes, while jointly developing new systems with intellectual property assigned to Elbit.
Focus on Drones, Secure Data Links
As part of the agreement, Elbit’s German unit is establishing a dedicated research and development structure to advance laser communication systems for military platforms.
Initial efforts will focus on integration with drones and ground-based systems.
Laser communications transmit data via light rather than traditional radio frequency (RF) signals, offering advantages such as higher throughput, resistance to electronic interference, and reduced susceptibility to interception.
Expanding European Defense Capabilities
The agreement supports Elbit’s broader strategy to expand its technological footprint in Europe.
The company has been increasing its presence in Germany in recent years, including investments in local production and development capabilities.
For Cucuyo, the partnership provides access to Elbit’s expertise in electro-optical systems, communications, and platform integration.
Financial details were not disclosed, but the companies indicated that initial products based on the licensed technology could enter service quickly.
Tags
Germany
_source.movement_title: 埃尔比特子公司与Cucuyo合作开发军用激光通信技术
_source.movement_abstract: 埃尔比特系统公司德国子公司与初创企业Cucuyo GmbH签署协议，获得其激光通信技术在军事领域的独家使用权。双方将共同开发新系统，知识产权归埃尔比特所有。该合作聚焦无人机和地面系统的激光通信整合，利用激光替代传统无线电频率信号传输数据，具备高吞吐量、抗电子干扰和低截获风险等优势。此次协议支持埃尔比特在欧洲的技术扩展战略，其近年来持续加强在德国的本地生产与研发能力。Cucuyo则借助埃尔比特在光电系统、通信和平台整合方面的专业经验推动技术应用。双方未披露财务细节，但表示基于该技术的首批产品可能较快投入使用。
_source.title: Elbit Secures Rights to German Laser Comms Tech for Defense Use
_source.trans_cont:
Elbit Systems的德国子公司已与初创企业Cucuyo GmbH签订协议，获得独家权利将该公司基于激光的通信技术用于军事应用。
根据协议，Elbit可以专门用于国防目的使用和进一步开发Cucuyo的技术，同时与Elbit共同开发新系统，相关知识产权归Elbit所有。
聚焦无人机与安全数据链
根据协议，Elbit的德国分公司将建立专门的研究开发结构，推进军用平台的激光通信系统发展。
初期工作将重点放在与无人机和地面系统的集成上。
激光通信通过光传输数据，而非传统无线电频率（RF）信号，具有更高的数据传输速率、抗电子干扰能力和更难被截获等优势。
拓展欧洲防务能力
该协议支持Elbit扩大其在欧洲技术影响力的更广泛战略。
近年来，该公司在德国的业务不断扩大，包括对本地生产和研发能力的投资。
对Cucuyo而言，此次合作使其能够获得Elbit在光电系统、通信和平台集成方面的专业知识。
财务细节未披露，但两家公司表示基于授权技术的首批产品可能很快投入使用。
标签
德国
_source.trans_title: 埃尔比特获得德国激光通信技术在国防领域的使用权

Shield AI has announced its plan to acquire California-based Aechelon Technology as it expands its autonomous systems portfolio.
Aechelon develops high-fidelity simulation and synthetic environments used by the US military and allied forces to prepare crews and evaluate advanced airborne systems, including within the Pentagon’s Joint Simulation Environment.
According to Shield AI, the acquisition will enhance its flagship Hivemind AI autonomy software by accelerating development through simulation.
Hivemind has already piloted more than 20 platforms since its inception, including F-16 jets, unmanned aerial systems, and robotic ground vehicles.
It has also been selected by the US Air Force as a mission autonomy provider for the Collaborative Combat Aircraft manned-unmanned airborne teaming program and is now undergoing flight testing.
Shield AI said that Aechelon will operate independently within Shield AI following the deal, with CEO Ignacio Sanz-Pastor continuing to lead the business and reporting directly to Steele.
“The acquisition of Aechelon will accelerate the work we are doing with Hivemind,” Shield AI CEO Gary Steele said.
“It’s an incredible company with a fantastic team and a leading technology that plays a role in how we think about the AI pilot development lifecycle.”
$1.5B in New Capital
Alongside the acquisition, Shield AI raised $1.5 billion at a $12.7 billion valuation, including a $1.5-billion round led by Advent International and co-led by JPMorganChase’s Security and Resiliency Initiative, alongside $500 million in preferred equity from Blackstone.
Blackstone also committed an additional $250-million delayed draw facility to “support future growth.”
Shield AI noted that part of the proceeds will back the upcoming Aechelon buyout, continued maturation of the Hivemind software, and developments for its X-BAT vertical takeoff and landing combat drone.
Tags
autonomous systems drones Hivemind mergers and acquisitions military training Shield AI training simulator
_source.movement_title: Shield AI收购Aechelon并融资15亿美元扩展自主系统业务
_source.movement_abstract: Shield AI宣布计划收购位于加州的Aechelon Technology，以扩展其自主系统产品组合。Aechelon专注于为美军及盟军开发高保真模拟和合成环境技术，用于飞行员培训和先进空中系统的评估，其技术已应用于五角大楼的联合模拟环境中。此次收购将加速Shield AI核心产品Hivemind AI自主软件的开发，该软件自推出以来已成功应用于超过20个平台，包括F-16战斗机、无人机及地面机器人。Hivemind已被美国空军选为联合战斗飞机项目的人机协同任务自主供应商，并正在开展飞行测试。同时，Shield AI完成15亿美元融资，公司估值达127亿美元，资金将用于Aechelon的收购、Hivemind软件优化及X-BAT垂直起降战斗无人机研发。Aechelon将保持独立运营，现任CEO Ignacio Sanz-Pastor将继续领导团队并直接向Shield AI CEO Gary Steele汇报。
_source.title: Shield AI Grows Simulation Capabilities With Aechelon Technology Buyout
_source.trans_cont:
Shield AI宣布计划收购位于加州的Aechelon Technology，以扩展其自主系统产品组合。Aechelon为美军及盟军开发高保真模拟和合成环境，用于训练机组人员并评估先进空中系统，包括五角大楼的联合模拟环境。据Shield AI称，此次收购将通过模拟加速其旗舰产品Hivemind自主软件的开发。自推出以来，Hivemind已成功在超过20种平台上进行试点，包括F-16战斗机、无人机系统和机器人地面车辆。它还被美国空军选为协作战斗飞机有人-无人空中编队计划的使命自主性提供商，目前正在进行飞行测试。Shield AI表示，收购后Aechelon将继续在Shield AI内部独立运营，由首席执行官Ignacio Sanz-Pastor继续领导业务，并直接向首席执行官Gary Steele汇报。“收购Aechelon将加快我们与Hivemind的合作工作，”Shield AI首席执行官Gary Steele表示。“这是一家令人惊叹的公司，拥有出色的团队和领先的科技，对我们的AI飞行员开发生命周期思考具有重要意义。”
15亿美元新资金
同时，Shield AI以127亿美元估值筹集了15亿美元资金，其中包括由Advent International牵头的15亿美元一轮融资，以及由摩根大通公司安全与韧性倡议联合牵头的融资，同时还获得了Blackstone提供的5亿美元优先股。Blackstone还承诺额外提供2.5亿美元的延期贷款，以“支持未来增长”。Shield AI指出，部分资金将用于即将进行的Aechelon收购、Hivemind软件的持续成熟以及其X-BAT垂直起降战斗无人机的发展。
标签

Regime change? Offramp? Disagreements with Israel? Jack Keane has the scoop.
Normally, I try to share my analysis as an introduction to our podcasts. In this case, the details are worth a deep dive. There are a number of reasons for I hope you will take the time: There is a lot — A LOT — of disinformation out there. And it’s not the garden variety Russian/Chinese fanning the flames; there are active efforts to sow seeds of doubt about the success of Epic Fury, the relationship with Israel, the President’s resolve, the reality on the ground, and much more. Part of the problem is journalists looking to confirm stories they’ve already written; another part is aggressive leaking from inside the Trump administration in an effort to undermine public confidence, sow seeds of doubt in the President’s mind, and foment economic fears; and of course, there is the partisan divide that cannot assess anything done by the Trump administration because of antipathy towards the President.
Like many of our readers, I have lots of questions about the ongoing war. Is the President all in? Is he looking for an offramp? What are the supposed “talks” with Iran? Are we really winning? Do Israel and the United States share the same definition of victory? What about regime change? And can there be victory without regime change? What about the nukes? What about Hormuz? What about the Arabs? NATO? And so much more.
Marc and I hit our great friend General Jack Keane with every one of those questions, and more. Sometimes more than once. Jack remains very close to decision makers in Washington and Jerusalem, and I can’t fault his frankness. One of my dear friends told me that he learned more from this pod than he has from reading the paper every day. I have to agree. Thank goodness for people like Jack. And early next week we’ll post our wide-ranging interview with Israeli ambassador to the United States Yechiel Leiter.
Read more in the WTH Substack here.
_source.movement_title: 中东战争深度解析：政权更迭、脱身策略与以色列分歧探讨
_source.movement_abstract: 作者在文章中强调当前中东战争报道中存在大量虚假信息和内部泄密问题，并邀请听众关注其与前美军参谋长联席会议副主席杰克·凯恩的深度访谈。访谈围绕多个关键议题展开：1. 特朗普政府是否已全面投入战争；2. 是否存在寻求脱身之路的可能；3. 美伊\"秘密会谈\"的真实情况；4. 以色列与美国对\"胜利\"定义的差异；5. 政权更迭是否为胜利必要条件；6. 伊朗核问题及霍尔木兹海峡局势；7. 阿拉伯国家及北约的立场。凯恩作为华盛顿和耶路撒冷高层密切联系者，提供了坦率见解。作者指出，部分记者为验证既有报道而传播不实信息，特朗普政府内部泄密者则试图动摇公众信心和总统决心，党派分歧也导致无法客观评估相关政策。文章强调通过专家访谈获取可靠情报的重要性，并预告将发布以色列驻美大使的专访。

政权更迭？撤军？与以色列的分歧？杰克·基恩有独家报道。
通常，我会在播客开始前分享我的分析。但这次，细节值得深入探讨。我之所以希望你花时间阅读，是因为存在大量虚假信息。这些信息并非普通的俄罗斯或中国煽风点火，而是有组织地播撒对“史诗怒火”行动成功与否、与以色列的关系、总统的决心、地面实际情况等的怀疑种子。问题的一部分在于记者们急于验证他们已经写好的报道；另一部分则是特朗普政府内部积极泄密，以削弱公众信心，向总统内心播撒怀疑，制造经济担忧；当然，还有无法客观评估特朗普政府所做一切的党派分歧。
和许多读者一样，我对这场持续的战争有很多疑问。总统是否全力以赴？他是否在寻找撤军的出路？所谓的与伊朗“谈判”到底是什么？我们真的在取得胜利吗？以色列和美国对胜利的定义是否一致？关于政权更迭又如何？没有政权更迭能否取得胜利？核武器问题呢？霍尔木兹海峡呢？阿拉伯国家呢？北约呢？还有更多问题。
我和马克向我们的好友、将军杰克·基恩提出了所有这些问题，甚至更多，有时反复提问。杰克依然与华盛顿和耶路撒冷的决策者保持密切联系，我无法否认他对问题的坦率。我的一位好朋友告诉我，他从这次播客中学到的东西比每天读报纸还要多。我不得不同意。幸好有像杰克这样的人。下周初，我们还将发布与美国驻以色列大使耶希埃尔·利特尔的广泛访谈。
了解更多，请阅读WTH Substack上的内容。
_source.trans_title: #伊朗战争：所有细节
_source.evidence: 文章主要讨论了伊朗战争中的虚假信息（disinformation）和认知战行动，提到了俄罗斯/中国煽动局势（Russian/Chinese fanning the flames），但这只是作为背景提及，并非文章核心事件。文章核心在于分析美国国内关于特朗普政府、以色列及伊朗战争的舆论战、信息战动态，以及美国内部的泄密和党派分歧对认知的影响。虽然提及了中国，但中国并非被攻击的核心对象，也不是文章描述的具体行动主体。文章描述的是认知域中的舆论对抗和信息战行动，属于具体的对抗行动及其动向。根据标签定义，[行动动向] 涵盖具体的舆论攻击行动和对抗动向。虽然涉及虚假信息，但更多是描述一种正在进行的认知对抗态势，而非单纯的技术研发或政策发布。由于文章主要聚焦于美国及其盟友（以色列）在伊朗战争背景下的认知域行动和舆论态势，且未明确针对中国大陆发起具体的敌情事件（涉我事件），也未涉及具体的演习、建军或技术武器化，因此归类为 [行动动向] 最为贴切，因为它描述了认知域内的具体对抗行动（如散布虚假信息、舆论攻击）。

_source.content:
Almost four years after launching a security feature called Lockdown Mode, Apple says it has yet to see a case where someone’s device was hacked with these additional security protections switched on.
“We are not aware of any successful mercenary spyware attacks against a Lockdown Mode-enabled Apple device,” Apple spokesperson Sarah O’Rourke told TechCrunch on Friday.
It’s the tech giant’s most recent affirmation that Apple devices with Lockdown Mode can withstand government spyware attacks, after
first making the claim
a year after the security feature’s debut.
Apple in 2022 announced Lockdown Mode
, an opt-in series of security protections that switches off certain features in iPhones and other Apple devices that are commonly exploited to hack targets with spyware. Apple specifically released this security mode to help at-risk customers defend themselves from the threats posed by government spyware made by companies like
Intellexa
,
NSO Group
, and
Paragon Solutions
.
In recent years, Apple has conceded that its customers can be hacked by spyware and has been more proactive about notifying customers who have been targeted.
Apple has
sent numerous batches
of
notifications
to users in over 150 countries, alerting them that they may have been hacked with spyware, which shows how much visibility the company now has on these types of attacks. Apple has never said how many users it has notified, but it’s likely fair to assume there have been dozens, if not more.
Donncha Ó Cearbhaill, the head of the security lab at Amnesty International, where he has investigated dozens of spyware attacks, said that he and his colleagues “have not seen any evidence of an iPhone being successfully compromised by mercenary spyware where Lockdown Mode was enabled at the time of the attack.”
Digital rights organizations like Amnesty International and the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab have documented several successful attacks on iPhone users, none of which have mentioned a bypass of Lockdown Mode. In at least
two
cases
, Citizen Lab researchers publicly said they had seen Lockdown Mode actively block spyware attacks,
one carried out with NSO’s Pegasus
, the other
with Predator spyware
, made by a company
now part of Intellexa
.
In at least one documented case of
a spyware attack targeting iPhones
, security researchers at Google
said
the spyware would bail out of trying to infect the victim if it detects Lockdown Mode, likely as a way to evade detection.
Patrick Wardle, an Apple cybersecurity expert and critic, says that Lockdown Mode is an important feature that makes it more difficult for spyware makers to attack Apple users.
“I think it’s safe to say, Lockdown Mode is one of the most aggressive consumer-facing hardening features ever shipped,” he told TechCrunch.
Wardle explained that by “shrinking the attack surface,” Lockdown Mode eliminates many techniques normally used to exploit the iPhone, and forces spyware makers to use more complex and expensive techniques to develop.
“It kills entire delivery mechanisms/exploit classes,” he added, “as it blocks most message attachment types, restricts WebKit features. This is really a huge reduction in remotely reachable attack surface, especially for zero-click exploit chains,” referring to hacks that can target people over the internet without any interaction from the victim.
It’s possible that Lockdown Mode has been bypassed, and neither Apple nor independent investigators have caught the attack. But given that Apple is typically publicly tight-lipped at the best of times, its latest statement marks a significant milestone for Lockdown Mode.
I have used Lockdown Mode for years, and I barely think about it —
except when it pops up notifications
that can be occasionally confusing. Some features that have been switched off require you to take an extra step, such as copying and pasting links from text messages to your browser. That’s why I, and several digital security experts, recommend anyone worried about being targeted by spyware or digital attacks to switch on Lockdown Mode.
_source.movement_title: 苹果锁定模式启用四年未发现间谍软件成功攻击
_source.movement_abstract: 苹果公司于2022年推出的锁定模式（Lockdown Mode）已运行四年多，官方声明该功能启用后尚未发现成功遭政府间谍软件攻击的案例。该模式通过关闭消息附件类型、限制WebKit功能等技术手段，有效防御由Intellexa、NSO Group等公司开发的间谍软件。苹果已向全球150多个国家的用户发送过攻击预警通知，但未披露具体数量。国际特赦组织安全实验室和多伦多大学公民实验室的研究显示，至少两起间谍软件攻击被锁定模式成功拦截，包括NSO的Pegasus和Intellexa旗下的Predator。谷歌安全团队还发现间谍软件在检测到锁定模式时会自动放弃攻击。专家认为该模式大幅缩小了攻击面，迫使攻击者采用更复杂技术，是消费者安全强化措施中的重要创新。尽管存在绕过可能性，但苹果对此保持保密，最新声明标志着该功能的重要里程碑。建议关注数字安全的用户启用此模式，尽管部分操作需额外步骤。
_source.title: Apple says no one using Lockdown Mode has been hacked with spyware
_source.trans_cont:
在推出名为“锁定模式”的安全功能近四年后，苹果公司表示，尚未发现有人在开启这些额外安全保护的情况下，其设备遭到黑客攻击。苹果发言人莎拉·奥里奥克（Sarah O’Rourke）周五对TechCrunch表示：“我们没有发现任何针对开启了锁定模式的苹果设备的成功的雇佣间谍软件攻击。” 

这是科技巨头对苹果设备在锁定模式下能够抵御政府间谍软件攻击的最新确认，此前在该安全功能推出一年后，苹果首次做出这一声明。2022年，苹果推出了锁定模式，这是一种可选的安全保护措施，会关闭iPhone及其他苹果设备中常被用来通过间谍软件攻击目标的功能。苹果特别推出这一安全模式，旨在帮助高风险用户防范由像Intellexa、NSO Group和Paragon Solutions等公司制造的政府间谍软件带来的威胁。

近年来，苹果承认其用户可能被间谍软件攻击，并更加积极地通知被针对的用户。苹果已向超过150个国家的用户发送了多批通知，提醒他们可能遭到间谍软件攻击，这表明该公司对这类攻击的可见度大幅提高。苹果从未透露通知了多少用户，但可以合理推测，受影响的用户数量可能数十人甚至更多。

国际特赦组织安全实验室负责人Donncha Ó Cearbhaill表示，他和同事“没有发现任何证据表明，当锁定模式开启时，iPhone曾被成功的雇佣间谍软件入侵。”像国际特赦组织和多伦多大学公民实验室这样的数字权利组织已经记录了多起针对iPhone用户的成功攻击，其中没有提到绕过锁定模式的情况。在至少两起案例中，公民实验室的研究人员公开表示，他们看到锁定模式成功阻止了间谍软件攻击，其中一起是使用NSO的“飞马”（Pegasus）间谍软件，另一起是使用由现属于Intellexa的公司开发的“猎手”（Predator）间谍软件。

在至少一起记录的针对iPhone的间谍软件攻击案例中，谷歌的安全研究人员表示，如果检测到锁定模式，间谍软件会放弃尝试感染受害者，这可能是为了逃避检测。

苹果网络安全专家兼批评者帕特里克·沃德尔（Patrick Wardle）表示，锁定模式是一项重要的功能，使间谍软件制造商更难攻击苹果用户。“我认为可以安全地说，锁定模式是苹果公司推出过的最激进的面向消费者的强化功能之一，”他对TechCrunch说道。

沃德尔解释说，通过“缩小攻击面”，锁定模式消除了许多通常用于利用iPhone的技术，迫使间谍软件制造商使用更复杂和昂贵的技术进行开发。“它彻底阻断了整个攻击机制/利用类别，”他补充道，“因为它阻止了大多数消息附件类型，限制了WebKit功能。这在很大程度上减少了远程可攻击的攻击面，尤其是针对零点击利用链的攻击，即无需受害者任何交互即可通过互联网攻击目标。”

虽然有可能绕过了锁定模式，而且苹果或独立调查人员尚未发现攻击，但考虑到苹果通常在公开场合非常谨慎，其最新声明标志着锁定模式的一个重要里程碑。

我已经使用锁定模式多年，几乎不怎么去想它——除了当它弹出通知时，这些通知有时会让人感到困惑。一些被关闭的功能需要用户多采取一步操作，例如从短信中复制粘贴链接到浏览器。因此，我以及几位数字安全专家建议，任何担心可能成为间谍软件或数字攻击目标的人，都应该开启锁定模式。
_source.trans_title: 苹果表示，使用锁定模式的用户中没有人被植入间谍软件进行黑客攻击

An in-depth
report
published last week by the Middle East Media Research Institute (
MEMRI
) detailed Iran-inspired and orchestrated violence and terror activity in the U.S.
U.S. intelligence agencies have long warned that Tehran’s ideological messaging and covert networks could inspire or enable attacks inside the U.S. The threat has only grown in recent years, as more operatives have been dispatched to the U.S. to scope out targets and even set up educational and religious institutions to spread Iran’s Islamic revolutionary ideology. Outreach to student groups has been ramped up, as have efforts to influence U.S. domestic policy. The report sets out these government warnings in recent years, including concerns about sleeper cells.
After reviewing Iran-linked terror activity and arrests and convictions of Iranian regime agents for attempted murder and other crimes, the report’s main authors, MEMRI Executive Director Steven Stalinsky, Lead Editor R. Sosnow, and Research Fellow Rachel Legow, examine in detail Iranian threats to attack inside the U.S. and to assassinate U.S. officials, including President Trump. It should be noted that just last week,
its top armed forces spokesman
warned that “parks, recreational areas, and tourist destinations” will not be safe for Iran’s enemies anywhere.
Now, as the Iranian regime faces the biggest threat in its history, its loyalists and agents across the U.S. are publicly displaying their support for the regime, its leaders, and its ideology. The report’s authors document these displays in detail; they include memorials for slain Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei held at
Islamic centers
that Iran help to create and through its disinformation campaign all across social media.

_source.movement_title: 伊朗在美国渗透活动及恐怖威胁报告
_source.movement_abstract: 美国中东媒体研究与信息研究所（MEMRI）上周发布一份深度报告，详细披露伊朗在美国境内策划和实施的暴力及恐怖活动。报告指出，伊朗情报机构长期通过意识形态宣传和秘密网络煽动或支持美国本土袭击，并在过去几年派遣更多特工赴美侦查目标、建立教育宗教机构传播革命思想。当前伊朗政权面临历史性威胁，其在美国的代理人和追随者通过社交媒体虚假信息运动及伊斯兰中心举办纪念活动等方式公开支持政权和领导人。报告特别强调伊朗武装力量发言人近期警告称，公园、休闲场所和旅游景点对伊朗敌人不再安全，同时记录了针对特朗普等美国官员的暗杀威胁。MEMRI执行主任史蒂文·斯塔林斯基等作者梳理了近年伊朗关联恐怖活动、特工逮捕及定罪案例，并分析伊朗对美国国内政策的渗透行为。
_source.title: New Report Exposes And Details Iranian Regime Supporters Across The U.S.
_source.trans_cont:
一份深入的报告上周由中东媒体研究中心（MEMRI）发布，详细描述了受伊朗启发和策划的在美国发生的暴力和恐怖活动。美国情报机构长期以来警告称，德黑兰的思想宣传和秘密网络可能会激发或协助在美国境内发动袭击。近年来，这一威胁不断加剧，因为越来越多的行动人员被派往美国，以侦察目标，甚至设立教育和宗教机构，传播伊朗的伊斯兰革命思想。对学生活动团体的渗透也有所增加，同时对影响美国国内政策的努力也在加强。该报告列举了近年来政府发出的这些警告，包括对潜伏细胞的担忧。

在回顾与伊朗有关的恐怖活动以及伊朗政权代理人因企图谋杀和其他罪行被逮捕和定罪的情况后，该报告的主要作者——MEMRI执行主任史蒂文·斯塔林斯基（Steven Stalinsky）、主编R.索诺夫（R. Sosnow）和研究员拉切尔·列戈（Rachel Legow）——详细分析了伊朗对美国境内发动袭击和暗杀美国官员（包括特朗普总统）的威胁。值得注意的是，就在上周，该机构的最高武装部队发言人警告称，“公园、休闲区和旅游景点”对伊朗的敌人来说将不再安全。

如今，随着伊朗政权面临历史上最大的威胁，其在美国的忠实支持者和代理人公开表达对政权、领导人及其意识形态的支持。该报告的作者详细记录了这些行为，其中包括在伊朗资助创建的伊斯兰中心举行的已故最高领袖阿里·哈梅内伊的纪念活动，以及通过社交媒体上的虚假信息宣传活动进行的宣传。阅读完整报告，请点击此处。
_source.trans_title: 新报告揭露并详细介绍了美国境内的伊朗政权支持者

(中央社布魯塞爾26日綜合外電報導)歐洲聯盟(EU)監管機構今天表示,Pornhub、Stripchat、XNXX與XVideos等成人平台因允許兒童接觸色情內容,被控違反歐盟科技法規,恐面臨巨額罰款。
路透社報導,歐盟當局依據「數位服務法」(Digital Services Act, DSA)調查10個月後,對Pornhub等成人網站提出指控,該法要求大型網路平台須加強打擊非法及有害內容。
歐盟執委會(European Commission)指控,塞浦路斯集團Aylo Freesites旗下Pornhub、塞浦路斯Technius子公司Stripchat、捷克NKL Associates旗下XNXX以及WebGroup Czech Republic經營的XVideos更關注自身名聲,而非未成年人的社會風險。
此外,歐盟執委會也強烈反對Pornhub等成人平台的自我聲明機制,因為用戶只需點擊確認自己已滿18歲,即可進入平台。
歐盟執委會指出,Pornhub、Stripchat、XNXX與XVideos需實施保護隱私的年齡驗證措施,以防止兒童接觸有害內容。
據報導,若上述相關公司最終被認定違反「數位服務法」,恐面臨相當於全球年營收6%的罰款。(編譯:陳正健)1150327
_source.movement_title: 欧盟拟重罚四大成人平台违规允许儿童接触色情内容
_source.movement_abstract: 欧盟监管机构指控Pornhub、Stripchat、XNXX和XVideos等成人平台允许儿童接触色情内容，违反《数字服务法》。经10个月调查后，欧盟委员会认为这些平台更关注自身声誉而非未成年人保护，特别是其仅通过用户点击确认年龄的机制存在漏洞。监管机构要求四家平台实施隐私保护的年龄验证措施，以防止儿童访问有害内容。若最终认定违规，相关公司将面临相当于全球年营收6%的罚款。

(中央社記者戴雅真東京27日專電)針對日本自衛官闖入中國駐日大使館事件,自民黨前外相河野太郎表示,此案恐被中國用於宣傳戰,對外界描繪出特定敘事,對日本國際形象造成影響;前環境大臣細野豪志也警告,相關問題不應被輕忽。
產經新聞報導,河野與細野在25日播出的YouTube節目中談及此案。警視廳指出,23歲陸上自衛隊3等陸尉村田晃大因涉嫌侵入位於東京的中國大使館遭逮,館內植栽中並發現疑似他攜入、刀刃長約18公分的刀具。
河野表示,「為什麼能進入那樣的地方,實在有很多不明白之處」。細野則指出,村田應該接受過將近1年自衛隊幹部訓練,「難道沒有在過程中被篩選出來嗎」,有必要進一步檢討。
兩人並以假設情境討論。細野說,「反過來說,如果有(中國)人民解放軍的軍官闖入北京日本大使館」,河野接下去說,「假若還揮舞刀子的話...」細野表示,「就算沒有揮刀,只是闖入,日本的輿論大概就會爆炸。」
河野表示,「會陷入混亂。」他進一步警告,在當前國際情勢下,這起事件可能會被解讀為「日本要回到軍國主義」的敘事。
細野強調,正因事實並非如此,更應妥善應對,「這件事不應輕忽」。
此外,兩人也談及日前舉行的日美領袖會談。河野表示,這次訪問最大目的,是要讓川普(Donald Trump)感到愉快。他並說,日本首相高市早苗最終完成任務返國,「我認為可以給100分滿分」。(編輯:田瑞華)1150327
_source.movement_title: 日前高官质疑自卫官闯入中国使馆事件处理
_source.movement_abstract: 日本自民党前外相河野太郎与前环境大臣细野豪志在YouTube节目中讨论了23岁陆上自卫队三等陆尉村田晃大涉嫌闯入中国驻东京大使馆事件。两人指出，该事件可能被中国用于构建特定叙事开展宣传战，影响日本国际形象。河野质疑自卫官为何能进入大使馆，认为事件暴露出安全漏洞，并警告在当前国际形势下可能被解读为日本重回军国主义的信号。细野强调必须妥善应对，指出村田应接受过近一年干部训练却未被筛选，需检讨训练机制，同时假设中国军官闯入日本大使馆将引发舆论强烈反弹。此外，两人还评价近期日美领导人会谈，河野认为日本首相高市早苗此行成功让特朗普感到满意，应给予满分评价。
_source.title: 自衛官闖中國使館 日前外相:恐被北京宣傳戰利用
_source.trans_cont:
（中央社记者戴雅真东京27日电）针对日本自卫官闯入中国驻日大使馆事件，自民党前外相河野太郎表示，此案可能被中国用于宣传战，对外界塑造特定叙事，影响日本国际形象；前环境大臣细野豪志也警告，相关问题不应被轻视。

产经新闻报道，河野与细野在25日播出的YouTube节目中谈及此事。警视厅指出，23岁的陆上自卫队三等陆尉村田晃大因涉嫌闯入位于东京的中国大使馆被逮捕，馆内植栽中发现疑似其携带、刀刃长约18厘米的刀具。

河野表示，“为何能进入那样地方，实在有很多不明白之处”。细野则指出，村田应接受过将近1年的自卫队干部训练，“难道没有在过程中被筛选出来吗”，有必要进一步检讨。

两人并以假设情境讨论。细野说，“反过来，如果有（中国）人民解放军军官闯入北京日本大使馆”，河野接下去说，“假若还挥舞刀子的话……”细野表示，“就算没有挥刀，只是闯入，日本舆论大概就会爆炸。”

河野表示，“会陷入混乱”。他进一步警告，在当前国际形势下，这起事件可能被解读为“日本要回到军国主义”的叙事。

细野强调，正因为事实并非如此，更应妥善应对，“这件事不应轻忽”。

此外，两人也谈及日前举行的日美领袖会谈。河野表示，此次访问最大目的，是让特朗普（Donald Trump）感到愉快。他并说，日本首相高市早苗最终完成任务回国，“我认为可以给100分满分”。（编辑：田瑞华）1150327
_source.trans_title: 自卫官闯入中国使馆 前外相：恐怕被北京宣传战利用
_source.evidence: 文章核心内容是关于日本自卫官闯入中国驻日大使馆事件，以及日本前外相河野太郎等人对此事件的评论。评论中明确提到该事件可能被中国用于'宣传战'，并担忧中国会利用此事件构建特定叙事（如'军国主义'叙事）来影响日本的国际形象。这属于针对中国大陆（作为被攻击对象或相关方）的敌情事件，涉及认知域中的舆论战、宣传战风险，符合'[涉我事件]'的定义（涉及中国大陆的敌情事件，非发起方）。虽然文中提到了'宣传战'，但这是日本官员对中国可能反应的担忧，而非中国正在发起的具体行动，因此不选'[行动动向]'。

_source.content:
The recent large-scale indictment of Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) information technology (IT) workers by the U.S. Department of Justice clearly demonstrates the escalating sophistication and severity of North Korea’s cyber operations. This law enforcement action underscores not merely the detection of illegal activity, but the fact that the DPRK is leveraging cyberspace in a systematic manner to generate revenue for the regime. As of 2024, DPRK IT workers are estimated to generate between $350 million and $800 million annually.
As UN sanctions have constricted traditional sources of foreign currency, the DPRK has increasingly relied on overseas IT workers disguised as legitimate employees. What initially appeared to involve ordinary software development or application design has evolved into a coordinated strategy of infiltration, revenue generation, and, in some cases, data theft and financial crime.
This report examines the evolution of DPRK IT workers’ operational tactics, the international expansion of their networks, and the limitations of existing responses. It argues that advisory- and sanctions-based measures alone are insufficient and calls for more proactive, government-led coordination and outreach to address this growing threat.
The Evolution of DPRK IT Workers’ Operational TacticsSince around 2017, DPRK IT workers have been creating fraudulent profiles, forged identities, and fake resumes to infiltrate freelance platforms and secure employment abroad. Initially, their work appeared to involve ordinary software development or application design, delaying recognition of the threat and enabling rapid proliferation.
During the hiring process, when video interviews were requested, accomplices appeared on camera while the DPRK worker redirected the conversation to a phone or chat-based format, citing supposed technical issues. In some cases, they remotely accessed the accomplice’s device to perform technical demonstrations during the interview.
Once remote work feasibility was confirmed, DPRK IT units collaborated with U.S.-based conspirators to operate “laptop farms,” enabling multiple simultaneous infiltrations. U.S. accomplices received and managed employer-issued laptops, while DPRK operatives remotely controlled them to impersonate numerous employees across several companies.
These workers do not merely conduct software development. They strategically infiltrate defense contractors, government contractors, and critical infrastructure organizations to obtain sensitive internal access. Once inside, they exfiltrate confidential data and intellectual property to DPRK or third-party criminal networks. Some groups install backdoors for follow-on operations or threaten data leaks after termination to extort money. Multiple cases show DPRK IT workers securing developer positions at cryptocurrency companies and directly stealing hundreds of millions of dollars in assets.
More recently, DPRK IT workers have aggressively integrated artificial intelligence (AI) into their disguise and infiltration tactics. They generate fake profile images, automatically produce large volumes of resumes and cover letters using generative AI tools, manipulate social media activity, and use deepfake video and audio during remote interviews.
These AI-enabled methods represent a shift from basic identity fraud to a highly structured and coordinated global infiltration strategy. This trend reinforces the need not only for companies, but also governments, to strengthen both defensive and policy responses, as these operations increasingly constitute a direct national security risk.
The International Expansion of DPRK IT Workers and AccomplicesDPRK IT workers and their accomplice networks have expanded their geographic scope beyond China and Russia—where they had traditionally operated—to new third-country destinations. Since 2020, they have increasingly been deployed to Equatorial Guinea, Laos, and the United Arab Emirates, and more recently to Cambodia, Guinea, Nigeria, and Tanzania, where they conduct remote work for U.S. companies to earn foreign currency. However, in the second half of 2024, as U.S. law enforcement measures intensified, some workers shifted operations to Europe, where oversight remains relatively less stringent.
In Europe, IT workers have engaged in coordinated activities across multiple countries—including Germany, Portugal, and the United Kingdom—leveraging numerous personas and AI-generated synthetic profiles to register on local employment platforms and global freelancing websites, and to apply for positions at defense contractors and government-related organizations. One notable case was identified in Serbia, where a DPRK IT worker infiltrated a token corporation and stole approximately $175,000 worth of cryptocurrency, subsequently transferring the funds to overseas accounts. This case demonstrates that North Korea is actively exploiting European financial and crypto-asset systems to construct a foreign currency procurement structure.
Such activities have also been detected across Asia. In Japan, multiple incidents have been uncovered involving DPRK IT workers engaged in fraudulent employment and illicit operations. In China, a North Korean worker attempting to steal military technology was arrested and detained, illustrating that the activities of these workers are expanding beyond conventional software development into strategically sensitive areas such as defense technology. These incidents indicate that their operations are no longer confined to North America and Europe; instead, they are spreading across Asia and expanding globally in both geographic and industrial dimensions.
These overseas operations would not be possible without the support of accomplices operating worldwide. Accomplice networks in the United States, Japan, Ukraine, and the United Arab Emirates collaborate with DPRK IT workers by managing laptop farms, laundering funds, managing stolen assets, forging identities, and establishing illicit remittance channels. This support network forms the critical infrastructure that enables the covert operations, revenue generation, and sanctions evasion activities of DPRK IT workers.
As North Korea’s concealment techniques and operational sophistication continue to advance, and as its networks of workers and accomplices expand globally, it is increasingly clear that the current international cooperation framework alone has limitations in mounting an effective response.
Limitations of International Responses to DPRK IT ActivitiesThe United States is the primary country where DPRK IT workers are most actively operating, and it has responded with the most robust measures, including various sanctions, to curb their employment activities within the country. As a result, by the second half of 2024, DPRK IT workers shifted their operations primarily to Europe, where oversight is relatively less stringent. Figure 1 summarizes guidance and advisories, sanctions, executive orders (EOs) and initiatives, and law enforcement actions issued by the Republic of Korea (ROK), the United States, and other countries, organized by release date. The figure illustrates that DPRK IT workers have long been recognized by the U.S. government as a serious threat, and the United States has actively responded through EOs, initiative, sanctions, and legal actions.
Initially, EOs 13722 and 13810 designated DPRK IT workers’ overseas deployment and related activities as sanctions targets, prohibiting their provision of software and technical services. However, the Covid-19 pandemic (March 2020–May 2023) led to a surge in remote work, enabling DPRK IT workers to work for U.S. companies remotely. Consequently, since 2022, U.S. government and intelligence agencies have issued a total of four documents, including one guidance and three public service announcements to alert companies to risk indicators and response measures. From 2023 onward, interagency collaboration among the U.S. Departments of Treasury, Justice, and State has intensified, resulting in large-scale sanctions and prosecutions targeting DPRK IT workers and networks.
In March 2024, the United States launched the “DPRK RevGen: Domestic Enabler Initiative,” prioritizing the identification and shutdown of laptop farms. The initiative disclosed multiple law enforcement actions against accomplices hosting laptop farms, DPRK IT workers involved, domains used for illicit employment, and associated revenues. Particularly, from the second half of 2025, large-scale joint law enforcement actions and multiple sanctions targeting DPRK IT workers have been publicly disclosed, reflecting a significant strengthening of U.S. response efforts.
Following the United States, the ROK has been the most active country in responding to DPRK IT worker operations. In December 2022, the ROK issued its first joint government advisory calling for enhanced verification of DPRK IT worker identities. Since then, the ROK has independently designated six entities and individuals associated with DPRK IT workers involved in overseas foreign currency–earning activities as sanctions targets. The ROK and the United States have also coordinated in responding to DPRK IT workers. In April 2023, the two countries jointly designated targets for sanctions for the first time, and to date, there have been three instances of joint target designations. Separately, in October 2023, both countries issued a joint government advisory updating their respective advisories with the latest trends.
In 2024, countries including Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, and the United Kingdom also joined the international effort by issuing advisories on DPRK IT workers’ disguised employment. This development reflects a growing recognition that the DPRK’s covert employment activities are not merely a foreign currency–earning issue, but also an international security and economic risk. Overall, Figure 1 demonstrates that the principal actors responding to DPRK IT worker operations have expanded from the ROK and the United States to other countries, including those in Europe, highlighting the need for a broader international response framework.
Figure 1 also highlights certain challenges. According to U.S. indictments, DPRK IT workers have been active since at least 2017. Their initial activities were disguised as legitimate employment, which delayed recognition of the associated risks by both the international community and private companies. The figure shows that substantial international responses only began in earnest around 2024.
During the Covid-19 pandemic, as remote work culture expanded, DPRK IT workers found it increasingly easy to participate in overseas corporate projects by posing as third-country workers. During this period, they are also believed to have rapidly enhanced both their technical capabilities and their identity-masking and money-laundering techniques. At the same time, international sanctions enforcement and broader multilateral responses remained largely stagnant, creating a widening gap between North Korea’s evolving methods and the international community’s ability to counter them.
As a result, advisory and sanctions-based responses have inherent limitations. DPRK IT workers are state-sponsored and systematically managed, allowing them to continuously develop innovative techniques and methods. In practice, new identity-masking and technical methods have repeatedly emerged immediately following sanctions. While the United States has combined executive orders, sanctions, prosecutions, and law enforcement actions, these measures alone have had limited effectiveness, as North Korea consistently develops new evasion methods to circumvent sanctions.
Consequently, advisory- and sanctions-based responses alone remain insufficient to fundamentally disrupt DPRK IT worker operations. While detection and response at the company level are important, the burden of identifying and mitigating these threats has largely been placed on individual companies, many of which lack the resources, visibility, or expertise to do so effectively. Moreover, the transnational and adaptive nature of DPRK IT worker networks limits the effectiveness of isolated, reactive measures.
These limitations underscore the need for a more proactive and coordinated approach led by governments. In particular, systematic outreach to domestic companies, structured engagement with international partners, and sustained public-private collaboration are essential to closing existing response gaps. Without stronger government-led efforts to disseminate risk awareness, share intelligence, and align international countermeasures, existing responses will continue to lag behind the evolving tactics of DPRK IT workers.
Government-led Outreach and Coordination to Counter DPRK IT Worker ThreatsDPRK IT worker operations are expected to persist through 2026 and continue expanding geographically as enforcement pressure intensifies in the United States. These operations are likely to leverage increasingly sophisticated techniques, including multimodal generative AI—including voice, text, and video deepfakes—to sustain disguised employment. At the same time, cryptocurrency-related companies and other digitally native sectors will remain high-value targets due to their remote work structures and the potential for rapid financial gain.
International sanctions and law enforcement actions have imposed tangible costs on these networks, but they have not fundamentally disrupted DPRK IT worker operations. The adaptive, state-sponsored nature of these activities enables rapid evolution in response to enforcement measures. Reliance on reactive, company-level detection alone places an unsustainable burden on individual companies and creates persistent gaps between emerging threats and effective countermeasures. Addressing these limitations requires a shift toward proactive, government-led outreach and coordination.
Lessons from the Private Sector: Implications for Government ActionCompanies face significant structural constraints when disclosing DPRK IT worker incidents. When a company inadvertently hires a DPRK IT worker, the resulting risks extend beyond technical compromise to reputational damage, customer attrition, legal exposure, and contractual liabilities. These factors strongly discourage voluntary disclosure, even when early reporting would benefit the broader ecosystem.
Nevertheless, in 2024, one cybersecurity company publicly disclosed an attempted internal intrusion linked to DPRK IT worker activity. The company documented the full recruitment process—including job postings, interview procedures, and identity verification steps—and immediately shared all relevant data with U.S. cybersecurity firm Mandiant and the FBI to support early-stage investigations. The company also publicly release lessons learned and response measures through its website.
Following the incident, the company conducted organization-wide employee training, implemented fingerprint-based identity verification, and restricted corporate laptop delivery to verified UPS shipments requiring photo identification. In addition, the company published a comprehensive white paper detailing insider-threat risks and preventive controls, and it continued to release updates on DPRK IT worker activity trends.
According to the company’s CEO, the decision to disclose was intended to raise awareness of the widespread nature of DPRK IT worker infiltration attempts and to warn other organizations of comparable risks. By transparently sharing its experience, the company contributed to elevating industry-wide security standards while reinforcing customer trust.
However, such best practices remain fragmented across jurisdictions and sectors, making comprehensive access difficult for most companies—particularly small- and medium-sized enterprises. This fragmentation highlights the limitations of relying solely on voluntary private sector disclosure. Accordingly, governments should assume a more active role in collecting, standardizing, and disseminating these lessons through sustained outreach efforts.
Centralized Information Sharing and Institutional Verification FrameworksGovernments already possess extensive intelligence related to DPRK cyber operations and IT worker networks, yet this information often fails to reach companies in a usable and timely manner. To close this gap, the ROK government should centrally aggregate and disseminate both best practices and DPRK IT worker–specific indicators—including email addresses, recurring account naming patterns, profile photos, commonly cited education and career information, and IP addresses associated with laptop farms.
Rather than creating new mechanisms, existing government–private sector information-sharing platforms focused on DPRK cyber threats should be expanded to incorporate these indicators. Centralization would significantly lower access barriers, enabling companies of all sizes to integrate this information directly into recruitment screening, identity verification, and internal security training processes.
In parallel, the ROK should consider establishing an institutional employment-eligibility and identity verification framework analogous to the U.S. I-9 and E-Verify systems. In the United States, these mechanisms have been used not only to confirm work authorization, but also to flag identity inconsistencies and third-country impersonation patterns relevant to DPRK IT worker investigations. A comparable system in the ROK would provide companies with an additional safeguard when pre-employment screening fails.
Reporting, Incentives, and Enforcement MechanismsTimely reporting remains critical to preventing escalation and secondary harm once DPRK IT worker activity is detected. However, incentives alone are unlikely to overcome companies’ reluctance to disclose incidents. A dual-track framework combining legal protections and meaningful penalties is therefore required to make reporting the rational choice rather than concealment.
The government should provide whistleblower protections and limited liability safeguards for companies that report suspicious activity promptly. At the same time, penalties—including increased fines—should be strengthened for companies that knowingly or negligently employ DPRK IT workers or fail to report suspicious indicators within a defined time frame. Enforcement should also extend to operational enablers, such as laptop farm operators and intermediaries who facilitate overseas employment and financial flows, as these actors are essential to sustaining DPRK IT worker networks.
International Outreach and the ROK’s Strategic LeadershipAlthough remote work is less prevalent in the ROK than in many Western economies, the country faces unparalleled national security exposure due to its geographic proximity to North Korea. This position confers both heightened risk and a unique responsibility to lead international awareness and coordination efforts.
Recent reporting indicates that DPRK IT worker activity has increased across Europe, where remote work adoption remains high and threat awareness comparatively low. The ROK should proactively engage European partners to emphasize that weak awareness in remote work environments can escalate into broader national and economic security risks. Similar outreach is warranted in Southeast Asia, Africa, and other regions where awareness remains limited.
In parallel, bilateral cooperation between the ROK and the United States—as well as trilateral coordination with Japan—should continue through regular advisories, working-level exchanges, and joint statements. Given the increasingly blurred line between DPRK IT workers and overtly malicious cyber actors, a new joint advisory emphasizing the growing use of direct exfiltration and intrusion tactics would reinforce shared threat perception and strengthen collective deterrence.
Ultimately, countering DPRK IT worker operations requires more than cooperation—it requires leadership. By centralizing information, institutionalizing verification mechanisms, incentivizing reporting, and proactively engaging international partners, the ROK can move from a reactive participant to a global agenda-setter in addressing this evolving threat.
Yena Kim is a senior researcher on the Cybersecurity Policy Research Team at the National Security Research Institute in the Republic of Korea. Donghee Kim is a senior researcher and manager of the Cybersecurity Policy Research Team at the National Security Research Institute in the Republic of Korea.

_source.movement_abstract: 美国司法部近期对朝鲜的信息技术（IT）人员的大规模起诉，揭示了朝鲜在网络攻击方面的高度复杂性和严重性。这些IT人员通过伪造身份、简历，伪装成合法员工，进入海外平台从事软件开发等任务，实际上却进行数据窃取、金融犯罪等活动，年收入估计达3.5亿至8亿美元。随着联合国制裁限制了朝鲜的传统外汇来源，其更依赖海外IT人员进行渗透和收入获取。报告指出，朝鲜IT人员的战术已从简单的身份欺诈演变为高度结构化的全球渗透策略，并利用人工智能技术提升伪装能力。此外，朝鲜IT人员的活动范围已扩展至欧洲等地区，利用当地平台和AI生成身份进行渗透，对国家安全构成直接威胁。
_source.post_location: 华盛顿特区西北罗德岛大道1616号
_source.site_name: 美国战略与国际问题研究中心
_source.title: Responding to the Evolution and Global Expansion of the DPRK IT Worker Threat
_source.trans_cont:
美国司法部最近对朝鲜民主主义人民共和国（DPRK）信息技术（IT）工作者的大规模起诉，清楚地表明了朝鲜网络行动的复杂性和严重性正在不断升级。这一执法行动不仅表明非法活动被发现，还表明DPRK正系统性地利用网络空间为政权创造收入。截至2024年，DPRK IT工作者每年估计可创造3.5亿至8亿美元的收入。
随着联合国制裁限制了传统外汇来源，DPRK越来越多地依靠海外IT工作者，这些工作者伪装成合法员工。起初看似普通的软件开发或应用程序设计，现已演变为一种协调的渗透、收入生成以及在某些情况下数据窃取和金融犯罪的策略。
本报告探讨了DPRK IT工作者操作战术的演变、其网络的国际扩展以及现有应对措施的局限性。报告认为，仅依靠建议和制裁措施是不够的，并呼吁采取更加积极、由政府主导的协调和对外交流，以应对这一日益严重的威胁。
DPRK IT工作者操作战术的演变自2017年左右以来，DPRK IT工作者开始创建虚假档案、伪造身份和假简历，以渗透自由职业平台并获得海外工作。起初，他们的工作似乎涉及普通的软件开发或应用程序设计，这延迟了对威胁的认识，并使威胁迅速扩散。
在招聘过程中，当要求视频面试时，同伙会出现在镜头前，而DPRK工作者则将对话转向电话或聊天格式，声称有技术问题。在某些情况下，他们远程访问同伙的设备，在面试中进行技术演示。
一旦远程工作的可行性得到确认，DPRK IT单位与美国的同伙合作，运营“笔记本电脑农场”，从而实现多个同时渗透。美国同伙接收和管理雇主发放的笔记本电脑，而DPRK操作人员则远程控制这些设备，以伪装成多家公司的多个员工。
这些工作者不仅仅是进行软件开发。他们战略性地渗透国防承包商、政府承包商和关键基础设施组织，以获取敏感的内部访问权限。一旦进入内部，他们将机密数据和知识产权转移至DPRK或第三方犯罪网络。一些小组安装后门以进行后续操作，或在被解雇后威胁数据泄露以勒索钱财。多个案例显示，DPRK IT工作者在加密货币公司获得开发职位，并直接窃取数亿美元的资产。
最近，DPRK IT工作者积极将人工智能（AI）整合到他们的伪装和渗透策略中。他们生成虚假的个人资料图片，使用生成式AI工具自动创建大量简历和求职信，操纵社交媒体活动，并在远程面试中使用深度伪造视频和音频。
这些AI驱动的方法标志着从基本的身份欺诈向高度结构化和协调的全球渗透策略的转变。这一趋势强化了不仅公司，而且政府需要加强防御和政策应对的必要性，因为这些操作日益构成直接的国家安全风险。
DPRK IT工作者和同伙的国际扩展DPRK IT工作者及其同伙网络已将地理范围扩展到中国和俄罗斯以外的第三国。自2020年以来，他们越来越多地被部署到赤道几内亚、老挝和阿拉伯联合酋长国，并且最近还扩展到柬埔寨、几内亚、尼日利亚和坦桑尼亚，他们为美国公司进行远程工作以赚取外汇。然而，在2024年下半年，随着美国执法措施的加强，一些工作者将业务转移到欧洲，因为那里的监管相对不那么严格。
在欧洲，IT工作者在多个国家（包括德国、葡萄牙和英国）开展协调活动，利用大量身份和AI生成的合成个人资料注册于本地就业平台和全球自由职业网站，并申请国防承包商和政府相关组织的职位。一个值得注意的案例是在塞尔维亚，一名DPRK IT工作者渗透了一家代币公司并窃取了价值约17.5万美元的加密货币，随后将资金转移到海外账户。这一案例表明，朝鲜正在积极利用欧洲的金融和加密资产系统来构建外汇采购结构。
此类活动也已在亚洲被发现。在日本，多个涉及DPRK IT工作者进行欺诈性就业和非法活动的案例被揭露。在中国，一名试图窃取军事技术的朝鲜工人被逮捕并拘留，这表明这些工作者的活动已扩展到传统软件开发之外的战略敏感领域，如国防技术。这些案例表明，他们的活动不再局限于北美和欧洲，而是正在向亚洲扩展，并在全球地理和工业维度上不断扩大。
这些海外活动在没有全球同伙支持的情况下是不可能的。美国、日本、乌克兰和阿拉伯联合酋长国的同伙网络与DPRK IT工作者合作，通过管理笔记本电脑农场、洗钱、管理被盗资产、伪造身份和建立非法汇款渠道来支持他们。这个支持网络构成了使DPRK IT工作者进行秘密行动、收入生成和规避制裁活动
_source.trans_title: 应对朝鲜IT工作者威胁的演变及全球扩张
_source.evidence: 文章主要描述了朝鲜（DPRK）IT人员利用AI技术、伪造身份等手段，在全球范围内（包括中国）进行网络渗透、窃取数据和金融犯罪的行动。文中明确提到在中国有朝鲜IT人员试图窃取军事技术并被逮捕的案例，且文章整体聚焦于敌对势力（朝鲜）针对全球（含中国）的具体网络攻击行动、战术演变及国际应对。根据标签定义，这属于针对中国大陆（作为相关方/受害方）的敌情事件，符合[涉我事件]的定义。虽然涉及AI技术，但核心是敌对势力的攻击行动而非单纯的技术研发；虽然涉及政策建议，但核心是描述敌情行动。因此，[涉我事件]是最准确的分类。

_source.content:
Anthropic’s signature AI model Claude is being used by the Pentagon during the U.S. military’s ongoing war against Iran, a Pentagon official confirmed Tuesday during a Senate subcommittee hearing.
Pentagon Chief Information Officer Kirsten A. Davies confirmed to Sen. Jack Reed (D-R.I.), the ranking member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, that the Pentagon is using the AI model as part of Operation Epic Fury.
“The use of the system is active right now. This is also why we provided for a measure of time we felt was reasonable, as well as an exception process for removal of the Anthropic systems,” Davies said while being questioned by Reed over the department designating the company as a supply chain risk.
Anthropic declined to comment when reached by The Hill.
Claude is used by the Pentagon for intelligence analysis but has become a rare flashpoint between the Trump administration and Silicon Valley.
Senior Pentagon leadership and military commanders were given a 180-day deadline to remove all of Anthropic’s AI products from their systems, with the Pentagon arguing in a March 6 memo, signed by Davies, that the company’s technology poses an “unacceptable supply chain risk for use in all systems and networks.”
Pentagon’s use of Claude by the U.S. Central Command in Iran was first reported by The Wall Street Journal.
The Pentagon and Anthropic have engaged in a weeks-long public spat over the terms of use of its AI model. After talks over safety guardrails on its AI models faltered, the Trump administration directed federal agencies to halt using its technology and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth formally labeled the firm as a supply chain risk, a designation typically reserved for foreign adversaries.
The designation would bar defense contractors from using Anthropic’s products.
Anthropic sued the Trump administration, saying the label and President Trump’s order are “unprecedented and unlawful.”
When asked by Reed why the designation was imposed, Davies said, since the Pentagon is being sued by the Anthropic, “I won’t go into the deep details of it,” but added that the department reached out to congressional offices to provide a briefing on the decision.
Anthropic will ask a federal judge in California on Tuesday to temporarily pause the Pentagon’s designation.
Reed said it seems “odd” that the Pentagon would continue to use Anthropic’s products since the company’s designation.
“Does that strike you as odd,” the Senate Democrat asked Davies.
“Senator, at no time, in any way, will we interfere with the success, the lethality and the resilience of our war fighters, and for that reason, we’ve provided what we feel is a reasonable amount of time for those systems to be replaced,” she told Reed.
“With President Trump’s great leadership, we have a number of technology companies that have come to the table wanting to do business with us as the Department of War and across the U.S. government,” Davies added. “So we know that we’ve architected this appropriately in order to use competitive advantage as well.”
_source.movement_title: 美国国防部使用Anthropic AI模型引发争议
_source.movement_abstract: 美国国防部正在使用Anthropic的AI模型Claude，用于对抗伊朗的军事行动。该消息由国防部首席信息官Kirsten A. Davies在参议院听证会上确认。Davies表示，国防部已给予180天的时间让各机构移除Claude系统，并认为其技术存在供应链风险。尽管如此，国防部仍在使用该系统。Anthropic拒绝评论此事，并计划向加州联邦法院申请暂停国防部的指定。参议员Jack Reed质疑为何在指定后仍继续使用Claude，Davies强调不会影响军事行动的成功，并称此举是为了保持竞争优势。
_source.title: Anthropic’s Claude used by Pentagon in war with Iran, official confirms
_source.trans_cont:
五角大楼官员周二在参议院下属委员会听证会上证实，美国军方在与伊朗的持续战争中正在使用Anthropic的标志性AI模型Claude。五角大楼首席信息官Kirsten A. Davies向参议院武装部队委员会排名成员Jack Reed（民主党，罗德岛州）确认，五角大楼正在使用该AI模型作为“雷霆怒火行动”的一部分。  
“目前系统正在被使用，这也是我们提供合理时间期限以及移除Anthropic系统的例外程序的原因。”Davies在被Reed询问关于部门将该公司列为供应链风险时说道。  
当《赫尔利报》联系Anthropic时，该公司拒绝发表评论。  
Claude被五角大楼用于情报分析，但已成为特朗普政府与硅谷之间罕见的争议焦点。高级五角大楼领导层和军事指挥官被给予180天的期限，以移除所有Anthropic的AI产品。在3月6日由Davies签署的一份备忘录中，五角大楼称该公司技术对所有系统和网络的使用构成了“不可接受的供应链风险”。  
《华尔街日报》首次报道了五角大楼在美国中央司令部在伊朗使用Claude的情况。  
五角大楼与Anthropic就其AI模型的使用条款展开了一场持续数周的公开争执。在关于其AI模型安全护栏的讨论陷入僵局后，特朗普政府指示联邦机构暂停使用其技术，国防部长Pete Hegseth正式将该公司列为供应链风险，这一标签通常保留给外国对手。  
这一标签将阻止国防承包商使用Anthropic的产品。  
Anthropic起诉特朗普政府，称该标签和特朗普的命令是“前所未有的且非法的”。  
当Reed询问Davies为何做出这一标签时，她说：“由于Anthropic正在起诉五角大楼，我不会深入细节。”但补充说，五角大楼已联系国会办公室，就这一决定提供简报。  
Anthropic将于周二向加州的一名联邦法官申请暂停五角大楼的这一标签。  
Reed表示，五角大楼继续使用Anthropic产品似乎“奇怪”。  
“这让你觉得奇怪吗？”参议院民主党人问Davies。  
“参议员，我们任何时候都不会干扰我们战士的成功、致命性和韧性，因此，我们提供了我们认为合理的时间，让这些系统被替换。”她告诉Reed。  
“在特朗普总统卓越的领导下，我们有许多科技公司愿意与我们——国防部以及美国政府——开展业务。”Davies补充道。“因此，我们知道我们已经正确地构建了这一机制，以利用竞争优势。”
_source.trans_title: 官方确认，五角大楼在与伊朗的战争中使用了Anthropic的Claude模型。
_source.evidence: 文章核心描述的是美国五角大楼在针对伊朗的战争行动（Operation Epic Fury）中，实际部署并使用Anthropic公司的Claude AI模型进行情报分析。这属于认知域/信息域中具体的作战对抗行动及技术应用动向。虽然涉及AI技术（技术武器）和供应链风险政策（理论政策），但文章强调的是‘正在进行的战争中使用’这一具体行动事实，而非单纯的技术研发或政策发布。根据标签定义，‘相关领域的具体作战、对抗等行动及其动向’最符合[行动动向]。

_source.content:
For developers using AI, “vibe coding” right now comes down to babysitting every action or risking letting the model run unchecked. Anthropic
says
its latest update to Claude aims to eliminate that choice by letting the AI decide which actions are safe to take on its own — with some limits.
The move reflects a broader shift across the industry, as AI tools are increasingly designed to act without waiting for human approval. The challenge is balancing speed with control: too many guardrails slows things down, while too few can make systems risky and unpredictable. Anthropic’s new “auto mode,” now in research preview — meaning it’s available for testing but not yet a finished product — is its latest attempt to thread that needle.
Auto mode uses AI safeguards to review each action before it runs, checking for risky behavior the user didn’t request and for signs of prompt injection — a type of attack where malicious instructions are hidden in content that the AI is processing, causing it to take unintended actions. Any safe actions will proceed automatically, while the risky ones get blocked.
It’s essentially an extension of Claude Code’s existing “dangerously-skip-permissions” command, which hands all decision-making to the AI, but with a safety layer added on top.
The feature builds on a wave of autonomous coding tools from companies like GitHub and OpenAI, which can execute tasks on a developer’s behalf.  But it takes it a step further by shifting the decision of when to ask for permission from the user to the AI itself.
Anthropic hasn’t detailed the specific criteria its safety layer uses to distinguish safe actions from risky ones — something developers will likely want to understand better before adopting the feature widely. (TechCrunch has reached out to the company for more information on this front.)
Auto mode comes off the back of Anthropic’s launch of
Claude Code Review
, its automatic code reviewer designed to catch bugs before they hit the codebase, and
Dispatch for Cowork
, which allows users to send tasks to AI agents to handle work on their behalf.
Auto mode will roll out to Enterprise and API users in the coming days. The company says it currently only works with Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6, and recommends using the new feature in “isolated environments” — sandboxed setups that are kept separate from production systems, limiting the potential damage if something goes wrong.
_source.movement_title: Anthropic推出Claude自动模式，AI自主判断操作安全性
_source.movement_abstract: Anthropic最新更新了Claude，引入了‘自动模式’（Auto mode），允许AI自主判断哪些操作是安全的，从而减少开发者对AI行为的干预。这一模式旨在平衡速度与控制，防止AI执行危险操作，同时避免过度限制影响效率。自动模式通过AI安全机制审查每个操作，检测潜在风险行为和提示注入攻击。该功能是Claude Code现有‘危险跳过权限’命令的扩展，但增加了安全层。Anthropic未详细说明安全层的具体标准，开发者在广泛采用前可能需要更多了解。该功能将首先向企业用户和API用户推出，目前仅支持Claude Sonnet 4.6和Opus 4.6，并建议在隔离环境中使用以降低风险。
_source.title: Anthropic hands Claude Code more control, but keeps it on a leash
_source.trans_cont:
对于使用AI的开发者来说，目前“即兴编码”意味着要么不断监督每一步操作，要么冒险让模型自行运行。Anthropic表示，其最新更新的Claude旨在消除这种选择，让AI自行判断哪些操作是安全的——但有一定的限制。这一举措反映了整个行业更广泛的转变，随着AI工具越来越多地被设计为无需等待人类批准即可行动。挑战在于平衡速度与控制：过多的限制会减缓效率，而过少的限制则可能导致系统风险和不可预测性。Anthropic最新推出的“自动模式”目前处于研究预览阶段（意味着可供测试但尚未成为最终产品），是其最新尝试在两者之间找到平衡点。

自动模式利用AI安全机制在执行每项操作前进行审查，检查是否有用户未请求的高风险行为，以及是否存在提示注入攻击——一种恶意指令隐藏在AI处理内容中的攻击方式，导致AI执行未预期的操作。所有安全的操作将自动执行，而高风险操作则会被阻止。

这实际上是Claude Code现有“危险跳过权限”命令的扩展，该命令将所有决策权交给AI，但在此基础上增加了一层安全机制。

该功能建立在GitHub和OpenAI等公司推出的自主编码工具浪潮之上，这些工具可以代表开发者执行任务。但与之不同的是，它进一步将何时请求权限的决策权从用户转移到AI本身。

Anthropic尚未详细说明其安全层用于区分安全操作和高风险操作的具体标准——开发者在广泛采用该功能前很可能希望更好地了解这些标准。（TechCrunch已联系该公司获取更多相关信息。）

自动模式是在Anthropic推出Claude代码审查功能之后推出的，该功能旨在代码进入代码库前发现错误，以及协作任务分发功能，允许用户将任务发送给AI代理代表其处理工作。

自动模式将在未来几天内向企业用户和API用户推出。该公司表示，目前该功能仅适用于Claude Sonnet 4.6和Opus 4.6版本，并建议在“隔离环境”——即与生产系统隔离
