Summary
Critics say curbs affect soldiers' communication and family contact
Authorities push MAX app, prompting concerns of surveillance
Telegram says it is committed to user privacy, free speech
Feb 11 (Reuters) - Russia's curbs on the messaging app Telegram could affect battlefield communications as well as prevent soldiers from keeping in touch with their families, critics charged on Wednesday in an angry backlash against the latest restrictions.
The state communications watchdog, which began limiting voice and video calls via the app last August, said on Tuesday it would impose
further curbs
because of a lack of action by Telegram to counter criminal and terrorist activity.
Sign up
here.
Some users have complained that the app has been noticeably slower this week.
In short video appeals, three men purporting to be members of a Russian anti-drone unit said Telegram was vital to their work and urged the watchdog not to interfere with it.
Sergei Mironov, leader of a pro-Kremlin parliamentary party, posted a link to the appeals and said soldiers' lives could be at stake.
"The guys are shedding blood there, they need normal communication, and besides Telegram, they often have nothing," he wrote. "Don't deprive them of what helps them fight the enemy and keep themselves alive."
Speaking separately to reporters, Mironov berated those responsible for impairing the app's performance as "idiots".
Telegram is a hugely popular channel for public and private communications in Russia and has long been the dominant platform for information - and disinformation - about the war in Ukraine.
USEFUL TOOL FOR FRONTLINE SOLDIERS
Russian military commentators have frequently described it as an important communications tool for frontline soldiers, though the Kremlin said it was sceptical about this.
"I don't think it's possible to imagine frontline communications being provided via Telegram or some other messaging service," its spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, told reporters.
He referred further questions to the Ministry of Defence, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Vyacheslav Gladkov, governor of the western Belgorod region which has frequently been struck by Ukrainian drones, said he was worried the latest moves could make it harder to deliver important safety announcements to residents.
"I'm concerned that the slowdown could impact the delivery of operational information to you if the situation worsens," he said, urging people to register with the state's rival MAX messaging system.
Critics say the authorities have clamped down on foreign-based platforms, also including Meta's WhatsApp and Apple's FaceTime, as a way of forcing people to adopt MAX, which they fear will be used by the authorities as a surveillance tool. State media have dismissed such concerns.
Telegram's Russian-born founder Pavel Durov said the app would remain committed to protecting free speech and user privacy "no matter the pressure".
Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the communications watchdog was simply doing its job.
"We can only express regret here; there's nothing good about this, but the law must be followed," he said.
Additional reporting by Dmitry Antonov
Editing by Gareth Jones

_source.movement_abstract: 俄罗斯对Telegram的限制措施引发了对其影响战场通讯和士兵与家人联系的担忧。俄国家通讯监管机构自去年8月起限制该应用的语音和视频通话功能，并因Telegram未有效应对犯罪和恐怖活动而进一步收紧管控。部分用户反映应用速度变慢，一些自称属于反无人机单位的人员呼吁不要干预Telegram。俄议员谢尔盖·米罗诺夫表示，士兵需要正常通讯，Telegram是他们的重要工具。俄政府发言人表示，Telegram无法作为前线通讯工具，而地方官员则担心限制措施可能影响安全信息传递。批评者认为，此举旨在推动使用国家主导的MAX应用，后者可能被用于监控。Telegram创始人帕维尔·杜罗夫强调将继续保护用户隐私和言论自由。
_source.title: Russia's curbs on Telegram prompt concern about impact on soldiers

总结
批评人士说，限制措施影响了士兵的沟通和家庭联系。
当局推Max应用，引发监控担忧
Telegram表示，它致力于保护用户隐私和言论自由
2月11日（路透社）-俄罗斯对消息应用Telegram的限制可能会影响战场通信，并阻止士兵与家人保持联系，周三，批评人士对最新的限制表示愤怒。
国家通信监管机构于去年8月开始限制通过该应用程序进行语音和视频通话，并于周二表示将强制执行。
进一步遏制
因为没有通过电报采取行动打击犯罪和恐怖主义活动。
报名参加
在这里。
一些用户抱怨称，该应用程序本周明显变慢了。
在简短的视频呼吁中，三名自称是俄罗斯反无人机部队成员的男子表示，电报对他们的工作至关重要，并敦促监管机构不要干涉。
亲克里姆林宫的议会政党领导人谢尔盖·米罗诺夫（Sergei Mironov）发布了这些呼吁的链接，并表示士兵的生命可能危在旦夕。
他写道：“这些家伙在那里流血，他们需要正常的通讯，除了电报，他们往往一无所有。”“不要剥夺帮助他们与敌人战斗并让自己活下去的东西。”
在单独接受记者采访时，米罗诺夫斥责那些损害应用程序性能的人是“白痴”。
在俄罗斯，电报是一个非常受欢迎的公共和私人通信渠道，长期以来一直是有关乌克兰战争的信息和虚假信息的主要平台。
前线士兵的有用工具
俄罗斯军事评论员经常将其描述为前线士兵的重要通信工具，尽管克里姆林宫表示对此持怀疑态度。
其发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫（Dmitry Peskov）告诉记者：“我认为不可能想象通过电报或其他信息服务提供前线通信。”
他将进一步的问题交给了国防部，国防部没有立即回应置评请求。
乌克兰西部别尔哥罗德（Belgorod）地区的省长维亚切斯拉夫•格拉德科夫（Vyacheslav Gladkov）表示，他担心最新的举动可能会加大向居民发布重要安全公告的难度。
他说：“我担心，如果情况恶化，放缓可能会影响向您提供运营信息。”他敦促人们在该州的竞争对手Max Messaging System注册。
批评人士表示，当局已经取缔了外国平台，包括Meta的WhatsApp和苹果的FaceTime，以此迫使人们使用Max，他们担心当局会将其用作监视工具。官方媒体否认了这种担忧。
出生于俄罗斯的Telegram创始人帕维尔·杜罗夫（Pavel Durov）表示，“无论压力有多大”，该应用都将继续致力于保护言论自由和用户隐私。
克里姆林宫发言人佩斯科夫表示，通信监管机构只是在履行自己的职责。
他说：“我们只能在这里表示遗憾；这没有什么好的，但必须遵守法律。”

Generative AI is rapidly becoming a critical component of information warfare. A number of violent non-state actors are beginning to embrace this new technology, which has substantially altered the information ecosystem within the ongoing Sudanese Civil War.
The information sphere has been an important aspect of human warfare
. The ancient Sumerians built massive monuments of their kings destroying their enemies, the pharaohs of Egypt spread state iconography of the “
” to foment xenophobia among their subjects, and the
was inflamed by rumors of Muslim atrocities in Jerusalem. With the development of the Internet and artificial intelligence (AI), the information sphere has taken on an
in warfare.
Africa is uniquely vulnerable to AI-generated content. Coordinated disinformation campaigns
across the continent since 2022, fueled in large part by Russia and China. Russia’s former Wagner Group, now known as Africa Corps, has played a large role in providing AI-generated imagery to the continent, including countries such as
, Mali, and Niger.
As AI continues to reshape the world, a number of terrorist organizations, also known as Violent Non-State Actors (VNSAs),
to adapt and employ this new technology. Although a 2021 conference held by the United Nations concluded that there was no definitive evidence to suggest that terrorist organizations had yet successfully employed AI, the global situation has rapidly changed since then. Organizations such as the Islamic State (IS) have employed open-source AI tools such as ChatGPT to enhance propaganda campaigns. After the March 2024 attack on a concert hall in Russia, IS affiliates widely disseminated AI-created propaganda videos across social media in a bid to gain new recruits; other uses include deepfake audio recordings of IS leaders that are
into multiple languages and propagated across the internet. Other examples include the use of
of wounded or dying infants and children in the Gaza conflict. However, for the most part, the use of AI beyond propaganda and recruitment appears to be largely “
”.
Unfortunately, this will likely not last long. The potential capabilities that AI could provide, from widespread social engineering to autonomous drones to potential chemical and biological weapons development, could
the impact of small, decentralized, and resource-poor VNSAs. Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal Muslimin (JNIM) may already be employing offline
to enhance drone strikes across sub-Saharan Africa; IS supporters have already expressed
in pursuing further uses of AI;
, such as Al-Qaeda, Hezbollah, and Hamas, are also experimenting with the use of AI. Most notably, a VSNA in Sudan has already begun the widespread use of generative AI in warfare – one of the
in history.
On 15 April 2023, following a prolonged stalemate after the 2019 ouster of President Omar Al-Bashir, Sudan’s fragile government collapsed into
. The two main actors in this conflict are the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), led by General Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan, and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary force led by General Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, better known as “Hemedti”. This conflict – complicated by regional loyalties, ethnic tensions, and outside interference – has been defined by a
affecting millions, brutal fighting, the reported deployment of
by the SAF, the
of humanitarian aid, and ethnic cleansing. In just one example, when the RSF captured the city of El Fasher on 26 October 2025 after a 500-day long siege, the paramilitary slaughtered an estimated
.
Despite its origins as a
employed by the Sudanese state for counterinsurgency,  the RSF has been quick to embrace new technologies and battlefield strategies, influenced by contacts with the
and a maze of other international commercial and military connections. The RSF has widely deployed
, including long-distance
, and even used precision drones as tools of assassination. In one notable event, the RSF attempted to take al-Burhan’s life in 2024 at a graduation ceremony with a
.
Disinformation has a long history in Sudan, and can be divided into several distinct phases. During the al-Bashir regime from 1989-2019, disinformation was widely employed as state propaganda designed to both fuel ethnic violence. The Janjaweed militia, the precursors of the RSF, were emboldened by
to commit mass atrocities during the infamous Darfur genocide. The regime also focused on targeting dissent; the
, founded in 2011, was particularly effective as a form of online surveillance used to target activists and suppress information. After the fall of al-Bashir’s government, both the SAF and the RSF often worked together to spread disinformation. Tactics included setting up fake protests to flush out dissenters, the mass use of bots to ban anti-government rhetoric online, and infiltrating anti-government message boards. These methods were remarkably sophisticated, and both sides used outside companies – including an Egyptian firm that provided a troll farm – to secure a grip on online discourse. With the outbreak of war, these two “
” are suddenly at odds, causing an increasingly violent war of information as both sides seek to “
”.
The RSF has proven particularly adept at
, with a significant portion of its budget going toward media and public relations. Examples include the RSF circulating pictures of fighters distributing medical aid after they were accused of slaughtering hundreds of patients at a hospital in el-Fasher, and their widespread use of brutal and violent rhetoric – one viral video shows a female RSF fighter calling for other RSF soldiers to rape women to “
”. Social media is essential to this strategy,
including WhatsApp, Facebook, TikTok, and Clubhouse. Both sides have also employed social media influencers – often acting under a veneer of neutrality while reinforcing certain points – to aid in disinformation goals.
Notably, the RSF appears to be more focused on an
; most of their posts are in English, and Hemedti has placed a strong emphasis on visiting international leaders. The paramilitary also has a strong preference for covering up its many atrocities and casting itself as a pro-democracy force fighting against an oppressive regime.
The RSF is also skilled at coordinated online campaigns – after the RSF’s capture of Merowe Airport, dozens of accounts on X (formerly Twitter) suddenly posted identical videos of the victorious troops, all within minutes of one another. This synchronized campaign falsely gave the impression of
for the paramilitary. Both sides have used similar tactics of flooding social media with coordinated waves of imagery and messages to create the illusion of popular support.
Information operations have long been identified as a
, particularly in insurgencies. A number of recent publications have noted the military potential of generative AI. AI-generated images may be employed for deception, to
among the enemy, to degrade the information sphere and manipulate public perception, and potentially
on an unprecedented scale. These techniques are already being employed in Sudan.
While disinformation has a long history in Sudan, the use of generative AI is a new phenomenon. Like many other VSNAs, the RSF has been quick to embrace the use of AI. As early as October 2023, an RSF-associated source released a campaign of AI-generated recordings of the former President al-Bashir. These clips, released as so-called “
” on a TikTok channel called ‘The Voice of Sudan’, were generated from a mixture of old audio files and news reports, and featured al-Bashir criticizing the SAF’s leader, al-Burhan. This caused a number of al-Bashir supporters to renege on their support of the SAF. This incident is particularly notable because it is “one of the first documented cases of generative AI being used as a
.” Other alleged “
” of politicians criticizing the SAF and discussing the possibility of joining the RSF have further sown confusion in the public sphere.
Generative AI has also been used to specifically target American interests in the region. In April 2023, another “
” was released, claiming to be from the U.S. Ambassador John Godfrey. In the recording, an AI-generated clone of Godfrey’s voice outlines a plan to increase secularism within Sudan. While the exact origin of the clip remains unknown, it was likely created by Islamist-linked networks to undermine Western influence within the region.
In the following months, RSF and RSF-affiliated sources continued to employ generative AI. In March 2024, another audio file that claimed to be a recording of al-Burhan ordering the mass killing of civilians was released online. The recording was viewed over 230,000 times, and so popular that it was shared by
. The next month, an AI-generated image of a building in Al-Jazeera University, allegedly bombed by the SAF, went viral on Facebook. Again, it was shared by many political and public figures across Sudan.
Interestingly, the SAF has attempted to take advantage of the RSF’s use of AI; at one point, the military claimed that all the recordings of Hemedti
and that the paramilitary leader was actually dead. While these accusations were patently untrue, they are yet another example of the constant disinformation war waged by both sides.
The SAF also appears to have begun to employ AI images; after the recent fall of el-Fasher, a number of
claiming to be from the city went viral. In one, a mother and her children are cowering in fear, supposedly in front of two RSF troops about to execute her; in another, an elderly woman stares directly into the camera as she sobs. Another video shows a crowd fleeing a burning village, as a woman calls out, “RSF has entered our neighborhood and
.” Other videos include scenes of begging Sudanese children – the most popular of these has received nearly 40 million views on TikTok. While these videos are highly convincing, fact-checkers have determined that they are false.  The SAF has even followed the RSF’s lead in AI-generated recordings of political leaders; one pro-SAF group called ‘Sea and River’ has circulated videos of
claiming to support the RSF, further inflaming ethnic tensions.
At the start of 2024,
of the Sudanese population had internet access. With such limited access to the online information sphere, it initially seems counterintuitive that the RSF would invest so heavily in AI-generated content.
However, Sudan is effectively in an
. Independent Sudanese media has largely collapsed in the past years, with hundreds of journalists forced to flee the country. The online presence of the populace is now increasingly split between supporters of the RSF and the SAF, further fueling ethnic tensions and sectarian violence. Hashtags such as “Truce is treason” have further limited any option for peaceful dissent in the increasingly radicalized environment. The areas that do have internet access are heavily restricted – for example, settlements under the RSF’s control may be able to gain internet access by using communal Starlink devices. However, these devices require an hourly fee and are constantly surveilled by RSF soldiers, allowing for
. Internet shutdowns are common, making the internet closer to a “
” that the paramilitary is able to shut off at will.
With the lack of any reliable media, tightly regulated internet access, and the chaos of war, rumors now act as the primary source of information in the collapsing public sphere. Both the RSF and the SAF are well aware of this and have specifically designed their disinformation to
through word-of-mouth. Through this method, digital warfare, even when deployed in a limited space,
to physical violence and further radicalized the population.
Unlike Russia and China, the
currently have a well-defined strategy regarding information warfare, and has traditionally followed a more defensive posture using such tactics. However, a number of US agencies are currently pursuing the use of AI to identify and counter hostile information campaigns. In 2023, the National Defense Authorization Act set aside $20 billion for AI research and development. The current Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, has also
the increased use of AI in the Department of War.
This increased research and development of AI may offer a potential counter to the enemy use of generative AI; as we have shown, it is already being deployed to
American interests within Sudan. It is almost certain that this tool will be used against American interests even more in the future.
While information warfare is as old as conflict itself, the use of generative AI is a completely new phenomenon. VSNAs across the world are quickly embracing this new technology, which has already been widely deployed within the information sphere of the ongoing Sudanese Civil War. The potential that this technology has to influence a populace, even in an environment with minimal internet access, should not be underestimated.
Generative AI has already been directly used to counteract American interests in Sudan. This threat will likely only exponentially increase in the future; American policy will need to adapt to counter the use of generative AI by geopolitical rivals.

_source.movement_abstract: 生成式人工智能正迅速成为信息战的关键组成部分。多个暴力非国家行为体（VNSAs）开始采用这一新技术，显著改变了苏丹内战等冲突的信息生态。信息领域在战争中一直扮演重要角色，从古代美索不达米亚的纪念碑到埃及法老的国家图腾，再到耶路撒冷的谣言传播，信息战贯穿历史。随着互联网和人工智能的发展，信息战的形态发生了巨大变化。非洲尤其容易受到AI生成内容的影响，自2022年以来，俄罗斯和中国主导的虚假信息活动在非洲大陆广泛展开。恐怖组织如“伊斯兰国”（IS）已使用开源AI工具如ChatGPT增强宣传，并在2024年俄罗斯音乐会袭击后广泛传播AI生成的宣传视频。AI在宣传和招募中的应用已初见成效，但其在其他领域的潜力仍待挖掘。苏丹内战中，苏丹武装部队（SAF）与快速支援部队（RSF）之间的冲突尤为复杂，涉及地区忠诚、民族紧张和外部干预，导致大规模流离失所、暴力冲突和人道主义危机。RSF已迅速采用新技术和战术，包括无人机和精准打击。虚假信息在苏丹历史上长期存在，从巴希尔政权时期的民族暴力到当前双方的网络操控，信息战已成为冲突的重要组成部分。

.古代苏美尔人建造了巨大的纪念碑，纪念他们的国王消灭敌人，埃及法老传播了国家肖像。
在他们的臣民中煽动排外情绪，
被穆斯林在耶路撒冷暴行的谣言所激怒。随着互联网和人工智能（AI）的发展，信息领域呈现出一种
在战争中。
非洲特别容易受到人工智能生成内容的影响。协调一致的假情报活动
自2022年以来，在很大程度上是由俄罗斯和中国推动的。俄罗斯的前瓦格纳集团（Wagner Group），即现在的非洲军团（Africa Corps），在向非洲大陆提供人工智能生成的图像方面发挥了很大作用，包括
马里和尼日尔。
随着人工智能继续重塑世界，一些恐怖组织，也被称为暴力非国家行为者（VNSA），

转换成多种语言并在互联网上传播。其他示例包括使用
在加沙冲突中受伤或垂死的婴儿和儿童。然而，在大多数情况下，除了宣传和招募之外，人工智能的使用似乎在很大程度上
".
不幸的是，这可能不会持续太久。从广泛的社会工程到自主无人机，再到潜在的化学和生物武器开发，人工智能可以提供的潜在能力可以

在整个撒哈拉以南非洲地区加强无人机打击；IS的支持者已经表示
进一步利用人工智能；
如基地组织、真主党和哈马斯，也在尝试使用人工智能。最值得注意的是，苏丹的VSNA已经开始在战争中广泛使用生成AI—
在历史上。
2023年4月15日，在2019年奥马尔·巴希尔总统下台后的长期僵局之后，苏丹脆弱的政府崩溃了

由SAF，
人道主义援助和种族清洗。仅举一例，当无国界记者组织在长达500天的围困后于2025年10月26日占领法希尔市时，准军事组织估计屠杀了
.
尽管它起源于
被苏丹政府雇佣来镇压叛乱，无国界记者组织已经迅速接受了新技术和战场战略，受到与苏丹政府接触的影响。
以及错综复杂的其他国际商业和军事联系。RSF已广泛部署
，包括长途
甚至使用精确无人机作为暗杀工具。在一个值得注意的事件中，无国界记者组织试图在2024年的毕业典礼上夺走阿尔布尔汉的生命。
.
虚假信息在苏丹有很长的历史，可以分为几个不同的阶段。在1989-2019年巴希尔政权期间，虚假信息被广泛用作国家宣传，旨在助长种族暴力。金戈威德民兵是无国界记者组织的前身，
在臭名昭著的达尔富尔种族灭绝期间犯下大规模暴行。该政权还侧重于针对持不同政见者；那

事实证明，RSF特别擅长

".社交媒体对这一战略至关重要。
包括WhatsApp、Facebook、TikTok和Clubhouse.双方还雇佣了社交媒体影响者——通常在中立的外表下行事，同时强化某些观点——来帮助实现虚假信息的目标。
值得注意的是，RSF似乎更侧重于
;他们的大部分帖子都是英文的，赫梅蒂非常重视来访的国际领导人。准军事部队还强烈倾向于掩盖其许多暴行，并将自己塑造成一支反对压迫政权的亲民主力量。
无国界记者组织还擅长协调在线活动——在无国界记者组织占领麦洛维机场后，X（前身为Twitter）上的数十个账户突然发布了胜利部队的相同视频，所有视频都在几分钟内相继发布。这种同步运动错误地给人一种印象
为准军事组织。双方都使用了类似的策略，在社交媒体上发布大量协调一致的图片和信息，以制造民众支持的假象。
长期以来，信息作战一直被视为
特别是在叛乱中。最近的一些出版物已经注意到了生成人工智能的军事潜力。AI生成的图像可用于欺骗，以
在敌人之间，降低信息领域和操纵公众的看法，并有可能
规模空前。这些技术已经在苏丹使用。
虽然虚假信息在苏丹有着悠久的历史，但生成人工智能的使用是一个新现象。与许多其他VSNA一样，RSF很快就接受了人工智能的使用。早在2023年10月，一个与RSF有关的消息来源就发布了一系列人工智能生成的前总统巴希尔的录音。这些剪辑，作为所谓的释放
在一个名为“苏丹之声”的TikTok频道上，由旧的音频文件和新闻报道混合而成，并以巴希尔批评苏丹武装部队领导人布尔汉为特色。这导致巴希尔的一些支持者背弃了对苏丹武装部队的支持。这一事件尤其值得注意，因为它是首批记录在案的生成人工智能被用作
."其他指称
政客们批评苏丹武装部队和讨论加入无国界记者组织的可能性，进一步在公共领域造成混乱。
生成人工智能也被用来专门针对美国在该地区的利益。2023年4月，另一个
被释放，声称是来自美国大使约翰·戈弗雷。在录音中，人工智能生成的戈弗雷声音的克隆概述了一项在苏丹增加世俗主义的计划。虽然这段视频的确切来源尚不清楚，但它很可能是由与伊斯兰主义者有联系的网络制作的，目的是削弱西方在该地区的影响力。
在接下来的几个月里，RSF和RSF附属来源继续使用生成人工智能。2024年3月，另一份声称是al-Burhan下令大规模杀害平民的录音文件在网上发布。这段录音被观看了230，000多次，非常受欢迎，以至于被
.第二个月，一张人工智能生成的据称被苏丹武装部队炸毁的半岛大学大楼的图片在Facebook上疯传。苏丹各地的许多政治和公众人物再次分享了这一点。
有趣的是，苏丹武装部队试图利用无国界记者组织对人工智能的使用。军方一度声称赫梅蒂的所有录音
准军事领导人实际上已经死了。虽然这些指控显然是不真实的，但它们是双方不断发动假情报战的又一个例子。
SAF似乎也开始使用AI图像；在法希尔最近陷落后，一些
声称来自这个城市的人在网上疯传。在一张照片中，一位母亲和她的孩子在恐惧中畏缩，据说是在两名即将处决她的RSF士兵面前。在另一张照片中，一位老年妇女正对着镜头啜泣。另一段视频显示，一群人正在逃离燃烧的村庄，一名妇女大声喊道：无国界记者已经进入我们的社区，
."其他视频包括苏丹儿童乞讨的场景——其中最受欢迎的视频在TikTok上获得了近4000万次观看。虽然这些视频很有说服力，但事实核查人员已经确定它们是假的。苏丹武装部队甚至效仿无国界记者组织的做法，由人工智能制作政治领导人的录音。一个名为“海洋和河流”的亲苏丹武装部队团体传播了以下视频
声称支持无国界记者组织，进一步加剧了种族紧张局势。
在2024年初，
的苏丹人可以上网。在对在线信息领域的访问如此有限的情况下，RSF在人工智能生成的内容上投入如此之多，最初似乎是违反直觉的。
然而，苏丹实际上处于
.独立的苏丹媒体在过去几年中基本崩溃，数百名记者被迫逃离该国。民众在网上的存在现在越来越分裂为无国界记者组织和苏丹武装部队的支持者，进一步加剧了种族紧张局势和宗派暴力。“休战即叛国”等话题标签进一步限制了在日益激进的环境中和平表达异议的任何选择。有互联网接入的地区受到严格限制——例如，无国界记者组织控制下的定居点可以通过使用公共星链设备获得互联网接入。然而，这些设备需要按小时收费，并由RSF士兵不断监视，允许
.互联网关闭是常见的，使互联网更接近
准军事部队可以随意关闭。
由于缺乏任何可靠的媒体，严格管制的互联网接入，以及战争的混乱，谣言现在成为崩溃的公共领域的主要信息来源。无国界记者组织和苏丹武装部队都很清楚这一点，并专门设计了他们的假情报
通过口碑。通过这种方法，数字化战争即使部署在有限的空间内，
身体暴力并进一步使人们变得激进。
与俄罗斯和中国不同，
目前有一个关于信息战的明确战略，并且传统上遵循使用这种战术的更具防御性的态势。然而，一些美国机构目前正在寻求使用人工智能来识别和对抗敌对的信息活动。2023年，《国防授权法案》拨出200亿美元用于人工智能研发。现任战争部长皮特·赫格塞斯也
战争部门越来越多地使用人工智能。
人工智能研究和开发的增加可能会为敌人使用生成人工智能提供一种潜在的对抗。正如我们所展示的，它已经被部署到
美国在苏丹的利益。几乎可以肯定，这一工具今后将更多地被用来损害美国的利益。
虽然信息战和冲突本身一样古老，但生成人工智能的使用是一个全新的现象。世界各地的VSNA正在迅速采用这一新技术，该技术已经在正在进行的苏丹内战的信息领域广泛部署。即使在互联网接入极少的环境中，也不应低估这项技术影响民众的潜力。
生成人工智能已经被直接用于对抗美国在苏丹的利益。这种威胁在未来可能只会呈指数级增长。美国的政策将需要调整，以对抗地缘政治对手对生成人工智能的使用。
_source.trans_title: 战争中的暴力非国家行为者和生成性人工智能：RSF和苏丹内战
_source.evidence: 文章主要描述了苏丹内战中，非国家行为体（如RSF和SAF）利用生成式AI（Generative AI）进行信息战、制造虚假视频和音频（Deepfake）以进行舆论攻击和招募的具体行动。虽然文中提到了俄罗斯和中国的AI虚假信息活动作为背景，但核心事件是苏丹冲突中的具体对抗行动（舆论战、虚假信息传播），且这些行动针对的是美国利益（如伪造美国大使言论），而非针对中国大陆的特定敌情事件。因此，该文章属于认知域中的具体对抗行动，最符合[行动动向]标签。

_source.content:
One of this year’s Oscar nominees for documentary filmmaking, “Mr. Nobody Against Putin,” provides a unique window into the mindset that Vladimir Putin’s Russia has generated and aggressively seeks to disseminate. It shows how the war against Ukraine is being presented to and digested by ordinary, small-town Russians.
The film was made by a Russian schoolteacher named Pavel Talankin working at the main school in Karabash, an industrial town of some 10,000 nestled in the Ural mountains.
The project started out as a mandated recording on how the school was complying with the new wartime program and curricular requirements imposed by Moscow, which turned into daily mandates for “patriotic” lessons about the army, the war and the need to mobilize society and keep it united. But after a while, Talankin realized that what he was recording was an important reveal of what Russia was doing to itself — not to mention to Ukraine — and he took his footage to the West.
The film covers the period between the start of Russia’s invasion in February 2022 and the summer of 2024. It includes clips of statements by Putin and other public officials on state-owned and controlled Russian television.
Putin announces on Feb. 24, 2022 that he has decided to initiate a “special military operation” out of “friendship and mutual aid” to the Donetsk and Luhansk “Peoples Republics.” Almost immediately thereafter, Moscow informs the school in Karabash that it must adopt changes to its daily schedule involving the content of classroom lessons, songs to be sung, the adoption of military drill marching and so on.
Each school day must begin with a military style flag presentation by the students, whose school appears to include primary and middle school grades. Children in the lower grades are trained to goose step in a rectangle around the main hallway, and they have to learn to memorize war poems in order “to help the army.”
Teachers must read prepared scripts to their students about Crimea wanting to join Russia and about how the special military operation is to demilitarize and denazify Ukraine, where, purportedly, decisions are made by “radicals, nationalists and neo-Nazis.” Some teachers struggle to pronounce the Russian words for “demilitarize” and “denazify,” and videos of their lessons must therefore be re-recorded.
Public statements on state-owned television about the “special military operation” include: “We shouldn’t kill them out of hate. We must kill them out of love, love for our children”;  “This operation is about revenge — we strike precisely for revenge;” and “This is a manifestation of our hate, a totally holy hate.”
A general bedecked with medals from his chest to his knees proclaims that “If we need to turn Kyiv into ruins and put our flag on top of these ruins, then this must be done.” And a local Russian Orthodox priest at Karabash’s commemoration of the “Great Patriotic War” (World War II) intones to the students gathered there, “You, young people, will have to carry the banner of absolute victory over evil.”
On the centennial of the founding of Lenin’s Young Pioneers, Putin unveils the creation of a new children’s patriotic Russian movement that he will chair personally. Three members of the mercenary Wagner Group are sent to Karabash to make a presentation to students involving land mines, rifles and bullet-proof vests, and they later sponsor a grenade throwing contest for the younger children.
One teacher whose lessons do not need to be re-recorded is the history teacher, Pavel Abdulmanov. He presents the government’s propaganda for the students with enthusiasm, sprinkling his lectures with tidbits of nonsense about how gas is so expensive in France and the rest of Europe that the French will soon have to revert to riding horses. He tells them that the “tiny island” of England killed its own people during World War II, that Russia “could destroy Ukraine in a couple of days,” and there are demonstrations in the U.S. in support of Russia.
During an interview with Talankin, Abdulmanov is asked which figures in Russian history he most admires, and he replies with Lavrentiy Beria, Viktor Abakumov and Pavel Sudoplatov, all high officials in Stalin’s secret police. The first two had the blood of multitudes on their hands. Sudoplatov was more specialized: He was Stalin’s special assassin for overseas political murders.
The film then records a citywide ceremony celebrating the school’s favorite teacher, to give him the keys to a new luxury apartment in the middle of town. The teacher chosen is none other than Abdulmanov.
Talankin, the quiet and unassuming teacher turned filmmaker, is its self-titled “Mr. Nobody.” His movie, now available on several streaming services, is an intentional reveal about today’s Russia, but it may also reveal that our administration’s approach to Russia’s war against Ukraine is, to put it diplomatically, uninformed.
That war is not in any sense analogous to disputes about real estate or development. The movie also exposes that earlier claims that the war had something to do with NATO enlargement were altogether delusional.
Bohdan Vitvitsky is a retired federal prosecutor and a former U.S. diplomat.
_source.movement_title: 纪录片揭示俄罗斯战争宣传与教育现实
_source.movement_abstract: 纪录片《无人先生对抗普京》由俄罗斯教师帕维尔·塔兰金拍摄，记录了2022年俄乌战争爆发后，俄罗斯学校如何按照莫斯科的指示进行爱国主义教育。影片展示了学生每天进行军事化仪式、学习战争诗歌、接受关于乌克兰‘去军事化’和‘去纳粹化’的宣传等内容。影片还呈现了普京等官员的讲话，以及教师们在教学中面临的挑战。影片揭示了俄罗斯社会对战争的极端态度和宣传手段，同时批评了西方对俄战争的误解。塔兰金将影片带到西方，希望通过纪录片揭示俄罗斯的现状及其对乌克兰的影响。
_source.title: Putin’s classroom propaganda includes goose steps and grenades
_source.trans_cont:
今年获得奥斯卡最佳纪录片提名的影片之一《无人反对普京先生》（Mr.Nobody Against Putin）提供了一个独特的窗口，让人们得以了解弗拉基米尔·普京（Vladimir Putin）领导下的俄罗斯所产生并积极寻求传播的心态。它展示了对乌克兰的战争是如何被普通的小城镇俄罗斯人所接受和消化的。
这部电影是由一位名叫帕维尔·塔兰金（Pavel Talankin）的俄罗斯教师拍摄的，他在卡拉巴什（Karabash）的主要学校工作，卡拉巴什是一个坐落在乌拉尔山脉的工业城镇，人口约1万。
该项目最初是一项关于学校如何遵守新的战时计划和莫斯科规定的课程要求的强制性记录，后来变成了关于军队、战争以及动员社会并保持团结的“爱国”课程的日常任务。但过了一段时间，塔兰金意识到，他所记录的是俄罗斯对自己所做的重要揭露——更不用说对乌克兰了——于是他把自己的录像带到了西方。
这部电影涵盖了从2022年2月俄罗斯开始入侵到2024年夏天这段时间。其中包括普京和其他政府官员在国有和控股的俄罗斯电视台发表的声明片段。
普京于2022年2月24日宣布，出于对顿涅茨克和卢甘斯克“人民共和国”的“友谊和互助”，他决定发起“特别军事行动”。此后，莫斯科几乎立即通知卡拉巴什的学校，它必须改变其日常时间表，包括课堂内容、要唱的歌曲、采用军事操练、行军等。
学校的每一天都必须以学生展示军旗开始，他们的学校似乎包括小学和中学年级。低年级的孩子们被训练在主走廊周围的长方形里走正步，为了“帮助军队”，他们必须学会背诵战争诗。
教师必须向学生宣读事先准备好的讲稿，内容是克里米亚想要加入俄罗斯，以及特别军事行动是如何使乌克兰非军事化和非纳粹化的，据称，乌克兰的决定是由“激进分子、民族主义者和新纳粹分子”做出的。一些教师很难说出“非军事化”和“非纳粹化”的俄语单词，因此他们的课程视频必须重新录制。
国有电视台关于“特别军事行动”的公开声明包括："我们不应该出于仇恨而杀害他们。出于爱，出于对我们孩子的爱，我们必须杀死他们。“这次行动是为了复仇——我们打击正是为了复仇；” “这是我们仇恨的表现，一种完全神圣的仇恨。”
一位从胸前到膝盖都挂满勋章的将军宣称，“如果我们需要把基辅变成废墟，并在这些废墟上插上我们的旗帜，那么就必须这样做。”一名当地的俄罗斯东正教牧师参加了卡拉巴什的“伟大卫国战争”纪念活动。（第二次世界大战）向聚集在那里的学生们吟诵道：“你们，年轻人，必须扛起绝对战胜邪恶的旗帜。”
在列宁青年先锋队成立一百周年之际，普京宣布成立一个新的俄罗斯儿童爱国运动，他将亲自主持该运动。三名雇佣军瓦格纳集团成员被派往卡拉巴什，向学生展示地雷、步枪和防弹背心，随后他们为年幼儿童举办手榴弹投掷比赛。
历史教师帕维尔·阿卜杜勒马诺夫（Pavel Abdulmanov）的课程不需要重新录制。他热情地向学生们展示了政府的宣传，在演讲中穿插了一些胡言乱语，比如法国和欧洲其他国家的天然气价格如此昂贵，以至于法国人很快将不得不重新骑马。他告诉他们，英国这个“小岛”在二战期间杀害了自己的人民，俄罗斯“可以在几天内摧毁乌克兰”，美国也有支持俄罗斯的示威活动。
在塔兰金的一次采访中，阿卜杜勒马诺夫被问到他最崇拜俄罗斯历史上的哪些人物，他回答说是拉夫连季·贝利亚、维克托·阿巴库莫夫和帕维尔·苏多普拉托夫，他们都是斯大林秘密警察的高级官员。前两个人手上沾满了群众的鲜血。苏多普拉托夫更专业：他是斯大林海外政治谋杀的特别杀手。
然后，影片记录了一场全市范围的仪式，庆祝学校最受欢迎的老师，给他市中心一套新的豪华公寓的钥匙。被选中的老师不是别人，正是阿卜杜曼诺夫。
安静而谦逊的教师出身的电影制作人塔兰金（Talankin）自称“无名小卒”。他的电影，现在可以在几个流媒体服务上观看，是对当今俄罗斯的有意揭露，但它也可能揭示我们的政府对俄罗斯对乌克兰战争的做法，用外交的话说，是不知情的。
这场战争在任何意义上都不类似于关于房地产或开发的争端。这部电影还揭露了早些时候关于战争与北约东扩有关的说法完全是妄想。
博赫丹·维特维茨基是一名退休的联邦检察官和前美国外交官。
_source.trans_title: 普京的课堂宣传包括正步和手榴弹。
_source.evidence: 文章核心内容是关于一部纪录片《无名先生对抗普京》（Mr. Nobody Against Putin），该纪录片揭露了俄罗斯在乌克兰战争背景下，通过教育系统（学校课程、教师授课、学生军训等）对民众进行大规模认知操控和宣传洗脑的具体行动。文中详细描述了俄罗斯政府强制学校修改课程、灌输战争理由（如“去纳粹化”）、组织军事化训练（如“鹅步”、投掷手榴弹）以及利用媒体和教师传播仇恨言论等具体行为。这属于典型的认知域对抗行动，即通过舆论、教育和宣传手段进行的认知攻击和操控。虽然涉及教育政策（理论政策）和军事训练（演习演训），但其核心在于描述俄罗斯针对乌克兰及国际社会发起的、具体的认知域作战行动和动向，而非单纯的国内政策发布或常规军事演习。因此，最匹配的标签是[行动动向]。

OpenAI announced Monday that it is bringing a custom version of ChatGPT to the Pentagon’s AI platform.
It joins other major AI companies, including Google and Elon Musk’s xAI, on the Defense Department’s platform GenAI.mil.
The custom ChatGPT will run on “authorized government cloud infrastructure with built-in safety controls and protections” and is approved for unclassified work, OpenAI said.
“We believe the people responsible for defending the country should have access to the best tools available, and it is important for the United States and other democratic countries to understand how, with the proper safeguards, AI can help protect people, deter adversaries, and prevent future conflict,” the company said in a press release.
OpenAI previously received a contract for up to $200 million with the Defense Department’s Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office last July as the agency sought to boost its AI adoption. Anthropic, Google and xAI also scored similar contracts.
Anthropic has reportedly clashed with the Pentagon in recent months over restrictions barring its AI model Claude from being used for domestic surveillance or autonomous lethal operations.
OpenAI said in Monday’s announcement that its models “incorporate safeguards at the model and platform level” and support “all lawful uses.”
_source.movement_title: OpenAI将定制版ChatGPT引入美军AI平台
_source.movement_abstract: OpenAI宣布将其定制版ChatGPT引入美国国防部的AI平台GenAI.mil，与其他主要AI公司如谷歌和xAI一同加入。该定制版ChatGPT将在授权政府云基础设施上运行，并具备内置安全控制和保护措施，适用于非机密工作。OpenAI表示，应让负责国防的人拥有最佳工具，并强调在适当保障下，AI可帮助保护人民、威慑对手并防止未来冲突。此前，OpenAI已与国防部签订价值达2亿美元的合同，推动AI应用。Anthropic、谷歌和xAI也获得了类似合同。Anthropic近期因AI模型Claude不得用于国内监控或自主致命行动与国防部发生冲突。OpenAI表示其模型在模型和平台层面均包含保障措施，支持所有合法用途。
_source.title: OpenAI opening ChatGPT access to Pentagon
_source.trans_cont:
OpenAI周一宣布，它将为五角大楼的人工智能平台带来一个定制版本的ChatGPT.
它加入了其他主要的人工智能公司，包括谷歌和埃隆·马斯克的XAI，在国防部的Genai.mil平台上。
OpenAI表示，定制的ChatGPT将在“具有内置安全控制和保护的授权政府云基础设施”上运行，并被批准用于非机密工作。
该公司在一份新闻稿中表示：“我们认为，负责保卫国家的人应该能够获得最好的工具，对于美国和其他民主国家来说，重要的是要了解如何在适当的保障措施下，人工智能可以帮助保护人民，威慑对手，并防止未来的冲突。”
去年7月，OpenAI曾与国防部首席数字和人工智能办公室签订了一份高达2亿美元的合同，该机构寻求促进其人工智能的应用。Anthropic、Google和Xai也获得了类似的合同。
据报道，Anthropic在最近几个月与五角大楼发生冲突，原因是禁止其人工智能模型Claude用于国内监视或自主致命行动。
OpenAI在周一的声明中表示，其模型“包含模型和平台级别的安全措施”，并支持“所有合法用途”。
_source.trans_title: OpenAI开放ChatGPT访问五角大楼
_source.evidence: 文章核心内容是OpenAI、Google等美国科技公司向美国国防部（五角大楼）提供定制化AI模型（ChatGPT等），用于提升其AI作战能力和防御能力。这属于认知域中关于'技术武器化'或'AI技术应用于军事对抗'的范畴。虽然涉及合同签署，但核心在于AI技术作为工具/武器被引入军事领域，而非单纯的机构成立（力量发展）或政策发布（理论政策）。根据定义，'技术武器'涵盖'相关领域的技术发展为武器的行动、探索、尝试（如AI武器化...）'，因此最匹配。

(中央社記者李雅雯台北11日電)大陸委員會(陸委會)今天發布2025年第4季中國大陸情勢報告重點摘要。官方統計顯示,台灣對陸投資持續縮減,2025年赴陸直接投資金額年減59%;核准陸資來台投資金額年減65.4%。
報告指出,中國大陸去年經濟成長率達5%,不過成長動能分化明顯,房市蕭條加劇、外國直接投資(FDI)持續放緩、通貨緊縮陰霾未散。綜整22家國際組織、智庫與法人預測,中國大陸今年經濟成長率在4.0%至4.8%間,平均為4.5%。
在兩岸經貿方面,台灣對陸投資持續縮減,2025年赴陸直接投資金額年減59%;核准陸資來台投資金額年減65.4%。
中國大陸2025年下半年度社會抗爭大量增加,研判主要原因在於經濟成長趨緩、青年失業日趨嚴重,加上地方政府財政困難導致維穩經費不足,大量失業農民工返鄉、滯鄉可能威脅基層治理的穩定。
中國大陸依循慣例在新年發表「新年賀詞」、「新年寄語」,總結過去一年成果外,也展望來年的對台工作。中國大陸領導人習近平在去年12月31日的新年賀詞強調「兩岸同胞血濃於水,祖國統一的歷史大勢不可阻擋」。
中共持續對台進行「法律戰」。中國大陸國台辦將內政部長劉世芳、教育部長鄭英耀列為「台獨頑固分子」,將時任一名高等檢察署檢察官列為「台獨打手幫凶」;中共官媒社群還轉發立法委員住處、工作場所等衛星圖,意圖威脅其人身安全。
中共對台操作軟硬兩手策略,例如台北─上海城市論壇(雙城論壇)在上海召開,上海市長龔正在論壇上強調「兩岸一家親」;惟論壇才剛結束,中共隨即對台發動「正義使命-2025」軍演,宣稱是對台獨及外部勢力的懲戒。(編輯:邱國強)1150211

_source.movement_title: 大陆情势报告：台资持续缩减 社会抗争增加
_source.movement_abstract: 大陆委员会发布2025年第4季中国大陆情势报告，指出台湾对大陆投资持续缩减，2025年赴陆直接投资金额年减59%，核准陆资来台投资金额年减65.4%。报告提到中国大陆去年经济成长率为5%，但成长动能分化，房市萧条、FDI放缓、通缩压力未散。国际组织预测今年经济成长率在4.0%-4.8%之间，平均4.5%。中国大陆下半年社会抗争增加，主因经济放缓、青年失业严重及地方政府财政困难。大陆持续对台进行法律战，将部分台湾官员列为‘台独顽固分子’，并采取软硬兼施策略，如举办双城论坛后随即进行军演。

If you’re like most Americans, your idea of global censorship is that it’s bad, but it doesn’t feel like a real threat to you.
The fact that 30 British subjects are arrested every day for speech crimes sounds dire but distant. The ongoing crusade to arrest and prosecute U.K. grandmothers and clergy members for tweets and peaceful protests is infuriating, but it is also far from our shores.
The same goes for Päivi Räsänen. A medical doctor, grandmother of 12, and member of the Finnish parliament, Räsänen is now awaiting a verdict at her nation’s high court that stems from a 2019 Twitter post that cited a Bible verse. This is yet another example which, while deeply troubling, sounds like it’s somebody else’s problem to deal with.
Unfortunately, the U.S. House of Representatives’ House Judiciary Committee has made clear in its recent findings, this form of crushing online censorship isn’t just headed to the U.S. It’s already here.
Chairman Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) has released subpoenaed evidence that European Union leaders have been pressuring American Big Tech platforms such as Google, Meta, TikTok, Twitter, and LinkedIn to censor content — including content they knew to be factually true — since at least 2015.
Over the last decade, the evidence shows E.U. commissioners effectively commandeering American tech companies as tools of censorship by strong-arming them to silence and punish users around the world.
By 2020, unelected bureaucrats in Brussels enjoyed a firm grip on virtually every social media platform on the Internet. The COVID-19 pandemic and concurrent social justice unrest became the ultimate test of narrative control over users worldwide — not just in the U.K. or the E.U., but also stateside.
Between 2022 — when Elon Musk purchased Twitter and converted it to X — and 2024, the E.U. Commission met more than 90 times with tech companies. The goal was obvious: to pressure the companies into adopting draconian and easily weaponizable speech restrictions styled as “community guidelines.” The underlying aim was to censor speech and speakers that challenged the commission’s preferred narratives.
Musk’s purchase of X threw a massive wrench into Brussels’ censorship apparatus, as did his defiance of now-disgraced E.U. Commissioner Thierry Breton’s demand that he censor his own exchange with President Trump.
Little wonder, then, that the E.U. Commission’s first exercise of its censorship authority under its so-called Digital Services Act came in the form of a $140 million fine against X in December. To reinforce that it means business, the Commission also launched a new investigation last month into Musk’s platform while expanding an existing probe that had begun in late 2023.
The E.U. Commission’s retributive fines and selective investigations of X are chilling. So is its longstanding power play to wield effective editorial control over the entire internet, including over what American citizens can say and see.
Jordan’s Committee held a hearing just 24 hours after publishing its findings, focusing on the threat that European law poses to Americans’ freedom of speech. Irish comedian Graham Linehan shared his experience of being caught in the gears of the global censorship machinery over an X post he had made while in Arizona. Räsänen recalled her initial shock at being interrogated and later prosecuted three times under a Finnish war crimes law, all for peaceably expressing views online and quoting scripture to support them.
“Increasingly, the fight for free speech is focused online, and we are seeing that censorship measures adopted in Europe do not remain confined to Europe,” Räsänen said. “This should concern every person that values freedom.”
Räsänen is right. The Digital Services Act and its sister legislation in the U.K. the Online Safety Act, exports to the U.S. the very same draconian speech codes that Finland has used to punish Räsänen. And because it is all online and carried out by non-government actors at Big Tech companies, the Digital Services Act bypasses the First Amendment’s protections, leaving American citizens every bit as vulnerable to censorship as our European cousins.
Thankfully, Jordan is bringing this issue to light for the American public. So are administration officials like Vice President J.D. Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy Sarah Rogers, who have all spoken out and taken decisive action to defend free speech for all Americans.
We are long past the point where censorship is someone else’s problem. Europe has built itself the infrastructure to impose global speech controls, and the Europeans don’t plan to exempt Americans.
Jeremy Tedesco is senior counsel and senior vice president of corporate engagement at Alliance Defending Freedom.
_source.movement_title: 欧盟推动全球内容审查 美国面临言论自由威胁
_source.movement_abstract: 文章指出欧洲联盟正通过《数字服务法案》等法律，对全球范围内的互联网内容进行审查和控制，包括对美国科技公司施压，要求其限制用户言论。欧洲官员自2015年起持续施压，迫使美国科技企业如谷歌、Meta、推特等进行内容审查，甚至在2020年后掌握对社交媒体平台的广泛控制权。欧盟委员会在2024年对推特（现X）处以1.4亿美元罚款，并展开进一步调查，以遏制与欧盟主流叙事相悖的言论。文章强调，这种全球性审查机制已影响到美国公民的言论自由，呼吁美国政府采取行动保护自由表达权利。
_source.title: Euro-censorship is starting to squeeze Americans’ freedom of speech
_source.trans_cont:
如果你像大多数美国人一样，你对全球审查制度的看法是，它是不好的，但它并不像是对你的真正威胁。
每天有30名英国公民因言论犯罪而被捕，这听起来很可怕，但却很遥远。正在进行的因推特和和平抗议而逮捕和起诉英国祖母和神职人员的运动令人愤怒，但它也远离我们的海岸。
Päivi Räsänen也是如此。Räsänen是一名医生，12个孩子的祖母，也是芬兰议会议员，她现在正在等待国家高等法院的判决，该判决源于2019年推特上的一篇引用圣经经文的帖子。这是另一个例子，虽然令人深感不安，但听起来像是别人要处理的问题。
不幸的是，美国众议院司法委员会（House of Representatives House Judjudiciary Committee）在其最近的调查结果中明确表示，这种形式的网络审查不仅仅是在美国，它已经在这里了。
主席Jim Jordan（R-Ohio）发布了传讯证据，表明欧盟领导人至少自2015年以来一直在向谷歌、Meta、TikTok、Twitter和LinkedIn等美国大型科技平台施压，要求其审查内容，包括他们知道是真实的内容。
在过去的十年里，有证据显示，欧盟委员通过强迫美国科技公司保持沉默和惩罚世界各地的用户，有效地将其作为审查工具。
到2020年，布鲁塞尔的非民选官僚几乎牢牢控制了互联网上的每一个社交媒体平台。Covid-19大流行和同时发生的社会正义动荡成为对全球用户叙事控制的终极考验——不仅在英国或欧盟，而且在美国本土。
从2022年埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）收购Twitter并将其转换为X到2024年，欧盟委员会与科技公司举行了90多次会议。他们的目标很明显：迫使这些公司采取严厉的、容易被武器化的言论限制，称之为“社区准则”。其根本目的是审查质疑委员会首选叙述的言论和发言者。
马斯克对X的收购给布鲁塞尔的审查机构带来了巨大的打击，他对现已名誉扫地的欧盟专员蒂埃里·布雷顿（Thierry Breton）要求他审查自己与特朗普总统的交流的蔑视也是如此。
因此，毫不奇怪，欧盟委员会根据其所谓的《数字服务法案》（Digital Services Act）首次行使审查权，是在去年12月对X处以1.4亿美元的罚款。为了强调这一点，欧盟委员会上个月还对马斯克的平台发起了一项新的调查，同时扩大了2023年底开始的现有调查。
欧盟委员会对X的报复性罚款和选择性调查令人不寒而栗。它长期以来的权力游戏也是如此，即对整个互联网进行有效的编辑控制，包括美国公民可以说什么和看什么。
约旦委员会在公布调查结果后仅24小时就举行了听证会，重点关注欧洲法律对美国言论自由构成的威胁。爱尔兰喜剧演员格雷厄姆·莱恩汉（Graham Linehan）分享了他在亚利桑那州发表的一篇X帖子被卷入全球审查机制的经历。Räsänen回忆起她最初被审问时的震惊，后来根据芬兰的战争罪法律被起诉了三次，都是因为在网上和平地表达观点并引用经文来支持他们。
Räsänen说：“争取言论自由的斗争越来越多地集中在网络上，我们看到欧洲采取的审查措施并不局限于欧洲。”“这应该关系到每一个珍视自由的人。”
Räsänen是对的。《数字服务法案》（Digital Services Act）及其在英国的姊妹法案《在线安全法案》（Online Safety Act）向美国输出了芬兰用来惩罚Räsänen的同样严厉的言论准则。由于这一切都在网上进行，并由大型科技公司的非政府人员执行，《数字服务法案》绕过了第一修正案的保护，使美国公民像我们的欧洲同胞一样容易受到审查。
令人欣慰的是，乔丹将这一问题公诸于众。副总统J·D·万斯（J.D.Vance）、国务卿马尔科·卢比奥（Marco Rubio）和负责公共外交的副国务卿莎拉·罗杰斯（Sarah Rogers）等政府官员也是如此，他们都大声疾呼并采取果断行动捍卫所有美国人的言论自由。
我们早就过了审查制度是别人的问题的阶段。欧洲已经为自己建立了实施全球言论控制的基础设施，而欧洲人并不打算豁免美国人。
杰里米·特德斯科（Jeremy Tedesco）是捍卫自由联盟（Alliance Defending Freedom）的高级顾问兼企业参与高级副总裁。
_source.trans_title: 欧洲审查制度开始挤压美国人的言论自由。
_source.evidence: 文章主要讨论了欧盟（EU）通过《数字服务法案》（DSA）等法规，施压美国科技巨头（如Google, Meta, X等）实施内容审查，并指出这种审查机制正在影响美国公民的言论自由。文章核心在于描述欧盟的立法政策（DSA）及其对全球（包括美国）言论空间的管控行动。虽然涉及具体的施压行动，但其根源和核心描述对象是欧盟的“法规”和“政策框架”（Digital Services Act, Online Safety Act）。根据标签定义，[理论政策] 涵盖“提出的理论、政策、法规、战略框架等”。虽然文章提到美国国会对此的反应，但文章主体是在阐述欧盟的审查政策及其影响，属于对特定域外政策/法规的讨论。然而，若从“认知域”对抗角度看，这是关于“审查”这一认知战手段的政策化描述。对比选项：[行动动向]通常指具体的作战或舆论攻击行动，而此处更多是制度性、法规性的描述；[涉我事件]通常指针对中国大陆的敌情，此处针对的是美国；[技术武器]指AI武器化等，此处是法规。因此，最贴切的是描述法规政策的[理论政策]。

_source.content:
(中央社記者吳柏緯布魯塞爾11日專電)歐盟國家近來頻繁遭到無人機侵擾,對於國家安全威脅日益升高。對此,歐盟發布因應無人機威脅的行動計畫,提升歐洲對無人機事件的準備,強化偵測能力與應對機制,同時加強防衛準備能力。
歐洲執委會於11日公布全新的「無人機與反無人機安全行動計畫」,強調無人機已成為現代經濟與社會不可或缺的一部分,然而近期涉及無人機的惡意與不負責行動,暴露了歐盟面臨重大且日益增長的安全挑戰。
無人機已被用於侵犯歐盟成員國領空、干擾機場運作,並險些與民航機發生相撞事故,突顯出包括航空安全在內安全架構的脆弱性。這類身分不明的無人機逕行飛越國界並接近禁制區,增加了區域安全緊張局勢,同時也作為測試歐盟準備狀態及應對、採取反制措施能力的工具。
這份計畫明確指出,這類的威脅程度橫跨不同層級,從過失、刑事到軍事活動,刻意模糊了民用與軍用領域的界限。這些安全威脅背後,潛伏著國家及與國家相關的敵對行為者、恐怖組織、有組織犯罪網絡和個人。
歐盟執委會說明,這項行動計畫的目的是加強歐盟層級的合作與團結、應對惡意無人機威脅。計畫將透過協調行動支援歐盟成員國,並聚焦幾項關鍵優先事項:提升應變準備、強化偵測能力、協調應對機制,以及加強歐盟的防衛準備能力。
在強化應對惡意無人機活動方面,歐盟執委會鼓勵有意願的國家聯合採購並部署反無人機系統,同時支持發展具有歐洲主權性的「指揮與控制」AI系統。另一方面,研議設立「快速反無人機緊急應變小組」,強化成員國間的支援機制。
歐盟執委會也建議成員國,支持每年舉辦大型的歐盟反無人機演習,以測試跨境合作與軍民協同能力。
至於強化歐洲對無人機威脅的防衛準備,這項計畫將補充並支持成員國透過創新與產業合作,提升歐洲軍事準備能力,包括確保關鍵原物料供應。同時透過「無人機聯盟」加強政府與產業間的合作。
歐盟執委會表示,這項計畫將隨威脅性質與演變而調整。為了落實協調與執行,將考慮與歐盟成員國共同設立戰略機制,確保彼此的聯繫與密切合作。同時建議成員國任命「國家無人機安全協調官」,以促進並監督國家層級的落實相關計畫。(編輯:陳承功)1150211

_source.movement_title: 欧盟发布无人机威胁应对行动计划
_source.movement_abstract: 欧盟近期频繁遭遇无人机侵扰，威胁日益升高。为此，欧盟发布应对无人机威胁的行动计划，提升侦测能力与应对机制，强化防卫准备。该计划强调无人机已成为现代经济与社会的重要组成部分，但近期涉及恶意和不负责任的无人机活动暴露了欧盟面临的安全挑战。无人机被用于侵犯领空、干扰机场运作，并险些与民航机相撞，凸显航空安全的脆弱性。计划指出威胁程度涵盖过失、刑事到军事活动，模糊了民用与军用界限。背后可能涉及国家行为者、恐怖组织、有组织犯罪网络和个人。行动计划旨在加强欧盟合作与团结，提升应变准备、侦测能力、协调应对机制及防务准备。计划支持联合采购反无人机系统、发展主权AI指挥与控制系统，并建议设立快速反无人机小组及举办演习。同时推动政府与产业合作，确保关键原物料供应，并建议成员国任命国家无人机安全协调官。

(中央社記者趙敏雅台北11日電)資安院公布,近半年接獲637件公務機關資安事件通報,其中以非法入侵為大宗。資安院指出,常見攻擊態樣包括冒牌軟體散播惡意程式、可攜式媒體設備(USB)感染蠕蟲、假借行政訴訟主題的社交工程郵件攻擊及水坑式攻擊。
根據最新一期資安週報,資安院表示,近半年總計接獲723件公務機關與特定非公務機關事件通報,公務機關與關鍵基礎設施面臨的風險來源不同,應採取相應的防護與因應策略。
其中,近半年公務機關資安事件通報有637件,以非法入侵為大宗,共410件。資安院說明,整體常見攻擊態樣共有4種,首先為冒牌軟體散播惡意程式,攻擊者假冒合法或常用軟體,誘使使用者下載或安裝,進而植入惡意程式,建立異常對外連線,作為後續控制或資料外傳的管道。
資安院指出,其次是可攜式媒體設備(USB)感染蠕蟲。攻擊者利用USB等可攜式媒體作為傳播媒介,當設備插入機關電腦時會自動執行惡意程式,造成端點遭入侵並產生異常行為,衍生橫向擴散或對外通訊風險。
資安院表示,第3為假借行政訴訟主題的社交工程郵件攻擊,攻擊者以政府機關高度關注的業務主題,如行政訴訟、公文往返等製作釣魚郵件,誘使人員開啟附件或點擊連結,藉此植入惡意程式或竊取資訊。
資安院說,第4為水坑式攻擊,為攻擊者入侵公務人員或特定族群常瀏覽的合法網站,植入惡意指令,讓使用者正常瀏覽過程中觸發惡意程式下載,導致端點受害並產生異常連線行為。
資安院提醒,在技術面上,應強化端點防護與異常行為監控機制,涵蓋惡意程式、異常連線、可疑指令執行及可攜式媒體使用情境,以降低端點遭入侵後對外通訊的風險;同時加強瀏覽行為與附件存取防護,避免因正常業務操作而觸發惡意程式下載。
此外,資安院建議,在管理面上,須持續強化人員對社交工程、水坑式攻擊及冒牌軟體等常見手法的風險意識,並建立可攜式媒體使用、軟體來源及外部網站存取管理原則,將使用情境納入資安治理與教育訓練範疇,透過技術防護與使用行為管理並行,降低相關風險。
至於特定非公務機關資安事件通報,資安院說明,以關鍵基礎設施提供者為主,集中於緊急救援與醫療、通訊傳播等領域。綜觀事件類型,以設備異常或設備毀損為主,常見情境包括系統營運異常導致服務中斷,或因颱風等外部環境因素影響,造成關鍵服務暫停或效能下降。
對此,資安院表示,這類事件多屬營運與環境因素所引發,顯示關鍵基礎設施除資安防護外,設備韌性、營運持續及環境風險因應能力,仍為確保服務穩定性的重要關鍵。(編輯:楊蘭軒)1150211

_source.movement_title: 台湾资安院：半年接获637件公务机关资安事件通报
_source.movement_abstract: 根据中央社报道，台湾资安院公布近半年接获637件公务机关资安事件通报，其中非法入侵占多数，共410件。资安院指出，常见攻击方式包括冒牌软件散播恶意程式、USB设备感染蠕虫、以行政诉讼为主题的钓鱼邮件攻击及水坑式攻击。针对不同风险来源，资安院建议强化端点防护与异常行为监控机制，并提升人员对社交工程等攻击手法的风险意识。此外，特定非公务机关的资安事件多集中于关键基础设施领域，如紧急救援与医疗、通讯传播等，事件类型以设备异常或毁损为主，多因营运与环境因素导致服务中断。
_source.title: 公務機關資安通報近半年637件 資安院揭4大攻擊樣態
_source.trans_cont:
(中央社記者趙敏雅台北11日電)資安院公布,近半年接獲637件公務機關資安事件通報,其中以非法入侵為大宗.資安院指出，常見攻擊態樣包括冒牌軟體散播惡意程式、可攜式媒體設備（USB）感染蠕蟲、假借行政訴訟主題的社交工程郵件攻擊及水坑式攻擊。
根據最新一期資安週報,資安院表示,近半年總計接獲723件公務機關與特定非公務機關事件通報,公務機關與關鍵基礎設施面臨的風險來源不同,應採取相應的防護與因應策略.
其中,近半年公務機關資安事件通報有637件,以非法入侵為大宗,共410件.資安院說明,整體常見攻擊態樣共有4種,首先為冒牌軟體散播惡意程式,攻擊者假冒合法或常用軟體,誘使使用者下載或安裝,進而植入惡意程式,建立異常對外連線,作為後續控制或資料外傳的管道.
資安院指出，其次是可攜式媒體設備（USB）感染蠕蟲。攻擊者利用USB等可攜式媒體作為傳播媒介，當設備插入機關電腦時會自動執行惡意程式，造成端點遭入侵並產生異常行為，衍生橫向擴散或對外通訊風險。
資安院表示,第3為假借行政訴訟主題的社交工程郵件攻擊,攻擊者以政府機關高度關注的業務主題,如行政訴訟、公文往返等製作釣魚郵件,誘使人員開啟附件或點擊連結,藉此植入惡意程式或竊取資訊.
資安院說,第4為水坑式攻擊,為攻擊者入侵公務人員或特定族群常瀏覽的合法網站,植入惡意指令,讓使用者正常瀏覽過程中觸發惡意程式下載,導致端點受害並產生異常連線行為.
資安院提醒,在技術面上,應強化端點防護與異常行為監控機制,涵蓋惡意程式、異常連線、可疑指令執行及可攜式媒體使用情境,以降低端點遭入侵後對外通訊的風險;同時加強瀏覽行為與附件存取防護,避免因正常業務操作而觸發惡意程式下載.
此外,資安院建議,在管理面上,須持續強化人員對社交工程、水坑式攻擊及冒牌軟體等常見手法的風險意識,並建立可攜式媒體使用、軟體來源及外部網站存取管理原則,將使用情境納入資安治理與教育訓練範疇,透過技術防護與使用行為管理並行,降低相關風險.
至於特定非公務機關資安事件通報,資安院說明,以關鍵基礎設施提供者為主,集中於緊急救援與醫療、通訊傳播等領域.綜觀事件類型,以設備異常或設備毀損為主,常見情境包括系統營運異常導致服務中斷,或因颱風等外部環境因素影響,造成關鍵服務暫停或效能下降.
對此,資安院表示,這類事件多屬營運與環境因素所引發,顯示關鍵基礎設施除資安防護外,設備韌性、營運持續及環境風險因應能力,仍為確保服務穩定性的重要關鍵.(編輯:楊蘭軒)1150211

The American Hospital Association (AHA), in collaboration with the FBI, has released a series of behavioral threat assessment and management (BTAM) resources developed in partnership with the FBI’s Behavioral Analysis Unit-1 (BAU).
Over the past two years, the FBI’s BAU has worked alongside AHA partners to support efforts aimed at preventing targeted violence in health care settings.
The newly released
leadership guide
outlines practical, evidence-based strategies to strengthen threat management protocols. It includes guidance on coordinating with local and federal law enforcement in implementing BTAM efforts, as well as training approaches to help health care teams better understand and apply threat assessment practices. The guide also features
case studies
from AHA members. These examples highlight how organizations have built and sustained BTAM teams, developed partnerships with law enforcement and community stakeholders, and trained the workforce on identifying targeted violence threats.
In addition, a companion resource
compendium
is designed for health care security professionals seeking a more detailed understanding of how hospitals and health systems are using BTAM frameworks to prevent targeted violence. The compendium provides expanded analysis and supporting material from researchers, security professionals and FBI personnel to complement the leadership guide.
Both resources are available through the ongoing partnership between the AHA and the FBI’s Behavioral Analysis Unit and are part of the AHA’s
Hospitals Against Violence initiative
. The initiative supports member hospitals and health systems in addressing workplace and community violence through structured prevention and response strategies.

_source.movement_title: AHA与FBI发布医疗反暴力资源指南
_source.movement_abstract: 美国医院协会（AHA）与联邦调查局（FBI）合作，发布了行为威胁评估与管理（BTAM）资源，旨在预防医疗环境中的针对性暴力。过去两年，FBI的行为分析单位（BAU）与AHA合作伙伴共同支持相关努力。新发布的领导指南提供了基于证据的策略，以加强威胁管理协议，包括与执法部门协调及培训医疗团队。指南还包含案例研究，展示组织如何建立BTAM团队、与执法和社区利益相关者合作以及培训员工识别威胁。此外，还有一本配套资源汇编，为医疗安全专业人员提供更详细的BTAM框架分析。这些资源是AHA与FBI合作的一部分，属于‘医院反暴力’计划，支持医院和医疗系统应对工作场所和社区暴力。
_source.title: FBI and American Hospital Association Release Behavioral Threat Assessment and Management Resources
_source.trans_cont:
美国医院协会（AHA）与美国联邦调查局（FBI）合作，发布了一系列与FBI行为分析单元-1（BAU）合作开发的行为威胁评估和管理（BTAM）资源。
在过去的两年里，联邦调查局的BAU一直与AHA合作伙伴合作，支持旨在防止卫生保健环境中有针对性的暴力行为的努力。
新发布的
领导指南
概述了加强威胁管理协议的基于证据的实用策略。它包括与地方和联邦执法部门协调实施BTAM工作的指导，以及帮助卫生保健团队更好地理解和应用威胁评估实践的培训方法。该指南还介绍了
案例研究
来自AHA会员。这些例子突出了各组织如何建立和维持BTAM团队，如何与执法部门和社区利益攸关方建立伙伴关系，以及如何培训工作人员识别有针对性的暴力威胁。
此外，同伴资源
简编
专为寻求更详细了解医院和卫生系统如何使用BTAM框架来防止有针对性的暴力的卫生保健安全专业人员而设计。该纲要提供了来自研究人员、安全专业人员和联邦调查局人员的扩展分析和辅助材料，以补充领导指南。
这两种资源都可以通过美国心脏协会和联邦调查局行为分析部门之间的持续合作获得，并且是美国心脏协会的一部分。
医院反暴力倡议
.该倡议支持成员医院和卫生系统通过结构化预防和应对战略解决工作场所和社区暴力问题。

_source.content:
Just before Christmas 2025, a bipartisan coalition of U.S. senators, including Lindsey Graham, Dick Durbin, Josh Hawley, Amy Klobuchar, Marsha Blackburn and Ashley Moody, introduced legislation to sunset Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act on January 1, 2027. If enacted, the sunset could break Big Tech’s seemingly impenetrable stranglehold on the legislative process, forcing Congress to protect kids online and secure Americans’ freedom from censorship.
Section 230, which dates to 1996, immunizes interactive computer services from being held legally responsible both for hosting user content and for blocking content that is obscene or objectionable. These immunities sought to encourage a competitive, decentralized and open internet ecosystem, while preventing the widespread proliferation of pornography on the early internet.
Nowadays, however, 230 allows Big Tech companies like Meta, Alphabet, Snap, TikTok and X to escape liability for addicting kids, exposing users to a constant deluge of dangerous, toxic and erotic content, and silencing conservative voices.
>>> How Congress Can Protect Children from Predatory Social Media and Pornography Platforms
Although members of Congress have introduced numerous legislative proposals, many intended to combat Big Tech’s abuses, the tech industry has spent millions to defeat them with near perfect success.
Under 230’s sweeping immunity shield, Big Tech wins by default. Without an end to the liability gravy train, there is little incentive for industry to come to the table. Sunsetting 230—ending one of Big Tech’s most prized subsidies—could finally break that trend. With the impending end of their 230-enabled fiefdoms, tech companies would have a strong incentive to negotiate reforms in good faith, rather than stall out every attempt to restrain their power.
A robust 230 reform package, negotiated in light of a fixed sunset, could also serve as a vehicle to enact other long-overdue tech legislation like the Kids Online Safety Act, which passed the Senate overwhelmingly in 2024, and comprehensive data privacy legislation modeled after the American Privacy Rights Act.
In the face of a clean sunset, Congress would be forced to do its job and finally hold Big Tech accountable. With our children and the future of free speech hanging in the balance, it’s time to put Big Tech on defense.
_source.movement_title: 美国参议院拟终止第230条以遏制科技巨头权力
_source.movement_abstract: 2025年圣诞节前夕，美国参议院跨党派议员联盟，包括林赛·格雷厄姆、迪克·杜宾、乔什·霍利、艾米·克罗布彻、马莎·布莱克本和阿什利·穆迪，提出立法，计划于2027年1月1日终止《通信 decency 法案》第230条。该条款自1996年起赋予互联网服务提供商对用户内容和过滤内容的法律豁免权，旨在鼓励开放的互联网生态。然而，如今该条款使科技巨头如Meta、Alphabet、Snap、TikTok和X得以逃避对成瘾性内容、危险内容及言论审查的责任。尽管国会已提出多项法案，但科技行业通过巨额资金成功阻挠。终止230条款将迫使科技公司重新谈判改革，推动其他重要立法如《儿童在线安全法案》和数据隐私法案，以实现对科技巨头的问责。
_source.title: A Measure That Would Force Big Tech To Protect Kids Online and Stop Censoring Conservatives
_source.trans_cont:
就在2025年圣诞节前，包括林赛·格雷厄姆、迪克·德宾、乔希·霍利、艾米·克洛布查尔、玛莎·布莱克本和阿什利·穆迪在内的美国两党参议员联盟于2027年1月1日提出了废除《通信内容端正法案》第230条的法案。如果获得通过，《日落法案》可能会打破大型科技公司对立法程序看似坚不可摧的束缚，迫使国会保护儿童上网，并确保美国人免受审查。
第230条可追溯到1996年，它使交互式计算机服务免于承担托管用户内容和阻止淫秽或令人反感的内容的法律责任。这些豁免旨在鼓励竞争性、去中心化和开放的互联网生态系统，同时防止早期互联网上色情内容的广泛扩散。
然而，如今，230让Meta、Alphabet、Snap、TikTok和X等大型科技公司逃脱了让孩子上瘾的责任，让用户不断接触到危险、有毒和色情的内容，并压制保守派的声音。
>>>国会如何保护儿童免受掠夺性社交媒体和色情平台的侵害
尽管国会议员提出了许多立法提案，其中许多旨在打击大型科技公司的滥用行为，但科技行业已经花费了数百万美元来击败他们，并取得了近乎完美的成功。
在230的全面免疫护盾下，大科技默认获胜。如果不结束这种责任的肥缺，工业界就没有什么动力回到谈判桌前。日落230-结束大型科技公司最有价值的补贴之一-可能最终打破这一趋势。随着230年封地即将结束，科技公司将有强烈的动机真诚地谈判改革，而不是拖延限制其权力的每一次尝试。
根据固定的日落时间谈判达成的强有力的230改革方案，也可以作为制定其他拖延已久的科技立法的工具，如2024年在参议院以压倒性优势通过的《儿童在线安全法案》，以及以《美国隐私权法案》为蓝本的全面数据隐私立法。
面对一个干净的日落，国会将被迫履行自己的职责，并最终追究大型科技公司的责任。随着我们的孩子和言论自由的未来悬而未决，是时候把大科技放在防御上了。
_source.trans_title: 这项措施将迫使大型科技公司保护儿童上网，并停止审查保守派。

_source.content:
Emily Harding testified before the House Homeland Security Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection about how the United States can strengthen its approach to offensive cyber operations as part of a broader national security framework, including the evolving roles of federal agencies and the private sector.
IntroductionWashington has failed to establish deterrence in the cyber domain, and our adversaries control the escalation ladder. Historically, U.S. foreign policy has rested on deterrence, with implied escalation dominance in any domain. But that foundation has failed in the context of cyber. U.S. responses to cyberattacks have been muted, and escalation dominance does not exist.
The U.S.’s offensive cyber capabilities are strong, perhaps unmatched. U.S. Cyber Command (CYBERCOM) has repeatedly proven its capability to disrupt adversary activity, when given the chance. This demonstrated skill, coupled with overall U.S. strength, makes deterrence in the cyber domain possible.
But to actually achieve deterrence, we need a mindset shift. We need to stop thinking about cyber attacks as inevitable nuisances and start seeing them for what they are: hostile action against the United States. Attacks are not always conducted by foreign States—we still need to draw a distinction between crime and hostile activity—but when they are, they should be treated as a type of warfare. China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea do not see a bright line between war and peace. Instead, they view cyber attacks as fitting on a spectrum of warfare. For them, competition with the United States is ongoing, and low-level elements of cyber warfare are not only acceptable, they are effective.
The Problem: Weak Defense and Absent DeterrenceU.S. defenses are unacceptably weak, for a set of logical reasons. The U.S. government and industry need to put considerable effort and resources toward making critical infrastructure and government systems resilient and ready for this new form of warfare. Systems must be able to fail, reset, and recover in minutes, not days, with minimal disruption to essential services.
We have a long way to go. A series of attacks in 2023 showed the severity of the gaps in stark relief. In November 2023, a designated terrorist group that is also the covert action arm of the Iranian government, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), attacked U.S. water plants. The stated target was an Israeli company that makes software for control systems, and the attack was meant to be retaliation for the war in Gaza. While the intent was to embarrass Israel, the facts are undeniable: A terrorist group attempted to impair water delivery to civilians in the United States. Also in late 2023, the National Security Agency (NSA) and cybersecurity researchers raised renewed alarm about China’s Volt Typhoon group. The attackers burrowed into U.S. water, power, and port systems across the mainland and in Guam. These accesses could give Beijing the capability to severely disrupt daily life, particularly around the U.S. military bases that would serve as the launching pads for U.S. troops in a Pacific fight.
These two egregious violations received little attention because they were cyberattacks, and “cyber” has been shunted into a silo of what tech people do behind the scenes. It’s separate, “technical,” and an afterthought, not an integrated tool of modern foreign policy. This mindset is a strategic mistake. While U.S. policymakers allow these de facto silos, our adversaries are aggressively pursuing an integrated strategy. While the United States seeks to protect civilians and carefully selects offensive cyber actions, adversaries are pushing the envelope.
Attacks like Iran’s and China’s should be viewed as part of a dangerous new phase in cyberwarfare, one for which U.S. systems and policy are ill-prepared. To test how policymakers might respond in a massive cyberattack on U.S. territory, CSIS ran a series of wargames. The results revealed the likely disastrous confusion that would occur in a cyber-first conflict, as policymakers lack shared frameworks and a coherent view on what constitutes an act of war or a proportional response in the cyber domain. Participants shared comments like “we should use a proportional response, as soon as we figure out what a proportional response is.” These exercises revealed that decision-makers do not fully understand how cyber attacks fit into traditional conceptions of the tools of foreign policy. The U.S. government has no hope of deterring, defending, and responding unless it begins to integrate cyber offense and defense into its own national security strategy. In the Trump Administration’s recently released National Security Strategy, its explicit mention of “offensive cyber operations” as part of a comprehensive U.S. government response capability is a positive development.
How to Fix It: RecommendationsThe U.S. government needs to establish a new framework for conceptualizing and responding to these kinds of attacks. To address this urgent need, CSIS created a Playbook for Winning the Cyber War, which lays out how to shift the mindset, plus actionable steps for building the larger capacity to fight this modern form of warfare. The steps are summarized below: creating a new declaratory policy, rethinking U.S. internal policies, building an international response, and operationalizing the shift.
Announce the Shift: A New Declaratory Policy on Cyber Warfare
The first part of a mindset shift is for the U.S. government to establish a new declaratory policy with the following key points:
Cyberattacks are attacks. If they imperil life, health, or safety, and particularly if they threaten critical infrastructure in a way that could create a mass casualty event, the U.S. government will treat them as they would any other attack on civilians.The United States can and will use all elements of state power to effectively defend the homeland against any threat, in any domain. Further, the U.S. prides itself on protecting innocent civilians, not targeting them, so it refuses to target civilian critical infrastructure. Therefore, a proportional response to a cyberattack on our critical infrastructure would be severe and likely include economic or military measures.The United States will assume any cyberattack on critical infrastructure has a destructive intent and respond accordingly.Internalize the Shift for US Decisionmakers
Redefine proportionality and escalation to include the big picture. Policymakers’ view of proportionality must expand beyond the most recent incident and consider the aggregate costs of a pattern of attacks, the long-term economic and security consequences of those attacks, and the message sent by inaction. A new policy, which could be called “cyber first–cyber optional,” must begin with explicit principles that the United States is redefining proportionality in the cyber domain, bolstering defense, and putting adversaries on notice that in the future the United States will retaliate for the overall pattern of behavior, not any one attack in isolation, and will use all tools at its disposal. A cyber response to a cyber attack is an option, but far from the only option.
Take the Shift International
Define international norms of behavior to establish a clear baseline for future action. This is a worthwhile exercise, even if many States are likely to ignore those norms. Defining the norms lays the groundwork for deterrence, because it reduces uncertainty around action when those norms are violated. Not just the statement, but the demonstration of will is critical to deterrence. A strong U.S. and allied response to the first cyberattack after the declaratory policy goes into place will help set a new tone.
Operationalize the Shift
Evolve offensive operations to operate as a strategic whole. Cyber policy plays a late, minor supporting role to the main characters in foreign policy. The needed evolution, then, depends on two actions: (1) sliding risk tolerance far higher, freeing operators to do more as the opportunity arises, and (2) shifting planning far to the left on the timeline, incorporating cyber tools in the early-stage policy planning process. Then, policymakers will be ready to run a new, more robust playbook to win the cyber war.
First, adjust risk tolerance. A shift toward a higher risk tolerance for rapid action is essential for a more flexible, aggressive approach. Cyber offense must combine long-term planned campaigns and instant opportunism. A large campaign is essential to create a coherent long-term approach, but within that campaign, operators must be prepared to seize upon a vulnerability in the rare moment it appears. Ideally policymakers would flip the risk calculus: The default answer to a proposed operation should be “yes,” and a naysayer must prove it is too risky instead of asking the operators to prove the operation is safe.
Second, collaborate early. Cyber, in its relative newness, often gets relegated to a last-minute add-on to an operational plan instead of playing an integrated role in a larger campaign. This approach can allow cyber activity to contribute somewhat, but only on the margins. Instead, planners should incorporate cyber operators into early-stage planning, particularly for contingency planning against a peer competitor. If developed early enough, cyber tools can distract and weaken an adversary, serving as a force multiplier for military and diplomatic action. Being ready to capitalize on lucky opportunities takes months of research, planning, and prepositioning. If cyber tools are to be available in moments of acute need, operators need lead time to plan.
This evolved model could be imagined as an octopus. Offensive cyber tools, at their best, are flexible, inventive, and opportunistic, akin to how an octopus hunts in the wild. Cyber offense must combine long-term planned campaigns and instant opportunism—like an octopus’s central brain and tentacles. An octopus camouflages itself perfectly, uses its tentacles to explore nooks and crannies, and squeezes into impossibly small corners to wait for its prey. Further, each tentacle acts independently but also as part of a whole. The central nervous system guides the effort, but a brain in each tentacle manages the search. An octopus model for offensive cyber operations might include strategic guidance from the NSC; interagency campaign planning; a forward-leaning approach to exploration and opportunism; and additional delegated responsibility to NSA, CIA, and CYBERCOM for execution of low- and moderate-risk missions.
With these pieces in place, run the playbook. CSIS’s report lays out these steps in detail, but the main point is this: Be bold. Match creative policy responses to the pain points of the particular attacker. Demonstrate that the United States will view a cyberattack that causes damage as just as serious as a kinetic attack.
Recommendations for CongressThe following Congressional actions can bolster cyber offensive capability, bolster domestic defense, and help create much-needed deterrence:
Create and fund a new Cyber Force: The cyber domain needs its own service, heavily weighted toward reserve forces, to recruit and retain the best cyber talent from the private sector.Fund cybersecurity: Congress should consider funding much-needed capital upgrades in government networks, allow more flexible spending for cybersecurity improvements, and require improved reporting and greater accountability for weak cyber defense inside government. They should also consider creating a combination of funding streams (carrots) and consequences (sticks) for critical infrastructure providers to significantly improve their resilience against attacks.Protect industry cyber fighters: Treat the private sector as real partners. Put in place protections for cyber operators who act in conjunction with the U.S. government, as so many from the private sector did in Ukraine.ConclusionA dramatic change is needed in the cyber domain. Washington urgently needs to integrate cyber into its broader foreign policy toolkit and determine how cyber activity aligns with larger foreign policy actions, including deterrence, proportional response, and international norms. In other words, the United States needs a new playbook to respond to increasingly disruptive and aggressive cyberattacks. For more, see CSIS’s A Playbook for Winning the Cyber War.
_source.movement_title: 美国需加强网络安全威慑与战略整合
_source.movement_abstract: Emily Harding在美国众议院国土安全委员会下属的网络安全与基础设施保护小组作证，强调美国需要加强在网络安全领域的进攻性网络行动，以构建更全面的国家安全框架。她指出，美国在网络安全领域未能建立有效的威慑，且对手控制了升级节奏。尽管美国拥有强大的进攻性网络能力，但目前的应对方式过于克制，缺乏威慑力。她认为，应将网络攻击视为敌对行为，而非单纯的犯罪活动，并需将网络作战纳入整体国家安全战略。2023年发生的多起网络攻击事件凸显了美国在防御上的薄弱，包括伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队对美国水厂的攻击以及中国Volt Typhoon小组对美国关键基础设施的渗透。这些事件表明，美国在应对网络战争方面准备不足，需建立统一的战略框架和响应机制。
_source.post_location: 华盛顿特区西北罗德岛大道1616号
_source.site_name: 美国战略与国际问题研究中心
_source.title: U.S. Cyber Capabilities to Deter and Disrupt Malign Foreign Activity Targeting the Homeland
_source.trans_cont:
哈丁（Emily Harding）在众议院国土安全委员会网络安全和基础设施保护小组委员会（House Homeland Security Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection）就美国如何加强进攻性网络行动作为更广泛的国家安全框架的一部分，包括联邦机构和私营部门不断演变的角色，作证。
引言华盛顿未能在网络领域建立威慑，而我们的对手控制着升级阶梯。从历史上看，美国的外交政策一直依赖于威慑，在任何领域都隐含着升级主导地位。但这一基础在网络环境中失败了。美国对网络攻击的反应是沉默的，升级优势并不存在。
美国的进攻性网络能力很强，也许是无与伦比的。美国网络司令部（Cybercom）已经多次证明，只要有机会，它就有能力破坏对手的活动。这种展示的技能，加上美国的整体实力，使网络领域的威慑成为可能。
但要真正实现威慑，我们需要转变心态。我们需要停止将网络攻击视为不可避免的滋扰，并开始看清它们的本质：针对美国的敌对行动。袭击并不总是由外国进行的——我们仍然需要区分犯罪和敌对活动——但当它们发生时，它们应该被视为一种战争。中国、俄罗斯、伊朗和朝鲜看不到战争与和平之间的明确界限。相反，他们将网络攻击视为一系列战争的一部分。对他们来说，与美国的竞争正在进行，网络战的低层次元素不仅是可以接受的，而且是有效的。
问题是：由于一系列合乎逻辑的原因，防御薄弱和缺乏威慑力是不可接受的。美国政府和工业界需要投入大量的精力和资源，使关键基础设施和政府系统具有弹性，并为这种新形式的战争做好准备。系统必须能够在几分钟（而不是几天）内发生故障、重置和恢复，并且对基本服务的中断最小。
我们还有很长的路要走。2023年发生的一系列袭击事件清楚地表明了差距的严重性。2023年11月，一个被认定的恐怖组织，同时也是伊朗政府的秘密行动部门，伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC），袭击了美国水厂。声明的目标是一家为控制系统制造软件的以色列公司，这次袭击是为了报复加沙战争。虽然其意图是让以色列难堪，但事实是不可否认的：一个恐怖组织企图破坏向美国平民供水。也是在2023年末，美国国家安全局（NSA）和网络安全研究人员再次对中国的“伏特”台风群发出警告。攻击者在美国大陆和关岛挖掘美国的水、电力和港口系统。这些通道可以让北京有能力严重扰乱日常生活，特别是在美军基地周围，这些基地将作为美军在太平洋作战的发射台。
这两个令人震惊的违规行为很少受到关注，因为它们是网络攻击，而“网络”已经被分流到技术人员在幕后所做的事情中。它是独立的，“技术性的”，是事后的想法，而不是现代外交政策的综合工具。这种心态是一种战略错误。虽然美国决策者允许这些事实上的筒仓，但我们的对手正在积极推行一体化战略。在美国寻求保护平民并谨慎选择进攻性网络行动的同时，对手正在挑战极限。
像伊朗和中国这样的攻击应该被视为网络战危险新阶段的一部分，美国的系统和政策对此准备不足。为了测试决策者如何应对对美国领土的大规模网络攻击，战略与国际研究中心进行了一系列军事演习。结果显示，在网络优先的冲突中，可能会出现灾难性的混乱，因为决策者缺乏共同的框架，对什么构成战争行为或网络领域的适当反应缺乏一致的看法。参与者分享了这样的评论：“一旦我们弄清楚什么是比例反应，我们就应该使用比例反应。”这些演习表明，决策者并不完全了解网络攻击如何符合外交政策工具的传统概念。美国政府没有希望进行威慑、防御和回应，除非它开始将网络进攻和防御纳入自己的国家安全战略。在特朗普政府最近发布的《国家安全战略》中，明确提到“进攻性网络行动”是美国政府全面应对能力的一部分，这是一个积极的发展。
如何修复：建议美国政府需要建立一个新的框架来概念化和应对这类攻击。为了满足这一迫切需求，战略与国际研究中心（CSIS）创建了一本赢得网络战争的剧本，其中列出了如何转变思维模式，以及建立更大能力以应对这种现代战争形式的可行步骤。这些步骤总结如下：制定新的宣言性政策，重新思考美国的内部政策，建立国际反应，并将这一转变付诸实施。
宣布转变：关于网络战的新宣言政策
思维转变的第一部分是美国政府制定一项新的宣言性政策，其要点如下：
网络攻击就是攻击。如果他们危及生命、健康或安全，特别是如果他们以可能造成大规模伤亡事件的方式威胁关键基础设施，美国政府将像对待任何其他针对平民的袭击一样对待他们。美国可以并将使用国家力量的所有要素来有效地保卫国土免受任何领域的任何威胁。此外，美国以保护无辜平民而不是以他们为目标而自豪，因此它拒绝以民用关键基础设施为目标。因此，对我们的关键基础设施遭受网络攻击的相应反应将是严厉的，可能包括经济或军事措施。美国将假定对关键基础设施的任何网络攻击都具有破坏性意图，并做出相应的反应。
重新定义比例和升级，以包括全局。决策者的相称性观点必须超越最近的事件，并考虑袭击模式的总成本、这些袭击的长期经济和安全后果以及不作为所发出的信息。一项可以被称为“网络优先——网络可选”的新政策必须从明确的原则开始，即美国正在重新定义网络领域的相称性，加强防御，并提醒对手，未来美国将对整体行为模式进行报复，而不是孤立地对任何一次攻击进行报复，并将使用其掌握的所有工具。对网络攻击的网络响应是一种选择，但远不是唯一的选择。
轮班国际
界定国际行为规范，为未来行动建立明确的基准。这是一项值得做的工作，即使许多国家可能无视这些准则。规范的定义为威慑奠定了基础，因为当这些规范被违反时，它减少了行动的不确定性。不仅仅是声明，意志的展示也是威慑的关键。在宣言性政策实施后，美国及其盟国对第一次网络攻击的强烈反应将有助于确定新的基调。
使转变具有可操作性
将进攻行动演变为战略整体行动。网络政策对外交政策中的主要人物起着后期的、次要的支持作用。因此，所需的变革取决于两个行动：（1）大幅提高风险容忍度，让运营商在机会出现时能够做更多事情；（2）将规划向时间线的左侧大幅移动，在早期政策规划过程中纳入网络工具。然后，政策制定者将准备好运行一个新的、更强大的剧本来赢得网络战争。
第一，调整风险承受能力。向快速行动的更高风险容忍度转变对于更灵活、更积极的方法至关重要。网络攻击必须结合长期计划的战役和即时的机会主义。大型活动对于创建连贯的长期方法至关重要，但在该活动中，运营商必须准备好在出现漏洞的罕见时刻抓住漏洞。理想情况下，政策制定者会改变风险计算：对提议的操作的默认答案应该是“是”，反对者必须证明风险太大，而不是要求操作者证明操作是安全的。
第二，尽早合作。网络，在其相对较新的时候，经常被降级为作战计划的最后一分钟的附加部分，而不是在更大的战役中发挥综合作用。这种方法可以让网络活动有所贡献，但只是在边缘上。相反，规划者应该将网络运营商纳入早期规划，特别是针对同行竞争对手的应急计划。如果开发得足够早，网络工具可以分散和削弱对手的注意力，成为军事和外交行动的力量倍增器。准备好利用幸运的机会需要几个月的研究，规划和预先定位。如果网络工具在紧急需求时刻可用，运营商需要提前计划。
这个进化的模型可以想象成章鱼。攻击性的网络工具，在最好的情况下，是灵活的、创造性的和机会主义的，就像章鱼在野外捕猎一样。网络攻击必须结合长期计划的行动和即时的机会主义就像章鱼的中央大脑和触角。一只章鱼完美地伪装自己，用它的触角探索角落和缝隙，并挤进小得不能再小的角落等待猎物。此外，每个触手都是独立的，但也是整体的一部分。中枢神经系统引导着努力，但每个触手中的大脑管理着搜索。进攻性网络作战的章鱼模型可能包括来自国家安全委员会的战略指导；机构间战役计划；探索和机会主义的前瞻性方法；并将执行低风险和中等风险任务的额外责任委托给国家安全局、中央情报局和赛博司令部。
准备好这些部分后，运行行动手册。战略与国际研究中心的报告详细列出了这些步骤，但要点是：要大胆。将创造性的策略响应与特定攻击者的痛点相匹配。证明美国将把造成损害的网络攻击视为与动能攻击一样严重。
对国会的建议以下国会行动可以加强网络攻击能力，加强国内防御，并帮助建立急需的威慑：
创建并资助一支新的网络部队：网络领域需要自己的服务，主要侧重于后备力量，以从私营部门招募和保留最优秀的网络人才。资助网络安全：国会应考虑资助政府网络急需的资本升级，允许更灵活的网络安全改进支出，并要求改进报告和加强对政府内部薄弱网络防御的问责。他们还应考虑为关键基础设施提供商创造资金流（胡萝卜）和后果（大棒）的组合，以显著提高其抵御攻击的能力。保护行业网络战士：将私营部门视为真正的合作伙伴。为与美国政府合作的网络运营商提供保护，就像许多私营部门在乌克兰所做的那样。结论网络领域需要进行重大变革。华盛顿迫切需要将网络整合到其更广泛的外交政策工具包中，并确定网络活动如何与更大的外交政策行动保持一致，包括威慑、比例反应和国际规范。换句话说，美国需要一个新的剧本来应对日益具有破坏性和侵略性的网络攻击。欲了解更多信息，请参阅战略与国际研究中心的《赢得网络战争的行动手册》。
_source.trans_title: 美国遏制和破坏针对美国本土的外国恶意活动的网络能力
_source.evidence: 文章主要讨论了美国在认知域/网络域面临的威胁（特别是来自中国和伊朗的攻击），并重点提出了应对策略、政策框架调整（如“新声明性政策”）、战略思维转变（将网络攻击视为战争行为）以及具体的政策建议（如国会应如何立法、建立新部队、调整风险容忍度等）。虽然文中提到了具体的攻击事件（涉我事件）和演习（演习演训），但这些是作为背景来支撑其核心论点：即美国需要制定新的战略、政策和理论框架来应对网络战。文章的核心意图在于提出一套应对网络战的理论、政策和战略框架，而非单纯报道某次具体行动或事件。因此，最匹配的标签是[理论政策]。

Around Cornell
News directly from Cornell's colleges and centers
An article about AI combatting conspiracy theories, co-authored by Cornell psychology researchers
Gordon Pennycook
and
David Rand
with a collaborator, has won the 2026
Newcomb Cleveland Prize
from the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS). The association’s oldest award, the prize is given to the authors of an outstanding research article published in the journal Science.
Credit:
Provided
Gordon Pennycook (left) and David Rand
“
Durably Reducing Conspiracy Beliefs Through Dialogues With AI
,” first published Sept. 13, 2024 in
Science
, shows that conversations with large language models can effectively
reduce individuals’ belief in conspiracy theories
– and that these reductions last for at least two months. The finding offers new insights into the psychological mechanisms behind the phenomenon as well as potential tools to fight conspiracies’ spread.
The award includes a $25,000 prize and will be presented during the AAAS Annual Meeting, held Feb. 12-14 in Phoenix.
“We are very honored to receive this prize and delighted that the committee saw the value of leveraging new technological innovations in generative AI to better understand our own psychology,” Pennycook said.
Pennycook, associate professor of psychology and Dorothy and Ariz Mehta Faculty Leadership Fellow in College of Arts and Sciences (A&S) and David Rand, professor in Cornell Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science, the Cornell SC Johnson College of Business and A&S, authored the study with Thomas Costello, lead author and assistant professor at Carnegie Mellon University.
According to Pennycook, the AAAS Newcomb Cleveland Prize last went to a social science article in 1981, to a foundational paper by political scientist Robert Axelrod and evolutionary biologist William Hamilton, “The Evolution of Cooperation.”
Read the story on the College of Arts and Sciences website.

_source.movement_title: 康奈尔研究获AAAS新康布奖：AI对话可减少阴谋论信念
_source.movement_abstract: 康奈尔大学心理学研究者戈登·彭尼库克和大卫·兰德与合作者共同撰写的研究论文《通过与人工智能对话持久减少阴谋论信念》获得了2026年美国科学促进会（AAAS）新康布奖。该研究发表于2024年9月13日的《科学》杂志，发现与大型语言模型的对话可以有效减少个人的阴谋论信念，并且这种效果至少持续两个月。研究为理解阴谋论的心理机制提供了新见解，并为遏制阴谋论的传播提供了潜在工具。该奖项包括25000美元奖金，并将在2026年2月12日至14日的AAAS年会上颁发。

-这些削减至少持续两个月。这一发现为这一现象背后的心理机制提供了新的见解，也为打击阴谋传播提供了潜在的工具。
该奖项包括2.5万美元的奖金，将于2月12日至14日在凤凰城举行的美国科学促进会（AAAS）年会上颁发。
彭尼库克说：“我们非常荣幸获得这个奖项，也很高兴委员会看到了利用生成人工智能的新技术创新来更好地理解我们自己的心理的价值。”
Pennycook，心理学副教授，艺术与科学学院（A&S）的Dorothy和Ariz Mehta教师领导研究员，以及康奈尔大学Ann S.Bowers计算与信息科学学院、康奈尔大学SC Johnson商学院和A&S的David Rand教授，与卡内基梅隆大学的首席作者和助理教授Thomas Costello共同撰写了这项研究。
根据彭尼库克的说法，美国科学促进会纽科姆克利夫兰奖上一次颁给一篇社会科学文章是在1981年，是政治学家罗伯特·阿克塞尔罗德和进化生物学家威廉·汉密尔顿的一篇基础论文《合作的进化》。

(中央社記者林宏翰洛杉磯10日專電)南加州華裔男子孫耀寧被控非法為中國政府做事,遭美國聯邦法院判刑4年,聯邦檢察官辦公室發言人麥克沃伊向中央社表示,美國執法機構絕不允許敵對外國勢力滲透美國政治體系。
美國司法部加州中區聯邦檢察官辦公室公共事務官麥克沃伊(Ciaran McEvoy)今天接受中央社訪問,揭露孫耀寧案中,中國如何透過代理人在美國進行政治滲透、情報蒐集的運作模式。
65歲男子孫耀寧(Yaoning "Mike" Sun)居住在加州奇諾崗市(Chino Hills)。他遭控配合中國政府官員指示,扶植親中政治人物贏得地方選舉,經營親中媒體平台,同時在前總統蔡英文訪美期間,向中國官員回報行程與資訊。
麥克沃伊指出:「美國執法機構不會允許敵對外國勢力滲透進入美國政治體系。中國持續不斷在美國進行情報工作,我們必須以同等堅決、毫不鬆懈的態度來應對,以確保國家安全。」
麥克沃伊說明,這類案件的嚴重程度是「當一個外國政府,特別是對美國不友善的外國政府,試圖影響美國的地方政治,協助特定人士當選市議員,本身就構成很大風險。更令人擔憂的是,這些人可能向上發展,進入州議會、擔任州長甚至國會議員」。
麥克沃伊指出,根據檢方證據,孫耀寧向中國官員撰寫報告,試圖爭取更多資金和任務指派。他在報告中聲稱2022年美國期中選舉,他成功組織團隊,協助「個案一」當選市議員,稱這個「個案一」為「新興的政治明星」。
司法部新聞稿沒有公布這名政治人物的身分,不過「洛杉磯時報」去年5月報導,孫耀寧2022年協助王愛琳(Eileen Wang)選上阿凱迪亞(Arcadia)市議員,兩人曾經是未婚夫妻關係。
孫耀寧遭到判刑4年之前不久,王愛琳今年2月就任阿凱迪亞市長,她去年5月向「洛杉磯時報」否認指控,並稱已經與孫耀寧解除婚約。
根據「洛杉磯時報」調查,孫耀寧引進已註冊為外國代理人的「龍鷹媒體集團」(EDI Media)資源,利用旗下「城市新聞網」(iCity News)在選前刊登多篇文章,力挺親中候選人王愛琳。
麥克沃伊指出,孫耀寧違法之處在於,未依規定通知美國政府,也就是沒有向美國司法部登記,他在美國擔任中華人民共和國的代理人。他指出,孫耀寧在認罪協議中坦承,從2022年到2024年接受中國政府官員指揮,擔任中共代理人,在美國推廣親中的宣傳內容。
根據檢方資料,2023年時任總統蔡英文訪美,過境洛杉磯,孫耀寧將行程通報給中國領事館官員。
孫耀寧也向中國官員報告「海外反華勢力」,包括支持台灣、西藏與新疆獨立及法輪功議題,並建議動用洛杉磯的組織來對抗這些勢力。他也向中國官員申請8萬美元(約新台幣254萬元)準備在美國國慶日於華府舉行親中示威。
麥克沃伊指出,中華人民共和國在美國的活動,多年來一直在執法部門的雷達上,美國政府嚴肅看待這類案件;全案最嚴重之處是「有人在隱瞞外國代理人的身分下,協助他人當選市議員,這件事情沒有告知選民」。(編輯:田瑞華)1150211

_source.movement_abstract: 美国联邦法院近日判处南加州华裔男子孙耀宁4年监禁，指控其为中华人民共和国从事非法活动，包括协助亲中政治人物赢得地方选举、经营亲中媒体平台及向中国官员汇报美国政治动态。联邦检察官麦卡沃伊指出，中国持续在美国进行情报工作，试图渗透美国政治体系，此案显示外国势力通过代理人影响美国地方政治，存在重大安全风险。孙耀宁承认从2022年至2024年接受中国官员指挥，担任中共代理人，并向中国报告美国政治动态及反华势力。此外，孙耀宁曾协助王爱琳当选市议员，王爱琳后就任市市长，但否认相关指控。
